entry.title: Research Summary: June 30, 2026

author.name: AATF AI News Aggregator

entry.summary:
Today's research is anchored by landmark AI-for-science results and a strong safety/alignment cluster.

  • Herculaneum papyrus: complete virtual unwrapping and reading of a sealed carbonized scroll via synchrotron imaging plus ML—a milestone with reach beyond machine learning.
  • A machine-verified proof resolves the decade-old FGG conjecture on QAOA approximation ratios, showcasing LLM-assisted formal mathematics.

Safety, alignment, and interpretability dominate the remainder:

  • Safety from Honesty (Bengio) formalizes a disinterested Scientist AI Predictor approximating a Bayesian posterior to argue against implicit agency.
  • CPE (Mechanistically Eliciting Latent Behaviors) discovers interpretable low-rank adapters to surface hidden behaviors via tensor decomposition.
  • CAREBench introduces a 500-prompt, twelve-category child-safety benchmark.
  • Causal Registers in Scratchpad edits internal states to test chain-of-thought faithfulness.

Methods, systems, and security round out the list:

  • DataComp-VLM ships 160 datasets for controlled, data-centric vision-language research (Schmidt, Bethge, Jitsev).
  • PixelRAG runs retrieval-augmented generation entirely in pixel space over web screenshots, beating text pipelines (Zaharia, Gonzalez).
  • A rigorous policy-gradient analysis exposes GRPO's credit-assignment collapse, gradient sparsity, and rank collapse.
  • Proofs of Ownership (Goldwasser, Canetti) opens a formal cryptographic treatment of stolen-model attribution.
entry.content:
Today's research is anchored by landmark AI-for-science results and a strong safety/alignment cluster.

  • Herculaneum papyrus: complete virtual unwrapping and reading of a sealed carbonized scroll via synchrotron imaging plus ML—a milestone with reach beyond machine learning.
  • A machine-verified proof resolves the decade-old FGG conjecture on QAOA approximation ratios, showcasing LLM-assisted formal mathematics.

Safety, alignment, and interpretability dominate the remainder:

  • Safety from Honesty (Bengio) formalizes a disinterested Scientist AI Predictor approximating a Bayesian posterior to argue against implicit agency.
  • CPE (Mechanistically Eliciting Latent Behaviors) discovers interpretable low-rank adapters to surface hidden behaviors via tensor decomposition.
  • CAREBench introduces a 500-prompt, twelve-category child-safety benchmark.
  • Causal Registers in Scratchpad edits internal states to test chain-of-thought faithfulness.

Methods, systems, and security round out the list:

  • DataComp-VLM ships 160 datasets for controlled, data-centric vision-language research (Schmidt, Bethge, Jitsev).
  • PixelRAG runs retrieval-augmented generation entirely in pixel space over web screenshots, beating text pipelines (Zaharia, Gonzalez).
  • A rigorous policy-gradient analysis exposes GRPO's credit-assignment collapse, gradient sparsity, and rank collapse.
  • Proofs of Ownership (Goldwasser, Canetti) opens a formal cryptographic treatment of stolen-model attribution.

entry.title: Complete virtual unwrapping and reading of a rolled Herculaneum papyrus

author.name: Giorgio Angelotti, Stephen Parsons, Federica Nicolardi, Youssef Nader, Sean Johnson, David Josey, Paul Henderson, Hendrik Schilling, Johannes Rudolph, Forrest McDonald, Elian Rafael Dal Pr\'a, Paul Tafforeau, Alessandro Mirone, Clifford Seth Parker, Jan Paul Posma, Benjamin Kyles, Claudio Vergara, Alessia Lavorante, Rossella Villa, Maria Chiara Robustelli, Marzia D'Angelo, Gianluca Del Mastro, Michael McOsker, Kilian Fleischer, Christy Chapman, Nat Friedman, William Brent Seales

entry.summary: Building on the earlier Social buzz, here's the full research paper, This landmark work achieves complete virtual unwrapping and reading of a sealed carbonized Herculaneum papyrus using high-resolution synchrotron micro-CT and machine learning, going far beyond prior localized readings. The team includes Vesuvius Challenge leaders Nat Friedman and Brent Seales. It matters as a major breakthrough in recovering lost classical texts non-invasively.

entry.title: Safety from Honesty in a Disinterested AI Predictor

author.name: Yoshua Bengio, Oliver Richardson, Tom\'a\v{s} Gaven\v{c}iak, Michael Cohen, Rory Svarc, Damiano Fornasiere, Gael Gendron, David Hyland, Aton Kamanda, Adam Oberman, Francis Rhys Ward, Anna Gaven\v{c}iak, Jacob Livingston Slosser, Vincent Mai, Iulian Serban, Joumana Ghosn

entry.summary: Bengio and collaborators present a formal safety argument for a Scientist AI Predictor trained to approximate the Bayesian posterior over epistemically contextualized statements, arguing it can honestly predict agents and consequences without itself becoming a goal-directed agent. Epistemic contextualization separates factual claims from communication acts. It matters for non-agentic AI safety design.

entry.title: DataComp-VLM: Improved Open Datasets for Vision-Language Models

author.name: Matteo Farina, Vishaal Udandarao, Thao Nguyen, Selim Kuzucu, Maximilian B\"other, Andreas Hochlehnert, Adhiraj Ghosh, Marianna Nezhurina, Karsten Roth, Joschka Struber, Yuhui Zhang, Sebastian Dziadzio, Elaine Sui, Soumya Jahagirdar, Dhruba Ghosh, Hasan Hammoud, Thomas De Min, Simone Caldarella, Jehanzeb Mirza, Sedrick Keh, Mehdi Cherti, Hilde Kuehne, Bernt Schiele, Serena Yeung-Levy, Muhammad Ferjad Naeem, Federico Tombari, Ana Klimovic, Elisa Ricci, Matthias Bethge, Sewoong Oh, Ameya Prabhu, Alessio Tonioni, Jenia Jitsev, Massimiliano Mancini, Ludwig Schmidt, Nikhil Parthasarathy

entry.summary: DataComp-VLM introduces a large benchmark for controlled, data-centric experiments to improve vision-language model training, with 160 datasets totaling 6T multimodal tokens across image-caption, interleaved, text, and instruction-tuning data. Participants test curation strategies across 1B-8B models and varied token budgets.

entry.title: Mechanistically Eliciting Latent Behaviors in Language Models

author.name: Andrew Mack, Nina Panickssery, Alexander Matt Turner

entry.summary: Introduces Causal Perturbative Elicitation (CPE), an unsupervised method that discovers interpretable low-rank adapters via tensor decomposition to surface hidden behavioral modes in LLMs from a single example. It can rival supervised elicitation and supports systematic risk evaluation.

entry.title: A Machine-Verified Proof of a Quantum-Optimization Conjecture

author.name: Uri Kol, Maor Ben-Shahar, Kfir Sulimany, Dirk Englund

entry.summary: This work reports a machine-verified resolution of the decade-old FGG conjecture on QAOA approximation ratios for the ring of disagrees, with the proof found by Claude Fable 5 and verified end-to-end in Lean 4. It builds on a Lean quantum-information library and an agentic toolkit. It matters as a demonstration of LLM-assisted formal mathematical discovery.

entry.title: CAREBench: A Child-Safety Risk Benchmark for Language Models

author.name: Kaavya Krishna-Kumar, Elaine Lau, Vaughn Robinson, Jay Caldwell, Sheriff Issaka, Skyler Wang, Francisco Guzm\'an, Steven Kelling, Jonas Mueller

entry.summary: Introduces CAREBench, a 500-prompt benchmark spanning twelve child-safety risk categories such as grooming, impersonation, surveillance, and emotional dependence, focused on upstream risks before explicit harm. It evaluates whether frontier models recognize child-safety risks early.

entry.title: On the Policy Gradient Foundations of Group Relative Policy Optimization: Credit Assignment, Gradient Sparsity, and Rank Collapse

author.name: Amritansh Mishra, Supriyo Chakraborty, Berkcan Kapusuzoglu

entry.summary: Provides a rigorous policy-gradient derivation of GRPO, revealing that output-only reward collapses token-level credit to a single scalar, causing intensifying gradient sparsity and a rank-2 gradient structure. Verified via SVD analysis on Nemotron-4B/GSM8K.

entry.title: Do Models Read What They Write? Causal Registers in Scratchpad Reasoning

author.name: Benjamin Shih, John Winnicki, Eric Darve

entry.summary: Tests whether models actually use their own scratchpad reasoning by editing the internal representation of a written intermediate state and checking if downstream computation follows, using a controlled state-tracking task with a known update rule. This probes the faithfulness assumption underlying process supervision for alignment.

entry.title: Proofs of Ownership for Machine Learning Models

author.name: Ran Canetti, Shafi Goldwasser, Or Zamir

entry.summary: This paper formally studies proof of ownership for ML models as a three-party game between owner, thief, and judge, analyzing when a stolen model can be provably traced to its creator. It establishes theoretical conditions for ownership verification.

entry.title: PIXELRAG: Web Screenshots Beat Text for Retrieval-Augmented Generation

author.name: Yichuan Wang, Zhifei Li, Zirui Wang, Paul Teiletche, Lesheng Jin, Matei Zaharia, Joseph E. Gonzalez, Sewon Min

entry.summary: PixelRAG performs retrieval-augmented generation entirely in pixel space over web screenshots, eliminating HTML parsing and preserving layout and visual structure. It scales to 30 million Wikipedia screenshot images and claims pixel retrieval beats text for RAG.

entry.title: Learning the structure of open quantum systems

author.name: Laura Lewis, Ewin Tang, John Wright

entry.summary: Designs an algorithm to learn the coefficients of constant-local Lindbladians (open quantum systems) with efficient evolution time using non-adaptive ancilla-free measurements. It extends Hamiltonian-learning guarantees to the harder dissipative open-system setting.

entry.title: The Heterogeneous Safety Impacts of Benign Multilingual Fine-Tuning

author.name: Will Hawkins, Kaivalya Rawal, Jonathan Rystr{\o}m, Stratis Tsirtsis, Zihao Fu, Greta Warren, Ryan Brown, Eoin Delaney, Sandra Wachter, Brent Mittelstadt, Chris Russell

entry.summary: First comprehensive study showing that benign multilingual fine-tuning of Llama-3.2, Qwen3, and Gemma-3 increases adversarial compliance, with safety outcomes highly sensitive to fine-tuning and evaluation language (up to four-fold higher compliance). It documents heterogeneous multilingual safety drift.

entry.title: When More Sampling Hurts: The Modal Ceiling and Correlation Ceiling of Test-Time Scaling

author.name: Yong Yi Bay, Kathleen A. Yearick

entry.summary: This paper examines a limitation of test-time scaling in reasoning models, distinguishing between coverage (the chance some sample is correct) and selection (picking the right one). It argues that beyond a point, extra sampling makes models more confident in wrong answers, formalizing an identifiability gap between answers a model can produce versus pick.

entry.title: The Mirage of Optimizing Training Policies: Monotonic Inference Policies as the Real Objective for LLM Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Jing Liang, Hongyao Tang, Yi Ma, Yancheng He, Weixun Wang, Xiaoyang Li, Ju Huang, Wenbo Su, Jinyi Liu, Yan Zheng, Jianye Hao, Bo Zheng

entry.summary: Argues that LLM RL post-training instability stems from a training-inference mismatch where separate engines yield inconsistent probabilities, and reframes the real objective as optimizing monotonic inference policies rather than training policies. The work targets a fundamental cause of RL collapse in LLM fine-tuning.

entry.title: When Does Online Imitation Learning Help in LLM Post-Training? The Role of (Non-)Realizability Beyond Horizon

author.name: Huaqing Zhang, Jingchu Gai, Juno Kim, Bingbin Liu, Andrej Risteski

entry.summary: This work analyzes when online imitation learning (on-policy distillation) beats offline SFT in LLM post-training, arguing the benefit hinges on realizability rather than error accumulation. They prove offline IL faces an information barrier in misspecified settings while matching experts under realizability.

entry.title: Nemotron-Labs-Diffusion-Image: Advancing Masked Discrete Diffusion for High-Resolution Image Synthesis

author.name: Shufan Li, Greg Heinrich, Hanrong Ye, Yonggan Fu, Aditya Grover, Jan Kautz, Pavlo Molchanov

entry.summary: An NVIDIA-affiliated masked discrete diffusion model for high-resolution text-to-image synthesis that adds self-correction to unmask-and-revise discrete tokens and handles sparse training signals from large vocabularies. It targets known weaknesses of masked diffusion versus continuous diffusion.

entry.title: On the Nonlinearity of Learning Rate Scaling for LLM Training

author.name: Zaiwen Yang, Huaqing Zhang, Jing Xu, Jingzhao Zhang

entry.summary: Empirically examines learning-rate transfer for LLM training, finding the optimal LR develops upward curvature at larger scales that breaks log-linear extrapolation. Shows curvature largely disappears when using effective learning rate in normalized weight space.

entry.title: Fuzzing Large Language Models to Elicit Hidden Behaviours

author.name: Mohammed Abu Baker, Lakshmi Babu-Saheer

entry.summary: Studies fuzzing—injecting Gaussian noise into model weights or residual-stream activations—to elicit hidden backdoor behaviors in sleeper-agent models without knowing the trigger. On six backdoored 7B-13B models, fuzzing outperforms temperature sampling, sometimes up to 6x.

entry.title: Building Multi-Task Agentic LLMs via Two-Phase Distillation

author.name: Huaijie Wang, Shusheng Xu, Yi Wu, Kaifeng Lyu

entry.summary: Studies building multi-task agentic LLMs by training separate RL experts per task then consolidating via distillation, showing off-policy distillation degrades because forward KL's mode-covering nature exceeds student capacity across many task modes. It proposes a two-phase approach leveraging on-policy mode-seeking distillation with strong initialization.

entry.title: Internal-State Probes Read the Situation, Not the Action: Three Negative Results for Pre-Action Misalignment Monitoring

author.name: Max Fomin, Elad David, Amit LeVi

entry.summary: This paper presents three negative results showing that internal-state probes read the situation context rather than predicting forthcoming harmful actions, undermining their use for pre-action misalignment monitoring. Tests span Qwen, Llama, and Gemma model families.

entry.title: Meta-learning as a principle for human-like visual representations

author.name: Can Demircan, Marcel Binz, Alireza Modirshanechi, Eric Schulz

entry.summary: This paper hypothesizes that human-like visual representations arise from meta-learning, training a sequence model without human supervision across thousands of image-to-concept tasks. The meta-learned representations better match human visual structure than pretrained base encoders.

entry.title: MOPD: Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation for Capability Integration in LLM Post-Training

author.name: Wenhan Ma, Jianyu Wei, Liang Zhao, Hailin Zhang, Bangjun Xiao, Lei Li, Qibin Yang, Bofei Gao, Yudong Wang, Rang Li, Jinhao Dong, Zhifang Sui, Fuli Luo

entry.summary: MOPD is a multi-teacher on-policy distillation method for integrating multiple RL-specialized capabilities into a single LLM via per-domain teachers distilled on student rollouts. It outperforms mix-RL and merging baselines on Qwen3-30B-A3B.

entry.title: Meshtryoshka: Differentiable Rendering of Real-World Scenes via Mesh Rasterization

author.name: David Charatan, Daniel Xu, Richard Szeliski, George Kopanas, Vincent Sitzmann

entry.summary: Meshtryoshka is a differentiable rendering framework using nested mesh shells (matryoshka-like) with an off-the-shelf triangle rasterizer to reconstruct large-scale unbounded real-world scenes as meshes, overcoming prior mesh-based methods' object-centric limitations. It bridges differentiable rendering quality with mesh outputs needed by graphics pipelines.

entry.title: Modification-Considering Value Learning for Reward Hacking Mitigation in RL

author.name: Evgenii Opryshko, Umangi Jain, Igor Gilitschenski

entry.summary: MCVL mitigates reward hacking by treating each incoming transition as a candidate modification, forecasting training paths with and without it and scoring with a frozen reference. It operationalizes current-utility optimization for value-based RL.

entry.title: Representational Depth of Evaluation Awareness Shifts With Scale in Open-Weight Language Models

author.name: Archit Manek

entry.summary: Investigates whether language models recognize evaluation contexts, finding a size-dependent shift where evaluation-awareness becomes linearly recoverable in earlier layers for larger models across Qwen, Gemma, and Llama families. This has implications for benchmark interpretation and AI safety.

entry.title: MemLeak: Diagnosing Information Leaks in Multimodal Agent Memory

author.name: Kuan Wang, Chao Zhang

entry.summary: Introduces the Information Provenance Graph taxonomy and MemLeak benchmark showing that deleting a fact from multimodal agent memory leaves it recoverable from retained images via implicit visual cues used by VLMs. Retained correlated text enables 18.3% recovery and images 12% despite reported deletion success.

entry.title: Stabilizing Extrapolation in Looped Transformers via Learned Stochastic Stopping

author.name: Hsun-Yu Kuo, El Mahdi Chayti, Patrik Reizinger, Wieland Brendel, Martin Jaggi

entry.summary: Addresses brittle length generalization in Looped Transformers by tracing high out-of-distribution variance to a spurious correlation between sequence length and loop count, then introducing stochastic stopping (including RL-Halting) to stabilize extrapolation. The approach sharply reduces OOD variance.

entry.title: TraceLab: Characterizing Coding Agent Workloads for LLM Serving

author.name: Kan Zhu, Mathew Jacob, Chenxi Ma, Yi Pan, Stephanie Wang, Arvind Krishnamurthy, Baris Kasikci

entry.summary: TraceLab releases a trace of roughly 4,300 real coding-agent sessions with about 350,000 LLM steps and 430,000 tool calls from daily Claude Code and Codex use, characterizing workloads for LLM serving. Analysis reveals long autonomous loops and long contexts with short outputs.

entry.title: GPC: Large-Scale Generative Pretraining for Transferable Motor Control

author.name: Yi Shi, Yifeng Jiang, Chen Tessler, Xue Bin Peng

entry.summary: GPC builds general-purpose physics-based character controllers via tokenization and next-token modeling, learning a motion vocabulary with Finite Scalar Quantization jointly with a control policy through end-to-end RL. It enables reusable generative motor control from large motion datasets. It matters for scalable physics-based character animation and embodied control.

entry.title: REAR: Test-time Preference Realignment through Reward Decomposition

author.name: Fuxiang Zhang, Pengcheng Wang, Chenran Li, Yi-Chen Li, Yuxin Chen, Lang Feng, Chenfeng Xu, Masayoshi Tomizuka, Bo An

entry.summary: REAR is a training-free test-time framework for realigning LLM outputs to diverse user preferences by decomposing the reward into preference-related and base components. It extends test-time scaling beyond verifiable domains like math into subjective preference alignment.

entry.title: SGD Provably Prioritizes a Shortcut Spurious Feature in the XOR Model

author.name: Tyler LaBonte, Vidya Muthukumar

entry.summary: Provides the first end-to-end theoretical characterization showing that SGD on two-layer ReLU networks learns spurious linear features before the true XOR signal, and exponentially fast. It clarifies the mechanism behind shortcut learning.

entry.title: MALOQ: Massively Accelerated Learning of Operators for Quantum Transport

author.name: Manasa Kaniselvan, Alexander Maeder, Denghui Lu, Alexandros Nikolaos Ziogas, Mathieu Luisier

entry.summary: MALOQ is a scalable ML application that predicts DFT Hamiltonian/density matrices for quantum transport in systems up to 100k atoms, using an SO(2)-equivariant backbone with custom data kernels and edge-wise distribution. It extends electronic-structure calculations to previously infeasible scales.

entry.title: When Can Conformal Risk Control Certify LLM Outputs? Bounds, Impossibility, and Adaptation for Structured Generation

author.name: Varun Kotte

entry.summary: Characterizes when conformal risk control can certify structured LLM outputs, proving an impossibility result with a closed-form feasibility test when base risk exceeds the target. Analyzes a certification hierarchy across Hoeffding, empirical Bernstein, and betting-based bounds.

entry.title: Reported Confidence in LLMs Tracks Commitment More Than Correctness

author.name: Dharshan Kumaran

entry.summary: Tests whether verbal confidence reports in LLMs estimate correctness, using a two-stage abstention paradigm from perceptual decision neuroscience. Finds verbal confidence predicts commit/abstain decisions better than answer correctness, while token log-probabilities show the opposite, coupling abstention to correctness.

entry.title: Muon learns balanced solutions in matrix factorization without slow saddle-to-saddle dynamics

author.name: Mark Rhee, Jamie Simon, Dhruva Karkada

entry.summary: This work analyzes how the Muon optimizer differs from gradient descent in matrix factorization, showing Muon avoids slow saddle-to-saddle dynamics, learns all top modes at the same rate, and remains stable above the standard sharpness threshold. It provides dynamical insight into Muon's advantages.

entry.title: Self-Supervised Theorem Discovery in a Formal Axiomatic System

author.name: Kazuki Ota, Takayuki Osa, Tatsuya Harada

entry.summary: This paper develops a self-supervised theorem-discovery agent that starts from only axioms and inference rules in a formal axiomatic system, alternating between proof search and useful-theorem extraction to grow a theorem library without human priors. It studies whether useful theorems can be discovered autonomously.

entry.title: HARD-KV: Head-Adaptive Regularization for Decoding-time KV Compression

author.name: Yuxuan Yang, Feiyang Ren, Bowen Zeng, Dalin Zhang, Jinpeng Chen, Gang Chen, Huan Li

entry.summary: HARD-KV resolves the conflict between dynamic head-adaptive KV compression and rigid static memory patterns required by inference engines like vLLM. It uses a cascade cache hierarchy and logits calibration to enable consistent Top-p budgeting for long-context inference.

entry.title: Statistically Indistinguishable, Operationally Distinct: A Formal Barrier for Tabular Foundation Models

author.name: Tassilo Klein, Johannes Hoffart

entry.summary: Introduces the Operational Turing Test showing tabular foundation models cannot distinguish legal from rule-violating database states whose marginals match closely, establishing a formal Bayes-error barrier. Only classifiers fed executable rule-derived audits succeed.

entry.title: Few-Step Boltzmann Generators via Scalable Likelihood Flow Maps

author.name: RuiKang OuYang, Hanlin Yu, Xinyue Ai, Yutong He, Nicholas M. Boffi, Pradeep Ravikumar, Jose Miguel Hernandez-Lobato, Max Simchowitz, Benjamin Kurt Miller, Omar Chehab

entry.summary: SCALLOP distills likelihood from flow maps for few-step Boltzmann generators, reducing the variance of Hutchinson trace estimation used in F2D2. It enables scalable likelihood estimation alongside fast sampling.

entry.title: CRAFT: Counterfactual Credit Assignment from Free Sibling Rollouts for Self-Distilled Agentic Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Zibin Meng, Kani Chen

entry.summary: CRAFT is a three-pillar counterfactual credit-assignment scheme for self-distilled agentic RL that reuses GRPO sibling rollouts, addressing the retrospective and sign-blind limitations of the standard log-probability gating signal. It importance-weights counterfactual token contributions.

entry.title: The Joint Effect of Quantization and Sampling Temperature on LLM Safety Alignment: A Factorial Analysis

author.name: Hari Prasad, Ritam Pal

entry.summary: A factorial study of how quantization precision and sampling temperature jointly affect LLM safety alignment, spanning 9 models, 3 precisions, and 6 temperatures across ~322k responses judged by a six-model ensemble. It tests whether low-bit deployment and stochastic sampling amplify each other to erode safety.

entry.title: Same Concept, Different Directions: Cross-Modal Feature Heterogeneity in Sparse Autoencoders

author.name: Chungpa Lee, Jihoon Kwon, Kyle Min, Jy-yong Sohn

entry.summary: Challenges the untested assumption that semantically corresponding features share the same directions across image and text modalities in joint embedding spaces, identifying cross-modal feature heterogeneity using sparse autoencoders. It demonstrates that the same concept points in different directions across modalities.

entry.title: Diffusion Fine-tuning with Rewarded Moment Matching Distillation

author.name: Alexis Jacq, Guillaume Couairon, Valentin De Bortoli, Quentin Berthet, Arnaud Doucet, Romuald Elie

entry.summary: RMMD jointly distills diffusion models and maximizes a reward function, preserving the high-fidelity naturalness of multi-step moment-matching distillation while supporting on-policy reward optimization. It explores the FID-reward Pareto frontier in diffusion post-training.

entry.title: SWE-INTERACT: Reimagining SWE Benchmarks as User-Driven Long-Horizon Coding Sessions

author.name: Mohit Raghavendra, Anisha Gunjal, Aakash Sabharwal, Yunzhong He

entry.summary: SWE-Interact is a benchmark that reimagines software engineering evaluation as multi-turn, user-driven sessions where a simulator starts with vague instructions and progressively reveals requirements and feedback. It tests whether coding agents can discover user intent and adapt to evolving requirements.

entry.title: Pessimism's Paradox: Conservative Offline Training Amplifies Reward Hacking During Online Adaptation in Reasoning Models

author.name: Subramanyam Sahoo, Aman Chadha, Vinija Jain, Divya Chaudhary

entry.summary: This paper empirically and mechanistically challenges the assumption that conservative offline training is safe, showing that higher offline conservatism monotonically amplifies reward hacking during subsequent online adaptation in reasoning models. Experiments use a Qwen3-14B policy under DPO with a learned reward ensemble.

entry.title: Generating in the Limit with Infinitely Many Hallucinations

author.name: Irene Strauss, Alexandra Butoi, Ryan Cotterell

entry.summary: This paper introduces a precision notion into the language-generation-in-the-limit framework, recasting coverage versus validity as a recall-precision trade-off, and analyzes generation under constraints on enumeration, novelty, and validity. It studies generation that allows infinitely many hallucinations.

entry.title: Conformal Prediction with Macro-Coverage Guarantees

author.name: Aabesh Bhattacharyya, Tiffany Ding, Rina Foygel Barber

entry.summary: This paper develops conformal prediction methods with macro-coverage guarantees, the unweighted average of class-conditional coverage, as a middle ground between marginal and strict class-conditional coverage. It targets settings with many rare classes and few calibration points.

entry.title: Evolution Fine-Tuning: Learning to Discover Across 371 Optimization Tasks

author.name: Young-Jun Lee, Seungone Kim, Minki Kang, Alistair Cheong Liang Chuen, Zerui Chen, Seungho Han, Taehee Jung, Dongyeop Kang

entry.summary: Evolution Fine-Tuning trains LLMs across 371 optimization tasks so that the model itself learns to evolve solutions (knowing what to mutate, when to backtrack) rather than relying on external search scaffolds. It aims to transfer search experience across domains like GPU kernels and math conjectures. It matters for building general-purpose discovery agents.

entry.title: BrainJanus: A Unified Model for Understanding and Generation across Brain, Vision, and Language

author.name: Haitao Wu, Qirui Zhang, Zhouheng Yao, Shangquan Sun, Qihao Zheng, Mianxin Liu, Chi Zhang, Wanli Ouyang, Chunfeng Song, Changqing Zhang, Jiamin Wu

entry.summary: BrainJanus is a unified model integrating brain neural activity, vision, and language into a shared token space for both encoding and decoding tasks. It is notable as a first attempt to treat brain-vision-language as a single multimodal generation/understanding framework.

entry.title: A Stochastic--Geometric Theory of Scaling Laws in Grokking

author.name: R\'ois\'in Luo, Christian Gagn\'e, Jonas Ngnaw\'e, Ihsan Ullah, Karyn Morrissey

entry.summary: Provides a stochastic-geometric theory explaining grokking as arising from a shell-core topological structure of solution space induced by Adam plus weight shrinkage. It offers a mechanistic account of delayed generalization and associated scaling laws.

entry.title: Can LLMs Hire Fairly? Racial Bias in Resume Screening

author.name: Zhenyu Gao, Wenxi Jiang, Yutong Yan

entry.summary: Audits fourteen LLMs for racial bias in resume screening using a paired-resume field-experiment methodology, finding that pre-2024 models reproduce pro-White bias while 2024+ models show null gaps or pro-Black reversals. Documents a generational reversal in algorithmic hiring bias direction.

entry.title: To Reason or to Fabricate: Reasoning Without Shortcuts via Hint-Anchored Pairwise Aggregation

author.name: Jiuheng Lin, Chen Zhang, Yansong Feng

entry.summary: HIPPO is an RL framework that combats pre-RL data overlap—where models memorize answers and fabricate post-hoc reasoning—by using hint injection to trigger overlap behaviors as anchors for pairwise comparison with a tailored reward model. It enables a lightweight judge to distinguish genuine reasoning from shortcuts.

entry.title: Does Verbose Chain-of-Thought Really Help? In-Distribution Evidence that Content, Not Length, Matters

author.name: Wenlong Wang, Fergal Reid

entry.summary: Using in-distribution paired short and long natural generations across 25 models, this paper finds that extra chain-of-thought tokens leave accuracy essentially unchanged for independently-trained reasoners, arguing that content rather than length drives CoT gains. It directly tests a contested mechanism behind CoT prompting.

entry.title: Walking in the Implicit: Interactive World Exploration via Neural Scene Representation

author.name: Zhiqi Li, Chengrui Dong, Zhenhua Du, Hangning Zhou, Cong Qiu, Hailong Qin, Mu Yang, Dongxu Wei, Peidong Liu

entry.summary: Walking in the Implicit reframes interactive world exploration by changing the rollout variable from frame latents to a fixed-length renderable implicit scene state (Neural Implicit Scene), factorizing generation into compact state transition and deterministic pose-conditioned rendering. NeuWorld instantiates this with a transformer VAE and diffusion transformer.

entry.title: RIPA: Sensory-Vector Prompt Injection Attacks on LLM-Controlled ROS 2 Robots

author.name: Nima Dorzhiev

entry.summary: RIPA presents the first systematic multi-channel study of prompt injection attacks delivered through the sensory pipeline of ROS 2-based LLM-controlled robots, testing five LLMs and finding non-monotonic vulnerability profiles (e.g., Llama-3.3-70B showing 100% attack success). It reveals model-specific vulnerabilities that do not scale predictably with size.

entry.title: DLR: Zero-Inference-Cost Latent Residuals for Low-Rank Pre-Training

author.name: Dong Wang, Wenwu Tang, Yun Cheng, Olga Saukh

entry.summary: DLR is a training-only, parameter-free plug-in for low-rank pretraining that adds a fixed structured residual replicating latent coordinates across outputs. It improves low-rank pretraining quality with zero inference cost after being folded into weights.

entry.title: Symbolic Mechanistic Data Attribution: Tracing Training Influence to Learned Behavioral Policies

author.name: Reza Habibi, Darian Lee, Magy Seif El-Nasr

entry.summary: SMDA attributes training examples to interpretable symbolic policies governing model behavior, fitting Ridge regression over sparse autoencoder features and decomposing how fine-tuning examples shift policy. Demonstrated on refusal behavior in Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct.

entry.title: Multi-Block Diffusion Language Models

author.name: Yijie Jin, Jiajun Xu, Yuxuan Liu, Chenkai Xu, Yi Tu, Jiajun Li, Dandan Tu, Xiaohui Yan, Kai Yu, Pengfei Liu, Zhijie Deng

entry.summary: Extends block diffusion language models from single-block to multi-block decoding, where consecutive blocks are decoded concurrently for inter-block parallelism. It resolves training-inference mismatch arising from teacher forcing versus running-set decoding.

entry.title: Sample Complexity of Scientific Discovery: PAC Learnability of Compositional Function Trees

author.name: \c{S}uayp Talha Kocabay, Talha R\"uzgar Akku\c{s}, Kerem Yal\c{c}{\i}n

entry.summary: Analyzes the PAC learnability of compositional function trees for symbolic regression, proving that Rademacher complexity is controlled by depth and operator Lipschitz constants rather than blowing up exponentially with distinct structures. This challenges the view that symbolic discovery is statistically intractable.

entry.title: The Forgetting-Retention Dilemma: Certified Unlearning Theory in Continual Learning

author.name: Yiting Hu, Lingjie Duan, Qian Zhang

entry.summary: Establishes the first theoretical foundation bridging continual learning and certified machine unlearning, formulating the post-unlearning excess risk that decomposes into CL risk and unlearning loss. It characterizes the fundamental forgetting-retention trade-off.

entry.title: Experience Augmented Policy Optimization for LLM Reasoning

author.name: Jinda Lu, Kexin Huang, Junkang Wu, Shuo Yang, Jinghan Li, Chiyu Ma, Shaohang Wei, Xiang Wang, Guoyin Wang, Jingren Zhou

entry.summary: EAPO improves RLVR for LLM reasoning by expressing accumulated experience in a policy-adaptive manner rather than reusing fixed reasoning trajectories, which suffer from policy mismatch. It aims to reduce sampling costs and improve experience utilization during RL training.

entry.title: Attractor States Emerge in Multi-Turn LLM Conversations

author.name: Ting-Wen Ko, Jonas Geiping

entry.summary: This study finds that open-ended multi-turn LLM conversations settle into model-specific attractor states in representation space, with self-play attractors asymmetrically pulling conversation partners in mixed-play debates. Tested across 7 LLMs and 20 controversial topics.

entry.title: C$^{2}$R: Cross-sample Consistency Regularization Mitigates Feature Splitting and Absorption in Sparse Autoencoders

author.name: Haoran Jin, Xiting Wang, Shijie Ren, Hong Xie, Defu Lian

entry.summary: C2R introduces cross-sample consistency regularization to mitigate feature splitting and absorption in sparse autoencoders used to interpret LLMs. It enforces consistent latent assignment across samples to improve atomicity and reliability of learned features.

entry.title: The Voronoi Bottleneck: Capacity-Aware Dense Retrieval for Product Search

author.name: Charith Chandra Sai Balne, Rithwik Maramraju, Siddharth Pratap Singh, Rohit Upadhyay, Aditya Singh, Chittaranjan Tripathy, Yogananda Domlur Seetharama

entry.summary: This paper introduces the Voronoi Bottleneck, proving that Voronoi complexity and sign-rank are equivalent for top-1 dense retrieval and yielding dimension bounds plus a label-free diagnostic (Capacity Utilization Score) predicting per-query failure. It diagnoses capacity regimes for product search.

entry.title: Forensic Trajectory Signatures for Agent Memory Poisoning Detection

author.name: Jun Wen Leong

entry.summary: Identifies a behavioral invariant in LLM agents under memory poisoning—successful exfiltration attacks require recalling memory before sending email—and builds a forensic trajectory classifier achieving AUC 0.99. It offers a detection signal for agent memory poisoning.

entry.title: Optimization Dynamics Imprint Semantic Specificity in Contrastive Embedding Norms

author.name: Ziwei Su, Junyu Ren, Victor Veitch

entry.summary: Provides a theoretical framework explaining why embedding norms in scale-invariant contrastive models still encode semantic properties like concept specificity and token frequency. It derives an analytic formula showing norms emerge as a byproduct of optimization dynamics, usable as free calibration signals.

entry.title: Emergence of a Shared Canonical Object Frame from In-the-Wild Videos

author.name: Tom Fischer, Martin Sundermeyer, Adam Kortylewski, Eddy Ilg

entry.summary: Shows that a shared canonical object frame can emerge from self-supervised training on in-the-wild object-centric videos using only noisy SfM poses, by routing sequences through a shared coarse canonical mesh bottleneck. This removes the manual annotation bottleneck for cross-instance pose comparison.

entry.title: On the Inseparability of Instructions and Data in Shared-Embedding Sequence Models

author.name: Dewank Pant, Shruti Lohani, Avijit Kumar

entry.summary: Proves that perfect prompt-injection prevention is mathematically impossible in shared-embedding architectures lacking enforced control-data separation, formalizing prompted systems and Semantic-Faithful Control with three impossibility results. A theoretical foundation for prompt-injection security.

entry.title: A Path-Space Formulation of Prediction in World Models: From a Single Action to Prediction, Planning, and Irreversibility

author.name: Gunn Kim

entry.summary: Proposes viewing world models as defining a probability measure over future trajectories using an Onsager-Machlup path-space formulation. Prediction, planning, and uncertainty emerge as operations on a single action functional, with entropy production decomposed into reversible and irreversible parts.

entry.title: DiLaServe: High SLO Attainment Serving for Diffusion Language Models

author.name: Tzu-Tao Chang, Benjamin Yuanyang Hong, Kiet Pham, Shivaram Venkataraman

entry.summary: DiLaServe is a serving system for diffusion language models that addresses speed-quality tradeoffs from confidence-based denoising, dynamic parallelization under load, and approximate KV caching with non-uniform per-step costs. It targets high SLO attainment.

entry.title: Bayesian Best-Arm Identification with Abstention: A Polynomial-to-Exponential Phase Transition

author.name: Yuqi Huang, Yunlong Hou, Vincent Y. F. Tan

entry.summary: Studies Bayesian fixed-budget best-arm identification with an abstention option, proving abstention induces a phase transition from polynomial to exponential decay of undetected error probability. Establishes matching information-theoretic bounds for Gaussian priors.

entry.title: Beyond Trajectory Matching: Reflow with Marginal Distribution Alignment

author.name: Chen Wang, Peiran Yun, Pan Xie, Ke Deng

entry.summary: Identifies a theoretical limitation in reflow-based diffusion distillation: trajectory matching can under-determine the student's induced distribution, so two students with equal trajectory loss can have different endpoint marginals. Proposes adding marginal distribution alignment.

entry.title: Randomized neural operator for parametric PDEs with fast training and conformal uncertainty quantification

author.name: Zirui Deng, Jingbo Sun, Deyu Meng, Fei Wang

entry.summary: PCA-RaNN is a randomized latent neural operator for parametric PDEs combining PCA dimensionality reduction, fixed random features, and a closed-form least-squares readout, reducing training time by one to three orders of magnitude. It adds conformal uncertainty quantification.

entry.title: Interpretable Inverse Design of Metal-Organic Frameworks with Large Language Model Agents

author.name: Kyungmin Nam, Seunghee Han, Jihan Kim

entry.summary: LLM4MOF is a closed-loop framework where language-model agents reason about chemistry, propose interpretable design hypotheses, build candidate metal-organic frameworks, and test them in simulation over ten autonomous iterations. It targets interpretable inverse design.

entry.title: IG-Lens: Exact Additive Probability Attribution Across Transformer Layers via Telescoping Integrated Gradients

author.name: Duc Anh Nguyen

entry.summary: Proposes IG-Lens, using telescoping integrated gradients to produce an exact additive decomposition of where a predicted token's probability is produced across transformer layers, in probability space rather than logit space. It overcomes the non-additivity and bias of logit-lens and direct-logit-attribution methods.

entry.title: PS-PPO: Prefix-Sampling PPO for Critic-Free RLHF

author.name: Doo Hwan Hwang, Kee-Eung Kim

entry.summary: Proposes Prefix-Sampling PPO, a critic-free RLHF method that exploits temporal redundancy by learning from intermediate prefixes rather than full trajectories, reducing optimization cost for long reasoning traces. Intermediate prefixes often already determine the final outcome.

entry.title: Predictive Objectives Discard Exogenous Control-Relevant Features: A Controlled Mechanistic Study

author.name: Ayan Pendharkar

entry.summary: Shows in a controlled mechanistic study that JEPA-style predictive objectives discard exogenous yet control-relevant features because they optimize temporal predictability rather than control-relevance, even when those features are trivially encodable. It uses a 2x2 design varying controllability and relevance and compares six objectives.

entry.title: On the Vulnerability of Parameter-Level Defenses to Model Merging

author.name: Kuangpu Guo, Qingyan Zheng, Jian Liang, Yongcan Yu, Zilei Wang, Ran He, Tieniu Tan

entry.summary: Analyzes parameter-level defenses against unauthorized model merging, revealing that protected task vectors are inherently small so protected weights remain dominated by the pretrained model, then proposes the Anchor-Guided Attack using the pretrained model as a reference to circumvent these safeguards. It exposes a vulnerability in existing merging defenses.

entry.title: Predict, Reuse, and Repair: Accelerating Dynamic Sparse Attention for Long-Context LLM Decoding

author.name: Tianyu Wang, Gourav Rattihalli, Aditya Dhakal, Junbo Li, Zhiwei Ren, Dejan Milojicic, Longfei Shangguan

entry.summary: PRR is a runtime that speeds up dynamic sparse attention for long-context LLM decoding by predicting likely KV blocks, speculating attention while block selection runs, and repairing missed blocks with a FlashAttention-based kernel. It targets the serialized selection-to-attention dependency that bottlenecks long-context inference.

entry.title: Arko-T: A Foundation Model for Text-to-Structured 3D Generation

author.name: Liang Wang, Zhaoyang Xi, Zekai Xiang, Heng Meng, Qishan Zhang, Pingyi Zhou, Jin Liu, Litao Chen

entry.summary: Arko-T is a 4B-parameter model that maps natural language directly into executable, editable parametric CAD programs, aligning data curation and supervision to a formal notion of design state. It outperforms seven frontier LLMs on most of 12 metrics at lower cost.

entry.title: The Fundamental Limits of Valid Transport Map Estimation

author.name: Sivaraman Balakrishnan

entry.summary: This short note formalizes estimating any valid transport map in a minimax framework, yielding sample complexity lower bounds for methods like flow matching and diffusion whose learned object is evaluated as a transport map. It clarifies fundamental statistical limits independent of optimal transport cost.

entry.title: One-Step Gradient Delay is Not a Barrier for Large-Scale Asynchronous Pipeline Parallel LLM Pretraining

author.name: Philip Zmushko, Egor Petrov, Nursultan Abdullaev, Mikhail Khrushchev, Samuel Horv\'ath

entry.summary: This work challenges the belief that gradient staleness destabilizes asynchronous pipeline-parallel LLM pretraining, showing one-step delay degradation depends strongly on optimizer choice. It demonstrates PipeDream-2BW-style schedules can work well, eliminating pipeline bubbles for higher throughput.

entry.title: Spectral phase transitions and trainability in neural network learning dynamics

author.name: Chanju Park, Dario Bocchi, Francesco D'Amico, Biagio Lucini, Gert Aarts

entry.summary: This paper frames neural network training as stochastic evolution of a random matrix ensemble and shows SGD induces a Baik-Ben Arous-Peche spectral transition where signal eigenvalues detach from the random bulk. It provides a dynamical account of low-dimensional structure emergence in weight spectra.

entry.title: MACROCAST: A Vintage-Consistent Time Series Foundation Model for Real-Time Macroeconomic Forecasting

author.name: Andrea Carriero, Davide Pettenuzzo, Shubhranshu Shekhar

entry.summary: MACROCAST is a lightweight time series foundation model for real-time macroeconomic forecasting that explicitly avoids both temporal contamination and revision bias, training only on data available to a real-time forecaster. It is pretrained on synthetic series in about one GPU-day then fine-tuned.

entry.title: Weak Dominant Balance for Robust Identification of Dynamically Consistent Fluid Flow Structure

author.name: Samuel Ahnert, Esther Lagemann, H. Jane Bae, Kunihiko Taira, Ricardo Vinuesa, Christian Lagemann, Steven L. Brunton

entry.summary: Weak dominant balance is a derivative-free framework that identifies localized physical mechanisms from noisy spatiotemporal data by projecting governing equations into a weak integral form using smooth test functions. This avoids the noise amplification of numerical differentiation that limited prior methods to clean simulations. It matters for extracting interpretable physics from real experimental measurements.

entry.title: Optimizing Expert-Designed Crystal Graph Networks for Band-Gap Prediction with an Autonomous LLM Research Loop

author.name: Chenmu Zhang, Boris I. Yakobson

entry.summary: This work shows a general-purpose coding agent autonomously built the most accurate band-gap prediction model on the MatBench benchmark without external pretraining, surpassing all seventeen expert-designed models by implementing known crystal-network methods. It demonstrates autonomous agent research on a fixed scientific benchmark. It matters for AI-driven materials science.

entry.title: Highly Data Parallelizable Estimation of the Sliced-Wasserstein Distance Using Cumulative Distribution Functions

author.name: Christophe Vauthier, Quentin M\'erigot, Anna Korba

entry.summary: Introduces a new family of estimators for the Sliced-Wasserstein distance based on cumulative distribution functions rather than quantile sorting, enabling massive data parallelism. This matters for scaling optimal transport methods to very large datasets without full-dataset access.

entry.title: Developmental Trajectories of Situation Modeling and Mentalizing in Transformer Language Models

author.name: Pamela D. Rivi\`ere, Cameron Jones, Sean Trott

entry.summary: Traces the developmental emergence of theory-of-mind (false belief) reasoning across training stages of Olmo2 and Pythia model suites. It finds such mentalizing depends on scale and training volume, emerges late, and is most improved by post-training like SFT and DPO.

entry.title: Masked Diffusion Decoding as $x$-Prediction Flow

author.name: Weitian Wang, Lianlei Shan, Shubham Rai, Cecilia De La Parra, Akash Kumar

entry.summary: Reinterprets masked diffusion language model decoding as clean-state x-prediction inducing a continuous flow in embedding space, replacing the all-or-nothing token commitment with accumulating partial belief. It improves performance under limited decoding budgets.

entry.title: The Verbose Context Problem in Medical Records

author.name: Shiva Kaul, Min-Gyu Kim, Anjum Khurshid, Sriram Vishwanath

entry.summary: A comprehensive empirical study of nineteen similarity metrics across nineteen encoders and seven datasets, establishing that embedding anisotropy determines whether cosine or rank/L1 metrics perform best. When variance is even, cosine wins; when concentrated, rank-based metrics beat cosine substantially.

entry.title: Smooth Scaling Laws Hide Stepwise Token Learning

author.name: Pingjie Wang, Zechen Hu, Peiru Yang, Fu Guo, Debing Zhang

entry.summary: Decomposes smooth language-model scaling laws into localized per-token learning events, fitting token loss trajectories with sigmoids to reveal a learning-time spectrum. Argues aggregate power-law loss emerges from concentrated stepwise token learning.

entry.title: Scaling the Horizon, Not the Parameters: Reaching Trillion-Parameter Performance with a 35B Agent

author.name: Lei Bai, Zongsheng Cao, Yang Chen, Zhiyao Cui, Shangheng Du, Yue Fan, Shiyang Feng, Zijie Guo, Haonan He, Liang He, Xiaohan He, Shuyue Hu, Yusong Hu, Songtao Huang, Yichen Jiang, Hao Li, Xin Li, Dahua Lin, Weihao Lin, Fenghua Ling, Dongrui Liu, Zhuo Liu, Runmin Ma, Chunjiang Mu, Haoyang Peng, Tianshuo Peng, Jinxin Shi, Luohe Shi, Boyuan Sun, Zelin Tan, Shengji Tang, Qianyi Wang, Yiming Wu, Yi Xie, Xiangchao Yan, Jingqi Ye, Peng Ye, Fangchen Yu, Jiakang Yuan, Bihao Zhan, Bo Zhang, Chen Zhang, Shufei Zhang, Shuaiyu Zhang, Wenlong Zhang, Yiqun Zhang, Junpeng Zhao, Zhijie Zhong, Bowen Zhou, Yuhao Zhou

entry.summary: Introduces Agents-A1, a 35B Mixture-of-Experts agentic model that reportedly reaches trillion-parameter-level performance by scaling agent horizon rather than parameters, using a long-horizon knowledge-action infrastructure and three-stage training. Builds agentic trajectories averaging 45K tokens.

entry.title: On Test-Time Scaling for Vision-Language Models

author.name: Fawaz Sammani, Tzoulio Chamiti, Nikos Deligiannis

entry.summary: This paper presents the first comprehensive study of test-time scaling for large vision-language models, evaluating nine LLM-derived scaling methods across multiple models, sizes, and six benchmarks to assess whether they transfer to LVLMs. It analyzes whether, when, and to what extent these approaches help in the multimodal setting.

entry.title: Flow Matching in Feature Space for Stochastic World Modeling

author.name: Francois Porcher, Nicolas Carion, Karteek Alahari, Shizhe Chen

entry.summary: FlowWM is a stochastic world model that performs flow matching directly within pretrained DINOv3 feature space to forecast uncertain futures while preserving information useful for downstream perception, overcoming VAE-latent perception limits and deterministic mode collapse. It addresses the high dimensionality of pretrained features that makes standard diffusion recipes suboptimal.

entry.title: MuseBench: Benchmarking Intent-Level Audiovisual Arts Understanding in MLLMs

author.name: Yuxuan Fan, Gyusik Seo, Jing Hao, Jaemin Cho, Mohit Bansal, Jaehong Yoon

entry.summary: MuseBench benchmarks intent-level audiovisual arts understanding in multimodal LLMs, evaluating reasoning about why creative choices express artistic meaning across cinema, visual arts, and game design rather than just perceptual recognition. It targets an underexplored aspect of artistic understanding.

entry.title: From Accuracy to Visual Dependence: Auditing and Filtering Modality Collapse in Traffic VideoQA

author.name: Sena Korkut, Mar\'ia Alejandra Bravo Sarmiento, Sanghwan Kim, Zeynep Akata

entry.summary: Audits four traffic-accident VideoQA benchmarks and finds VLMs perform competitively without video input, indicating reliance on textual shortcuts (modality collapse). It introduces Blind Gap and Visual Gain diagnostics to quantify genuine visual dependence and filter benchmark questions.

entry.title: CouCE: A Unified Causal Framework for Debiased Deep Metric Learning

author.name: Xin Yuan, Zhenyang Niu, Meiqi Wan, Huilin Zhu, Xin Xu, Kui Jiang

entry.summary: ViDiHand leverages representations from a pretrained video diffusion model to reconstruct 4D two-hand pose from egocentric video, adapting it via a hand-overlay rendering objective. It argues video generative models implicitly learn occlusion reasoning and motion dynamics insufficiently captured by scarce hand-pose annotations.

entry.title: Orca: The World is in Your Mind

author.name: Yihao Wang, Yuheng Ji, Mingyu Cao, Yanqing Shen, Runze Xiao, Huaihai Lyu, Senwei Xie, Euan Liu, Klara Tian, Tianfeng Long, Yichi Zhang, Zhengliang Cai, Ruike Chen, Jifan Zhao, Ruochuan Shi, Zihan Tang, Jing Lyu, Wenxing Tan, Ningbo Zhang, Yangtao Hu, Yuming Gao, Xiansheng Chen, Junkai Zhao, Congsheng Xu, Boan Zhu, Ziqi Wang, Yupu Feng, Qiongqiong Zhang, Yingli Zhao, Yulong Ao, Shaoxuan Xie, You Liu, Guocai Yao, Leiduo Zhang, Xiaodan Liu, Yunyan Zhang, Yance Jiao, Xinyan Yang, Jiaxing Wei, Xu Liu, Tengfei Pan, Shaokai Nie, Chunlei Men, Sen Cui, Xiaojie Jin, Hongyang Li, Jianlan Luo, Yao Mu, Yunchao Wei, Jun Yan, Hang Zhao, Xiaolong Zheng, Jiaming Li, Yonghua Lin, Tiejun Huang, Zhongyuan Wang, Pengwei Wang

entry.summary: Orca is presented as an initial general world foundation model that learns a unified world latent space via Next-State-Prediction, combining unconscious learning from continuous video with conscious learning from language-described events and VQA. It aims to unify understanding, prediction, and action over multimodal world signals.

entry.title: VLK: Learning Humanoid Loco-Manipulation from Synthetic Interactions in Reconstructed Scenes

author.name: Yen-Jen Wang, Jiaman Li, Sirui Chen, Takara E. Truong, Pei Xu, Pieter Abbeel, Rocky Duan, Koushil Sreenath, Angjoo Kanazawa, Carmelo Sferrazza, Guanya Shi, Karen Liu

entry.summary: VLK generates vision-language-kinematics supervision synthetically by reconstructing metric-scale indoor scenes with 3D Gaussian Splatting, synthesizing navigation and object-interaction trajectories using privileged information, and rendering paired egocentric observations. It produces 48,000 paired trajectories without human teleoperation for humanoid loco-manipulation.

entry.title: ReGuide: From Test-Time Guidance to Self-Improving Diffusion Policies

author.name: Tzu-Hsiang Lin, Srinivas Shakkottai, Dileep Kalathil, P. R. Kumar

entry.summary: ReGuide is a self-improving framework for diffusion policies that treats test-time guided rollouts as reusable on-policy recovery data, using phase-conditioned guidance to generate corrective trajectories. It addresses covariate shift in behavior-cloned policies.

entry.title: Invariant Reasoning Directions in Latent Trajectories of Language Models

author.name: Arun Vignesh Malarkkan, Manan Roy Choudhury, Utkarsh Byahut, Yash Ravindra Charde, Vivek Gupta, Yanjie Fu

entry.summary: TILR identifies stable low-rank invariant directions in latent reasoning trajectories of language models by analyzing contrastive refinement signals between strong and weak trajectories. It offers a training-free intervention to manipulate reasoning directions.

entry.title: Towards Evaluating Data Priors for Tabular Foundation Models

author.name: Zeynep T\"urkmen, K\"ur\c{s}at Kaya, Alexander Pfefferle, Frank Hutter

entry.summary: Builds a unified interface to evaluate data-generating priors in tabular foundation models independently of architecture and training protocols. Trains a fixed architecture on tasks from different priors to compare their effects.

entry.title: Learning to Bid in Discriminatory Auctions with Budget Constraints

author.name: Negin Golrezaei, Sourav Sahoo

entry.summary: Studies repeated bidding in multi-unit discriminatory auctions under budget constraints, developing polynomial-time learning algorithms based on shortest paths in a DAG that achieve sublinear regret in both full-information and bandit settings. Exploits utility decomposition across units.

entry.title: Interventional Flow Matching: Prospective Dose-Response Forecasting with Velocity-Field Jacobian Regularization

author.name: Amirreza Dolatpour Fathkouhi, Justin Lee, Heman Shakeri

entry.summary: Interventional Flow Matching is a continuous-time generative framework for prospective dose-response forecasting in glucose management, conditioning a flow-matching velocity field on patient history and planned drivers with Jacobian regularization. It treats prediction as an interventional rather than observational problem.

entry.title: Agentic Safety is an Epistemic Property, Not a Behavioral One

author.name: Charles L. Wang, Keir Dorchen, Peter Jin

entry.summary: This position paper argues that agentic AI safety should be treated as an epistemic property of an evolving learner rather than a behavioral property of the current policy. It introduces teachability as the capacity to preserve future corrective leverage as systems learn and self-modify.

entry.title: Exploring the Cryptographic Limits of Transformer Networks

author.name: Stefan Domunco, Andis Draguns, Philip Torr, Isaac Robinson, Christian Schroeder de Witt

entry.summary: This paper maps specific cryptographic constructions (Keccak, Merkle-Damgard, Merkle Trees) to transformer architectures via threshold circuits, exploring whether transformers can implement cryptographic functions and thus gain source-free randomness for steganography. It connects circuit-complexity results to AI-collusion safety concerns. It matters for understanding steganographic risks in colluding AI agents.

entry.title: Latent Bridges for Multi-Table Question Answering

author.name: Simone Varriale, Tamara Cucumides, Floris Geerts, Paolo Papotti

entry.summary: GRAB is a constructor-encoder-bridge pipeline for multi-table QA that lifts relational data into a heterogeneous graph, encodes via message passing, and transfers signals to a frozen LLM through query-conditioned latent tokens. It trains only a lightweight 91M graph encoder while preserving LLM reasoning.

entry.title: How Anthropomorphic Language Impacts Public Perceptions of AI

author.name: Betty Li Hou, Sophie Hao, Sunoo Park, Tal Linzen

entry.summary: A controlled user study (N=815) measuring how anthropomorphic language in AI discourse shifts public perceptions of large language models versus recommendation systems. It quantifies how human-attributing framing affects understanding and expectations of AI.

entry.title: Anisotropy Decides Cosine vs. Rank Metrics for Text Embeddings

author.name: V. S. Raghu Parupudi

entry.summary: Measures content redundancy in a production-scale LLM-generated clinical corpus (2.51 billion tokens from 167,034 patient narratives), introducing provenance-based redundancy decomposition. Finds only 10.9% of output is trainable-unique while 79.4% is redundant, warning that token counts vastly overstate information content.

entry.title: DCGrasp: Distance-aware Controllable Grasp Generation

author.name: Hiroyasu Akada, Jes\'us P\'erez, Emre Aksan, Vasileios Choutas, Cristian Romero, Alberto Garcia-Garcia, Vladislav Golyanik, Christian Theobalt, Thabo Beeler

entry.summary: DCGrasp is a distance-aware controllable 3D grasp generation system built on a novel grasp energy term using signed distance profiles between hand vertices and object surfaces. It enables flexible control and generalization across diverse object geometries for robotics and XR.

entry.title: Illuminating Unified Multimodal Model for Free-form Interleaved Text-Image Generation

author.name: Chonghuinan Wang, Zhikai Chen, Chunwei Wang, Yecong Wan, Junwei Yang, Zhixin Wang, Wei Zhang, Jiaqi Xu, Renjing Pei, Xiaohe Wu, Fan Li, Wangmeng Zuo

entry.summary: ILLUME-X is a unified multimodal model enabling high-quality free-form interleaved text-image generation through an expanded data pipeline, progressive training, and stabilized multimodal training. It aims to let models autonomously generate interleaved text-image sequences.

entry.title: MUSE: Unlocking Timestep as Native Task Steering for One-Step Dense Prediction

author.name: Shuo Zhou, Zhaoxin Li, Xiujuan Chai

entry.summary: MUSE reveals that the native fixed sinusoidal timestep embedding in one-step diffusion models can be repurposed as an endogenous task-steering signal, enabling parameter-free multi-task dense prediction in a single model. It avoids parameter-heavy adapters, experts, or learnable task tokens.

entry.title: Constrained Tabular Diffusion for Finance

author.name: Michael Cardei, Jose M Munoz, Oscar Barrera, Shreyas K Chandrahas, Partha Saha

entry.summary: CTDF integrates a training-free feasibility operator into the reverse-diffusion sampling loop of tabular diffusion models to enforce hard regulatory and economic constraints. Experiments report zero constraint violations on financial datasets.

entry.title: How Token Influence Decays with Distance: A Green-Function View of Trained Language Models

author.name: Matthias Br\"andel, Stephan K\"ohler, Oliver Rheinbach

entry.summary: Studies how next-token prediction changes under small perturbations of earlier token embeddings in trained Transformers, using a Green-function analogy from differential equation solvers. Computes empirical distance-dependent influence decay.

entry.title: GLACIER: Rethinking Mass Spectrum Prediction as an Object Detection Problem

author.name: Rui-Xi Wang, Runzhong Wang, Connor W. Coley

entry.summary: GLACIER reframes MS/MS spectrum prediction as object detection on molecular graphs, treating fragmentation as detecting subgraphs and their spectral contributions. Its single-stage transformer improves accuracy and inference speed over two-stage models.

entry.title: BaRA: Bayesian Adaptive Rank Allocation for Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning

author.name: Zhibin Duan, Yuhong Wang, Jiahong Fu, Zongsheng Yue, Bo Chen, Zongben Xu

entry.summary: BaRA is a Bayesian adaptive rank allocation framework for parameter-efficient fine-tuning that models posterior distributions over adaptation parameters with context-dependent ranks. It addresses LoRA's fixed-rank rigidity and miscalibration in low-data regimes.

entry.title: Depth Exploration for LLM Decoding

author.name: Weisi Yang, Zipeng Sun, Stephen Xia

entry.summary: DEX is a lossless depth-adaptive decoding algorithm that replaces single-exit-depth selection with parallel exploration over multiple candidate depths, validated against the final-depth model. It exploits that many tokens become predictable at intermediate layers.

entry.title: Optimizer Memory Makes Shuffle Order a First-Order Source of Fine-Tuning Noise

author.name: John Sweeney

entry.summary: Shows that data shuffle order can be a first-order rather than second-order source of fine-tuning noise because fixed-clock optimizers like AdamW advance moment buffers by step index, making a single seed potentially flip close A/B comparisons. It provides a fit-free way to estimate this noise.

entry.title: How AI settled the complexity of the oldest SGD algorithm

author.name: Micha{\l} Derezi\'nski, Xiaoyu Dong

entry.summary: A narrative paper recounting how AI models contributed to discovering the worst-case complexity of the 1937 Kaczmarz algorithm, the earliest known instance of stochastic gradient descent. It blends mathematical complexity analysis with a story of AI-assisted theory discovery.

entry.title: Towards Generalizable and Evidential Nuclear Magnetic Resonance-Based Molecular Structure Elucidation via Large Language Model Agent

author.name: Zheng Fang, Chen Yang, Yusen Tan, Yunpeng Zhao, Fanjie Xu, Hongxin Xiang, Hanyu Sun, Hanyu Gao, Xiaojian Wang, Wenjie Du, Yuqiang Li, Jun Xia

entry.summary: Presents NMRAgent, an LLM-powered evidential reasoning agent for NMR-based molecular structure elucidation that integrates spectral analysis tools with chemical knowledge graphs to provide atom-level interpretability. It bridges the gap between black-box de novo models and database retrieval.

entry.title: Accelerating Q-learning through Efficient Value-Sharing across Actions

author.name: Prabhat Nagarajan, Brett Daley, Martha White, Marlos C. Machado

entry.summary: Introduces a mean-expansion layer that accelerates Q-learning by sharing value structure across actions within a state and reformulating the problem to avoid slow movement from near-zero initialization. It addresses inefficiencies in independent state-action value updates.

entry.title: Theory of Continual Learning Against Data Poisoning Attacks

author.name: Yiting Hu, Lingjie Duan

entry.summary: Develops a theoretical framework analyzing data poisoning attacks and defenses in regularization-based continual learning, modeling the adversary-defender interaction as an online zero-sum game. It establishes a fundamental limit that no defense succeeds beyond a linear poisoning proportion.

entry.title: DuoMem: Towards Capable On-Device Memory Agents via Dual-Space Distillation

author.name: Peyman Hosseini, Ondrej Bohdal, Ahmed Alajrami, Andrea Maracani, Ignacio Castro, Matthew Purver, Mete Ozay, Savas Ozkan, Taha Ceritli

entry.summary: Introduces DuoMem, a dual-space distillation framework transferring procedural problem-solving from large teacher models to compact on-device students via context-space distillation (using teacher-generated memories) and parameter-space distillation. It enables memory-augmented agents on resource-constrained devices.

entry.title: Beyond Drug Discovery: The Nanotechnology Molecular Optimization (NMO) Benchmark

author.name: Matthias Blaschke, Daniel Kienzle, Zsuzsanna Koczor-Benda, Julian Lorenz, Rainer Lienhart, Fabian Pauly

entry.summary: Introduces the Nanotechnology Molecular Optimization benchmark for generative molecular design, replacing proxy drug-likeness oracles with quantum simulations to target quantum materials science beyond drug discovery. It serves as both a rigorous ML testbed and a nanotechnology discovery engine.

entry.title: B3O: Scalable Boltzmann Batch Bayesian Optimization

author.name: Maximilian Bloor, Liyuan Xu, Hrvoje Stojic, Victor Picheny

entry.summary: Proposes B3O, a scalable large-batch Bayesian optimization framework that reframes batch generation as sampling directly from the Boltzmann distribution defined by the acquisition function, avoiding bottlenecks and diversity erosion of existing methods. It proves only negligible additional regret from this sampling.

entry.title: When Is a Draft Accepted? A Theory of Acceptance in Speculative Decoding

author.name: Aaryam Sharma

entry.summary: Develops theory for speculative decoding acceptance in practical regimes (greedy decoding, relaxed acceptance, tree-based candidates) rather than the exact distribution-preserving setting, characterizing acceptance via lower level sets of the target distribution and exact KL relationships. It explains when drafts are accepted in deployed systems.

entry.title: FlexTab: A Flexible Encoder-Decoder Architecture for In-Context Learning Across Diverse Tabular Tasks

author.name: Marek Polewczyk, Maximilian Schambach, Marco Spinaci, Sam Thelin, Johannes H\"ohne

entry.summary: Introduces FlexTab, a flexible encoder-decoder architecture for tabular in-context learning that pairs a single task-agnostic encoder producing target-agnostic row embeddings with task-specific decoders, demonstrated across classification, regression, anomaly detection, clustering, entity matching, and relational entity classification. It decouples feature representation from prediction target.

entry.title: DRIFT: Difficulty Routing Self-DIstillation with Rhythm-Gated Exploration and Success BuFfer Training

author.name: Haisen Luo, Yiwei Liu, Haoning Wang, Dan Liu, Junxi Yin, Haotian Wang, Lei Zhang, Xiaoyu Tian, Shuaiting Chen, Yuansheng Song, Baoyan Guo, Xiongfei Yan, Bolan Yang, Chengwei Liu, Ming Cui, Jiong Chen

entry.summary: Proposes DRIFT, an online self-evolution policy optimization framework for LLM self-improvement without external expert supervision, using Difficulty Routing and Rhythm Gating to track problem-level learning progress and adapt optimization, plus a success buffer. It avoids over-optimizing easy problems and better explores borderline cases.

entry.title: Beyond IID: How General Are Tabular Foundation Models, Really?

author.name: Lennart Purucker, Andrej Tschalzev, Nick Erickson, Gioia Blayer, David Holzm\"uller, Alan Arazi, Alexander Pfefferle, Mustafa Tajjar, Ga\"el Varoquaux, Frank Hutter

entry.summary: This work questions how well tabular foundation models generalize beyond IID benchmarks, arguing that fragmented evaluation protocols cause the field to focus on easy datasets and marginal gains. It calls for harder, unified benchmarking of tabular foundation models.

entry.title: MuonSSM: Orthogonalizing State Space Models for Sequence Modeling

author.name: Thai-Khanh Nguyen, Ngoc-Bich-Uyen Vo, Thieu N. Vo, Tan M. Nguyen, Cuong Pham

entry.summary: MuonSSM stabilizes state space model training by conditioning the geometry of memory updates using a momentum pathway and a Newton-Schulz transformation on low-rank input injections, yielding bounded spectrally conditioned updates. It preserves parallel scan complexity while improving gradient propagation.

entry.title: Convergence of Continual Learning in Homogeneous Deep Networks

author.name: Matan Schliserman, Gon Buzaglo, Itay Evron, Daniel Soudry

entry.summary: This paper characterizes weakly regularized continual classification in homogeneous deep networks as sequential projections onto task margin sets, generalizing prior linear/single-task analyses. It shows global convergence generally fails but establishes local linear convergence under regularity conditions.

entry.title: Turn-Averaged SAEs for Feature Discovery and Long-Context Attribution

author.name: Kevin Der, Harish Kamath, Ben Thompson

entry.summary: Turn-averaged SAEs represent an entire Human or Assistant conversation turn with a fixed number of features by reconstructing the average activation, avoiding the linear scaling of active features with context length. They better capture high-level turn characteristics and simplify long-context attribution.

entry.title: Neuromorphic Energy-Aware Learning for Adaptive Deep Brain Stimulation

author.name: Binh Nguyen, Colleen Josephson, Mircea Teodorescu, Gert Cauwenberghs, Jason Eshraghian

entry.summary: This work introduces energy-aware reinforcement learning that incorporates actuator energy directly into the reward, demonstrated in closed-loop deep brain stimulation using a deep spiking Q-network trained in a biophysical brain circuit model. It learns to suppress pathological oscillations while minimizing total system energy.

entry.title: A Theoretical Interpretation of In-Context Learning via Probabilistic Modeling

author.name: Zhenyu Liu, Huaze Tang, Shao-Lun Huang

entry.summary: This paper presents a probabilistic model for in-context learning and derives ICL performance for general parametric distributions and exponential families. It explains how the number of demonstrations, model sensitivity to parameter variation, and demonstration-query similarity affect performance.

entry.title: FlipGuard: Defending Large Language Models Against Quantization-Conditioned Backdoor Attacks

author.name: Aoying Zheng, Anqi Du, Zizhuang Deng, Yuxuan Chen

entry.summary: FlipGuard is a proactive defense against quantization-conditioned backdoor attacks, where malicious behavior stays dormant in full-precision models and activates only after quantization. It selectively perturbs weights before quantization to break alignment between weight patterns and quantization boundaries without needing training data or trigger samples.

entry.title: Evidence-Informed LLM Beliefs for Continual Scientific Discovery

author.name: Dhruv Agarwal, Reece Adamson, Andrew McCallum, Peter Clark, Ashish Sabharwal, Bodhisattwa Prasad Majumder

entry.summary: This work addresses the static treatment of Bayesian surprise in autonomous scientific discovery loops by introducing evidence-informed LLM beliefs whose priors update with accumulated evidence. This makes surprisal non-stationary, mirroring human reasoning for continual discovery. It matters for improving LLM-driven hypothesis search and verification.

entry.title: Local-Minima-Preserving Continuous Relaxation of Ising Problems

author.name: Debraj Banerjee, Santanu Mahapatra, Kunal N. Chaudhury

entry.summary: Proposes a polynomial continuous relaxation of Ising problems that provably preserves a one-to-one correspondence between local minima, enabling gradient-based optimizers like ADAM for combinatorial problems. Matters for solving MAX-CUT and related NP-hard problems via continuous optimization.

entry.title: RenderFormer++: Scalable and Physically Grounded Feed-Forward Neural Rendering

author.name: Huangsheng Du, Haoran Zhu, Youcheng Cai, Jinyang Meng, Ligang Liu

entry.summary: RenderFormer++ is a feed-forward neural rendering framework adding physics-informed transport guidance and hierarchical object-centric tokenization to improve physical consistency and scalability of global illumination. It addresses quadratic attention bottlenecks in triangle-level rendering transformers.

entry.title: SEATauBench: Adapting Tool-Agent-User Evaluation Into Low-Resource Southeast Asian Languages

author.name: My Chiffon Nguyen, Aulia Adila, Saksorn Ruangtanusak, Kittiphat Leesombatwathana, Vissuta Gunawan Lim, Patomporn Payoungkhamdee, Samuel Cahyawijaya

entry.summary: SEATauBench adapts the TauBench tool-agent-user evaluation to five Southeast Asian languages with progressively localized settings. It finds English agent capabilities transfer reasonably for conversation language but degrade sharply as tool specs and task context localize.

entry.title: Majority Vote Silences Minority Values: Annotator Disagreement at the Hate/Offensive Boundary in HateXplain

author.name: Joshua Muhumuza, Joab Ezra Agaba, Mercy Amiyo

entry.summary: Shows that 42.6% of annotator disagreement in HateXplain concentrates at the hate/offensive boundary and that majority-vote aggregation systematically erases minority value perspectives. Demonstrates accuracy drops across hard-, soft-, and per-annotator-label models on disagreement posts.

entry.title: EntroRouter: Learning Efficient Model Routing via Entropy Regulation

author.name: Kaiyi Zhang, Xueliang Zhao, Zhuocheng Gong, Wei Wu, Yankai Lin

entry.summary: EntroRouter is a single-round LLM routing framework treating entropy regulation as a core objective to avoid a failure mode called Trust Region Collapse, where strong pre-training priors suppress capable experts under sparse supervision. It decouples reasoning from routing using soft supervision initialization.

entry.title: AURORA: Asymmetry and Update-Induced Rotation for Robust Hallucination Detection in Large Language Models

author.name: Zishuai Zhang, Hainan Zhang, Zhiming Zheng

entry.summary: AURORA is a hallucination detection framework that shifts focus from static hidden-state probes to weight-gradient dynamics, using asymmetry and update-induced rotation signals for robust cross-dataset detection. It addresses degradation of existing methods under cross-dataset evaluation.

entry.title: Coverage-Driven KV Cache Eviction for Efficient and Improved Inference of LLM

author.name: Shuvendu Roy, Mengyao Zhai, Hossein Hajimirsadeghi, Golnoosh Samei

entry.summary: Proposes a coverage-driven KV cache eviction strategy for efficient LLM inference that preserves long-context reasoning better than attention-sparsity-based eviction. It identifies that performance drops stem from poor token coverage and addresses memory overhead during inference.

entry.title: Diagnosing and Mitigating Context Rot in Long-horizon Search

author.name: Shijie Xia, Yikun Wang, Zhen Huang, Pengfei Liu

entry.summary: This paper diagnoses context rot in long-horizon deep search, showing that flagship open-source models prematurely give up or provide uncertain answers as context grows, and proposes mitigation strategies. It empirically characterizes a practically important failure mode in long-context agents.

entry.title: JASPR: Joint Spatial Representation learning of histology and spatial genomics for improved virtual genomic screening and clinical prognostication

author.name: Marija Pizurica, Eric Zimmermann, Neil Tenenholtz, James Hall, Olivier Gevaert, Ava P. Amini, Lorin Crawford, Kristen A. Severson

entry.summary: JASPR is a self-supervised framework jointly learning representations from H&E histology images and spatial transcriptomics via cross-modal reconstruction with explicit spatial context, for virtual genomic screening and prognosis. It addresses the lack of methods integrating spatial context across modalities.

entry.title: JuZhou 1.0 Technical Report: The First Edge-Native Text-to-Image Foundation Model Trained Entirely on China-Developed AI Accelerators

author.name: Ce Chen, Congrui Wang, Yonglin Li, Zhenchen Wan, Mingyang Geng, Junhao Xiao, Zhengpeng Xing, Yaqing Hu, Yao Wu, Zhaoyang Qu, Long Lan, Xinwang Liu, Yingqi Peng, Shijia Li, Zufeng Zhang, Chen Ma, Jingjing Zhou, Xingyu Wang, Qilin Lu, Bin Jiang, Qilin Sun, Shanzhi Gu, Yaoguang Jin, Tongliang Liu, Kede Ma, Yifan Peng

entry.summary: JuZhou 1.0 is an ultra-lightweight (~0.387B parameter) text-to-image foundation model designed for fully offline on-device execution, trained entirely on China-developed AI accelerators using rectified flow plus DMD2 distillation for 4-step inference and Chinese semantic alignment. It targets edge T2I deployment with privacy and low latency.

entry.title: Mural: Transferring LLM knowledge to image generation via Mixture-of-Transformers

author.name: Achin Jain, Jie An, Siddharth Chaudhary, Davide Modolo

entry.summary: Mural integrates a frozen reasoning-capable LLM with a diffusion-based image generator via shared attention in a Mixture-of-Transformers architecture, investigating how much of the LLM's knowledge remains accessible during text-to-image training on standard text-image pairs and what new capabilities emerge. It explores transferring LLM knowledge to image generation.

entry.title: Early Warning Signals for OpenVLA Failure under Visual Distribution Shift

author.name: Dipesh Tharu Mahato, Rachel Ren

entry.summary: This work tests whether OpenVLA internal activations contain linearly decodable signals predicting near-term task failure under visual distribution shift, training lightweight probes on logged activations. A layer-16 logistic probe achieves AUROC 0.972 for predicting failure within 15 steps under occlusion that drops success from 57 to 17 percent.

entry.title: See Only When Needed: Context-Aware Attention Intervention for Mitigating Hallucinations in LVLMs

author.name: Yuqing Lei, Wenbo Lyu, Yingjun Du, Xiantong Zhen, Cees G. M. Snoek, Ling Shao

entry.summary: Context-aware Attention Intervention (CAI) is a training-free, inference-time method to reduce object hallucinations in large vision-language models by selectively strengthening visual attention only where and when needed. It applies entropy- and depth-gated attention adjustments for uncertain tokens rather than uniformly boosting visual signals.

entry.title: Explainability-Aware Frustum Attack: Exposing Structural Vulnerabilities in LiDAR-Based 3D Object Detectors

author.name: Chengzeng You, Binbin Xu, Soteris Demetriou

entry.summary: This work uses explainability-guided adversarial analysis to expose structural vulnerabilities in LiDAR-based 3D object detectors, introducing a saliency method that aggregates integrated-gradient attributions to find efficient attack regions. It moves beyond physical realizability to understanding detector reliance patterns.

entry.title: One Forward Beats Two: InnerZoom for Accurate and Efficient GUI Grounding

author.name: Chen Liu, Ling Chen, Hanzhang Zhou, Liangyu Chen, Chenglin Cai, Xin Yu, Steven Hoi, Yue Wang
