entry.summary: InnerZoom improves GUI grounding by exploiting that target-region awareness emerges in intermediate decoder layers but is lost before coordinate prediction, achieving accuracy gains in a single forward pass instead of crop-and-rerun. It avoids the latency of external ZoomIn-style methods.

entry.title: SciIR: A Large-scale Training Dataset and Benchmark for Scientific Image Reasoning Generation

author.name: Zhiyuan Ma, Zhengfeng Shi, Yuning An, Peize Li, Jiabao Wei, Ruijie Li, Junhao Xiao, Jianjun Li, Bowen Zhou

entry.summary: SciIR is a large-scale dataset and benchmark for scientific image reasoning generation, formalizing scientific reasoning into entity structure, scientific process, and scientific law dimensions inspired by Peirce's semiotic triad. It provides over 80,000 scientific image-text pairs to train and evaluate logical, semantically-aligned scientific image generation.

entry.title: VisReflect: Latent Visual Reflection for Fine-Grained Perception in Long Visual Context

author.name: Xiaoqian Shen, Mohamed Elhoseiny

entry.summary: VisReflect introduces latent visual reflection for fine-grained perception in long visual contexts, mitigating the visual attention sink where irrelevant tokens absorb attention as token count grows. It avoids unreliable explicit bounding-box prediction and extra forward passes of prior methods.

entry.title: Behavior Uncloning: Distilling Mode Redirection into Policy Weights without Inference-Time Steering

author.name: Hao Wang, Jiuzhou Lei, Dayou Li, Bangya Liu, Minghui Zheng, Manling Li, Ruohan Zhang, Zhiwen Fan

entry.summary: MoRE addresses unsafe behavior modes learned by behavior-cloned policies by distilling mode-redirection signals into policy weights through a short uncloning step, avoiding inference-time overhead or full retraining. It uses a retain loss to preserve desired behaviors while steering away from unsafe ones.

entry.title: AnyBody: Free-Form Whole-Body Humanoid Control from Arbitrary Keypoint Guidance

author.name: Shuning Li, Sikai Li, Jiachen Li, Mingyu Ding

entry.summary: AnyBody is a unified whole-body humanoid controller driven by arbitrary subsets of body keypoints chosen at deploy time, using a single latent motion representation distilled from a privileged teacher. It avoids reliance on full-body motion capture and separate upper/lower body decomposition.

entry.title: Trust Your Instincts: Confidence-Driven Test-Time RL for Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Siyao Chen, Jiakang Yuan, Jiaxin Wang, Tao Chen

entry.summary: T2VLA is an architecture-agnostic test-time reinforcement learning framework that leverages the internal generation confidence of vision-language-action models as an evaluative signal, since higher-confidence trajectories correlate with success. It enables self-bootstrapping policy improvement without external rewards.

entry.title: Heterogeneous Tactile Transformer

author.name: Jianxin Bi, Qiang Wang, Jayaram Reddy, Kelvin Lin, Soibkhon Khajikhanov, Ruihan Gao, Harold Soh

entry.summary: The Heterogeneous Tactile Transformer learns shared representations across different tactile sensors using sensor-specific encoders, a shared trunk, masked reconstruction, and cross-modal alignment, pretrained on a new 1.6M-frame paired tactile dataset. It enables learning contact-rich manipulation from diverse tactile data at scale.

entry.title: Behavior Prompting Policy: Demonstrations as Prompts for Manipulation

author.name: Austin Patel, Ben Pekarek, Joel Enrique Castro Hernandez, Shuran Song

entry.summary: Behavior Prompting Policy enables robots to perform new tasks at inference time from a single human demonstration (a behavior prompt) via an in-context visuomotor architecture, supported by a handheld data-collection interface and new evaluation benchmarks. It identifies task diversity as the primary driver of the prompting capability.

entry.title: A Sieve-Accelerated Quadrature Method for Exact Privacy Accounting in the 2020 U.S. Decennial Census

author.name: Buxin Su, Weijie Su, Chendi Wang

entry.summary: Introduces a sieve-accelerated quadrature method for exactly computing the differential privacy profile of large-scale 2020 U.S. Census data releases that inject integer-valued Gaussian noise. Exact accounting lets the Census Bureau use the minimum noise for a given privacy budget, enhancing data utility for funding and redistricting.

entry.title: DiScoFormer: One transformer for density and score, across distributions

author.name: Unknown

entry.summary: Allen AI introduces DiScoFormer, a transformer-based estimator that infers both density and score from a finite sample in a single forward pass, generalizing kernel density estimation. It is designed to stay accurate in high-dimensional and out-of-distribution settings without retraining per distribution. This is original machine learning architecture research.

entry.title: Priced Motion Through Optimal Faces: A Normal-Fan Geometry for Non-Stationary Adversarial MDPs

author.name: Kai Hidajat

entry.summary: Develops a normal-fan geometry for finite-horizon adversarial MDPs with fixed transitions, arguing that the cost of non-stationarity depends on whether loss movement changes the optimal policy, not raw movement size. Occupancy measures form a polytope where each loss exposes an optimal face.

entry.title: PCGD: Physics-Guided Conditional Graph Diffusion for TCAD Device Simulation

author.name: Yihan Zhang, Zhiteng Zhang, Kun Chen, Chen Wang

entry.summary: PCGD is a physics-guided conditional graph diffusion framework for TCAD semiconductor device simulation operating on unstructured meshes, predicting coupled electrostatic and carrier density fields. It uses a condition-aware MeshGraphNet denoiser with cross-attention for boundary conditions.

entry.title: NeuReasoner: Theory-grounded Mapping of Reasoning Elicitation Boundaries

author.name: Aydin Javadov, Shyngys Aitkazinov, Tobias Hoesli, Florian von Wangenheim, Bjoern Schuller, Joseph Ollier

entry.summary: Introduces NeuReasoner, a theory-grounded elicitation instrument pairing a Neuro Lens (functional specificity) with a Cognitive Lens (Erotetic Theory of Reasoning) to map which cognitive tasks can be recovered from base LLMs through elicitation and where recovery fails. It tests the claim that reasoning is largely latent in base models beyond math and coding.

entry.title: Improved Multi-Dimensional Forecasting for Swap Regret

author.name: Joey Rivkin, Ramiro N. Deo-Campo Vuong, Robert Kleinberg, Chido Onyeze, Erald Sinanaj, Eva Tardos

entry.summary: This paper improves swap-regret guarantees for forecasting to multiple downstream best-responding agents, giving a polynomial-time algorithm achieving order root-kT regret in two-dimensional outcome spaces, beating prior bounds and avoiding exponential runtime. It matters for online learning and game-theoretic forecasting theory.

entry.title: Field Order Should Not Matter: Permutation-Invariant Embedding Model Fine-Tuning for Structured Metadata Retrieval

author.name: Aivin V. Solatorio, Olivier Dupriez, Rafael Macalaba

entry.summary: Shows that field ordering during serialization silently controls retrieval quality in fine-tuned embedding models for structured metadata, and proposes permutation-invariant fine-tuning with random field dropout. It binds meaning to field labels rather than position.

entry.title: H-GRPO: Permutation-Invariant Reinforcement Learning for Grounded Visual Reasoning

author.name: Eric Peh, Debaditya Roy, Basura Fernando

entry.summary: H-GRPO enhances grounded visual reasoning in VLMs by decomposing global queries into atomic sub-questions, each requiring an explicit sub-answer and localized evidence bounding box, with permutation-invariant reinforcement learning. It aims to improve both performance and interpretability while reducing shortcut reliance.

entry.title: A Classifier-Agnostic Zero-Shot Adversarial Attack Detection via CLIP

author.name: Hodaya Krakover, Meir Yossef Levi, Eyal Gofer, Guy Gilboa

entry.summary: A4D is a completely black-box, zero-shot adversarial attack detector using prompt-based CLIP similarity scores, claimed to be the first to use CLIP for this task. It exploits CLIP's sensitivity to small imperceptible non-semantic perturbations to detect attacks without knowing the classifier or attack type.

entry.title: OmniCoT: A Benchmark for Global and Multi-Step Panoramic Reasoning

author.name: Haocong He, Chenfei Liao, Zichen Wen, Zihao Dongfang, Xu Zheng, Bin Ren, Chang Su, Zixin Zhang, Harold Haodong Chen, Hongfei Zhang, Weijia Li, Kailun Yang, Conghui He, Xuming Hu, Nicu Sebe, Linfeng Zhang

entry.summary: OmniCoT is a panoramic spatial reasoning benchmark designed for global, multi-step reasoning over the full 360x180 field of view, addressing existing benchmarks' focus on local cues and few-step queries. It aims to fully exploit panoramas' advantage for embodied intelligence applications.

entry.title: Tandem Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards

author.name: Difan Jiao, Raghav Singhal, Robert West, Ashton Anderson

entry.summary: Extends tandem training (a strong senior model co-generating with a frozen weaker junior to remain compatible) to reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards, addressing RLVR's tendency to drift reasoning toward unreadable patterns. Aims at human/weaker-agent usability.

entry.title: The Contagion Tensor: A Framework for Measuring Output-Distribution Coupling in Multi-Agent LLM Systems -- and Auditing the Claims It Enables

author.name: Zewen Liu

entry.summary: Introduces the Contagion Tensor and Coupling Amplification Factor to measure how LLM output distributions couple across modalities, agents, and time in multi-agent systems. Notably, it audits its own claims, showing an apparent super-linear effect collapses under ablation.

entry.title: A Novel Latent-Class Attack and its Detection by Class Subspace Orthogonalization

author.name: Guangmingmei Yang, David J. Miller, George Kesidis

entry.summary: Proposes a latent-class data poisoning attack where poisoned examples from an unknown novel class are mislabeled to a known target, making the model treat the novel class as a sub-class. Also introduces a class-subspace-orthogonalization defense to detect it.

entry.title: Dead-Direction Conditioners: Gauge-Equivariant Preconditioning for Deep Networks

author.name: Tejas Pradeep Shirodkar

entry.summary: DDC is a gauge-equivariant preconditioner that lifts base optimizers into G-equivariant ones, conditioning optimizer state in the orbit decomposition of an invariant metric to keep trajectories on the symmetry quotient. It handles four architectural symmetries.

entry.title: Adaptive Block Diffusion: Resolving Training-Inference Mismatch in Diffusion Language Models

author.name: Gagan Jain

entry.summary: Adaptive Block Diffusion resolves the training-inference mismatch in diffusion language models by optimizing denoising risk over a distribution of prefix-window configurations, treating configuration as a stochastic variable. It needs no architectural changes.

entry.title: Reliability, Faithfulness, and the Limits of Post-hoc Explanations of Opaque Scientific Models

author.name: Nick Oh, Helen Jin

entry.summary: A philosophical-methodological argument that reliability plus faithfulness of post-hoc explanations is insufficient to support claims about how a scientific phenomenon is structured. It distinguishes matching outcomes and matching the model from matching the mechanism.

entry.title: Self-Supervised Calibration of Scientific Instruments Using Physical Consistency Constraints

author.name: M. Rejmund (GANIL, CEA/DRF - CNRS/IN2P3, Bd Henri Becquerel, BP 55027, F-14076, Caen Cedex 5, France), A. Lemasson (GANIL, CEA/DRF - CNRS/IN2P3, Bd Henri Becquerel, BP 55027, F-14076, Caen Cedex 5, France)

entry.summary: Introduces a physics-informed self-supervised framework that jointly learns latent detector calibration parameters and predictions from raw measurements using physical consistency constraints, without pre-calibrated signals or labels. Demonstrated for ionic charge-state determination in the VAMOS++ spectrometer.

entry.title: Anti-Collapse Dynamics and the Emergence of Multi-Time-Scale Learning in Recurrent Neural Networks

author.name: Lorenzo Livi

entry.summary: This paper studies why recurrent networks struggle with long-range dependencies, showing that the decay rate of past-input influence is not fixed by architecture but emerges from coupling between state and parameter dynamics, settling into collapsed (exponential forgetting) or anti-collapsed (power-law) regimes. It offers theory for when multi-time-scale learning emerges in RNNs.

entry.title: A Diagnostic Framework and Multi-Evaluator Audit of Evaluator-Driven Preference Dynamics in Self-Adapting LLM Agents

author.name: Liu Zewen

entry.summary: Provides a diagnostic framework (EPC with a Multimodal Preference Collapse Index and coupling matrices) to detect when proprietary LLM evaluators drift and invalidate measurements within weeks, documenting a GPT-4o May-to-June shift. It audits evaluator-driven preference dynamics in self-adapting LLM agents.

entry.title: Exploiting Local Flatness for Efficient Out-of-Distribution Detection

author.name: Seonghwan Park, Hyunji Jung, Dongyeop Lee, Namhoon Lee

entry.summary: Provides a systematic investigation of loss-landscape curvature for out-of-distribution detection, showing OOD inputs exhibit larger Hessian curvature than in-distribution data with the gap widening under stronger inputs, and exploits local flatness for efficient post-hoc OOD detection. It reduces the computational cost of curvature-based methods.

entry.title: Online Data Selection for Instruction Tuning via Gaussian Processes

author.name: Jun Wang, Quoc Phong Nguyen, Julien Monteil, Vu Nguyen

entry.summary: Proposes GAIA, an online data selection framework for instruction tuning that uses Gaussian Process regression to model continuous utility manifolds across the semantic space, overcoming batch-constrained methods limited to local utility. An adaptive strategy fusion mechanism dynamically prioritizes high-utility samples.

entry.title: DreamForge-World 0.1 Preview: A Low-Compute Real-Time Controllable World Model

author.name: Daniyel Ayupov, Artur Markov-Tsoy

entry.summary: Presents DreamForge-World 0.1 Preview, a low-compute real-time controllable world model adapting the LongLive autoregressive video stack with a residual action pathway, supporting keyboard/mouse control, mid-stream reprompting, and minute-scale 480p rollouts at up to 15 FPS on a single RTX 4090. It targets consumer-GPU interactive world simulation.

entry.title: FlowAWR: Online Adaptive Flow Reinforcement via Advantage-Weighted Rectification

author.name: Zheming Fu, Ruizhe He, Wei Shang, Xiaoxiao Ma, Lei Wang, Chang Liu, Siming Fu

entry.summary: Proposes FlowAWR, an online adaptive flow reinforcement method that recasts continuous generative policy optimization as advantage-weighted supervised regression toward velocity fields, avoiding training-inference inconsistencies of SDE-sampler-based density approximations and improving on heuristic fixed-magnitude corrections. It aligns optimization strength with relative quality.

entry.title: HSAP: A Hierachical Sequence-aware Parallelism for Hybrid-Context Generative Models

author.name: Songxin Zhang, Zejian Xie, Zhuoyang Song, Cong lin, Junyu Lu, Jiaxing Zhang, Bingyi Jing

entry.summary: HSAP is a hierarchical sequence-aware parallelism framework that correctly computes causal attention on hybrid-context packed sequences while preserving high parallelism degree. It addresses cross-contamination problems in existing sequence parallelism approaches for training large models.

entry.title: ReFreeKV: Towards Threshold-Free KV Cache Compression

author.name: Xuanfan Ni, Liyan Xu, Chenyang Lyu, Longyue Wang, Mo Yu, Lemao Liu, Fandong Meng, Jie Zhou, Piji Li

entry.summary: ReFreeKV proposes threshold-free KV cache compression that avoids the input/domain-specific budget thresholds required by prior pruning methods, which fail on diverse open-domain inputs. It aims for robust memory reduction without per-input tuning.

entry.title: Vision-driven Preference Synthesis for Mitigating Hallucinations in VLMs

author.name: Yunhun Nam, Jongheon Jeong

entry.summary: ViPSy constructs preference data for reducing VLM hallucinations that are both policy-aligned and visually grounded, addressing limitations of intervention-based deviation and sampling-based underuse of visual information. It improves visual faithfulness via better preference pair construction.

entry.title: J-LAW: Joint Localization and Actionable World Modeling via Coupled Latent Factor Graphs

author.name: Guanqun Cao, Liang Chen

entry.summary: J-LAW proposes a coupled factor graph that jointly optimizes metric object poses, latent world states, and latent landmark embeddings, bridging classical SLAM and action-conditioned world models. A learned pose-latent coupling lets better localization improve the world model and vice versa.

entry.title: Cybersecurity is the True Frontier for Generative AI Success or Failure

author.name: Edward Raff, Maor Ashkenazi, Sagar Samtani, David J. Elkind, Sven Krasser

entry.summary: This position paper argues that cybersecurity is the true proving ground for generative AI and LLM agents, given enormous data scale, costly and ambiguous expert labeling, and adversarial actors actively subverting detection. It frames cybersecurity workflows as a stress test of many ML challenges at once.

entry.title: The strength of clinical evidence is recoverable from language model representations but not from their stated grades

author.name: Soroosh Tayebi Arasteh

entry.summary: Across 45k clinical claims and 22 open-weight LLMs, this study finds that evidence strength is linearly decodable from model activations even though the models fail to state it accurately when asked. It distinguishes this signal from truth and controls for lexical confounds. It matters for clinical evidence summarization safety and interpretability.

entry.title: Hierarchical Experimentalist Agents

author.name: Abhranil Chandra, Sankaran Vaidyanathan, Utsav Dhanuka, Varun Gandhi, Scott Niekum

entry.summary: HExA is an in-context self-improvement framework where LLM agents learn from active experimentation, iteratively designing query-relevant experiments and building a reusable library of composable skills. It targets novel domains where parametric knowledge and retrieval fail. It matters for agents that must learn from interaction rather than priors.

entry.title: Your Data Manifold is Secretly a Reward Model: Shell-LCC for Text-to-Video Generation

author.name: Shihao Zhang, Yuguang Yan, Junzhe Zhang, Wei Zhao, Bohan Wang, Hanwang Zhang

entry.summary: Shell-LCC argues the data manifold itself can serve as a reward model for text-to-video generation, deriving dense, differentiable, nearly cost-free reward signals by encouraging video latents to lie on the high-quality SFT data manifold. This avoids costly reward models, human annotations, and DPO overhead. It matters for efficient alignment of T2V diffusion models.

entry.title: Non-parametric recovery of causal diffusion mechanisms from steady-state observations

author.name: Richard Schwank, Mathias Drton

entry.summary: Develops non-parametric methodology to recover causal diffusion drift mechanisms from cross-sectional steady-state observations, assuming known acyclic causal structure. Motivated by destructive-measurement settings like gene expression.

entry.title: Learning from Mistakes: Rollout-Retrieval Lifelong Policy Learning for Autonomous Driving

author.name: Cheng Gong, Haoyang Wang, Chao Lu, Zirui Li, Jianwei Gong

entry.summary: Proposes a rollout-retrieval lifelong learning framework for autonomous driving policies that accumulates corrective knowledge from a policy's own closed-loop mistakes while retaining prior competence. It targets continual improvement on long-tail traffic scenarios.

entry.title: Uncertainty-Aware Generation and Decision-Making Under Ambiguity

author.name: Nico Daheim, Iryna Gurevych

entry.summary: Develops uncertainty-aware decision-making algorithms based on Bayesian decision theory and risk-averse strategies for LLM tasks like tutoring and peer reviewing. It emphasizes trustworthy decision-making over just improving model quality.

entry.title: Phonological Perception of Sign Language Models

author.name: Kayo Yin, Jessica Carter, Alex Xijie Lu, Annemarie Kocab

entry.summary: Probes whether sign language recognition models perceive abstract phonological features (handshape, location, movement) using minimal pairs and alignment with human behavioral data. Finds emergent phonological sensitivity with clear architecture-dependent differences.

entry.title: Why Struggle with Continuous Latents? Interpretable Discrete Latent Reasoning via Rendered Compression

author.name: Shuochen Chang, Qingyang Liu, Shaobo Wang, Bingjie Gao, Qianli Ma, Haonan Zhao, Yibo Miao, Yulin Sun, Zelin Peng, Jiangtong Li, Li Niu

entry.summary: Introduces Discrete Latent Reasoning (DLR), which converts continuous latent reasoning states into explicit discrete tokens via a render-based compression scheme, aiming to make latent reasoning trainable and interpretable. Targets the cost of long chain-of-thought sequences.

entry.title: Timesteps of Mamba Align with Human Reading Times

author.name: Yuji Yamamoto, Shinnosuke Isono, Yoshinobu Kawahara, Sho Yokoi

entry.summary: Shows that Mamba's input-dependent discretization timestep at each layer significantly predicts human per-word reading times, even controlling for GPT-2 surprisal. Argues state-space models offer a new lens on real-time human language processing.

entry.title: GUICrafter: Weakly-Supervised GUI Agent Leveraging Massive Unannotated Screenshots

author.name: Sunqi Fan, Lingshan Chen, Runqi Yin, Qingle Liu, Yongming Rao, Meng-Hao Guo, Shi-Min Hu

entry.summary: GUICrafter is a weakly-supervised GUI agent that leverages massive unannotated screenshots to reduce reliance on costly human annotations, targeting better cross-device generalization and fine-grained visual grounding. It addresses a major data bottleneck in building GUI agents.

entry.title: Self-Evolving World Models for LLM Agent Planning

author.name: Xuan Zhang, Wenxuan Zhang, See-Kiong Ng, Yang Deng

entry.summary: WorldEvolver is a self-evolving world model framework that revises its deployment-time context while keeping the agent and model parameters frozen, using episodic memory, semantic heuristic extraction, and selective foresight filtering. It aims to make LLM-agent foresight more reliable for long-horizon planning.

entry.title: Obliviate: Erasing Concepts from Autoregressive Image Generation Models

author.name: Hossein Shakibania, Jonas Henry Grebe, Tobias Braun, Ege Aktemur, Saleh Aslani, Mehmet G\"orkem Yi\u{g}it, Marcus Rohrbach

entry.summary: Obliviate is a guidance-based concept erasure method for autoregressive image generation, using KL-based supervision over visual token distributions and trajectory-level updates to remove harmful or unsafe concepts. It fills a gap as concept erasure has been largely unexplored for autoregressive image models amid the move to unified multimodal architectures.

entry.title: TrafficAlign: Aligning Large Language Models for Traffic Scenario Generation

author.name: Zhi Tu, Liangkun Niu, Tianyi Zhang

entry.summary: TrafficAlign is a framework that fine-tunes LLMs to generate realistic traffic scenarios from real driving videos, aligning model outputs with real-world distributions. It reveals up to 10.8 percent more collisions than prior methods and reduces collision rates when used to retrain driving models.

entry.title: Benchmark AUC Is Not Deployable Reliability: A Cross-Dataset Audit of Off-the-Shelf Features for Surveillance Video Anomaly Detection

author.name: Mohammadreza Rashidi

entry.summary: This cross-dataset audit shows that high same-scene ROC-AUC on video anomaly detection benchmarks (avg 0.704) collapses to near-chance (0.499) when training and testing on different datasets, using frozen off-the-shelf embeddings. It demonstrates benchmark AUC does not equal deployable reliability.

entry.title: Consistency as Inductive Bias: Learning Cross-View Invariance for Robust Multimodal Reasoning

author.name: Xin Zou, Haolin Deng, Yibo Yan, Shuliang Liu, Kening Zheng, Zhiwei Jin, Chen Chen, Haonan Lu, Xuming Hu

entry.summary: ConsistRoll introduces cross-view consistency as an inductive bias for multimodal LLMs, enforcing that semantically equivalent views of the same instance yield identical answers during reinforcement learning. It reuses GRPO group sampling to inject this constraint, addressing a gap where standard RLVR rewards views independently.

entry.title: Building artificial intelligence virtual tissue (AIVT) for tissue state representation, feature prediction, and dynamic simulation

author.name: Qiqi Lu, Qianjin Feng, Shaoqun Zeng, Shenghua Cheng

entry.summary: Proposes the concept of AI Virtual Tissue (AIVT), a framework grounded in spatial multimodal data for learning unified, spatially resolved, dynamically manipulable representations of tissue states and transitions. It aims to model tissue homeostasis and pathology beyond conventional computational methods.

entry.title: Argus: Metric Panoramic 3D Reconstruction for Indoor Scenes

author.name: Xi Li, Linyuan Li, Yan Wu, Tong Rao, Kai Zhang, Xinchen Hui, Cihui Pan

entry.summary: Argus performs metric panoramic 3D reconstruction for indoor scenes via a feed-forward network, supported by the Realsee3D dataset of 10K scenes with 299K panoramic viewpoints. It uses a learned covisibility module to select an optimal reference view and avoid global pose drift in sparse captures.

entry.title: Hyper-Network Neural Functional Maps for Unsupervised Robust 3D Shape Matching

author.name: Dongliang Cao, Florian Bernard

entry.summary: Introduces a hyper-network that predicts non-linear neural functional maps for unsupervised robust 3D shape matching, better aligning truncated spectral bases under partiality, topological noise, and raw point clouds. It refines standard functional maps with an MLP whose weights are conditioned on the input.

entry.title: A Multi Center Breast FNAC Whole-Slide Cytology Dataset for AI-Assisted Patch-Wise Classification Using C1 to C5 Reporting Categories

author.name: Garima Jain, Abhijeet Patil, Surabhi Jain, Sanghamitra Pati, Amit Sethi, Sandeep Mathur, Pulkit Verma, Nishi Halduniya, Jatin Kashyap, Sharat Kumar, Simmi Kharb, Sunita Singh, Sucheta Devi Khuraijam, Sushma Khuraijam, Ratan Konjengbam, Arvind Kumar, Deepali Tirkey, Saurav Banerjee, Shivani Kalhan, Rakesh Kumar Gupta, Ranjana Solanki, Deepika Hemranjani, Shashank Nath Singh, Uma Handa, Manveen Kaur, B. G. Malathi, Yogender P., Niraj Kumari, Shruti Gupta, Indu R. Nair, Vidya C., Basumitra Das, Sunil Kumar Komanapalli, Ravindra Karle, Tanaya Kulkarni, Vandana Raphael, Biswajit Dey, Vaishali Gaikwad, Nilam Adhav

entry.summary: Presents a multi-center breast FNAC whole-slide cytology dataset with C1-C5 reporting labels, comprising 470 WSIs from 321 patients across Indian tertiary centers with 7,398 expert-verified annotated patches. It releases NDPI slides and annotations for AI-assisted patch-wise classification.

entry.title: UniGP: Taming Diffusion Transformer for Prior-Preserved Unified Generation and Perception

author.name: Qin Guo, Hao Luo, Dongxu Yue, Weixuan Jin, Xiao Fu, Fan Wang, Dan Xu

entry.summary: UniGP is a diffusion transformer framework built on MMDiT that unifies controllable image generation and dense prediction through simple joint training, preserving the backbone's versatile priors without task-specific designs. It captures the joint distribution of images under different conditions.

entry.title: Robust and Efficient Monocular 3D Gaussian SLAM for Kilometer-Scale Outdoor Scenes

author.name: Sicheng Yu, Dongxu Shen, Beizhen Zhao, Guanzhi Ding, Hao Wang

entry.summary: KiloGS-SLAM is a monocular 3D Gaussian Splatting SLAM system scaling to kilometer-level outdoor scenes, addressing fragile long-term tracking and memory overhead via a motion-adaptive hybrid tracking module with a three-tier solving pipeline. It dynamically switches between Essential matrix and PnP models and can invoke a foundation model to rescue trajectories.

entry.title: TacGen: Touch Is a Necessary Dimension of Physical-World Representation -- Addressing Tactile Data Scarcity with Scalable Vision-to-Touch Alignment and Generation

author.name: Wanghao Ye, Aarosh Das, Sihan Chen, Yiting Wang, Bowei Tian, Guoheng Sun, Shwai He, Zheyu Shen, Ziyao Wang, Yexiao He, Zhaoyi Liu, Meng Liu, Yuning Zhang, Meng Feng, Ziyi Wang, Yilong Dai, Yifei Dong, Siyuan Peng, Zhenle Duan, Joshua Liu, Lang Xiong, Ang Li

entry.summary: TacGen addresses tactile data scarcity by combining vision-touch contrastive alignment with a latent-space generator that synthesizes tactile representations from RGB images. It demonstrates measurable gains in predicting physical properties like mass, density, and hardness.

entry.title: Learning Transferable Dynamics Priors from Action to World Modeling

author.name: Ze Huang, Jiahui Zhang, Hairuo Liu, Chenxi Zhang, Ran Cheng, Li Zhang

entry.summary: A2World pretrains a multi-view action-conditioned diffusion world model on large-scale robot manipulation data to learn transferable dynamics priors. The learned model can serve as a real-world simulator for policy evaluation and what-if analysis.

entry.title: Hierarchical Policy Learning via Spectral Decomposition

author.name: Shuxin Cao, Liquan Wang, Walker Byrnes, Yiye Chen, Yilun Du, Animesh Garg

entry.summary: Causal Spectral Policy decomposes robot action sequences via discrete cosine transform, separating low-frequency global motion intent from high-frequency execution refinements, then generates coarse-to-fine actions causally. It outperforms baselines in simulation and real-world tests.

entry.title: Sequential Planning via Anchored Robotic Keypoints

author.name: Bryce Grant, Aryeh Rothenberg, Logan Senning, Zonghe Chua, Zach Patterson, Peng Wang

entry.summary: SPARK is a training-free neurosymbolic manipulation system that uses a single Gemini call to compose a typed behavior tree of composable primitives, focusing computation on perception where position/task changes most cause failures. It reaches 43.7% on LIBERO-PRO cells, more than doubling code-generation-agent and VLA baselines.

entry.title: Testing hypotheses via orthogonalization

author.name: Ameer Dharamshi, Runjia Zou, Daniela Witten

entry.summary: Proposes a new hypothesis testing framework that adds and subtracts external symmetric-shift noise to partition data into two pieces, then orthogonalizes one against the other under the null and tests whether orthogonalization succeeded as a valid test. It enables valid testing in modern settings with abstract nulls, data reuse, and minimal assumptions.

entry.title: SceneBot: Contact-Prompted General Humanoid Whole Body Tracking with Scene-Interaction

author.name: Sirui Chen, Shibo Zhao, Zhen Wu, Jiaman Li, Guanya Shi, C. Karen Liu

entry.summary: SceneBot is a unified humanoid whole-body motion-tracking framework conditioned on reference motions and per-link contact labels, with hindsight scene reconstruction inferring interaction graphs from retargeted human motion. Handles locomotion, terrain, and contact-rich manipulation.

entry.title: Fisher-Routed Mixture of Experts for Federated Class-Incremental Learning

author.name: Wenhao Yuan, Chenchen Lin, Jian Chen, Jinfeng Xu, Zewei Liu, Edith Cheuk Han Ngai

entry.summary: FedFMX uses a Fisher-routed mixture of experts for federated class-incremental learning, routing samples to expert subsets that balance new knowledge acquisition and retention. Tackles capacity conflict, non-IID heterogeneity, and class misalignment.

entry.title: How Far Can Sharpness and Complexity Jointly Explain Generalization?

author.name: Ziyu Cheng, Xitong Zhang, Longxiu Huang, Rongrong Wang

entry.summary: Studies the joint explanatory power of sharpness and complexity for generalization using linear regression and a Pareto-based analysis. Proposes function-space realizations of both factors that are less parameter-dependent.

entry.title: KrishokChat: A Citation-Grounded Dataset and Benchmark for Bengali Agricultural Advisory

author.name: Khan Raiyan Ibne Reza, Omar Ibne Shahid

entry.summary: KrishokChat is the first citation-grounded Bengali agricultural instruction-tuning dataset, built from 290 knowledge nodes and 129 manuals, expanded to 145,500 QA pairs with safety instances. Each instance carries verified citation provenance for low-resource crop advisory.

entry.title: STEMGym: Benchmarking Sequential Decision-Making under Dose Budgets in Autonomous Electron Microscopy

author.name: Can Polat, Erchin Serpedin, Mustafa Kurban, Hasan Kurban

entry.summary: Introduces STEMGym, an open-source Gymnasium benchmark of physics-simulated scanning transmission electron microscopy worlds for sequential decision-making under electron-dose budgets. Surprisingly, it finds that smarter adaptive navigation is not the dominant lever for sample-efficient acquisition.

entry.title: Dual-Flow Reinforcement Learning with State-Aware Exploration

author.name: Qijun Li, Zheng Fu, Qi Song, Yifei He, Weitao Zhou, Kun Jiang, Diange Yang

entry.summary: Proposes Dual-Flow RL, an actor-critic framework using conditional flow matching to jointly model continuous multimodal return distributions and multimodal policies for continuous control. It addresses biased value estimation and mode collapse with state-aware exploration.

entry.title: Robust Strategic Classification under Decision-Dependent Cost Uncertainty

author.name: Sura Alhanouti, G\"uzin Bayraksan, Parinaz Naghizadeh

entry.summary: Proposes a two-stage robust optimization framework for strategic classification where manipulation costs are decision-dependent and uncertain, since today's algorithmic decisions influence tomorrow's gaming costs. It moves beyond prior assumptions of fixed, decision-independent manipulation costs.

entry.title: Understanding Evaluation Illusion in Diffusion Large Language Models

author.name: Hengxiang Zhang, Jiaxi Ren, Hongxin Wei

entry.summary: This paper rigorously evaluates decoding methods for diffusion LLMs and finds that method rankings are highly sensitive to prompt template choice, producing an evaluation illusion where single-template tests overstate gains. It cautions against biased conclusions in dLLM efficiency research. It matters for trustworthy evaluation of emerging diffusion language models.

entry.title: SEVA: Self-Evolving Verification Agent with Process Reward for Fact Attribution

author.name: Aojie Yuan, Yi Nian, Haiyue Zhang, Zijian Su, Yue Zhao

entry.summary: SEVA is a self-evolving fact-attribution verification agent that emits evidence alignments, reasoning chains, calibrated confidence, and a six-category error diagnosis, trained with RL using a decomposed process reward to avoid advantage collapse from binary rewards. It improves auditability over opaque binary verifiers. It matters for reliable hallucination detection in LLM agents.

entry.title: Automating the Design of Embodied AgentArchitectures

author.name: Jian Zhou, Sihao Lin, Jin Li, Shuai Fu, Gengze Zhou, Qi Wu

entry.summary: This work extends Agent Architecture Search to perceptual embodied agents, introducing AgentCanvas, a typed-graph runtime hosting embodied executors as editable node-and-wire programs, and KDLoop, a coding-agent search procedure. It automates design choices about memory, perception, and model-call connectivity for embodied agents. It matters for automated embodied-agent architecture design.

entry.title: OLIVE: View-Augmented Latent Prediction with Waveform Reconstruction for Speech SSL

author.name: Karl El Hajal, Mathew Magimai. -Doss

entry.summary: OLIVE is a self-supervised speech representation framework jointly optimizing masked latent prediction and waveform reconstruction. It produces representations supporting generation, speaker, recognition, and semantic tasks under one objective.

entry.title: Factorizable Normalizing Flows for parameter-dependent density morphing

author.name: Davide Valsecchi, Mauro Doneg\`a, Rainer Wallny

entry.summary: Factorizable Normalizing Flows model parameter-dependent density deformations via a reference flow composed with a learnable polynomial transformation factorized over parameters. It targets high-energy-physics problems where densities shift with continuous parameters.

entry.title: $\mu$Flow: Leveraging Average Images for Improving Generalisation of Deepfake Faces Detectors

author.name: Orazio Pontorno, Mattia Litrico, Luca Guarnera, Mario Valerio Giuffrida, Sebastiano Battiato

entry.summary: muFlow is a one-class deepfake detector trained only on real images, exploiting that averaging multiple images amplifies consistent generative traces. It improves cross-generator generalization without needing fake examples.

entry.title: Conversational Domain Adaptation of IndicTrans2 across 21 Indic Languages via Experience Replay and Model Soups

author.name: Aditya Pratap Singh

entry.summary: Adapts IndicTrans2 to conversational register across 21 Indic languages using experience replay and model souping to avoid catastrophic forgetting of the general domain. Achieves conversational gains in all 21 languages while matching FLORES performance.

entry.title: How to Leverage Synthetic Speech for LLM-Based ASR Systems?

author.name: Yanis Labrak, Dairazalia Sanchez-Cortes, Sergio Burdisso, S\'everin Baroudi, Shashi Kumar, Esa\'u Villatoro-Tello, Srikanth Madikeri, Manjunath K E, Old\v{r}ich Plchot, Kadri Hacio\u{g}lu, Petr Motlicek, Andreas Stolcke

entry.summary: Studies how to best use synthetic TTS speech for training LLM-based ASR in privacy-constrained domains by probing where a SLAM-ASR backbone separates real from synthetic speech. Localizes the discriminative signal to early-to-middle layers.

entry.title: Towards Physical Intuitions for Alignment Dynamics: A Case Study With Randomness Crystallization

author.name: Kunal Samanta, Ari Holtzman, Peter West

entry.summary: A position paper proposing thermodynamic phase-transition theory as a vocabulary for understanding post-training alignment dynamics, using a randomness-crystallization case study with liquid, nucleation, and crystalline phases. Aims to make alignment dynamics more principled.

entry.title: SUMO: Segment and Track Any Motion with Nonlinear State Space Models

author.name: Kexin Tian, Sixu Li, Keshu Wu, Yang Zhou, Zhengzhong Tu

entry.summary: SUMO is a zero-shot, training-free framework unifying visual object tracking and moving object segmentation by integrating nonlinear state space models with vision-based segmentation. It uses a robotics-inspired unscented filter to capture complex, nonlinear object motion.

entry.title: Learning Efficient 4D Gaussian Representations from Monocular Videos with Flow Splatting

author.name: Shengjun Zhang, Jinzhao Li, Xin Fei, Yueqi Duan

entry.summary: Flow Splatting learns efficient 4D Gaussian representations from monocular videos by constructing a velocity field and rendering optical flow to supervise dynamics learning. It addresses long training, slow rendering, and high memory of prior 4D Gaussian methods.

entry.title: GeoEdit: Geometry-Aware Object Editing via Dual-Branch Denoising

author.name: Yi He, Jiangming Wang, Xinyu Wang, Mark Fong, Songchun Zhang, Yuxuan Xue, Hai-Tao Zheng, Yue Ma

entry.summary: GeoEdit is a training-free pipeline for geometry-aware object editing (translation, rotation, scaling) in single photos while obeying 3D physical constraints, decoupling rigid object geometry from free background synthesis. It uses a lift-manipulate-render-denoise approach to avoid perspective violations and ghosting.

entry.title: Latent Noise Mask for Reducing Visual Redundancy in Multimodal Large Language Models

author.name: Kai Jiang, Ruishu Zhu, Siqi Huang, Hongyuan Zhang, Xuelong Li

entry.summary: Lens (Latent Noise Mask) reduces visual redundancy in multimodal LLMs by scoring which visual tokens support the current question via a lightweight Lens Evidence Token and preserving them during decoding. It aims to improve fine-grained visual reasoning by reasoning with cleaner visual cues in latent space.

entry.title: Intermediate Text Representation Guided Text-to-Image Generation for Enhancing One-and-Only Alignment

author.name: Soyoun Won, Aryan Yazdan Parast, Basim Azam, Jean Honorio, Naveed Akhtar

entry.summary: Addresses concept association bias in text-to-image diffusion models, especially for one-and-only objects with single canonical forms, via an information-theoretic analysis showing final text embeddings discard concept information present in intermediate layers. It uses intermediate text representations to enhance prompt alignment.

entry.title: FFAvatar: Feed-Forward 4D Head Avatar Reconstruction from Sparse Portrait Images

author.name: Jianjiang Yao, Ke Xian, Renxiang Dai, Robert Caiming Qiu

entry.summary: FFAvatar is a transformer-based 3D Gaussian framework for fast, animatable 4D head avatar reconstruction from one or more portrait images, supporting incremental reconstruction as views are added. It uses alternating attention to disentangle identity from expression and viewpoint.

entry.title: Beyond Point Estimates for Glaucoma Visual Field Forecasting with Diffusion Models

author.name: Marta Colmenar Herrera, Pablo M\'arquez Neila, \c{S}erife Seda Kucur Erg\"unay, Martin S. Zinkernagel, Raphael Sznitman

entry.summary: Applies conditioned denoising diffusion models to glaucoma visual field forecasting, formulating it as probabilistic prediction to generate distributions of plausible future visual fields from irregular longitudinal observations. It produces well-calibrated uncertainty rather than single deterministic predictions.

entry.title: OWMDrive: Causality-Aware End-to-End Autonomous Driving via 4D Occupancy World Model

author.name: Junjie Cheng, Ruiqi Song, Ye Wu, Nanxing Zeng, Ximiao Li, Yunfeng Ai

entry.summary: OWMDrive is a generative end-to-end autonomous driving framework built on a 4D occupancy world model performing multi-step 3D occupancy forecasting as a conditional prior for causality-aware planning. It addresses unstable or overly conservative planning under occlusions and unexpected events.

entry.title: Critical Interval MSE: Toward Reliable Offline Validation for Robot Manipulation Policies

author.name: Haoxu Huang, Tongsam Zheng, Yifan Chen, Jiacheng You, Yang Gao

entry.summary: Critical Interval MSE proposes an offline validation metric for robot manipulation policies that restricts error computation to task-critical segments and adds action-alignment, improving correlation with real-world performance over plain validation loss. It addresses the costly bottleneck of real-world policy evaluation.

entry.title: Chronos: A Physics-Informed Full-History Framework for Non-Markovian Long-Horizon Manipulation

author.name: Yulin Zhou, Yimeng Wang, Nengyu Wang, Shaojia Xing, Shiyun Tu, Xiang Li, Jingkai Zhang, Ningbo Jiang, Yuankai Lin, Hua Yang, Xiangrui Zeng, Zhouping Yin

entry.summary: Chronos is a physics-informed full-history framework for non-Markovian long-horizon manipulation that elevates observation history to the latent state of policy dynamics, fusing observation and proprioception into time-aligned state tokens processed by a selective state space model. It addresses memory-dependent tasks where identical observations demand different actions.

entry.title: Mitigating LLM-based p-Hacking by Preregistering for the Next LLM

author.name: Maria Thomas, Kristina Gligoric, Nihar B. Shah

entry.summary: Proposes a protocol to mitigate p-hacking in LLM-based research by preregistering the analysis plan along with eligible future models, then running confirmatory analysis on the first eligible LLM released after preregistration. Leverages the unknowability of future model behavior.

entry.title: Halt Fast! Early Stopping for Certified Robustness

author.name: Andrew C. Cullen, Paul Montague, Benjamin I. P. Rubinstein

entry.summary: Presents a meta-learning framework for anytime-valid certified robustness via randomized smoothing, using a lightweight meta-learner to predict image-specific priors for a sequential E-process, achieving a 20-fold reduction in sample complexity. Addresses RS's extreme computational cost.

entry.title: Hierarchical Decision Making with Structured Policies: A Principled Design via Inverse Optimization

author.name: Yuexuan Wang, Jingyuan Zhou, Kaidi Yang

entry.summary: Proposes a principled design for the lower-level optimization in hierarchical RL-OC architectures using inverse optimization, addressing constraint satisfaction and myopic objectives. Aims to combine RL flexibility with optimal control guarantees.

entry.title: Multi-Agent Routing as Set-Valued Prediction: A WildChat Benchmark and Cost-Aware Evaluation

author.name: Ananto Nayan Bala, Faisal Muhammad Shah

entry.summary: Frames multi-agent/tool routing from prompts as set-valued prediction, introducing a 3,000-prompt benchmark derived from WildChat over 12 agents with cost-aware evaluation. Compares routing methods on set-level metrics, latency, and weighted-cost settings.

entry.title: BrainRiem: Riemannian Prototype Learning for Source-Free Cross-Site Brain Network Diagnosis

author.name: Kunyu Zhang, Tianxiang Xu

entry.summary: Frames online multi-human multi-robot teaming as a linear matching bandit, assigning robots with unknown features to human agent sets over rounds. LinMatch uses optimistic matching solved via the Hungarian algorithm with novel regret bounds.

entry.title: Blackknife: Hard-Label Query-Limited Black-Box Attacks on Heterogeneous Graph Neural Networks

author.name: Honglin Gao, Junhao Ren, Lan Zhao, Yue Yang, Jindong Chang, Gaoxi Xiao

entry.summary: Blackknife is a hard-label, query-limited, structure-limited black-box evasion attack on heterogeneous graph neural networks, assuming no access to model internals or confidence scores. It targets realistic closed-system deployments.

entry.title: SP-CACW: Convergence-Aware Client Weighting for Selfish Personalized Learning

author.name: Yaron Kiselman, Kfir Y. Levy

entry.summary: SP-CACW is a convergence-aware client-weighting framework for selfish personalized federated learning, where a target client selects peer aggregation weights by minimizing an upper bound on its convergence error. It can zero-out harmful peers and provides convergence guarantees.

entry.title: Prototype Latent World Model Replay for Class-Incremental Learning

author.name: Weizhi Nie, Hui Wang, Weijie Wang, Yuting Su

entry.summary: Prototype Latent World Model Replay is a memory-free class-incremental learning framework storing old classes as distributions over stable hidden states rather than images. It samples old latent states to train a lightweight adapter and classifier alongside new features.

entry.title: Simplifying Flow Matching Transformations with Low-Rank Mixture Models

author.name: Liam A. Kruse, Houjun Liu, Alexandros E. Tzikas, Mansur M. Arief, Mykel J. Kochenderfer

entry.summary: Proposes using mixtures of probabilistic principal component analyzers as the latent density for normalizing flows instead of a standard normal, reducing topological mismatch between latent and data distributions for faster convergence. The work simplifies learned flow transformations.

entry.title: RoAd-RL: A Unified Library and Benchmark for Robust Adversarial Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Adithya Mohan, Daniel Kriegl, Torsten Sch\"on

entry.summary: Presents RoAd-RL, an open-source library and benchmark for robust adversarial reinforcement learning providing unified abstractions for policies, attacks, defenses, and robustness metrics with reproducible pipelines integrated with Stable-Baselines3 and Gymnasium. It evaluates DQN, PPO, and SAC under 192 attack-defense configurations.

entry.title: Decision-Value Attribution in Predict-then-Optimize Systems

author.name: Konstantinos Ziliaskopoulos, Alexander Vinel, Alice E. Smith

entry.summary: Proposes Decision Value Attribution, a Shapley-based framework that explains the downstream decision value in predict-then-optimize pipelines rather than just the forecasts, since large forecast changes may not alter decisions while small ones can. It defines cooperative games over information sources and optimization parameters.

entry.title: Neural Subspace Reallocation: Continual Learning as Retrieval-Based Subspace Memory Management

author.name: Byeong Hoon Yoon

entry.summary: Introduces Neural Subspace Reallocation, reframing continual learning as memory management over parameter subspaces by compressing LoRAs via SVD, banking them, recalling related past adapters by embedding similarity, and reallocating the active subspace. It proves regret bounds showing memoryless allocation underperforms history-aware policies.

entry.title: KnowsTFM: Knowledge-Informed Fine-Tuning of Small Tabular Foundation Models

author.name: Boshko Koloski, Xiangjian Jiang, Senja Pollak, Bla\v{z} \v{S}krlj, Mateja Jamnik, Nikola Simidjievski

entry.summary: Proposes KnowsTFM, knowledge-informed fine-tuning of small tabular foundation models using curated relational knowledge from knowledge graphs and banks, to improve performance in niche domains where data is scarce, high-dimensional, and distribution-shifted. It addresses cases where tabular foundation models fail to beat domain-specific methods.

entry.title: Exploring Differences Between Tabular Enterprise Data and Public Benchmarks

author.name: Myung Jun Kim, Maximilian Schambach, Frank Essenberger, Andre Sres, Johannes H\"ohne

entry.summary: This study compares tabular enterprise data with public benchmarks, showing they differ markedly in statistics and that models like TabPFN performing well on standard benchmarks may fail on real enterprise data. It highlights a gap between academic benchmarking and business applications.

entry.title: RadarTwin: Scene-Specific mmWave Radar Simulation and Learning for Mobile Indoor Perception

author.name: Emily Bejerano, Federico Tondolo, Devang Gupta, Aaron Mano Cherian, Taeyoo Kim, Ayaan Qayyum, Xiaofan Yu, Xiaofan Jiang

entry.summary: RadarTwin generates deployment-specific mmWave radar training data from 3D reconstructions, using a vision-language model to infer surface materials and a physics-based ray tracer for FMCW measurements with multi-bounce propagation. It studies sim-to-real transfer with paired real-simulated datasets.

entry.title: MammoFlow: Multiview Mammogram Synthesis with Anatomically Consistent Flow Matching

author.name: Yuexi Du, Leya Barrientos, Laura Sheiman, John Lewin, Hemant D. Tagare, Nicha C. Dvornek

entry.summary: MammoFlow synthesizes multiview mammograms by leveraging the geometric relationship between craniocaudal and mediolateral oblique views, using an alignment module that searches affine transforms and a pixel-space self-consistency loss based on Earth Mover's Distance. It enforces 3D consistency during flow-matching generation.

entry.title: Depth-Staggered Fibonacci Spacing for Sparse Attention: Static Schedules Beat Learned Dilation and Extrapolate Where Dense Attention Fails

author.name: Chad A. Capps

entry.summary: This paper studies sparse self-attention where queries attend to a local window plus Fibonacci-spaced offsets with a per-layer scalar, comparing fixed, learned, static stagger, and coprime schedules across 21 small language models. It finds static per-layer staggered spacing beats learned dilation and extrapolates where dense attention fails.

entry.title: A Neuroimaging Simulation Framework for Developing and Evaluating Causal AI

author.name: Eryn Libert-Scott, Emma A. M. Stanley, Vibujithan Vigneshwaran, Matthias Wilms, Erik Y. Ohara, Nils D. Forkert

entry.summary: This paper presents a neuroimaging simulation framework that generates synthetic T1-weighted MRI adhering to a user-specified causal structure linking non-image variables to image-derived biomarkers. It produces ground-truth datasets for developing and evaluating causal AI in medical imaging.

entry.title: HorizonRelight: Relighting Long-horizon Videos Consistently via Diffusion Transformers

author.name: Jing Yang, Mayoore Jaiswal, Zian Wang, Steven Zeng, Rochelle Pereira, Yajie Zhao, Jianyuan Min

entry.summary: HorizonRelight reframes long-horizon video relighting as temporally conditioned latent domain translation, enforcing cross-chunk continuity by propagating target-domain latents and using masked self-conditioning. This fixes temporal discontinuities from chunked sliding-window inference on diffusion backbones trained on short clips. It matters for consistent controllable video relighting.

entry.title: Bidirectional Autoregressive Latent Diffusion for Forward and Inverse Magnetohydrodynamics

author.name: Alexander Scheinker

entry.summary: This work presents a bidirectional autoregressive latent diffusion model for forward and inverse magnetohydrodynamics prediction, using forward-backward consistency as a self-supervised metric for test-time uncertainty and error estimation without ground truth. It demonstrates potential as a non-invasive plasma diagnostic. It matters for ML-based plasma physics and uncertainty-aware scientific surrogates.

entry.title: MATCH: Modulating Attention via In-Context Retrieval for Long-Context Transformers

author.name: Linrui Ma, Chun Hei Lo, Xinyu Wang, Peng Lu, Xihao Yuan, Hanting Chen, Kai Han, Xinghao Chen, Chengjun Zhan, Hanlin Xu, Yichun Yin, Lifeng Shang, Feng Wen, Boxing Chen, Yufei Cui

entry.summary: MATCH augments sparse attention mechanisms with a dynamic in-context retrieval system to recover long-range information that rigid local windows discard, improving long-context performance while keeping efficiency. It matters for scalable long-context Transformers. Authors are affiliated with Huawei.

entry.title: Structural Certification for Reliable Physical Design with Language Models

author.name: Nakul Vyas, Iliya D. Stoev

entry.summary: PHACT is a propose-certify loop where an unreliable language model proposes physical designs and a deterministic engine alone certifies them as certified, impossible, or unknown, deriving certified quantities from fixed inputs to make forgery impossible. Across eighty adversarial trials it produced zero false certifications. It matters for reliable LLM-assisted physical design.

entry.title: A Distributionally Robust Framework for Learned Reconstructions in Inverse Problems

author.name: Floor van Maarschalkerwaart, Subhadip Mukherjee, Christoph Brune, Marcello Carioni

entry.summary: This work develops a structured distributionally robust optimization framework for learned inverse-problem reconstruction, restricting the ambiguity set to perturbations aligned with the data-acquisition physics rather than uniformly perturbing the joint distribution. This avoids the over-conservatism of standard Wasserstein DRO. It matters for noise-robust learned reconstruction operators.

entry.title: Bridging the NISQ and Fault-Tolerant Regimes: Generative-ML-Assisted Quantum Selected CI for Molecular Simulations

author.name: Anurag K. S. V., Ashish Kumar Patra, Manas Mukherjee, Ruchika Bhat, Sai Shankar P., Rahul Maitra, Jaiganesh G

entry.summary: Presents a hybrid quantum-classical workflow for molecular binding-energy calculation, integrating a linear-scaling CNOT UCCSD ansatz and generative-ML-assisted quantum selected configuration interaction. It reduces parameter initialization cost and bridges NISQ and fault-tolerant regimes.

entry.title: Legal Domain Adaptation of Modern BERT Models

author.name: Dominik Stammbach, Peter Henderson

entry.summary: Studies legal-domain adaptation of ModernBERT by further pretraining on US court opinions, showing significant gains over vanilla ModernBERT despite the base model's large pretraining corpus. It confirms domain adaptation still pays off and beats from-scratch training.

entry.title: Can OCR-VLMs Read Devanagari? A Stress-Test Benchmark and Post-Correction Study

author.name: Aditya Pratap Singh

entry.summary: Stress-tests ten OCR systems on Devanagari (Hindi) including classical, open VLMs, specialized OCR-VLMs, and frontier closed models under degradation and real scans, plus a post-correction study. Finds clean text fails to differentiate systems while degradation separates them.

entry.title: MIThinker: A Plug-and-Play Policy-Optimized Thinker For Motivational Interviewing Counseling

author.name: Yizhe Yang, Palakorn Achananuparp, Heyan Huang, Jing Jiang, Ee-Peng Lim

entry.summary: MIThinker is a lightweight plug-and-play thinking model that generates therapeutic thoughts to guide motivational interviewing counseling agents in strategy selection and response generation. It uses an automated pipeline reverse-engineering counselor thoughts plus two-stage policy-optimized training.

entry.title: mamabench and mamaretrieval: Benchmarks for Evaluating Medical Retrieval-Augmented Generation in Maternal, Neonatal, and Reproductive Health

author.name: Yi Ren

entry.summary: Releases two benchmarks for maternal, neonatal, and reproductive health: mamabench (25,949 QA items) and mamaretrieval (3,185 queries with graded relevance over a 63,650-chunk corpus). It fills a gap in medical RAG evaluation for under-served midwifery domains.

entry.title: Which Tokens Need Context? A Reference-Based Analysis of Translation Responsibility Using Fertility and Entropy

author.name: Ramakrishna Appicharla, Baban Gain, Santanu Pal, Asif Ekbal

entry.summary: Proposes a post-hoc, model-agnostic framework using word-alignment-derived fertility and entropy measures to quantify which tokens depend on context in translation. It identifies context-sensitive tokens like pronouns without requiring discourse test sets or model internals.

entry.title: SHOVIR: A Benchmark for Evaluating Vision Shortcut Learning in Radiology Report Generation

author.name: Filippo Ruffini, Marco Salm\'e, Rosa Sicilia, Valerio Guarrasi, Paolo Soda

entry.summary: SHOVIR is a benchmark for evaluating vision shortcut learning in radiology report generation, extending chest X-ray datasets with per-box labels and occlusion experiments to test whether diagnostic statements actually rely on visible pathological evidence. It exposes a failure mode where models exploit priors rather than image content.

entry.title: Predicting Metastatic Risk from Primary Tissue Architecture via Distance-Aware Spatial Modeling

author.name: Sandesh Pokhrel, Hamid Manoochehri, Bodong Zhang, Beatrice S Knudsen, Tolga Tasdizen

entry.summary: This paper predicts distant metastatic risk from primary tumor histology using distance-aware spatial modeling that explicitly captures geometric arrangements among tumor cells, fibroblasts, and lymphocytes, overcoming Multiple Instance Learning's discarding of spatial layout. It argues metastatic potential is dictated by tumor microenvironment geometry.

entry.title: MAVIN: Multi-Shot Audio-Visual Generation with Narrative Control

author.name: Kaiqi Liu, Yunyao Mao, Ziqi Cai, Zheng Geng, Jing Wang, Qiulin Wang, Xintao Wang, Pengfei Wan, Kun Gai, Shuchen Weng, Boxin Shi

entry.summary: MAVIN is presented as the first framework for multi-shot audio-visual generation with customized narrative control, using boundary-aware attention and ID-aware propagation to resolve temporal misalignment and multi-subject controllability. It addresses incomplete scripting in coherent multi-shot generation.

entry.title: One Scene, Two Depths: Probing Geometric Ambiguity in Monocular Foundation Models

author.name: Xiaohao Xu, Feng Xue, Xiang Li, Haowei Li, Shusheng Yang, Tianyi Zhang, Matthew Johnson-Roberson, Xiaonan Huang

entry.summary: This work probes geometric ambiguity in monocular depth foundation models using transparent scenes where a single ray contains multiple valid surfaces, introducing MD-3k, a two-layer ordinal benchmark to measure depth-layer preference. It shows monocular depth reduces layered geometry to an annotation convention rather than scene truth.

entry.title: LWDrive: Layer-Wise World-Model-Guided Vision-Language Model Planning for Autonomous Driving

author.name: Chen Yang, Yuhao Wei, Ze Xu, Ziheng Zou, Shuang Liang, Delin Ouyang, Lingfeng Qi, Jie Li, Guofa Li

entry.summary: LWDrive is a vision-language model planning framework for autonomous driving that refines coarse VLM-generated trajectories using layer-wise world-model guidance. It treats VLM output as an intent prior, expands candidate trajectories, and progressively refines them for geometrically accurate planning.

entry.title: Variance Reduction on the Camera Axis: Multi-View Score Distillation for 3D

author.name: Marian Lupascu, Mihai Sorin Stupariu, Ionut Mironica

entry.summary: MV-SDI reduces gradient variance in score distillation for text-to-3D by aggregating K views per step at fixed UNet budget, isolating the sampling axis from prior quality without retraining the diffusion model. This improves 3D shape consistency through variance reduction alone.

entry.title: Cross-Modal Iteration Distillation for Robust IHD Screening: The IDNet Framework and A New Benchmark

author.name: Yongchang Gao, Junjie Pang, Shuaiyu Yang, Yusheng Yang, Xichao Jia, Shaojie Li, Hongfei Zhang, Jia Mu

entry.summary: IDNet is a multimodal framework for ischemic heart disease screening from color fundus photography, using a cross-modal distillation aggregator to integrate left-eye, right-eye, and sparse clinical features. It also contributes a reproducible UK Biobank benchmark of over 50,000 images.

entry.title: Early Cue Precision Shapes Visual Shortcut Learning in Controlled Cue-Manipulation Benchmarks

author.name: Chanho Park, Woochan Lee, Janyeong Oh, Geongho Gong, Minshu Kim, Yeachan Kwak, Seongim Choi

entry.summary: Investigates how early cue precision shapes visual shortcut learning across synthetic shape-texture, sequential digit, frozen-representation, and CIFAR-10 texture-overlay benchmarks. It finds degraded-but-predictive input does not substitute for cue decorrelation in preventing shortcut reliance.

entry.title: FastPano3D: Feed-Forward Indoor Panoramic 3D Reconstruction from a Single Image

author.name: Jianqiang Li, Liumei Zhang, Wenjia Guo, Tianlong Feng, Yongzhi Liao, Di Lu, Hanchi Ren, Jingjing Deng

entry.summary: FastPano3D is a feed-forward framework generating renderable 3D Gaussian representations from a single panoramic image, handling equirectangular distortions and non-uniform feature distributions. It avoids multi-view supervision and per-scene optimization for rapid indoor reconstruction.

entry.title: Residual-Guided Expert Specialization for Incomplete Multimodal Learning

author.name: Seunghun Baek, Jihwan Park, Jaeyoon Sim, Minjae Jeong, Hoseok Lee, Won Hwa Kim

entry.summary: MARS is a mixture-of-experts framework for incomplete multimodal learning that guides expert specialization based on residual deviations between incomplete and complete representations. It derives a privileged residual signal during training to handle missing modalities at inference.

entry.title: REPAIR-Bench: A Benchmark for Robot Error Perception And Interaction Recovery

author.name: Giuliano Pioldi, Yashika Batra, Arman Ibrayeva, Yuanchen Bai, Purnjay Maruur, Promise Ekpo, Angelique Taylor

entry.summary: REPAIR-Bench is a benchmark for robot error perception and interaction recovery built on 214 interaction trials from 41 participants, spanning four induced failure types with synchronized facial action units, head pose, speech, and affect/recovery reports. It moves beyond binary failure detection toward modeling the full failure lifecycle in HRI.

entry.title: FutureNav: Unified World-Action Modeling for Vision-and-Language Navigation

author.name: Lingfeng Zhang, Zeying Gong, Xiaoshuai Hao, Haoxiang Fu, Qiang Zhang, Mingliang Zhou, Hangjun Ye, Xiaojun Liang, Junwei Liang, Wenbo Ding

entry.summary: FutureNav is a VLM-based unified world-action modeling framework for vision-and-language navigation in continuous environments that jointly encodes text, visual, and spatial features and optimizes four objectives for simultaneous world-state and action modeling. It explicitly models and predicts future world states rather than only direct action generation.

entry.title: Internalizing the Future: A Unified Agentic Training Paradigm for World Model Planning

author.name: Xuan Zhang, Zhijian Zhou, Lingfeng Qiao, Yulei Qin, Ke Li, Xing Sun, Xiaoyu Tan, Chao Qu, Yuan Qi

entry.summary: Proposes training a single autoregressive LLM agent to verbalize prospective state rollouts and plan-conditioned success estimates, internalizing world-model planning. Identifies a format-capability gap where naive fine-tuning yields superficial foresight mimicry.

entry.title: Position: The Term "Machine Unlearning" Is Overused in LLMs

author.name: Sangyeon Yoon, Yeachan Jun, Albert No

entry.summary: A position paper arguing that the term machine unlearning is overused in LLM research and should be reserved for dataset-defined deletion that approximates retraining without a specified forget set. Distinguishes policy-driven tasks like refusal from true unlearning.

entry.title: Bifocal Diffusion Language Models: Asymmetric Bidirectional Context for Parallel Generation

author.name: Yuhang Chen, Xianfeng Wu, Jinhao Duan, Mingfu Liang, Xiaohan Wei, Yunchen Pu, Fei Tian, Chonglin Sun, Parish Aggarwal, Frank Shyu, Luke Simon, Sandeep Pandey, Xi Liu, Tianlong Chen

entry.summary: Bifocal dLLMs resolve the bidirectional-vs-causal attention dilemma in discrete diffusion language models through asymmetric bidirectional context, enabling KV caching while preserving generation quality. Targets efficient batch-serving for parallel diffusion generation.

entry.title: Closed-Form Steepest Descent Direction toward Flat Minima: Reducing Upper Bounds on the Loss Hessian Eigenspectrum in Neural Networks

author.name: Yuto Omae, Kazuki Sakai, Yohei Kakimoto, Makoto Sasaki, Yusuke Sakai, Hirotaka Takahashi

entry.summary: The authors analytically derive the gradient of an upper bound on the loss Hessian eigenspectrum (Wolkowicz-Styan bound) to steer training toward flat minima. This connects data distribution and network parameters to flat-minima directions in closed form, supporting the flatness-generalization hypothesis.

entry.title: Deterministic Decisions for High-Stakes AI. A Zero-Egress Pipeline with the Deployability of RAG and the Accuracy of Machine Learning

author.name: Craig Atkinson

entry.summary: Identifies intervention bias in zero-shot LLM educational advisors, which recommend action even when an oracle policy mandates inaction, yielding high false-positive rates. Shows supervised policy learning eliminates this bias in a zero-egress deterministic pipeline. References use GPT-4o.

entry.title: Speculative Pre-Positioning: Decoding Stateful Sessions to the Next Decision Point Off the Critical Path

author.name: Victor Norgren

entry.summary: Introduces speculative pre-positioning, which uses idle accelerator time in stateful inference sessions to decode forward to the next decision point using the target model itself with no draft model, moving cross-request prefill off the critical path. A confidence gate can answer from a cached distribution.

entry.title: What Drives the Inlier-Memorization Effect? A Theory of Outlier Detection via Early Training Dynamics

author.name: Kunwoong Kim, Dongha Kim

entry.summary: Provides a theoretical study of the inlier-memorization effect, where deep models memorize normal data before outliers, used as an unsupervised outlier-detection signal. Using a simple autoencoder, it proves under mild assumptions that inliers are memorized while outliers are not.

entry.title: Bandwidth Selection in Kernel Density Estimation for Model Calibration

author.name: Han Zhou, Teodora Popordanoska, Matthew Blaschko

entry.summary: Introduces Risk Alignment, a framework for selecting kernel bandwidth in KDE-based model calibration by aligning KDE-reconstructed risk with empirical risk, addressing the failure of standard MLE bandwidth selection for calibration tasks. It provides theoretical justification for the approach.

entry.title: Discovering Collaboration from Novelty: Random Network Distillation for Clustered Federated Learning

author.name: Davide Domini, Gianluca Aguzzi, Ivana Dusparic, Danilo Pianini, Mirko Viroli

entry.summary: This paper uses Random Network Distillation prediction error as a novelty-based similarity signal to discover client clusters in federated learning before training, decoupling clustering from the main loop. It mitigates non-IID degradation while reducing computation and communication.

entry.title: RADIANT-PET: Reasoning-Augmented PET/CT Lesion Segmentation with Large Language Models and Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Jiasheng Wang, Tanun Jitwatcharakomol, Piyawadee Jongpradubgiat, Simeng Zhu

entry.summary: RADIANT-PET couples a permissive voxel-level PET/CT segmentation model with LLM-based lesion-level adjudication that classifies candidate uptake regions as true lesion or false positive using structured descriptions and reports. Reinforcement learning strengthens lesion-level reasoning.

entry.title: Variance Reduction for Stochastic Gradient Generalized Non-reversible Langevin Monte Carlo Algorithms

author.name: Bingye Ni, Xiaoyu Wang, Yingli Wang, Lingjiong Zhu

entry.summary: This work derives a central limit theorem and variance-reduction analysis for stochastic gradient Euler-Maruyama estimators of generalized non-reversible Langevin dynamics, characterizing the limiting variance via the Poisson equation. It identifies conditions under which anti-symmetric perturbations reduce asymptotic variance.

entry.title: Residual-Guided Dictionary Learning for Spectrally Accurate Koopman Approximation

author.name: George Coote, Matthew J. Colbrook

entry.summary: This paper makes spectral reliability the objective of Koopman dictionary learning by training neural-network dictionaries to minimize residual DMD residuals rather than just next-step prediction. It also penalizes the condition number to prevent collapse. It matters for producing trustworthy Koopman spectra for nonlinear dynamics.

entry.title: Geometric Algebra Meets Cartesian Tensors: Higher-Order Equivariance for Interatomic Potentials

author.name: Can Polat, Erchin Serpedin, Mustafa Kurban, Hasan Kurban

entry.summary: CliffordSTF couples Clifford geometric algebra multivectors with closed-form symmetric-traceless Cartesian tensor tracks to add higher-order equivariance to interatomic potentials, fixing the poor force-direction prediction of Cl(3,0) models. It restores the rank-2 component missing from per-edge bilinears. It matters for accurate machine-learning force fields in molecular simulation.

entry.title: MemDelta: Controlled Baselines and Hidden Confounds in Agent Memory Evaluation

author.name: Kuan Wang

entry.summary: MemDelta is a controlled evaluation protocol varying one component at a time to isolate agent-memory gains from confounds in the LLM, embedding model, or retrieval pipeline on LongMemEval-S. It finds rankings reverse across model families and that confounds heavily distort reported gains. It matters for trustworthy agent-memory evaluation.

entry.title: EvalSafetyGap: A Hybrid Survey and Conceptual Framework for LLM Evaluation-Safety Failures

author.name: Bu\u{g}ra Alperen Ulu{\i}rmak, Rifat Kurban

entry.summary: EvalSafetyGap combines a hybrid systematic survey with a conceptual framework and a ten-model audit across eight evidence streams—benchmark validity, LLM-as-judge reliability, jailbreak robustness, reward hacking, interpretability, and governance—covering 2018-2026 evaluation-safety work. It frames the shared measurement problem where scores improve while latent properties remain unverified. It matters for understanding evaluation-safety failures.

entry.title: TRACE: A Concept Bottleneck Model for Longitudinal 3D Glioblastoma Response Assessment

author.name: Alia Tarek, Hamsa Saberr, Hamza Elghonemy, Youssef Afify, Tamer Basha, Omair Shahzad Bhatti, Abdulrahman M. Selim, Hasan Md Tusfiqur Alam Daniel Sonntag

entry.summary: Proposes TRACE, an interpretable concept bottleneck model aligned with RANO 2.0 criteria for classifying glioblastoma treatment response from longitudinal 3D MRI. It matters because it makes clinical predictions inspectable and correctable rather than black-box.

entry.title: Correct codes for the wrong reasons? validating LLMs as measurement instruments for theoretical constructs

author.name: Manuel Pita

entry.summary: Argues that LLM-human coding agreement does not establish construct validity and proposes grain calibration, which decomposes constructs into clause-level components tested with extractive evidence and combined via explicit theory-derived rules. It targets valid use of LLMs as measurement instruments in social science.

entry.title: DriftGuard: Safety-Aware Multi-Monitor Detection and Selective Adaptation for Evolving Toxicity Moderation

author.name: Yuting Xin, Hanyu Cai, Binqi Shen, Lier Jin, Lan Hu

entry.summary: DriftGuard is a safety-aware adaptive toxicity moderation framework combining multi-monitor drift detection (identity-harm, uncertainty, false-negative risk) with selective model updating. It targets safety-relevant shifts missed by global distributional drift detectors.

entry.title: Labeling Training Data for Entity Matching Using Large Language Models

author.name: Aaron Steiner, Christian Bizer

entry.summary: Investigates knowledge distillation workflows where an LLM teacher labels entity-matching training pairs to train faster small student models, avoiding manual task-specific data. It examines whether LLM-labeled data can fully replace human-annotated training sets.

entry.title: Neural Procedural Memory: Empowering LLM Agents with Implicit Activation Steering

author.name: Chengfeng Zhao, Yuqiao Tan, Shizhu He, Yequan Wang, Jun Zhao, Kang Liu

entry.summary: Proposes Neural Procedural Memory (NPM), a training-free framework that encodes agent procedural memory as implicit activation steering rather than retrieved textual instructions. Aims to fix the text-action disconnect in RAG-based agent guidance.

entry.title: Can LLM-as-a-Judge Reliably Verify Rubrics in Agentic Scenarios?

author.name: Yangda Peng, Yunjia Qi, Hao Peng, Haotian Xia, Guanzhong He, Xintong Shi, Richeng Xuan, Songyuanyi Lu, Yixian Liu, Zhichao Hu, Yuhong Liu, Lei Hou, Bin Xu, Juanzi Li

entry.summary: Introduces RuVerBench, a benchmark of 2,458 instances probing whether LLM-as-a-Judge reliably verifies rubrics in agentic deep-research and coding scenarios. Conducts a systematic meta-evaluation of judge reliability on long, complex outputs.

entry.title: LatentRevise: Learning from Zero-Hit Reasoning

author.name: Yiqiu Guo, Xueting Han, Qi Jia, Guangtao Zhai, Jing Bai

entry.summary: Proposes LatentRevise, a first-order latent revision method that recovers RLVR training signal from zero-hit hard prompts by optimizing reasoning-prefix embeddings using failed rollouts anchored to gold answers. Targets the sampling frontier where correct trajectories are rarely sampled.

entry.title: Parametric Skills

author.name: Xuan Zhao, Haonan He, Qingyu Yang, Minglei Li, Jingqi Ye, Zelin Tan, Bo Wan, Peng Ye

entry.summary: Introduces ParametricSkills, which converts free-form textual skill recipes into model parameters at test time, enabling context-free skill exploitation. Aims to overcome models' difficulty locating and following key instructions in long-context agentic settings.

entry.title: Morphing into Hybrid Attention Models

author.name: Disen Lan, Jianbin Zheng, Yuxi Ren, Xin Xia, Xuanda Wang, Xuefeng Xiao, Xipeng Qiu, Yu Cheng

entry.summary: Formulates hybrid attention layer selection as a budget-constrained subset-optimization problem and proposes FlashMorph, which accounts for interdependent layer effects when converting Transformers to hybrid linear/full attention. Improves long-context efficiency over heuristic layer-selection methods.

entry.title: Data Provenance for Image Auto-Regressive Generation

author.name: Bihe Zhao, Louis Kerner, Michel Meintz, Tameem Bakr, Franziska Boenisch, Adam Dziedzic

entry.summary: This paper studies data provenance for image autoregressive models, showing that the next-token generation process leaves characteristic patterns enabling reliable attribution of generated images to their source model. It supports misinformation detection and content attribution.

entry.title: SIGNET: Motion-Level Knowledge Transfer for Cross-Language Sign Language Translation

author.name: Sobhan Asasi, Ozge Mercanoglu Sincan, Richard Bowden

entry.summary: SIGNET enables motion-level knowledge transfer for cross-language sign language translation without gloss annotations, leveraging the insight that pretrained models capture transferable motion-level visual patterns across sign languages despite grammatical and lexical differences. It improves scalability and cross-lingual transfer in SLT.

entry.title: Personalizing MLLMs via Reinforced Multimodal Reference Game

author.name: Deepayan Das, Davide Talon, Yiming Wang, Massimiliano Mancini, Elisa Ricci

entry.summary: This work proposes a Reinforced Reference Game to personalize multimodal LLMs, training them to produce accurate, discriminative descriptions of user-specific concepts free of distracting state and context details via reinforcement learning. It improves unique identification of personal concepts among visually similar items.

entry.title: When Does Synthetic CT Transfer? A Label-Free Donor/Host Diagnostic for Medical Vision-Language Model Routing on Real Lung CT

author.name: Fakrul Islam Tushar

entry.summary: This work proposes a label-free donor/host diagnostic to predict whether synthetic CT competence will transfer to real lung CT for medical vision-language model routing. It distinguishes donor-driven from host-driven competence across multiple VLMs and datasets with strong predictive correlations.

entry.title: MIRROR: Aligning Semantic Relations from Language to Image via Gromov--Wasserstein

author.name: Hong-Han Wang, Yuntao Wang, Hu Ding

entry.summary: MIRROR uses Gromov-Wasserstein optimal transport regularization to transfer relational structure from language to visual representations in MLLMs, addressing the failure to preserve inter-concept relationships across the modality gap. It targets a structural blind spot in projection-based alignment.

entry.title: Scenes as Objects, Not Primitives: Instance-Structured 3D Tokenization from Unposed Views

author.name: Mijin Yoo, In Cho, Subin Jeon, Jiwoo Lee, Eunbyung Park, Seon Joo Kim

entry.summary: This work proposes a feed-forward framework that decomposes a scene into instance-structured 3D token groups directly from unposed multi-view images, pairing instance tokens with anchor tokens decoded into Gaussians. It provides object-centric units for reconstruction, segmentation, and manipulation.

entry.title: Reliability-Prioritized Fine-Grained Generation in Multimodal Large
