entry.title: A3M: Adaptive, Adversarial and Multi-Objective Learning for Strategic Bidding in Repeated Auctions

author.name: Junhan Li, Yuxin Zhang, Haoran Wang, Minghao Chen

entry.summary: A3M is a deep reinforcement learning framework for strategic bidding in repeated multi-unit auctions with bandit feedback, integrating an actor-critic backbone, an opponent model for fictitious play against non-stationary adversaries, and a multi-objective reward. It moves beyond rigid explore-then-exploit schedules.

entry.title: ScAle: Attention Head Scaling as a Minimal Adapter for Spatial Reasoning in Vision Language Models

author.name: Rahul Chowdhury, Timothy A Rupprecht, Xuan Shen, Pu Zhao, Yanzhi Wang

entry.summary: ScAle is an ultra-lightweight adapter that learns a small set of scalar coefficients to modulate last-token attention and MLP activations in frozen VLMs, improving spatial reasoning without modifying pretrained weights. It builds on the observation that rescaling activations significantly affects performance. It matters for parameter-efficient enhancement of VLM spatial reasoning.

entry.title: Diagnosing and Mitigating Retrieval Bottlenecks in LLM-Based Cold-Start Recommendation

author.name: Zhe Dong (University of Maine at Presque Isle), Fang Qin (Stanford University), Manish Shah (Independent Researcher), Yicheng Wang (Independent Researcher)

entry.summary: This work tests the assumption that LLM rerankers help cold-start and long-tail recommendation, finding that in a positive-controlled regime calibrated LLM rerankers fail to consistently beat collaborative and content baselines, with retrieval coverage being the more severe bottleneck. It separates reranking quality from retrieval coverage. It matters for realistic assessment of LLMs in recommenders.

entry.title: Gravitational Duals from Equations of State II: Large Hierarchies and False Vacua

author.name: Raul Jimenez, David Mateos, Pavlos Protopapas, Pau Sol\'e-Vilar\'o, Pedro Taranc\'on-\'Alvarez, Pablo Tejerina-P\'erez

entry.summary: This paper extends Physics-Informed Neural Network reconstruction of holographic duals to regimes with large hierarchies and false vacua, recovering bulk scalar potentials from boundary thermodynamic data in settings with exotic RG flows and near-degenerate states. It matters for the gauge/gravity inverse problem in theoretical physics.

entry.title: Clinical Reasoning Graphs: Structured Evaluation of LLM Diagnostic Reasoning Reveals Competence Without Consistency

author.name: Nisarg A. Patel (University of California, San Francisco)

entry.summary: Introduces clinical reasoning graphs extracted from LLM diagnostic traces using a domain ontology, applied to 750 traces over 50 NEJM CPC cases. Finds LLMs reach competent diagnostic accuracy but lack consistent structured reasoning schemas across similar cases.

entry.title: CORTEX: High-Quality Cross-Domain Organization of Web-Scale Corpora through Ontological Corpus Graph

author.name: Chengtao Gan, Xiaoke Guo, Yushan Zhu, Zhaoyan Gong, Zhiqiang Liu, Songze Li, Huajun Chen, Wen Zhang

entry.summary: Presents CORTEX, a framework that organizes web-scale corpora into an Ontological Corpus Graph with quality-refined content, a lightweight ontology, and structured knowledge layers. Moves corpus construction from flat document filtering to structured knowledge organization for staged LLM training.

entry.title: CLEAR-MoE: Shared-Basis Expert Extraction from Frozen Vision Transformers via Calibration-Driven Layer Selection

author.name: Md Irtiza Hossain, Humaira Ayesha, Junaid Ahmed Sifat

entry.summary: CLEAR-MoE is a post-training pipeline that converts a frozen pretrained Vision Transformer into a sparse Mixture-of-Experts model without updating backbone weights, using layer scoring, SVD-based shared-basis decomposition, and lightweight cluster-supervised routers. It retains nearly all dense accuracy while introducing sparsity.

entry.title: SATB-VR: Training Few-Step Video Restoration Diffusion Model using SNR-Aware Trajectory Blending

author.name: Haoran Bai, Xiaoxu Chen, Xiaoyu Liu, Zongsheng Yue, Sibin Deng, Wangmeng Zuo, Ying Chen

entry.summary: SATB-VR is a few-step video restoration diffusion model that uses an auxiliary predictor to skip early low-SNR denoising steps and an SNR-Aware Trajectory Blending strategy to resolve train-inference discrepancy from joint training. It balances efficiency with fine texture recovery.

entry.title: Enhancing Part-Level Point Grounding for Any Open-Source MLLMs

author.name: Jin-Cheng Jhang, Fu-En Wang, Xin Yang, Nan Qiao, Lu Xia, Min Sun, Cheng-Hao Kuo

entry.summary: This method equips any open-source MLLM with accurate 2D part-level point grounding by leveraging the models' internal attention to synthesize grounding-aware queries, going beyond object-level grounding. It targets fine-grained tasks like robotic manipulation.

entry.title: DR-GS: Physically-Based Deformable and Relightable 2D Gaussians

author.name: Jiaxin Li, Tong Wu, Yi Wei, Tailin Wu, Li Zhang

entry.summary: DR-GS is a physically-based deformable and relightable 2D Gaussian framework that disentangles geometry, illumination, and material for inverse rendering. It addresses illumination being incorrectly baked into textures and enables post-reconstruction material editing under deformation.

entry.title: FiRe: Frequency Reparameterization as a Preconditioner for Periodic Implicit Neural Representations

author.name: Harinandan Shukla, Rajarshi Verma, Jitin Singla

entry.summary: FiRe reparameterizes per-neuron frequency in periodic implicit neural representations via a low-rank gating path, acting as an implicit preconditioner that improves optimization conditioning at initialization via NTK analysis. It accelerates convergence without changing activation functions.

entry.title: ReMAP-PET: Beyond Visual Understanding -- Learning Region-Guided Metabolic Alignment Semantics from Brain PET

author.name: Dasen Dai, Yanteng Zhang, Shuoqi Li, Yuxiang Wei, Hongjie Yu, Qingxin Zhang, Qizhen Lan, Jagath C. Rajapakse, Vince D. Calhoun

entry.summary: ReMAP-PET learns region-guided metabolic semantics from brain PET by supervising a 3D ResNet with standardized uptake value ratio profiles via joint regression and contrastive objectives, going beyond generic volumetric encoding. It achieves low SUVR error on neurodegenerative assessment tasks.

entry.title: Accurate Recognition of Pneumonia and COVID-19 by Geometric Shape Normalization of Lung Region using Automatic Landmark Detection and Piecewise Affine Warping

author.name: Salvador E. Ayala-Raggi, Rafael Alejandro Cruz-Ovando, Lauro Reyes-Cocoletzi, Aldrin Barreto-Flores

entry.summary: UniVAD v2 is a two-sided support-conditioned boundary construction framework for unified few-shot visual anomaly detection across categories, domains, and scenarios, capturing both local correspondences and global support-query relations. It adds abnormal-side evidence for deployment-specific tolerance.

entry.title: Latent-CURE for Breast Cancer Diagnosis

author.name: Weiyi Zhao, Xiaoyu Tan, Lu Gan, Liang Liu, Xihe Qiu

entry.summary: Latent-CURE is a breast ultrasound diagnostic framework using asymmetric weighted chain-of-thought reasoning in latent space to counter shortcut learning under epidemiological class imbalance. It forces sequential clinical-style inference to avoid bypassing rare malignant indicators.

entry.title: LETT-NeXt: A Lightweight RECIST-Guided Model for 3D CT Lesion Segmentation

author.name: Sebastian Aas, Elias Stenhede, Arian Ranjbar

entry.summary: LETT-NeXt is a lightweight RECIST-guided model for 3D CT lesion segmentation, encoding RECIST lines and endpoints as prompt channels with a compact MedNeXt-v2 encoder-decoder and adaptive zoom inference. It was developed for a CVPR 2026 pan-cancer segmentation competition, achieving 79.4 Dice.

entry.title: Human2Any: Human-to-Robot Transfer via Constraint-Aware Compositional Planning

author.name: Shuo Cheng, Chuye Zhang, Alfred Cueva, Caelan Garrett, Ajay Mandlekar, Danfei Xu

entry.summary: Human2Any learns reusable object-centric interaction priors from human videos (without real-world robot demonstrations in target contexts) by representing manipulation as object-object interaction motion, then composes them with robot-side feasibility reasoning and motion planning. It addresses embodiment mismatch and scene variation in human-to-robot transfer.

entry.title: Cross-Spectral Stereo Inertial Odometry

author.name: Seungsang Yun, Hyunsoo Jang, Tai Hyoung Rhee, Hyunho Song, Hyeonjae Gil, Ayoung Kim

entry.summary: Presents an asynchronous real-time cross-spectral visual-thermal-inertial odometry system that temporally decouples high-latency cross-spectral matching to provide robustness against correlated single-spectrum failures in degraded environments. It addresses the appearance gap between visible and thermal modalities.

entry.title: Legible Shared Autonomy: Implicit Communication of Robot Belief through Motion

author.name: Jinwei Liu, Pengfei Li, Shaofeng Chen, Tao Wang, Yun-Bo Zhao

entry.summary: Proposes legible shared autonomy that communicates the robot's inferred goal belief implicitly through motion, addressing the problem that ambiguous shortest-path assistance fails to reveal which goal the robot inferred. It targets assistive arm control for users with motor impairments.

entry.title: ToE: A Hierarchical and Explainable Claim Verification Framework with Dynamic Multi-source Evidence Retrieval and Aggregation

author.name: Zhaoqi Wang, Zijian Zhang, Kun Zheng, Zhen Li, Xin Li, Chunlei Li, Jiamou Liu

entry.summary: ToE (Tree of Evidence) is a hierarchical, explainable fact-checking framework modeling each claim as a dynamically expanding argument tree, combining RL-driven multi-source retrieval and evidence aggregation. Addresses AI-generated misinformation and retrieval poisoning.

entry.title: Lifted Causal Inference

author.name: Malte Luttermann, Tanya Braun, Ralf M\"oller, Marcel Gehrke

entry.summary: Extends lifted probabilistic inference to causal inference in relational domains, introducing parametric causal factor graphs with formal intervention semantics and a Lifted Causal Inference algorithm that speeds up causal effect computation. Maintains exact answers.

entry.title: Retroactive Advantage Correction: Closed-Form V-Trace Bias Correction for Delay-Aware RLHF

author.name: Arnav Raj

entry.summary: Retroactive Advantage Correction (RAC) addresses asynchronous reward signals in production RLHF by queuing pending slow completions and reinjecting them as clipped residuals into later optimizer steps, with provable unbiasedness conditions. Targets delayed verifiers and slow judge ensembles.

entry.title: HybridCodec: Modeling Discrete and Continuous Representations for Efficient Speech Language Models

author.name: Artem Ploujnikov, Francesco Verdini, Samir Sadok, Mirco Ravanelli

entry.summary: HybridCodec combines temporally compressed discrete tokens with dimensionality-reduced continuous residuals for efficient speech language models, using a hybrid Transformer with autoregressive discrete inference and non-autoregressive continuous prediction. Mitigates information loss from discretization.

entry.title: What Was That Again? Certified Robustness for Automatic Speech Recognition

author.name: Andrew C. Cullen, Neil Marchant, Jiani Xie, Paul Montague, Benjamin I. P. Rubinstein

entry.summary: Applies a certification-inspired dual-gate diagnostic pipeline to automatic speech recognition, using a Two-Sided Atomic Audit and Rank-Based Tournament to certify token existence and adversarial exclusion without oracle transcriptions. Decreases WER and improves recall under perturbations.

entry.title: Enhancing Numerical Prediction in LLMs via Smooth MMD Alignment

author.name: Zhuo Zuo, Li Yue, Wenhao Zheng, Chenpeng Wang, Xianggen Liu

entry.summary: Proposes Smooth Maximum Mean Discrepancy (SMMD), a training objective incorporating value-distance kernels over numeric tokens and graph-based smoothness to make LLM numeric predictions reflect the metric structure of values rather than treating numbers as unstructured categories. Improves numerical precision.

entry.title: NLL-Guided Full-Attention Layer Selection for Training-Free Sliding-Window Adaptation

author.name: Qiong Tang, Xiangkun Hu, Xiangyang Liu, Yiran Chen, Yunfan Shao

entry.summary: Proposes NLL-guided layer selection, a training-free method choosing which layers retain full attention in hybrid full/sliding-window models by measuring negative log-likelihood degradation on answer tokens. Achieves 64.6% accuracy on LongMemEval using only a quarter of full-attention layers.

entry.title: On design-unbiased algorithmic Machine Learning

author.name: Li-Chun Zhang, Siu-Ming Tam, Luis Sanguiao-Sande, Wesley Yung, Anders Holmberg

entry.summary: Studies conditions under which ML algorithms like kNN and random forest can produce design-unbiased predictions for finite populations, relevant to official statistics. Examines sampling, tuning, and out-of-sample evaluation for unbiasedness.

entry.title: On Surrogate Modeling of Static Response of AM Short-Fiber Thermoplastics Using Graph Neural Networks

author.name: Pharindra Pathak (Auburn University, Oakridge National Lab, NASA Glenn Research Center, Auburn University, Auburn University), Vipin Kumar (Auburn University, Oakridge National Lab, NASA Glenn Research Center, Auburn University, Auburn University), Trenton M. Ricks (Auburn University, Oakridge National Lab, NASA Glenn Research Center, Auburn University, Auburn University), Suhasini Gururaja (Auburn University, Oakridge National Lab, NASA Glenn Research Center, Auburn University, Auburn University), Siddhartha Srivastava (Auburn University, Oakridge National Lab, NASA Glenn Research Center, Auburn University, Auburn University)

entry.summary: A GNN surrogate model predicts the static mechanical response of additively manufactured short-fiber thermoplastics, capturing mesoscale fiber orientation, clustering, and porosity effects. It offers a tractable alternative to expensive finite element simulations.

entry.title: I-BBS: Coordinate-Free Inference of Latent Sub-Manifolds Using Random Distance Matrix Theory

author.name: Igor Halperin

entry.summary: Develops I-BBS, a coordinate-free method using random distance matrix theory (from the Bogomolny-Bohigas-Schmit spectrum) to identify a low-dimensional latent sub-manifold from a high-dimensional distance matrix alone, without accessing the ambient vector space. It works even when that space is partly observable or undefined.

entry.title: GLIP: Graph and LLM Joint Pretraining for Graph-Level Tasks

author.name: Haoxin Sun, Yiqing Lin, Yajun Huang, Chenhui Dong, Mingjun Li, Zhongzhi Zhang

entry.summary: Introduces GLIP, a joint pretraining framework combining graph neural networks and LLMs specifically for underexplored graph-level tasks, where most prior GNN-LLM work focuses on node and edge level. It involves LLMs in graph pretraining to address label scarcity.

entry.title: Data-Driven Energy-Based Learning via Gibbs Measures on Hierarchical Structures

author.name: L. U. Abdullaev, F. Herrera, U. A. Rozikov, M. V. Velasco

entry.summary: Introduces a data-driven probabilistic framework treating empirical loss as an interaction potential to define energy-based Gibbs measures on hierarchical structures, yielding a family of equilibrium learning states rather than a single optimum. It derives fixed-point equations connecting loss landscapes to probabilistic learning states.

entry.title: Towards Continual Motion-Language Agents: LoRA Variants for Incremental Motion Understanding and Generation

author.name: Bertram Taetz, Hugo Albuquerque Cosme da Silva, Gabriele Bleser-Taetz

entry.summary: Investigates continual learning for bidirectional motion-language agents that both understand (motion-to-text) and generate (text-to-motion) human movement without catastrophic forgetting, introducing LoRA variants to mitigate inter-task interference on a frozen LLM backbone. It studies the stability-plasticity trade-off under sequential task exposure.

entry.title: Scalar Representations of Neural Network Training Dynamics

author.name: Pedro Jim\'enez-Gonz\'alez, Miguel C. Soriano, Lucas Lacasa

entry.summary: Treats neural network training trajectories as temporal networks and applies scalar-embedding strategies to obtain a low-dimensional representation of high-dimensional training dynamics. Using an MLP on MNIST, it shows the embedding preserves key dynamical features including sensitivity to initial conditions.

entry.title: Spectral Perturbation of the Empirical Fisher Information Matrix under Weight Quantization

author.name: Rahid Zahid Alekberli, Hikmat Karimov

entry.summary: This paper studies spectral perturbation of the empirical Fisher Information Matrix under input distribution shift and weight quantization, proving conditions under which out-of-distribution inputs elevate the top eigenvalue and deriving a directional eigenvalue perturbation bound. It connects curvature geometry to quantization effects.

entry.title: Selective Memory Retention for Long-Horizon LLM Agents

author.name: Pranath Reddy

entry.summary: TraceRetain is a lightweight bounded-memory framework for frozen LLM agents that scores and evicts memory entries by interpretable features. The study finds clean benchmarks like ALFWorld do not naturally exhibit the memory pollution that retention policies target, while a noisy-write stress test does. It matters for understanding when memory management actually helps agents.

entry.title: Benchmarking Geospatial Foundation Models for Agriculture Applications

author.name: Zhuocheng Shang, Sanmay Das, Ahmed Eldawy

entry.summary: This benchmark systematically tests the geographic transferability of geospatial foundation models (Prithvi, SpectralGPT, SatMAE) on multi-temporal crop segmentation and change detection across four U.S. states with region-disjoint splits. All three degrade sharply under regional distribution shift, predicting only common crops. It matters for honest assessment of remote-sensing foundation models in agriculture.

entry.title: Rethinking Generative Reconstruction Attacks against Graph Neural Network Models

author.name: Adebayo Keji, Sayanton Dibbo

entry.summary: This paper introduces two novel graph inversion attacks against GNNs—graph-label conditioned and embedding-label conditioned—that reconstruct sensitive training graph data from model predictions and intermediate representations. It exposes privacy vulnerabilities in GNNs. It matters for graph-data privacy and security.

entry.title: First-Order Temporal Logic Tensor Networks

author.name: Luca Boscarato, Ivan Donadello, Alessandro Artale, Marco Montali, Fabrizio Maria Maggi

entry.summary: FOT-LTN extends Logic Tensor Networks to first-order linear temporal logic, enabling neuro-symbolic reasoning over objects whose properties and relations change over time with fuzzy real-valued semantics. It fills a gap where temporal neuro-symbolic work was limited to propositional or interval logics. It matters for temporal neuro-symbolic AI.

entry.title: Few-Shot Domain Incremental Learning via Continual Vision-Language Consolidation

author.name: Naeem Paeedeh, Mahardhika Pratama, Wolfgang Mayer, Mukesh Prasad, Weiping Ding, Yew-Soon Ong

entry.summary: This paper introduces few-shot domain incremental learning and proposes Continual Vision-Language Consolidation, using latent space reservation in the base domain with dual coalescent projection as parameter-efficient fine-tuning to handle extreme data scarcity across new domains. It matters for continual adaptation under data shortages.

entry.title: CAN We Trust Your Results? A Cross-Dataset Study of Automotive IDS Evaluation

author.name: Beatrix Koltai, Gergely Acs, Andras Gazdag

entry.summary: Introduces a benchmarking framework for consistent cross-dataset evaluation of automotive CAN-bus intrusion detection systems, exposing that reported performance often depends on dataset-specific quirks. It improves reproducibility in vehicle network security.

entry.title: EVLA: An Electro-Aware Multimodal Assistant for Physically-Grounded Driving Reasoning and Control

author.name: Yuxin Liu, Zihan Chen, Haoyu Wang, Mingxuan Zhang, Ruijie Lin, Siyuan Zhao

entry.summary: EVLA is an electro-aware vision-language driving assistant that fuses visual, textual, and electrified-powertrain state (motor torque, battery SOC) into a shared latent with energy-aware reasoning. It aims to make driving decisions physically grounded in real-time vehicle dynamics.

entry.title: BERTomelo: Your Portuguese Encoder Best Friend

author.name: Renn\^e Ruan Alves Oliveira, Gustavo Cordeiro Galv\~ao Van Erven, Lu\'is Paulo Faina Garcia

entry.summary: BERTomelo is a next-generation monolingual Portuguese encoder pretrained from scratch using the ModernBERT architecture to overcome scalability and efficiency limits of prior Portuguese models. It targets deep contextual understanding for Portuguese NLP tasks.

entry.title: Two-Stage Prompt Optimization for Few-Shot Relation Extraction: From Reasoning-Guided Search to Gradient-Guided Refinement

author.name: Aunabil Chakma, Mihai Surdeanu, Eduardo Blanco

entry.summary: Proposes a two-stage prompt optimization framework combining reasoning-based search with gradient-guided local refinement (GradPO) for few-shot relation extraction with smaller models. Reports state-of-the-art on FS-TACRED with Qwen3-4B.

entry.title: ARKD: Adaptive Reinforcement Learning-Guided Bidirectional KL Divergence Distillation for Text Generation

author.name: Zilong Liu, Xuewen Zhang, Jinrui Xing, Juyi Qiao, Huiyong Wang, Junming Jiao

entry.summary: Presents ARKD, which uses a policy network to dynamically weight forward and reverse KL divergence during LLM knowledge distillation, balancing primary distribution fitting with long-tail modeling. Guided by immediate reward signals for dual alignment.

entry.title: Information Dynamics of Language Communication

author.name: Leonardo S. Goodall, Andrea I. Luppi, Pedro A. M. Mediano

entry.summary: Introduces an information-theoretic framework using LLMs as probabilistic estimators to quantify directed semantic transfer entropy and partial information decomposition between conversational interlocutors. Detects redundant, unique, and synergistic semantic contributions in communication.

entry.title: LEDGER: Scaling Agentic Document Editing with Dependency-aware Graph Retrieval

author.name: Mike Hang Wang, Utkarsh Garg, Reza Davari, Huitian Jiao, Hao Cheng, Baolin Peng, Tao Ge, Si-Qing Chen

entry.summary: Introduces LEDGER for agentic editing of long structured documents, building a lightweight dependency graph of hierarchy, references, and semantic relations so graph-guided retrieval selects only necessary context. Improves consistency across six SOTA models on a 1.9k-case benchmark.

entry.title: GPTNT: Benchmarking Real-Time Collaboration Between Multimodal Agents on Keep Talking And Nobody Explodes

author.name: Amit Parekh, Sabrina McCallum, Kareem Al-Hasan, Malvina Nikandrou, Alessandro Suglia, Ioannis Konstas

entry.summary: Introduces GPTNT, a benchmark built on the cooperative game Keep Talking and Nobody Explodes where two multimodal agents with information asymmetry must coordinate under time pressure to defuse bombs. Studies collaboration conditions usually examined in isolation.

entry.title: Animation2Code: Evaluating Temporal Visual Reasoning in Video-to-Code Generation

author.name: Anya Ji, Abhijith Varma Mudunuri, David M. Chan, Alane Suhr

entry.summary: Introduces Animation2Code, a benchmark of 1,069 web-animation videos paired with HTML/CSS/JS to evaluate whether VLMs can reconstruct executable animation code from motion. Proposes appearance and temporal similarity metrics to disentangle visual fidelity from temporal alignment.

entry.title: PolicyGuard: A Dialogue-Grounded Sub-Agent Verifier for Policy Adherence in LLM Agents

author.name: Seongjae Kang, Taehyung Yu, Sung Ju Hwang

entry.summary: Argues policy adherence in LLM agents is broader than blocking actions and proposes PolicyGuard, a dialogue-grounded sub-agent verifier that uses full conversation context, self-reasoning over policy, and conversation-specific remediation. Targets multi-turn workflows needing confirmations and prerequisite reads.

entry.title: The Complexity Ceiling Benchmark: A Multi-Domain Evaluation of Sequential Reasoning Under Depth Scaling

author.name: Shubh Chapra, Dhruv Kumar, Murari Mandal, Yash Sinha

entry.summary: Introduces the Complexity Ceiling Benchmark measuring how reasoning decays with sequential depth across spatial state-tracking, symbolic pointer manipulation, and transitive relational inference. Finds geometric per-step decay with widely separated domain ceilings, with relational inference collapsing by just five steps.

entry.title: Know Before You Fetch: Calibrated Retrieval-Budget Allocation for Retrieval-Augmented Generation

author.name: Zhe Dong (University of Maine at Presque Isle), Fang Qin (Stanford University), Manish Shah (Independent Researcher), Yicheng Wang (Independent Researcher)

entry.summary: This work reframes adaptive RAG as calibrated retrieval-budget allocation, deciding per query whether to answer closed-book, retrieve compact or full context, or abstain, by calibrating uncertainty signals into correctness probabilities. It provides a probability interface for graded context selection and selective abstention.

entry.title: SatSplat: Geometrically-Accurate Gaussian Splatting for Satellite Imagery

author.name: Shuang Song, Jiyong Kim, Rongjun Qin

entry.summary: SatSplat adapts 2D Gaussian Splatting to satellite photogrammetry with an affine camera approximation and in-splat camera refinement, aiming for geometrically accurate, efficient 3D reconstruction robust to multi-date illumination changes. It is presented as the first 2DGS adaptation to satellite imagery.

entry.title: LogiCo: A Unified Framework for Logical and Structural Anomaly Detection

author.name: Ximiao Zhang, Min Xu, Xiuzhuang Zhou

entry.summary: LogiCo is a unified framework for both logical and structural anomaly detection using component-level feature reconstruction to capture inter-component logical constraints rather than explicit global semantic modeling. It aims to overcome the trade-off where structural methods miss logical anomalies and vice versa.

entry.title: FreqOrtho-SR: Frequency-Guided Orthogonal Expert Learning for Real-World Image Super-Resolution

author.name: Minh Son Hoang, Dinh Phu Tran, Quyen Nguyen Duc, Dam Hoang Phuong, Daeyoung Kim

entry.summary: FreqOrtho-SR is a real-world image super-resolution method using a frequency-guided mixture of LoRA experts routed by FFT-based degradation features and orthogonal expert learning to genuinely expand perceptual capacity beyond the pixel subspace. It addresses fidelity-quality balancing and adaptation to diverse degradations.

entry.title: A Physics-Grounded Benchmark for Multi-Agent Dynamics in World Models

author.name: Nuo Chen, Lulin Liu, Zihao Li, Ziyao Zeng, Zihao Zhu, Wenyan Cong, Junyuan Hong, Yunhao Yang, Zhengzhong Tu, Yan Wang, Boris Ivanovic, Marco Pavone, Zhangyang Wang, Yang Zhou, Zhiwen Fan

entry.summary: This work introduces a training-free transition-aware best-of-N sampling scheme for chest X-ray report generation that explicitly encodes the change between prior and current exams via set-to-set directional vectors. It targets the longitudinal change reporting central to radiology practice.

entry.title: ASTAD: Asymmetric Style Transfer for Synthetic-to-Real Adaptation in Autonomous Driving

author.name: Dingyi Yao, Xinqi Zhang, Lihui Peng, Jianming Hu, Danya Yao, Yi Zhang

entry.summary: ASTAD introduces an asymmetric style-transfer task for synthetic-to-real adaptation in autonomous driving, where synthetic data has perfect labels but real reference images lack them. It avoids the symmetric semantic guidance assumption that incurs annotation costs or misalignment.

entry.title: Occlusion-Robust Multi-Object Decoupling for Physics-Based Interaction

author.name: Xin Dong, Wenfeng Deng, Yansong Tang

entry.summary: This work proposes a mask-free method for multi-object 3D reconstruction from sparse occluded views, reformulating object decoupling as a sparse-view reconstruction problem on 3D Gaussian Splatting. It enables physically plausible interaction via Material Point Method simulation.

entry.title: SAD-GS: Learning Reliable 3D Semantic Gaussian Fields via Dynamic Geo-Semantic Anchoring

author.name: Yufei Zhang, Chenlu Zhan, Gaoang Wang, Hongwei Wang

entry.summary: SAD-GS learns reliable 3D semantic Gaussian fields by addressing unreliable 2D supervision through dynamic geo-semantic anchoring, distilling per-view embeddings into consensus text anchors. It mitigates semantic identity drift and boundary leakage in open-vocabulary 3D scene understanding.

entry.title: Resonant Brane Splatting for Arbitrary-Scale Super-Resolution

author.name: Giulio Federico, Giuseppe Amato, Claudio Gennaro, Fabio Carrara, Marco Di Benedetto

entry.summary: Resonant Brane Splatting replaces flat Gaussians with expressive Brane primitives that emit spatially varying colors to model local contrast and textures within a single footprint, accelerating arbitrary-scale super-resolution. It avoids the rasterization bottleneck of overlapping splats.

entry.title: From Phase to Phenomenon: Self-Supervised Learning of Subsurface Scattering with Minimal Phase-shift Inputs

author.name: Arjun Majumdar, Raphael Braun, Andreas Engelhardt, Hendrik PA. Lensch

entry.summary: This work presents a self-supervised pretraining framework for learning subsurface scattering light-transport representations from only eight high-frequency phase-shift profilometry images per view. A tailored augmentation strategy outperforms ImageNet-style augmentations and transfers to relighting tasks.

entry.title: CellDETR: A Detection-Guided Framework for Scalable Cell Representation Learning from Histopathology Images

author.name: Shikang Zhang, Guojun Li, Yicong Mao, Chulin Sha

entry.summary: CellDETR is a detection-guided framework built on Deformable DETR for scalable cell-level representation learning from histopathology whole-slide images, with location feature decoupling and box-constrained attention. It outperforms prior methods on supervised cell classification on PanNuke.

entry.title: Rank-Aware Hyperbolic Alignment for Vision-Language Dataset Distillation

author.name: Jongoh Jeong, Sun-Kyung Lee, Kuk-Jin Yoon

entry.summary: This work proposes rank-aware hyperbolic alignment for vision-language dataset distillation, controlling dominant alignment capacity given rank-deficient image-text correlation rather than enforcing full-dimensional Euclidean alignment. It compresses paired datasets for efficient contrastive model training.

entry.title: Progressive Self-Supervised Learning with Individualized Community Assignment for Brain Network Analysis

author.name: Hairui Chen, Yanwu Yang, Jianfeng Cao, Hanyang Peng, Chenfei Ye, Ting Ma

entry.summary: BrainPICM is a self-supervised framework for brain network analysis using progressive individualized community-aware masking, formulating ROI-to-community mapping as unbalanced optimal transport with confidence-guided curriculum masking. It captures subject-specific functional organization that generic masking ignores.

entry.title: AerialMetric: Benchmarking and Adapting UAV Monocular Metric Depth Estimation in the Real World

author.name: Zhongqiang Song, Guanying Chen, Yuqi Zhang, Yin Zou, Chuanyu Fu, Zhiyuan Yuan, Chuan Huang, Shuguang Cui, Xiaochun Cao

entry.summary: AerialMetric is a benchmark dataset for monocular metric depth estimation under UAV aerial viewpoints, comprising four complementary subsets spanning photogrammetry, controlled acquisition, synthetic scenes, and in-the-wild imagery. It addresses the domain gap of models trained on ground-level data.

entry.title: TopoAgent: An Agentic Framework for Automated Topology Learning in Medical Imaging

author.name: Guangyu Meng, Pengfei Gu, Xueyang Li, Yiyu Shi, Erin Wolf Chambers, Danny Z. Chen

entry.summary: TopoAgent is described as the first LLM-based agentic framework that automatically selects the most suitable topological descriptors for converting persistence diagrams or images into feature vectors in medical imaging. It addresses reliance on fixed default descriptors in topological data analysis.

entry.title: Graph-GSReg: Leveraging 3D Scene Graphs for Gaussian Splatting Registration

author.name: Jaewon Lee, Mangyu Kong, Euntai Kim

entry.summary: Graph-GSReg reformulates 3D Gaussian Splatting registration as a graph registration problem by constructing a 3D scene graph from a 3DGS and its rendered images. It avoids learning-based dataset training and expensive image-based refinement for merging multiple Gaussian scenes.

entry.title: Robust Trajectory Distillation: Hybrid Reweighting Meets Teacher-Inspired Targets

author.name: Kaifeng Chen, Lechao Cheng, Jiyang Li, Shengeng Tang, Fan Zhang, Yantao Pan, Yaxiong Wang, Tuanrui Hui, Zhun Zhong

entry.summary: A trajectory-based dataset distillation framework that suppresses label noise while preserving transferable knowledge, avoiding relabeling or clean anchor sets. It combines hybrid reweighting with teacher-inspired targets to keep distilled subsets robust under noisy supervision.

entry.title: Traffic-CBM: A Structurally Interpretable Multimodal Framework for Encrypted Traffic Classification

author.name: Honglei Jin, Wenshuo Chen, Shaofeng Liang, Haozhe Jia, Menshuo Zhao, Shuxu Jin, Songning Lai, Yutao Yue

entry.summary: Traffic-CBM is a structurally interpretable multimodal framework for encrypted traffic classification that organizes flow statistics, packet sequences, and byte-level features into a hierarchical concept space of scalar evidence summaries. It aims to make classification decisions transparent rather than opaque.

entry.title: Scene-aware Prediction of Diverse Human Movement Goals

author.name: Qiaoyue Yang, Amadeus Weber, Magnus Jung, Ayoub AI-Hamadi, Sven Wachsmuth

entry.summary: Proposes a scene-aware generative method for predicting diverse human movement goals using RGB scene context and human cues, addressing the stochasticity of long-term human trajectory and motion prediction. It avoids reliance on explicit scene semantic knowledge required by prior methods.

entry.title: Goku: A Million-Scale Universal Dataset and Benchmark for Instruction-Based Video Editing

author.name: Sen Liang, Cong Wang, Zhentao Yu, Fengbin Guan, Zhengguang Zhou, Teng Hu, Youliang Zhang, Yuan Zhou, Xin Li, Qinglin Lu, Zhibo Chen

entry.summary: Goku is a 2-million-pair instruction-based video editing dataset and benchmark that extends beyond single-task appearance edits to multi-task and structural manipulations like precise subject motion control. It includes a decomposition-based data synthesis pipeline and progressive filtering for reliability.

entry.title: ReactiveBFM: Reactive Closed-Loop Motion Planning Towards Universal Humanoid Whole-Body Control

author.name: Xiao Chen, Weishuai Zeng, Xiaojie Niu, Zirui Wang, Jianan Li, Huayi Wang, Furui Xu, Jiahe Chen, Weixiang Zhong, Lihe Ding, Kailin Li, Jiangmiao Pang, Tai Wang, Tianfan Xue, Jingbo Wang

entry.summary: ReactiveBFM is a real-time closed-loop planning-control framework for humanoid whole-body control that mitigates cumulative exposure bias via a scheduled prefix sampling curriculum, forcing the generative planner to learn error-recovery from imperfect physical states. It enables reactive coordination beyond replaying pre-defined reference motions.

entry.title: The Human Creativity Benchmark

author.name: Aspen Hopkins, Allison Nulty, Alexandria Minetti, Anoop Pakki, Angad Singh

entry.summary: This paper analyzes black-box forgery attacks on semantic watermarks embedded in diffusion model initial noise through a rate-distortion lens, identifying an irreducible distortion floor caused by proxy-target model mismatch. It characterizes the distortion as structured geometric deviations on the latent manifold.

entry.title: You Only Touch Once: 6-DoF Object Pose Estimation from Single Tactile Contact

author.name: Pengfei Ye, Yuxiang Ma, Haonan Chen, Guangming Wang, Yixiong Jing, Brian Sheil, Yilun Du, Edward Adelson

entry.summary: YOTO is a tactile-only system that recovers full 6-DoF object pose from a single pair of simultaneous contacts without contact history, representing each contact as a local 3D point cloud, localizing it via a coarse-to-fine network, and solving pose with a closed-form normal-aware SVD. It works where vision fails under occlusion, poor lighting, and reflective or transparent surfaces.

entry.title: SPACE: Swarm Pheromone Fields for Adaptive Collision-Aware Exploration

author.name: Haohua Que, Haojia Gao, Mingkai Liu, Qian Zhang, Jiajun Sun, Fei Qiao

entry.summary: SPACE uses ant-inspired pheromone fields to coordinate decentralized exploration of large robot swarms, balancing safety and efficiency by managing congestion at doorways and dense traffic. It is evaluated on realistic building floorplans.

entry.title: Understanding LLM Intervention Explanations in Multi-Party Human-Robot Interaction

author.name: Micol Spitale, Massimiliano Nigro, Emily Cross

entry.summary: This study investigates how LLM-based orchestrators decide when and why to intervene in multi-party human-robot group conversations, using a 24-group between-subjects user study comparing homogeneous and heterogeneous robot roles. It examines intervention explanations in social robotics.

entry.title: TACO: A Test and Check Framework for Robust Pose Graph Optimization

author.name: Emilio Olivastri, Alberto Pretto, Tobias Fischer

entry.summary: TACO is a robust pose graph optimization framework that filters outliers from incorrect place-recognition associations by incrementally finding an approximation to the maximally consistent measurement set, rather than explicitly classifying inliers/outliers. It improves SLAM trajectory quality under perceptual aliasing.

entry.title: Sphere-VIO: Fast and Robust Visual-Inertial Odometry via Unified Spherical Representation for Heterogeneous Multi-Camera Systems

author.name: Yueteng Yang, Yusen Xie, Hao Wei, Qianhao Wang, Boyu Zhou, Fei Gao, Jun Ma, Jinni Zhou

entry.summary: Sphere-VIO is a lightweight filter-based visual-inertial odometry framework using a unified spherical representation to support heterogeneous multi-camera systems with cross-camera feature tracking and stable depth estimation. It addresses the lack of unified compatibility in existing fixed-setup VIO algorithms.

entry.title: RoamFlow: Reinforcement-Aligned One-Step Action MeanFlow Policy for Image-Goal Navigation

author.name: Zixuan Zhang, Yuqi Chen, Junjie Gao, Siyuan Song, Yongzhou Pan, Beichen Wang, Mir Feroskhan

entry.summary: Proposes a message-passing algorithm for distributed collaborative localization that unifies Gaussian belief propagation with mean-field approximation and uses a normalizing-flow-based learnable gradient estimator for non-conjugate nonlinear terms. End-to-end training tunes the flow parameters.

entry.title: AERIS: Aerial-Edge Role-Driven Intelligence at Runtime via Orchestrated Language-Model Swarm

author.name: Jiabin Lou, Haopeng Wang, Xinyu Liu, Yu Zhang, Rongye Shi, Wenjun Wu

entry.summary: AERIS is an edge deployment framework that organizes small language models with lightweight perception and control modules into runtime-instantiable roles for aerial platforms, dynamically rebinding them across executors under heartbeat-constrained scheduling. It enables long-horizon instruction decomposition via attention-subgoal alignment.

entry.title: Self-supervised Geometry Reasoning for LiDAR Simultaneous Localization and Mapping

author.name: Jiwoo Kim, Jinwoo Lee, Woojae Shin, Giseop Kim, Hyondong Oh

entry.summary: Proposes a self-supervised framework that learns explicit symbolic local geometry representations (per-point Gaussian covariances) to recursively improve LiDAR SLAM, addressing noisy hand-crafted geometry estimates in sparse or low-resolution point clouds. It works without dense geometry labels.

entry.title: Multivariate Varying-Coefficient BART with Graphical Horseshoe Priors

author.name: Soham Ghosh, Sameer K. Deshpande

entry.summary: Develops multiVCBART, a multivariate varying-coefficient Bayesian additive regression tree framework that jointly models flexible outcome-specific nonlinear coefficients and scientifically meaningful residual dependence among related outcomes, using graphical horseshoe priors. It overcomes restrictive tree-sharing or oversimplified mean structures in existing methods.

entry.title: Import AI 463: Self-improving robots; a 10k Chinese GPU cluster; and an elegiac essay for the human era

author.name: Jack Clark

entry.summary: An issue of Jack Clark's Import AI newsletter highlighting NVIDIA's ENPIRE framework that gives physical robots an autonomous experiment-execute-evolve loop akin to AI agents, plus coverage of a 10k Chinese GPU cluster and an essay on the human era. It curates and contextualizes recent AI developments. The piece is high-quality research journalism.

entry.title: JD Oxygen AI Item Center (Oxygen AIIC) V1: An Industrial-Scale LLM/VLM-Centric Solution for Item Understanding, Management, and Applications

author.name: Oxygen AIIC, Chan Long, Chao Liu, Chaofan Chen, Chaohui Dong, Chunyuan Guo, Danping Liu, Debin Liu, Deping Xiang, Fulai Xu, Guangyue Liu, Hao Li, Huichun Hu, Jian Yang, Jianan Wang, Jianbo Zhao, Jiaoyang Li, Jiaxing Wang, Jinglong Li, Jinjin Guo, Jun Fang, Jun Liu, Kai Zhou, Li Wang, Lili Gao, Liying Chen, Luning Yang, Mengdi Zhou, Pengzhang Liu, Qi Lv, Qianyun Wang, Qixia Jiang, Ruyue Li, Shimu Liang, Shuxing Wang, Sijie Zhang, Siqi Li, Tianhao Gao, Wang Ke, Weihu Huang, Wencan Lai, Wenjie Zhang, Xiaohui Zhang, Xiaojing Dong, Ya Liu, Yifeng Zhang, Yixiang Wang, Yongtai Zhang, Yongyi Liao, Zhaoru Chen, Zhen Chen, Zhiyong Ma, Zhiyuan Liu, Zhongwei Liu, Ziyan Xing

entry.summary: Describes JD's Oxygen AI Item Center, an industrial-scale LLM/VLM platform for e-commerce item knowledge production and management across tens of billions of SKUs. Built on ontology engineering and addresses fast-emerging concepts at massive scale.

entry.title: Speculative Refinement: A Hybrid Autoregressive Diffusion Decoding Strategy and Its Behavior Across Benchmarks

author.name: Aditi Gupta, Neel Mishra, Kushagra Trivedi, Pawan Kumar

entry.summary: SpecRef is a training-free hybrid decoding method warm-starting a masked diffusion language model from an autoregressive draft via entropy-guided masking, evaluated across six benchmarks. Surfaces findings about how evaluation protocols conflate structural and logical correctness.

entry.title: CBD: API-Only LLM Black-Box Unlearning through Controlled Behavioral Divergence

author.name: Zhiqiang Xie, Yijing Lin, Zhipeng Gao, Dong In Kim

entry.summary: CBD enables API-only black-box LLM unlearning through controlled behavioral divergence, removing the influence of undesired data without access to parameters or logits while preserving utility on similar retained data. Targets edge-device API-served LLMs.

entry.title: Flexformer: Flexible Linear Transformer with Learnable Attention Kernel

author.name: Haoran Zhang, Feng Zhou

entry.summary: Flexformer is a flexible linear Transformer that learns attention kernels in a fully data-driven manner by treating spectral frequencies of random Fourier features as trainable parameters, with stationary and nonstationary variants. Improves expressiveness over fixed-kernel linear attention while keeping linear complexity.

entry.title: RS-Diffuser: Risk-Sensitive Diffusion Planning with Distributional Value Guidance

author.name: Shiqiang Gong

entry.summary: RS-Diffuser is a risk-sensitive offline reinforcement learning diffusion planner combining diffusion-based trajectory generation with distributional value critics to account for rare catastrophic outcomes that risk-neutral diffusion planners overlook. Targets safety-critical offline RL.

entry.title: Machine-learnable Sets

author.name: Veit Elser, Manish Krishan Lal

entry.summary: Proposes a formal definition of machine-learnable discrete sets based on bounded-complexity Boolean autoencoders, where elements are easily recognized, generated, and learned. Demonstrated on Rorschach-like patterns and wilder sets.

entry.title: AMR: Adaptive Modality Routing for Multimodal Polyglot Speaker Identification

author.name: Chuxiao Zuo, Yao Zhu, Minqiang Xu, Manhong Wang, Yunke Zhang, Fei Huang

entry.summary: AMR is an adaptive modality routing module for multimodal polyglot speaker identification that assesses per-sample input quality and dynamically fuses modalities to handle missing modalities and language mismatch. Designed for the POLY-SIM 2026 challenge.

entry.title: Atompack: A Storage and Distribution Layer for Read-Heavy Atomistic ML Training Datasets

author.name: Ali Ramlaoui, Daniel T. Speckhard, Sagar Pal, Fragkiskos D. Malliaros, Alexandre Duval, Victor Schmidt

entry.summary: Presents Atompack, an append-oriented storage format and distribution layer optimized for the read-heavy, shuffle-intensive workload of atomistic ML training datasets, distinct from interactive scientific data curation. It efficiently appends records then commits an immutable index for high random-indexed throughput.

entry.title: Structure-Preserving Document Translation via Multi-Stage LLM Pipeline: A Case Study in Marathi

author.name: Manasi Waghe, Danish Chandargi, Mohammad Aamir Rayyan, Raviraj Joshi, A. R. Deshpande

entry.summary: This paper presents a structure-preserving multi-stage LLM pipeline for translating Marathi government documents to English while maintaining layout fidelity and domain terminology. It integrates layout-aware OCR with translation to address accessibility barriers in regional-language official documents.

entry.title: Two kinds of robustness are not the same: disentangling fault tolerance and low-SNR robustness in multi-domain event detection on real data

author.name: Isao Kurosawa

entry.summary: This paper disentangles two conflated notions of robustness—fault tolerance under sensor failure and robustness to low-SNR signals—in multi-domain event detection on real data from seismic, DAS, and industrial vibration sources. It argues architectural complexity is often wrongly credited with robustness. It matters for honest evaluation of detector reliability.

entry.title: How Far Do On-Prem Open LLMs Get on Text-to-SQL? A Cross-Family Size x Technique Frontier on BIRD

author.name: Vladimir Beskorovainyi

entry.summary: This reproducible benchmark evaluates on-premises open-weight LLMs (Qwen2.5-Coder, CodeLlama, Llama-3.x) on the BIRD Text-to-SQL split under a matched protocol, ablating schema linking, self-correction, and self-consistency with paired McNemar tests. Key finding: generation matters more than raw size. It matters for organizations needing private Text-to-SQL.

entry.title: Physically-Constrained Harmonic Separation for Robust Heart and Respiratory Rate Estimation from Wrist Photoplethysmography

author.name: Nouhaila Fraihi, Ouassim Karrakchou, Mounir Ghogho

entry.summary: PCHS frames heart-rate and respiratory-rate estimation from wrist PPG as an analysis-by-synthesis harmonic-separation problem where accelerometer signals condition artifact separation rather than directly regressing vitals. It adds physiological interpretability and identifiable structure lacking in unconstrained deep learning. It matters for robust wearable vital-sign monitoring under motion.

entry.title: DistilledGemma: Balanced Efficiency-Accuracy for Person-Place Relation Extraction from Multilingual Historical Articles

author.name: Youssef Aboelwafa, Ahmed Samir, Nagwa Elmakky, Marwan Torki

entry.summary: DistilledGemma is a three-stage knowledge-distillation pipeline for person-place relation extraction from multilingual historical newspapers, distilling chain-of-thought traces from a Gemma teacher into an efficient student. It balances accuracy and computational cost for the HIPE-2026 shared task.

entry.title: LUMEN: Cost-Transparent Multi-Agent Pipeline for Automated Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis

author.name: Yen-Hsun Huang (Department of Education, Taipei Veterans General Hospital, Taipei, Taiwan), Yu-Shiou Lin (Department of Psychiatry, Taipei Veterans General Hospital, Taipei, Taiwan)

entry.summary: Presents LUMEN, an open-source 11-agent pipeline automating six systematic-review and meta-analysis phases with deliberate model routing, and uniquely reports end-to-end cost breakdowns. Quantifies the cost-quality trade-off of architectural choices for evidence synthesis.

entry.title: Enhancing Layer Interaction Using Key-Correlated Layer Attention

author.name: Jianlong Xiong, ChuanBo Xie, Le Yu, Quansong He, Tao He

entry.summary: Key-Correlated Layer Attention (KCLA) enhances inter-layer interactions in deep networks with linear complexity, motivated by the observation that Key representations across layers are highly cosine-similar. It addresses the quadratic cost of standard layer attention while improving long-range cross-layer dependency modeling.

entry.title: CCRC: A Change-Aware Captioning and Reasoning Chain for Image Change Captioning and Segmentation

author.name: Jinhong Hu, Xiaoping Wang, Shuyin Huang, Guojin Zhong, Kaitai Liu, Kai Lu

entry.summary: CCRC introduces Image Change Captioning and Segmentation as a new joint task and proposes a dual-chain framework decoupling change description (chain-of-change-captioning) from pixel-level segmentation, with change-aware attention modules. It adds spatial grounding to traditional image change captioning.

entry.title: From Fog Chamber to Aircraft Window: Pixel-Registered Imaging and Synthetic Fine-Tuning Enable Cross-Domain Defogging

author.name: Alexander Ingold, Sabina D. Menon, Manya Yellepeddy, Alec Ikei, John D. Hodges, Jordan Baker, Syed N. Qadri, Rajesh Menon

entry.summary: This work builds a deep defogging pipeline pretrained on controlled laboratory fog and fine-tuned with domain-randomized synthetic fog, demonstrating zero-shot cross-domain generalization from a fog chamber to in-flight iPhone footage through an aircraft window with no target-domain training. It uses a single-camera fog imager producing thousands of pixel-aligned foggy/clear pairs.

entry.title: Spatially Localized Image Degradation Embeddings for Image Quality Assessment

author.name: Krishna Srikar Durbha, Hassene Tmar, Ping-Hao Wu, Ioannis Katsavounidis, Alan C. Bovik

entry.summary: SLIDE-IQA introduces spatially localized degradation embeddings for no-reference image quality assessment, exposing a blind spot in SSL encoders that uniformly apply distortions. A dual-branch ViT injects spatially bounded degradation cues to improve sensitivity.

entry.title: Robust Zero-shot Anomaly Detection under Limited Auxiliary Anomaly Priors

author.name: Guanyu Lu, Fang Zhou, Cheqing Jin

entry.summary: DIVE is the first approach to address zero-shot anomaly detection under limited auxiliary anomaly priors, learning generic anomaly concepts through shallow-and-deep text embedding injection and a disentanglement mechanism. It resolves performance degradation when auxiliary data lacks anomaly diversity.

entry.title: VCS-SLAM: Geometry-Validated Semantic Evidence Fusion for 3D Gaussian SLAM

author.name: Raman Jha, Shuaihang Yuan, Yi Fang

entry.summary: VCS-SLAM is a geometry-validated semantic evidence fusion framework for RGB-D 3D Gaussian SLAM that weights semantic observations by geometric reliability rather than treating them uniformly. It reduces persistent semantic artifacts from occlusions and ambiguous geometry.

entry.title: Rectifying Mask via Entropy for Distractor-Free 3DGS in Ambiguous Scenarios

author.name: Wongi Park, Jiyeon Lim, Minjae Lee, Myeongseok Nam, Seongjun Choi, Jungwoo Kim, Soomok Lee, William J. Beksi, SangHyun Lee

entry.summary: RefineSplat constructs transient masks via an entropy-aware adaptive masking method to identify ambiguous distractors for distractor-free 3D Gaussian Splatting, and introduces entropy-aware density control. It also releases an Ambiguous wild dataset for validation.

entry.title: Learning Where and When: Patch-Based Spatiotemporal Localization in Weakly Supervised Video Anomaly Detection

author.name: Hamza Karim, Nghia Nguyen, Lokman Bekit, Yasin Yilmaz

entry.summary: This work introduces a patch-based spatiotemporal framework for weakly supervised video anomaly detection that jointly localizes where and when anomalies occur, using grid-level patch features and a Proximity-Aware Top-k selection under multiple instance learning. It adds spatial localization that prior temporal-only methods neglect.

entry.title: Efficient Visual Pointing for Embodied AI:Agent-Driven Data Synthesis, Cross-Block Attention, and Iterative Correction

author.name: Zijian Hong, Qi Lv, Yuxiang Xie, Jianming Xing, Xiang Deng, Weili Guan, Liqiang Nie

entry.summary: A competition solution for visual pointing in embodied AI that maps language instructions to pixel coordinates, combining agent-driven data synthesis, cross-block attention, and iterative correction. It achieved second place at PointArena 2026 with 77.2% accuracy.

entry.title: Optimizing Image Preparation and Compression for Face Recognition within 1024 Bytes

author.name: Paul Andreas, Torsten Schlett, Christoph Busch

entry.summary: Presents a lightweight real-time underwater image enhancement framework combining a reparameterizable convolution with fixed DCT priors and a frequency-guided dual-path attention module. It injects frequency-domain awareness into ultra-lightweight CNNs for deployment on resource-constrained underwater systems.

entry.title: The Speedup Paradox: Rethinking Inference Speed-Quality Trade-off in Embodied Tasks

author.name: Yujin Wang, Junli Chen, Yixuan Li, Shunan Dong, Huazhong Yang, Yongpan Liu, Hongyang Jia

entry.summary: This paper studies the speed-quality trade-off in embodied tasks, showing that closed-loop effects unique to embodied execution can make faster, lossy inference counterintuitively beneficial, and proposes a task-level inference framework (TISED). It argues per-step efficiency metrics fail to capture true task-level performance.

entry.title: FADA: Few-Shot Domain Adaptation via Dynamics Alignment for Humanoid Control

author.name: Angchen Xie, Nikhil Sobanbabu, Ishayu Shikhare, Alan Wang, Max Simchowitz, Guanya Shi

entry.summary: FADA is a three-stage Planner-Inverse Dynamics Model framework for few-shot domain adaptation in high-precision humanoid control, aligning target-domain dynamics under changes in terrain, payload, or actuator response. It bridges the gap between zero-shot domain randomization and heavy adaptation pipelines.

entry.title: TAP-VLA: Tactile Annotation Prompting for Vision Language Action Models

author.name: Mark Van der Merwe, Mohamad Louai Shehab, Jayjun Lee, Youngsun Wi, Yinpei Dai, Dmitry Berenson, Nima Fazeli

entry.summary: TAP-VLA integrates tactile sensing into Vision-Language-Action models via tactile annotation prompting, supplying tactile-derived force information without adding a new input modality that would cause distribution shift and erode pre-training. It enables contact-aware manipulation while preserving the benefits of large-scale vision-language pre-training.

entry.title: MoPe: Motion Permanence for Robust Monocular Gaussian Mapping in Dynamic Environments

author.name: Qixin Xiao

entry.summary: MoPe introduces motion permanence to monocular Gaussian Splatting SLAM, treating dynamic-ness as a temporal property rather than per-frame appearance to avoid ghosting artifacts when moving objects pause or reappear. It improves mapping stability in dynamic environments.

entry.title: Privacy-Preserving Decentralized Cooperative Localization with Range-Only Measurements: A Convex Optimization Based Approach

author.name: Nitesh Kumar, Reyshwanth Ganeshan, Sixu Li, Sivakumar Rathinam, Swaroop Darbha

entry.summary: Proposes a natively privacy-preserving decentralized cooperative localization framework using convex optimization with range-only measurements and bounded uncertainty, avoiding accuracy-degrading noise or expensive cryptography. It targets privacy-sensitive multi-robot missions.

entry.title: Flying to Image-Specified Objects: 3D Quadrotor Navigation via Cross-Graph Memory and Viewpoint Planning

author.name: Junjie Gao, Yuqi Chen, Yongzhou Pan, Yaosheng Deng, Jiaping Xiao, Mir Feroskhan

entry.summary: Proposes a hierarchical framework for quadrotor instance-specific image-goal navigation that separates high-level decision making from low-level motion, generating viewpoint-aware action nodes around frontiers and target objects using cross-graph memory. It addresses 3D control, limited field of view, and safety constraints.

entry.title: Towards Reliable and Robust LLM Planning: Symbolic Feedback-Driven Iterative Self-Refinement Framework

author.name: Jiajing Zhang, Jiamei Jiang, Chenyang Zhang, Feifei Mo, Linjing Li, Daniel Zeng

entry.summary: Proposes a symbolic feedback-driven iterative self-refinement framework to improve LLM robustness and reliability in long-horizon planning by mapping logical symbols to natural language. Uses iterative correction guided by symbolic verification.

entry.title: Grounded Iterative Language Planning: How Parameterized World Models Reduce Hallucination Propagation in LLM Agents

author.name: Xinyuan Song, Zekun Cai

entry.summary: Introduces Grounded Iterative Language Planning (GILP), which combines a small trained parameterized world model with an agent-based LLM planner and operational hallucination metrics to reduce hallucination propagation. Compares two world-model families on graph-planning benchmarks.

entry.title: Agent-Native Immune System: Architecture, Taxonomy, and Engineering

author.name: Bo Shen, Lifeng Chang, Tianyuan Wei, Yunpeng Li, Feng Shi, Yichen Han, Peijie Gao, Shiyi Kuang, Xin Chang, Dehui Li

entry.summary: Introduces the Agent-Native Immune System (ANIS), a biologically inspired endogenous defense architecture embedded in an agent's cognitive loop to counter runtime threats like memory poisoning and tool-chain manipulation. Provides architecture and taxonomy.

entry.title: GRAFT: Biological Graph and Hypergraph Benchmarks for Linked Gene Expression and Phenotypic Trait Prediction in Arabidopsis thaliana

author.name: Manuel Serna-Aguilera, Vanshika Jindal, Fiona L. Goggin, Jiamei Li, Aranyak Goswami, Alexander Bucksch, Suxing Liu, Khoa Luu

entry.summary: GRAFT introduces biological graph and hypergraph benchmarks linking gene expression and phenotypic traits in Arabidopsis thaliana for the genome-to-phenome challenge. Addresses the lack of datasets connecting gene expression and trait data.

entry.title: The Context-Ready Transformer

author.name: Mahesh Godavarti

entry.summary: Introduces the context-ready transformer, a recurrent architecture that pre-contextualizes each token before it enters a transformer block using a cached summary of past context and a correction network. Can convert pretrained transformers and trains via unrolled parallelization.

entry.title: Do Speech Emphasis Models Generalize across Languages and Emotions?

author.name: Megan Wei, Deepali Aneja, Jiaqi Su, Yunyun Wang, Haonan Chen, Zeyu Jin

entry.summary: Introduces MMEE, a multilingual multi-emotion emphasis corpus of 10,000 expressive utterances across 7 languages and 34 emotion/style categories, and benchmarks emphasis detection across cross-lingual, multilingual, and cross-emotion settings. Shows multilingual training improves robustness over monolingual models.

entry.title: Entropy Regularized Reinforcement Learning for Zero-Sum Stochastic Differential Games in a Regime-Switching Jump-Diffusion Process

author.name: Congde Hu, Zhuo Jin, Danping Li, Lin Xu

entry.summary: Introduces an entropy-regularized RL framework for zero-sum stochastic differential games under regime-switching jump-diffusion processes. Derives coupled HJBI equations and expresses equilibrium strategies via value-function gradients.

entry.title: Active Quantum Kernel Acquisition for Gaussian Process Regression

author.name: Jian Xu, Delu Zeng, Qibin Zhao

entry.summary: Extends shot-budget-aware quantum kernel estimation from classification to Gaussian process regression, deriving closed-form pair-level sensitivities for downstream quantities like posterior variance and marginal likelihood. Aims to reduce circuit executions on near-term quantum hardware.

entry.title: When Prices Double in a Week: Forecasting of Agricultural Volatility in Import-Isolated Markets

author.name: Ranuga Weerasekara, Heshan Nethmina, Manuja Ranathunga, Vinma Wettasinghe, Dinithi Navodya, Subavarshana Arumugam, Nirasha Munasinghe, Nisansa de Silva, Sandareka Wickramanayake

entry.summary: Develops a supply-chain-aware ML framework to forecast vegetable price volatility in import-isolated Sri Lankan markets, modeling two cultivation seasons. Uses gradient-boosted ensembles with weather, diesel, and exchange-rate features tuned via Optuna.

entry.title: Adaptive Financial Transformer with Regime-Gated Attention for Stock Return Prediction

author.name: Dishan Sarkar

entry.summary: The Adaptive Financial Transformer uses a market regime encoder, adaptive gate network, and regime-gated attention to bias self-attention by semantic relationships among financial indicators for stock return prediction. It also corrects backtesting issues that inflate performance.

entry.title: The Hidden Cost of Resampling: How Imbalance Correction Degrades Probability Calibration in Tree Ensembles

author.name: Zewen Liu

entry.summary: Empirically examines how class-imbalance correction via SMOTE and resampling degrades probability calibration in tree ensembles across five datasets and two models. It finds SMOTE's calibration cost is real but small and offers guidance on when it matters and how to fix it.

entry.title: EVAF: A Test-Retest Protocol for Selective Parametric Consolidation

author.name: Haoliang Han

entry.summary: Introduces EVAF, an Echo-Valence Attractor Field mechanism for gated LoRA consolidation, with a test-retest protocol to measure selective parametric consolidation of agent experiences under interference. It preferentially consolidates high-valence, high-surprise experiences while preserving factual memory.

entry.title: Toward an Energy-Optimized Operation of Data Centers Located in Wind Farms Using Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Jan Stenner, Alexander Kilian, Sebastian Peitz, Hermann de Meer

entry.summary: Studies reinforcement learning as an online controller for curtailment-aware workload shifting in wind-turbine-integrated HPC data centers, introducing a reproducible fixed-day simulation framework. It finds pure RL has a credit-assignment problem and evaluates imitation learning and potential-based shaping as countermeasures.

entry.title: Curvature-Weighted Gradient Diversity: A Noise Measure for Geometry-Adaptive SGD Schedules

author.name: Muhammad Hamza (Indian Institute of Technology Kharagpur), Ayush Goel (Indian Institute of Technology Kharagpur)

entry.summary: CWGD introduces a curvature-aware gradient noise measure that weights per-sample gradient diversity by the inverse square root of the Hessian, providing a tighter proxy for effective optimization noise. They prove a CWGD-modulated cosine learning-rate schedule can reduce the error floor for convex quadratics.

entry.title: TextClusterLab: An Integrated Framework for Reliable Text Clustering Studies

author.name: Daoming Wan, Yizheng Huang, Jimmy X. Huang

entry.summary: TextClusterLab provides an integrated framework for reliable text clustering studies, including an LLM-driven synthetic text dataset generator to address the lack of suitable benchmarking data for text-specific clustering. It targets reproducibility and benchmarking gaps.

entry.title: In-Vehicle Digital Twin-Based Collision Warning Framework with Sybil Attack Detection

author.name: Mohammad Imtiaz Hasan, Abyad Enan, Jean Michel Tine, Araf Rahman, M Sabbir Salek, Mashrur Chowdhury

entry.summary: This paper presents an in-vehicle digital twin-based collision warning framework with built-in Sybil attack detection, integrating a Temporal Convolutional Network to learn temporal dependencies for connected vehicles. It targets real-time cyberattack detection in safety-critical CV applications.

entry.title: AnTenA: Actionable and Explainable Tensor Analysis System with Large Language Models

author.name: Dawon Ahn, Auder Der, Evangelos E. Papalexakis

entry.summary: AnTenA leverages LLMs to explain hidden co-clustered latent patterns extracted from tensor decompositions of human narratives, using task-agnostic and task-specific prompts. It evaluates explanations via forward and backward inference tasks.

entry.title: Evidence-Based Text-Conditioned 3D CT Synthesis for Ovarian Cancer

author.name: Francesca Pia Panaccione, Eugenio Lomurno, Francesca Fati, Carlotta Pecchiari, Marina Rosanu, Luigi De Vitis, Lucia Ribero, Gabriella Schivardi, Giovanni Damiano Aletti, Nicoletta Colombo, Maria Francesca Spadea, Francesco Multinu, Matteo Matteucci, Elena De Momi

entry.summary: OvESyn generates synthetic text-conditioned 3D CT scans for ovarian cancer without requiring paired radiology reports, instead building standardized findings from imaging descriptors and clinical metadata. It addresses data scarcity and privacy in a domain where prior synthesis methods only worked on chest CT. It matters for expanding generative medical imaging to underserved cancer types.

entry.title: Fourier Neural Operators with Least-Squares Readout Refit for Learning Random Obstacle-to-Solution Maps

author.name: Chenhui Zhu, Fei Wang

entry.summary: This paper asks whether vision models truly recognize objects or only fit surface-level local cues, formalizing the question via syntactic distance that measures class separability through operation symmetry. Using visual self-referential instances where local cues provide no stable basis, it probes deeper recognition ability. It matters for understanding the limits of vision-model perception.

entry.title: Boundary Degree as a Node-level Feature for Epidemic Scenario Identification in Agent-based Cascade Simulations

author.name: Amro Alabsi Aljundi, Galen Harrison, Jiangzhuo Chen, Abhijin Adiga, Anil Kumar Vullikanti, Madhav V. Marathe

entry.summary: This paper proposes boundary degree—the count of an infected node's uninfected contacts—as a per-node cascade feature for identifying epidemic scenarios from disease cascades, improving accuracy by 19% on realistic contact networks. It also provides theoretical grounding for edge-feature importance. It matters for epidemic simulation analytics.

entry.title: Staged Hybridisation for Visual Quantum Reinforcement Learning via Knowledge Distillation

author.name: Javier Lazaro, Juan-Ignacio Vazquez, Pablo Garcia-Bringas

entry.summary: Studies knowledge distillation as a staged hybridization strategy for visual quantum reinforcement learning, distilling a classical teacher policy into compact quantum-compatible heads over a frozen encoder. It sidesteps the difficulty of training hybrid quantum agents end-to-end from pixels.

entry.title: Knowing in Advance When an Evolutionary Outer Loop Will Not Help: A Pre-Registered Cheap-Baseline Screening Rule

author.name: Ramchand Kumaresan

entry.summary: Proposes a pre-registered screening rule that decides before implementation whether an expensive evolutionary outer loop over network parameters will beat a cheap single-shot alternative, via a recovery ratio metric. It aims to avoid wasted compute on outer loops unlikely to help.

entry.title: Resolution Thresholds in VLM Detection of Harmful ASCII Art Across Construction Modes and Languages

author.name: Yikai Hua, Peter West

entry.summary: Investigates how image resolution affects VLMs' ability to detect harmful text encoded as ASCII art across eight construction modes and two languages. Identifies detection-failure thresholds relevant to jailbreak-resistant content moderation.

entry.title: How Far Can You Get Without a GPU? A Systematic Benchmark of Lightweight Hallucination Detection Across Question Answering, Dialogue, and Summarisation

author.name: Kriti Faujdar, Smit Kadvani

entry.summary: Systematically benchmarks five lightweight, CPU-feasible hallucination-detection methods (ROUGE-L, semantic similarity, BERTScore, NLI, and an ensemble) across QA, dialogue, and summarization. Asks how far resource-constrained detection can go without GPUs or proprietary APIs.

entry.title: CaresAI at CT-DEB26: Detecting Dosing Errors In Clinical Trials Using Domain-Specific Transformer Embeddings and Classification Models

author.name: Leon Hamnett, Favour Igwezeke, Joseph Itopa Abubakar, Mary Adetutu Adewunmi

entry.summary: Proposes proactive routing for efficient visual reasoning, pairing a small draft model with a large target model and learning a reliable query-difficulty signal before generation. Avoids post-hoc token probabilities and data-sensitive supervised routing.

entry.title: Regime-Aware Peer Specialization for Robust RAG under Heterogeneous Knowledge Conflicts

author.name: Bo Wang, Heyan Huang, Yaolin Li, Yanghao Zhou, Jiahao Teng, Ziyi Yang, Ge Shi, Chong Feng

entry.summary: Proposes RAPS-DA, a regime-aware peer-specialization framework for RAG that separates reliable, partially reliable, and adversarial retrieved context to avoid conflating learning signals. Handles heterogeneous knowledge conflicts at sample and finer granularities.

entry.title: Detecting Clinical Hallucinations in LVLMs via Counterfactual Visual Grounding Uncertainty

author.name: Xiao Song, Haonan Qin, Zhaoxu Zhang, Jiong Zhang, Yuqi Fang, Caifeng Shan

entry.summary: Proposes a vision-traceable hallucination-detection framework for clinical LVLMs that grounds claimed entities on the input image via a medical-adapted Qwen-VL verifier without internal model access. Uses counterfactual entity perturbation to estimate visual-evidence uncertainty.

entry.title: LAMP: Lean-based Agentic framework with MCP and Proof Repair

author.name: Santhana Srinivasan R, Maithilee Patawar

entry.summary: Presents LAMP, a Lean 4 agentic theorem-proving framework using MCP and automated proof repair, contributing formalized lemmas for the under-represented domain of Combinatorics on Words. Addresses gaps where Mathlib-centered provers lack domain lemmas.

entry.title: DNA Language Models: An Assessment of Pre-Training for Fine-Tuning Tasks

author.name: Romain Karpinsky, Julien Mozziconacci, Micka\"el Delcey

entry.summary: This paper benchmarks DNA language models, comparing transformer-based approaches like DNABERT2 against convolutional models like ConvNova, and questions whether costly transformer pretraining and BPE tokenization justify their gains for genomic fine-tuning tasks. It provides a systematic comparison missing from the field.

entry.title: SemDynReg: Semantics-Guided Deformation Regularization for Dynamic 3D Gaussian Splatting

author.name: Ruitao Chen, Mozhang Guo, Jinge Li

entry.summary: SemDynReg introduces a semantics-guided framework for deformable 3D Gaussian Splatting that enforces object-level dynamic regularization using SAM segmentation masks and object-ID maps to achieve spatially consistent per-object deformation. It reduces inconsistent deformations and unwanted coupling between objects in dynamic scenes.

entry.title: Beyond Backscatter: AlphaEarth Land-Cover Priors for Rapid SAR Flood Segmentation Across Foundation Backbones

author.name: Sanjay Thasma, Yu-Hsuan Ho, Ali Mostafavi

entry.summary: This study tests whether stable land-cover priors improve post-event SAR flood segmentation when no matched pre-event image exists, comparing four backbones with different pretraining regimes. It provides practical insight for emergency flood mapping using foundation model features.

entry.title: FDM-MFVT: Few-step Sampling Diffusion Model for Mask-Free Virtual Try-On

author.name: Jiaxin Liu, Xiaoye Liang, Lai Jiang, Mai Xu, Jun Liu

entry.summary: FDM-MFVT is a few-step diffusion model for mask-free virtual try-on, using noise optimization and instruction-driven modules to generate high-fidelity try-on images in only 6 steps. It removes the need for masks and costly auxiliary networks.

entry.title: Learning to Adaptively Allocate Gaussians for Arbitrary-Scale Image Super-Resolution

author.name: Giulio Federico, Giuseppe Amato, Claudio Gennaro, Fabio Carrara, Marco Di Benedetto

entry.summary: This method learns to adaptively allocate Gaussians for arbitrary-scale image super-resolution, concentrating representational resources where structural complexity demands rather than processing pixels uniformly. It enables continuous magnification with efficiency.

entry.title: Bricker to BRACE: A Bracket Exposure RAW Dataset and Restoration Model for Flicker-Banding

author.name: Zihan Zhou, Libo Zhu, Jue Gong, Zhiyi Zhou, Jiezhang Cao, Yong Guo, Yulun Zhang

entry.summary: BRACE tackles flicker-banding artifacts in screen-captured photos via a new bracketed RAW dataset (Bricker) built with ray-traced simulation and a multi-frame restoration model. It distinguishes display-modulation artifacts from genuine texture better than single-frame parametric methods.

entry.title: CogSENet: Blind Image Deblurring with Blur-Conditioned Semantic Routing and Explicit Frequency Fusion

author.name: Pan Wang, Yihao Hu, Xiujin Liu

entry.summary: CogSENet is a blind image deblurring framework inspired by the eagle's visual system, using a semantic-driven state space module with differentiable routing and explicit frequency fusion. It aims to differentiate valid textures from artifacts under spatially varying real-world degradations.

entry.title: Real-Time Underwater Image Enhancement via Frequency-Guided Dual-Path Attention

author.name: Leshen Zhang, Ao Li, Ce Zhu

entry.summary: Proposes a point cloud transformer for remote, automated assessment of physical rehabilitation exercises from RGBD joint movement data, enabling cost-effective at-home monitoring without expensive preprocessing. It aims to extract more relevant features than existing rehabilitation assessment approaches.

entry.title: On the Faithfulness of Post-Hoc Concept Bottleneck Models

author.name: Laines Schmalwasser, Jan Blunk, Niklas Penzel, Julia Niebling, Joachim Denzler

entry.summary: This paper critically examines post-hoc concept bottleneck models, showing that high task accuracy can be achieved even with semantically meaningless concept projections (e.g., random projections). It analyzes the learned projections directly to identify failure modes in faithfulness.

entry.title: Towards in-the-wild Egocentric 3D Hand-Object Pose Estimation

author.name: Siddhant Bansal, Zhifan Zhu, Shashank Tripathi, Jiahe Zhao, Michael J. Black, Dima Damen

entry.summary: This work targets in-the-wild egocentric 3D hand-object pose estimation, introducing EPIC-Contact (2.3K clips with dense bijective 3D hand-object contact correspondences) and HOPformer, an end-to-end transformer that jointly predicts bimanual hand and object pose. It addresses occlusion and supervision scarcity.

entry.title: CORE Planner: Contextual-memory Oriented Reinforcement-learning in Unknown Environments for Robot Navigation

author.name: Jintao Kong, Zhihao Zhang, Weihuang Chen, Liming Chen, Zhongyu Guo, Shuaiyu Liu, Hongbin Sun

entry.summary: CORE Planner combines traditional planning with reinforcement learning for robot navigation in unknown environments, using a sparse visibility graph for structured representation and contextual memory. It aims to overcome limited environmental memory and sim-to-real transfer challenges.

entry.title: MTD-Map: Single-Stage Long-Term LiDAR Map Maintenance Framework via Mixture Transition Distribution

author.name: TaeYoung Kim, Gilhwan Kang, Tae Ihn Kim, Seungwon Song, Hun Keon Ko

entry.summary: MTD-Map is a single-stage LiDAR map maintenance framework that handles both dynamic object removal and change detection without separate modules, using Mixture Transition Distribution modeling of occupancy transitions. A recursive formulation captures high-order temporal dependencies.

entry.title: Real-Time Compliance and Position Control of a Hyper-redundant Soft Robotic Arm

author.name: Runze Zuo, Tianhua Zou, Naike Wu, Mingyuan Li, Daniel Bruder

entry.summary: Presents a hyper-redundant soft robotic arm with a rigid articulated backbone and antagonistic pneumatic muscles allowing each axis to simultaneously adjust angle and stiffness for real-time compliance and position control. The design makes tip compliance predictable enough for quantitative commands.

entry.title: Data-Driven Modeling and Control for Tethered Space Systems with Koopman-Informed Graphs

author.name: Ao Jin, Yifeng Ma, Panfeng Huang, Fan Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes Koopman Graph Dynamics combining global linear Koopman operator evolution with local graph neural network topological priors to model flexible tethered space systems, then builds an MPC controller on this representation. It targets high-dimensional nonlinear orbital tether/net dynamics.

entry.title: Robust Extended Kalman Filter for Land Navigation Using Massive Array of MEMS IMUs

author.name: Omer Hanani, Alon Kipnis

entry.summary: Proposes a robust Extended Kalman Filter architecture for land navigation using hundreds of low-cost MEMS IMUs, with a pre-filtering framework (RISAF) combining dynamic percentile gating and real-time bias tracking to suppress anomalous readings and bias drift before the EKF prediction step. It aggregates many sensors without increasing filter computational burden.

entry.title: Understanding Rollout Error in Graph World Models

author.name: Xinyuan Song, Zekun Cai

entry.summary: Studies long-horizon rollout error in Graph World Models, formulating fixed-edge and dynamic-edge frameworks and deriving rollout bounds that separate topology-induced from model-induced error amplification. Provides theoretical grounding for graph-structured planning.

entry.title: Not All Relations Rotate Alike: Transformation-Aware Decoupling for Viewpoint-Robust 3D Scene Graph Generation

author.name: Jingjun Sun, Chaowei Wang, Zhirui Liu, Jiaxu Tian, Ming Yang, Yaoxing Wang, Shan Gao

entry.summary: Identifies that 3D scene graph generation models fail to produce relation predictions consistent with viewpoint rotations, distinguishing directional predicates (which should rotate) from contact/semantic predicates (which should not). Proposes transformation-aware decoupling for viewpoint robustness.

entry.title: CoIn: Comprehensive 2D-3D Inpainting with Gaussian Splatting Guidance

author.name: Hana Kim, Minje Kim, Tae-Kyun Kim

entry.summary: CoIn bridges 2D inpainting models and 3D Gaussian Splatting through a multi-stage consistency pipeline supporting arbitrary-shaped masks and tasks beyond object removal, like object insertion. Uses reference-adaptive Gaussian Splatting with feature attention.
