entry.title: BiPACE: Bisimulation-Guided Policy Optimization with Action Counterfactual Estimation for LLM Agents

author.name: Hanyang Wang, Weijieying Ren, Yuxiang Zhang, Ding Cao, Zhizhao Zeng, Ke Zeng, Tianxiang Zhao

entry.summary: BiPACE is a bisimulation-guided policy optimization method for LLM agents that addresses a state-action credit mismatch in stepwise group-based RL, where observation-hash partitions are too fine on the state side and within-group means too coarse on the action side. It uses bisimulation grouping and action counterfactual estimation for better credit assignment in long-horizon tasks.

entry.title: OncoSynth: Synthetic data generation for treatment effect estimation in oncology

author.name: Octavia-Andreea Ciora, Julian Welzel, Dennis Frauen, Maresa Schr\"oder, Marie Brockschmidt, Harry Amad, Thomas Callender, Mihaela van der Schaar, Stefan Feuerriegel

entry.summary: OncoSynth is a causally-aware diffusion-based framework for generating synthetic oncology cohorts that preserve causal relationships between covariates, treatments, and outcomes, enabling accurate population- and patient-level treatment effect estimation. It is evaluated on large lung and breast cancer datasets where patient-level data access is restricted.

entry.title: SARA: Unlocking Multilingual Knowledge in Mixture-of-Experts via Semantically Anchored Routing Alignment

author.name: Tianyu Dong, Yangyang Liu, Jiang Zhou, Xinwei Wu, Xiaohu Zhao, Hao Wang, Heng Liu, Linlong Xu, Longyue Wang, Weihua Luo, Shaolin Zhu, Deyi Xiong

entry.summary: SARA proposes semantically anchored routing alignment to improve multilingual knowledge in Mixture-of-Experts models by aligning low-resource language token routing with high-resource anchors. It addresses cross-lingual routing divergence that limits expert sharing. Relevant for improving MoE multilingual capability.

entry.title: MiniOpt: Reasoning to Model and Solve General Optimization Problems with Limited Resources

author.name: Ke Zhao, Zixiang Di, Hong Qian, Xiang Shu, Yaolin Wen, Qitao Shi, Bingdong Li, Xingyu Lu, Xiangfeng Wang, Jun Zhou, Ke Tang, Yang Yu

entry.summary: MiniOpt is an RL framework that trains LLMs to model and solve general optimization problems via a reasoning-to-model-and-solve paradigm with limited training resources. It avoids large supervised datasets and costly reasoning annotations through a reward called OptReward. Matters for resource-efficient optimization-oriented LLMs.

entry.title: Privacy Vulnerabilities of Attention Layers in Tabular Foundation Models and Protection of High-Risk Queries

author.name: T\^ania Carvalho, Maxime Cordy

entry.summary: This paper demonstrates privacy vulnerabilities in tabular foundation models, showing that in-context learning predictions via attention leak enough information for membership inference attacks. It proposes AMIA, a shadow-model-free attack exploiting attention concentration, plus a protection scheme for high-risk queries. Matters for privacy of in-context tabular models.

entry.title: Learning Action Priors for Cross-embodiment Robot Manipulation

author.name: Dong Jing, Tianqi Zhang, Jiaqi Liu, Jinman Zhao, Zelong Sun, Li Erran Li, Zhiwu Lu, Mingyu Ding

entry.summary: This work proposes pretraining the action module of vision-language-action models with cross-embodiment motion priors before cross-modal alignment, rather than learning motion from scratch. A two-stage framework equips the action module with cross-embodiment temporal dynamics. Relevant for cross-embodiment robot manipulation.

entry.title: A Single Stepsize Suffices for Unprojected Linear TD(0): Simultaneous Robust and Fast Rates via Polyak--Ruppert Averaging

author.name: Wei-Cheng Lee, Francesco Orabona

entry.summary: This paper proves that a single stepsize schedule suffices for unprojected linear TD(0) with Polyak-Ruppert averaging under Markovian sampling, providing high-probability guarantees that iterates stay bounded without projections or knowledge of curvature. It establishes simultaneous robust and fast convergence rates. Matters for RL theory foundations.

entry.title: The Geometry of Sequential Learning: Lie-Bracket Prediction of Transfer Order

author.name: John Sweeney

entry.summary: This work shows that the local order effect in sequential learning curricula is governed by the Lie-bracket commutator of gradient update fields, yielding a pairwise score for whether A-then-B or B-then-A is better. It defines a Lie-Bracket Tournament with efficient Borda scoring via Hessian-vector products. Matters for curriculum and data-ordering decisions in training.

entry.title: Certification of Machine Learning Models via Directional Sharpness

author.name: Gefei Tan, Adria Gascon, Sarah Meiklejohn, Mariana Raykova

entry.summary: This work proposes certifying machine learning models via directional sharpness, addressing the unreliability of test accuracy and computational cost of full sharpness metrics when training is perturbed. It targets trustworthy assurance of model quality and generalization. Relevant for model certification under potentially tampered training. Authors from Google DeepMind.

entry.title: Efficient Analytic Uncertainty Quantification for Multi-Modal Regression

author.name: Kun Jin, James Harrison, Jiawei Li, Sihan Liu, Jiayi Liu, Randolph Linderman, Yuening Li, Arnab Bhadury, Sourabh Prakash Bansod, Liang Liu, Jasper Snoek

entry.summary: This paper extends variational Bayesian inference uncertainty quantification to semi-parametric multi-modal regression, providing efficient analytic variance estimation where standard single-peak Gaussian assumptions fail. It addresses the gap where semi-parametric methods perform well but lack efficient uncertainty quantification. Relevant for trustworthy large-scale regression. Authors include Jasper Snoek.

entry.title: The Generalization Spectrum: A Chromatographic Approach to Evaluating Learning Algorithms

author.name: Jinghan Zhang, Zerui Cheng, Shiqi Chen, Ge Zhang, Wenhao Huang, Jiashuo Liu, Junxian He, Tianle Cai

entry.summary: The Generalization Spectrum introduces a chromatographic evaluation framework that measures per-sample generalization by constructing test variants ordered by increasing transfer distance. It exposes how far knowledge from one training example transfers, a dimension invisible to standard i.i.d. benchmarks.

entry.title: ROAD-VLA: Robust Online Adaptation via Self-Distillation for Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Kejing Wang, Toan Nguyen, Minh Hoang Nguyen, Simon Khan, Flora D. Salim

entry.summary: ROAD-VLA proposes advantage-guided self-distillation for online adaptation of vision-language-action models, constructing a proximal teacher directly in action space by perturbing action-token logits with calibrated advantage estimates. This converts sparse rewards into dense token-level supervision, addressing the modality gap between symbolic guidance and low-level actions.

entry.title: Concept Removal for Frontier Image Generative Models

author.name: Aditya Kumar, Pierre Joly, Adam Dziedzic, Franziska Boenisch

entry.summary: This work introduces a concept-removal method for frontier diffusion and autoregressive image models (SD3.5, Flux, Infinity) that replaces the internal bottleneck layer with a transcoder structuring activations into distinct features. This enables selective disabling of concept-specific signals while preserving overall generation quality.

entry.title: AgentOdyssey: Open-Ended Long-Horizon Text Game Generation for Test-Time Continual Learning Agents

author.name: Zheyuan Zhang, Zehao Wen, Alvin Zhang, Andrew Wang, Jianwen Xie, Daniel Khashabi, Tianmin Shu

entry.summary: AgentOdyssey is an evaluation framework that procedurally generates open-ended long-horizon text games to test test-time continual learning agents on exploration, knowledge acquisition, episodic retention, and long-horizon planning. It interleaves learning and inference throughout deployment, breaking the assumption that learning stops at test time.

entry.title: Beyond Next-Observation Prediction: Agent-Authored World Modeling for Sequential Decision Making

author.name: Guangfeng Cai, Kaibing Yang, Shuo He, Yu Li, Shengtian Yang, Jiaqi Lv, Lei Feng

entry.summary: Proposes Agent-Authored World Modeling (AAWM), where an LLM agent identifies what it needs to know before acting and builds decision-oriented training targets instead of generic next-observation prediction. This better aligns world modeling with the agent's actual decision needs in sequential tasks.

entry.title: OPERA: Aligning Open-Ended Reasoning via Objective Perplexity-based Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Wenxuan Jiang, Zining Fan, Zijian Zhang, Xuecheng Wu, Hongming Tan, Haoyang Dai, Xiaoyu Li, Xuezhi Cao, Ninghao Liu

entry.summary: OPERA replaces unreliable LLM-as-judge rewards for open-ended reasoning tasks with intrinsic rewards derived from perplexity dynamics, quantifying uncertainty reduction at reflective states. It aims to stabilize RL for creative and open-ended generation.

entry.title: Tracing Target Answers in Poisoned Retrieval Corpora via Token Influence Attribution

author.name: Yan-Lun Chen, Pin-Yu Chen, Chia-Mu Yu, Ying-Dar Lin, Yu-Sung Wu, Wei-Bin Lee

entry.summary: TRACE is a lightweight detection framework that identifies RAG corpus poisoning by tracing answer-related tokens via token influence attribution, avoiding heavy auxiliary classifiers. It shows strong detection across QA benchmarks and six LLMs.

entry.title: VPA-Guard: Defending and Benchmarking Image-to-Video Generation Against Visual Prompt Attacks

author.name: Yining Sun, Haoyu Kang, Jiajun Wu, Heng Zhang, Danyang Zhang, Zhenjun Zhao, Haochen Han, Fangming Liu, Wai Kin Victor Chan, Alex Jinpeng Wang

entry.summary: VPA-Guard introduces VVA-Bench, the first systematic benchmark for visual prompt attacks on image-to-video generation, where static cues like arrows and emojis are interpreted as harmful temporal instructions. It defends and benchmarks against an underexplored I2V threat.

entry.title: UniTeD: Unified Temporal Diffusion for Joint Perception and Planning in Autonomous Driving

author.name: Bo Zhao, Xinting Zhao, Naifan Li, Erkang Cheng, Haibin Ling

entry.summary: UniTeD proposes a unified temporal diffusion framework that jointly models perception and planning in autonomous driving through shared iterative denoising, rather than confining diffusion to a separate planning module. By enabling bidirectional information flow, it aims to reduce error propagation from perception to planner and improve robustness.

entry.title: MVTrack4Gen: Multi-View Point Tracking as Geometric Supervision for 4D Video Generation

author.name: JoungBin Lee, Jaewoo Jung, Jongmin Lee, Tongmin Kim, Hyunsung Kim, Takuya Narihira, Kazumi Fukuda, Jahyeok Koo, Jisang Han, Yuki Mitsufuji, Seungryong Kim

entry.summary: MVTrack4Gen uses multi-view point tracking as geometric and motion supervision to train novel-view video generation from monocular references, avoiding reliance on inaccurate explicit 3D reconstruction. This motion-aware framework improves geometric and motion consistency relative to camera-conditioning-only methods.

entry.title: Cross-Attention Multimodal Learning for Predicting Response to Neoadjuvant Imatinib in Gastrointestinal Stromal Tumors: A Multicenter Retrospective Study

author.name: Fariba Tohidinezhad, Douwe J. Spaanderman, Natalia Oviedo Acosta, Kaouther Mouheb, Karthik Prathaban, David F. Hanff, Dirk J. Gr\"unhagen, Cornelis Verhoef, Joris M. van Sabben, Evelyne Roets, Jette J. Slettenhaar, Hans Gelderblom, Ingrid M. E. Desar, Anna K. L. Reyners, Neeltje Steeghs, Stefan Klein, Martijn P. A. Starmans

entry.summary: This multicenter retrospective study develops an explainable cross-attention multimodal deep learning framework integrating CT imaging and clinical variables to predict response to neoadjuvant imatinib in gastrointestinal stromal tumors. It uses self-supervised pretraining across 935 patients and prediction on 213, addressing an unmet clinical prediction need.

entry.title: RGB: RL Guided Whole-Body MPPI for Humanoid Control

author.name: Yunsoo Seo, Sol Choi, Euncheol Im, Myo Taeg Lim, Yisoo Lee

entry.summary: RGB is an RL-guided whole-body MPPI framework for humanoid control where a pretrained RL policy acts as a sampling prior biasing model-predictive path integral rollouts, with task objectives specified as modular cost terms. This add-on lets new feedback objectives be added without retraining the RL policy.

entry.title: Memory Retrieval in Visuomotor Policies for Long-Horizon Robot Control

author.name: Rutav Shah, Yisu Li, Femi Bello, Yuke Zhu, Roberto Mart\'in-Mart\'in

entry.summary: This work studies memory retrieval in visuomotor policies for long-horizon robot control, using transformer attention over long contexts to recall past information such as object placements and completed tasks. It identifies and addresses challenges like spurious correlations when integrating learned retrieval into imitation learning from offline data.

entry.title: GRAFT: Graph-Based Affordance Transfer via Part Correspondence

author.name: Mengying Lin, Utkarsh Mishra, Ajay Mandlekar, Danfei Xu

entry.summary: GRAFT is a geometry-aware framework for zero-shot robotic manipulation transfer using just one demonstration per object, representing objects as part-based graphs supporting global retrieval, part correspondence, and fine-grained contact-point matching. It combines semantic and geometric similarity which semantics-only retrieval neglects.

entry.title: DeformGen: Dynamics-Based Topology Augmentation for Deformable Manipulation Policy Learning

author.name: Zili Lin, Wenyao Zhang, Yuyang Zhang, Zekun Qi, Junyan Lin, Hanxin Zhu, Jiaolong Yang, Zhibo Chen, Yao Mu, Xiaokang Yang, Xin Jin, Wenjun Zeng

entry.summary: TacVerse is a multi-sensor dataset and benchmark for cross-sensor vision-based tactile perception, containing 106,800 tactile images from seven sensors and supporting shape classification, grating classification, and force regression under within-sensor, zero-shot transfer, and few-shot settings. It probes how poorly tactile generalization transfers across sensor designs.

entry.title: Risk-Averse AIs

author.name: wdmacaskill

entry.summary: Argues for training AIs to be risk-averse in resources (diminishing marginal utility) as both a usefulness preservation and a safety measure, since misaligned but risk-averse AIs would prefer guaranteed modest payments over low-probability rebellion. Sketches training methods and argues risk aversion is a broad, easy-to-reward target.

entry.title: Uncertainty Quantification for Computer-Use Agents: A Benchmark across Vision-Language Models and GUI Grounding Datasets

author.name: Divake Kumar, Sina Tayebati, Devashri Naik, Amanda Sofie Rios, Nilesh Ahuja, Omesh Tickoo, Ranganath Krishnan, Amit Ranjan Trivedi

entry.summary: Argus is a cross-regime benchmark for post-hoc uncertainty quantification in single-step executable GUI grounding for computer-use agents, spanning 27 methods across 4 open-weight VLMs and 4 datasets plus an 8-method closed-source matrix across frontier vendors. It investigates whether UQ method rankings remain stable as agent, benchmark, or interface change.

entry.title: $\text{DT}^2$: Decision-Targeted Digital Twins

author.name: Harry Amad, Mihaela van der Schaar

entry.summary: DT-squared introduces decision-targeted digital twin training, proving that minimizing one-step transition errors can produce models that rank policies suboptimally under limited capacity. It instead uses fitted Q-evaluation to train twins that preserve policy value rankings for decision-making.

entry.title: Efficient and Trainable Language Model Test-Time Scaling via Local Branch Routing

author.name: Yutong Yin, Mingyu Jin, Jin Pan, Changyi Yang, Zijie Xia, Dhruv Pai, Shuming Hu, Zhen Zhang, Chenyang Zhao, Jinman Zhao, Wujiang Xu, Raymond Li, Xin Eric Wang, Julian McAuley, Zhaoran Wang

entry.summary: Local Branch Routing is a token-level test-time scaling framework that expands a small local lookahead tree, forwards all sampled branches through the LM, and uses a lightweight trainable router to select the committed subtree. It enables each token decision to use evidence beyond the root next-token distribution while avoiding expensive full solution-level search.

entry.title: From Rubble Simulation to Active Magnetic Mapping: Quantum Sensing for Disaster Response

author.name: Samuel Tovey, Stefan Prestel, Hiroshi Yamauchi

entry.summary: DeformGen is a dynamics-based topology augmentation framework for deformable manipulation policy learning, expanding the valid state distribution by applying localized physical disturbances and forward-simulating dynamics to obtain topology-coherent configurations. It addresses why pose-perturbation augmentation fails for high-dimensional, physics-constrained deformable objects.

entry.title: Do vision-language models search like humans? Reasoning tokens as a reaction-time analog in classic visual-search paradigms

author.name: Farahnaz Wick

entry.summary: Tests whether vision-language models exhibit human-like visual search signatures by using reasoning-token counts as an analog of reaction time across classic attention paradigms. Bridges cognitive science methodology and VLM evaluation.

entry.title: To Isolate or to Score? Model-Adaptive Assessment for Cost-Efficient Multi-Agent RAG

author.name: Jungseob Lee, Chanjun Park, Heuiseok Lim

entry.summary: A controlled study of training-free interventions in multi-agent RAG for 7B-9B models, revealing that weaker models benefit mainly from per-document isolation rather than scoring quality, with gains up to 50 points. Offers model-adaptive guidance for cost-efficient RAG.

entry.title: WinDOM: Self-Family Distillation for Small-Model GUI Grounding

author.name: Chengheng Li-Chen, Zhiqian Zhou, Hao Chen, Nicolas Chauvin

entry.summary: Introduces WinDOM, a DOM-harvested GUI grounding corpus requiring no human annotation, and Self-Family Distillation to push small ~2B GUI-grounding agents combining SFT and RL. Targets cheap on-device GUI grounding.

entry.title: RWGBench: Evaluating Scholarly Positioning in Related Work Generation

author.name: Anzhe Xie, Weihang Su, Jiaxin Mao, Yiqun Liu, Shaoping Ma, Qingyao Ai

entry.summary: Introduces RWGBench to evaluate related-work generation as a citation-level scholarly positioning task rather than summarization, surfacing failures like inappropriate citation selection that similarity metrics miss. Improves evaluation of scientific writing by LLMs.

entry.title: Stable-Shift: Biologically Structured Prediction of Transcriptional Responses to Unseen Gene Perturbations

author.name: Sajib Acharjee Dip, Liqing Zhang

entry.summary: Introduces Stable-Shift, a structured method predicting transcriptional responses to unseen gene perturbations by fitting a low-rank response basis on training perturbations and predicting coordinates from biological context via graph convolution. Targets extrapolation in functional genomics.

entry.title: What Do Language Priors Contribute to Darcy-Flow Inversion? A Mechanistic Audit

author.name: Taiga Saito, Yu Otake, Daijiro Mizutani, Sopheakpolin Mom

entry.summary: Mechanistically audits whether sentence embeddings of qualitative geological descriptions can serve as inference-time priors for a learned Darcy-flow inverse solver, finding text conditioning cuts reconstruction error by 81% mostly via a categorical class-level constraint. Bridges language priors and physics-based inversion.

entry.title: Power-Flexible AI Data Centers: A New Paradigm for Grid-Responsive Compute

author.name: Chris Williams, Philip Colangelo, Ayse Coskun, Ethan Levine, Andy Neale, Ciaran Roberts, Shayan Sengupta, Nikhil Shirolkar, Varun Sivaram, Sarah Soares, Ethan Tiao, Scott Underwood, Daniel Wilson, Frank Sharp, Luke Wainwright, Harry Petty, Scott Wallace, Brandon Records

entry.summary: This article proposes treating GPU AI data centers as grid-interactive assets that dynamically modulate power consumption in response to electricity-grid conditions, integrating grid signals, workload scheduling, and power telemetry. It matters for managing the growing strain AI infrastructure places on power systems.

entry.title: Hitting a Moving Target: Test-Time Adaptation for AI Text Detection under Continual Distribution Shift

author.name: Kevin Ren, Manish Raghavan, Nikhil Garg

entry.summary: This work proposes a test-time adaptation approach for AI text detection that handles continual distribution shifts (adversarial humanization, new LLMs, temporal drift) by exploiting inference-time homogeneity among unlabeled samples via semi-supervised learning. It addresses a persistent practical weakness of supervised detectors.

entry.title: Compositional Behavioral Semantics for State Abstraction in Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Yivan Zhang, Ziyan Luo, Manuel Baltieri

entry.summary: This paper presents a unified compositional framework for specifying and analyzing behavioral structures (value functions, invariants, bisimulation, behavioral metrics) in RL based on local one-step descriptions of dynamics. It establishes a general principle for which structures are provably preserved under state abstraction.

entry.title: Reliability-Asymmetric Spacecraft Autonomy: Co-Designing a Capable Learned GNC Stack with a Verified, Adaptation-Aware Runtime Shield

author.name: Alireza Shojaei

entry.summary: AMPLE-GNC is a three-tier guidance-navigation-control stack for spacecraft autonomy combining a small foundation-model commander that maps natural language to PDDL+, a constraint verifier, and a fault-adaptive controller, all bounded by a runtime shield with machine-checked temporal-logic invariants. It pursues autonomy that is both capable and certifiable for deep-space missions.

entry.title: Evaluating LLMs on Real-World Software Performance Optimization

author.name: Ezgi Sar{\i}kayak, Wenchao Gu, Hesham Ghonim, Chunyang Chen

entry.summary: SWE-Pro is a repository-level benchmark for evaluating LLMs on real-world software performance optimization, derived from 102 expert-written optimizations and capturing trade-offs between execution time and memory under measurement noise and variable inputs. It moves beyond isolated-function, single-metric benchmarks.

entry.title: Steering Vision-Language Models with Joint Sparse Autoencoders

author.name: Huizhen Shu, Xuying Li, Hongxu Lin, Wenjie Sun, Hui Li

entry.summary: JSAE is a Joint Sparse Autoencoder that uses an explicit alignment constraint to jointly factorize pooled vision and language activations into shared interpretable features for vision-language models, enabling controllable cross-modal steering. Applied to LLaVA, it recovers recognizable cross-modal concepts and reveals a layer-dependent steering asymmetry.

entry.title: Space-Efficient Language Generation in the Limit

author.name: Nicolas Flammarion, Chirag Pabbaraju, Hristo Papazov, Miltiadis Stouras, Ola Svensson

entry.summary: This paper develops a theory of language generation in the limit under space-efficiency constraints, where a learner observes adversarial streams and must output hallucination-free hypotheses bounded by memory. It characterizes the strongest possible generation guarantees for memory-bounded learners using DFA-recognized language classes. Matters for theoretical foundations of bounded-resource learning.

entry.title: Enhancing Brain MRI Anomaly Detection and Reasoning with ROI Rethink and Synthetic Data

author.name: Shangkun Li, Jie Xu, Yi Guo, Zeju Li, Yuanyuan Wang

entry.summary: BrReMark introduces explicit region marking into brain MRI diagnosis, where the model generates abnormality hypotheses, grounds them via bounding boxes, then re-examines marked evidence to verify conclusions. Training combines SFT on reasoning trajectories with RL using a composite reward. Matters for auditable, spatially grounded medical VLMs.

entry.title: SpeechEQ: Benchmarking Emotional Intelligence Quotient in Socially Aware Voice Conversational Models

author.name: Liang-Yuan Wu, Zih-Ching Chen, Tongshuang Wu, Chao-Han Huck Yang, Hua Shen

entry.summary: SpeechEQ is a benchmark evaluating emotional intelligence and sociolinguistic reasoning of speech-language models through 2,265 multi-turn dialogues across 15 EQ subscales grounded in EQ-i 2.0 theory. It moves beyond isolated text or passive acoustic perception to active cross-modal dialogue. Matters for socially aware voice conversational AI.

entry.title: Don't Go Breaking My LLM: The Impact of Pruning Attention Layers on Explanation Faithfulness and Confidence Calibration

author.name: Pietro Tropeano, Maria Maistro, Tuukka Ruotsalo, Christina Lioma

entry.summary: This paper studies how pruning attention layers in LLMs affects explanation faithfulness and confidence calibration across five LLMs and eight datasets, an unstudied dimension of attention pruning. While pruned models retain accuracy, their interpretability properties degrade. Matters for trustworthy model compression.

entry.title: Bias-Controlled Primal-Dual Natural Actor-Critic: Optimal Rates for Constrained Multi-Objective Average-Reward RL

author.name: Ankur Naskar, Swetha Ganesh, Vaneet Aggarwal

entry.summary: This paper proposes a bias-controlled primal-dual natural actor-critic achieving optimal rates for constrained multi-objective average-reward RL with concave scalarization, addressing the bias from nonlinearity where expectation of gradient differs from gradient of expectation. It controls bias propagation through actor-critic estimates. Matters for safe multi-objective RL theory.

entry.title: Neural operator-based digital twins for modeling amyloid-$\beta$ and tau propagation and treatment optimization in Alzheimer's disease

author.name: Xiaofeng Xu, Tingting Dan, Zifan Zhou, Bin Li, Guorong Wu, Wenrui Hao

entry.summary: This work builds neural operator-based patient-specific digital twins modeling amyloid-beta and tau propagation on the cortical surface via reaction-diffusion dynamics, learning unknown nonlinear aggregation mechanisms from sparse noisy longitudinal PET data and enabling treatment optimization. Relevant for personalized Alzheimer's modeling.

entry.title: The Interplay of Harness Design and Post-Training in LLM Agents

author.name: Kyungmin Kim, Youngbin Choi, Seoyeon Lee, Suhyeon Jun, Dongwoo Kim, Sangdon Park

entry.summary: This study examines how harness design (tool exposure, descriptions, observation augmentation) interacts with post-training in LLM agents, extending ALFWorld to treat the harness as a controllable dimension and to evaluate under task and tool shifts. It challenges the common treatment of scaffolding as a fixed engineering detail.

entry.title: Improving Neural Network Training by Decoupling the Magnitude and Direction of Weight Vectors

author.name: Alexander H\"agele, Alejandro Hern\'andez-Cano, Atli Kosson, Martin Jaggi

entry.summary: This work proposes decoupling the magnitude and direction of weight vectors during training, noting that standard optimizers like Adam and Muon couple these dynamics so neither is directly governed by the learning rate. It aims to reduce reliance on weight decay and warmup for stable large-scale training.

entry.title: TurboMPC: Fast, Scalable, and Differentiable Model Predictive Control on the GPU

author.name: Gabriel Bravo-Palacios, Jianghan Zhang, Zachary Pestrikov, Brian Plancher, Thomas Lew

entry.summary: TurboMPC is a fully GPU-resident, differentiable model predictive control solver supporting state and control inequality constraints, implicit integrators, cross-time-coupled costs, and slack variables. It combines SQP with an ADMM inner solver and implicit differentiation in a co-designed JAX-CUDA implementation for scalable robotics.

entry.title: Statistically Valid Hyperparameter Selection: From Tuning to Guarantees

author.name: Amirmohammad Farzaneh, Osvaldo Simeone

entry.summary: This monograph presents a unified statistical framework for reliable hyperparameter selection centered on the learn-then-test paradigm, formulating tuning as multiple hypothesis testing over candidate hyperparameters. It provides formal statistical guarantees on reliability and safety, unlike best-effort grid or Bayesian search.

entry.title: Constraint Tax in Open-Weight LLMs: An Empirical Study of Tool Calling Suppression Under Structured Output Constraints

author.name: Fangzheng Li, Aimin Zhang, Chen Lv

entry.summary: Documents a reproducible Tool Suppression phenomenon where open-weight LLMs stop invoking tools when JSON Schema structured-output constraints are simultaneously enabled, despite each capability working independently. It characterizes this constraint tax across multiple model families.

entry.title: Neural Network Quantization by Learning Low-Loss Subspaces

author.name: Vladimir Protsenko, Mikhalina Kharkevich, Alexander Vashchilko, Vladimir Kryzhanovskiy

entry.summary: Proposes neural network quantization by constructing quantized models that lie within low-loss connected subspaces of the full-precision loss landscape, automatically preserving performance. It leverages the geometry of low-loss subspaces to avoid degradation.

entry.title: V-Zero: Answer-Label-Free On-Policy Distillation with Contrastive Evidence Gating for Fine-Grained Visual Reasoning

author.name: Haoxiang Sun, Zhihang Yi, Langxuan Deng, Yuhao Zhou, Peiqi Jia, Jian Zhao, Li Yuan, Jiancheng Lv, Tao Wang

entry.summary: V-Zero performs answer-label-free on-policy distillation with contrastive evidence gating for fine-grained visual reasoning, revisiting OPD as negative-free stop-gradient alignment. It avoids costly RL exploration and textual supervision for MLLM visual reasoning.

entry.title: Graph it first! Enabling Reasoning on Long-form Egocentric Videos through Scene Graphs

author.name: Agnese Taluzzi, Riccardo Santambrogio, Simone Mentasti, Chiara Plizzari, Matteo Matteucci

entry.summary: This work introduces Egocentric Scene Graphs, temporally grounded structured representations, to enable long-form egocentric video question answering without massive frame subsampling. The graph-first approach compresses temporal and contextual information into a form MLLMs can reason over within token limits.

entry.title: A Leakage-Aware Comparative Benchmark of Machine Learning, Deep Learning, and Transformer Models for Reliable Leukemia Detection

author.name: Nisreen Albzour

entry.summary: This paper exposes patient-level data leakage in leukemia classification benchmarks where image-level partitioning inflates performance, and establishes a strict subject-disjoint benchmark across LightGBM, SVMs, EfficientNets, and ViT-Tiny. It evaluates discrimination plus calibration on truly unseen subjects.

entry.title: ASSCG: Just-Right Gating over Chattering for Fast-Slow LLM Planning in Autonomous Driving

author.name: Sining Ang, Yuan Chen, Liu Haiyan, Xuanyao Mao, Jason Bao, Xuliang, Bingchuan Sun, Yan Wang

entry.summary: ASSCG formulates slow-system invocation in fast-slow LLM autonomous-driving planners as a resource-aware sequential decision problem, making frame-level Query/Cache/Drop decisions using an RWKV backbone trained with SFT plus compute-aware RL. It avoids hand-designed triggers that either over-call or mistime the expensive slow system.

entry.title: 1000 Rallies: An Event-Camera Dataset and Real-Time Learned Ball-State Estimation for Robotic Table Tennis

author.name: Raphaela Kreiser, Asude Aydin, Yin Bi, Claudio Fanconi, Peter D\"urr, Naoya Takahashi

entry.summary: This work releases 1000 Rallies, an event-camera dataset for robotic table tennis, and a real-time learned ball-state estimator exploiting microsecond temporal resolution and motion-blur immunity of event cameras. It addresses the absence of large-scale event-based perception datasets for fast sports dynamics.

entry.title: BFMTrack: Latent Sequence Optimization for Physics-Based Motion Tracking with Behavioral Foundation Models

author.name: Thomas Rupf, Agon Serifi, David M\"uller, Sammy Christen, Ruben Grandia, Espen Knoop, Moritz B\"acher

entry.summary: BFMTrack introduces Latent Sequence Optimization to enable physics-based behavioral foundation models to track time-varying motion sequences, which their latent spaces do not natively support. It combines simulation rollouts with policy-gradient updates rather than relying on heuristic moving-window averaging.

entry.title: DynaMOMA: Instantaneous Prediction of Grasp Poses for Mobile Manipulation of Dynamic Objects

author.name: Zhinan Yu, Junyan Xu, Jiazhao Zhang, Zheng Qin, Yijie Tang, Yuhang Huang, Yihan Cao, Zhiyuan Yu, Yongjun Wang, Renjiao Yi, Chenyang Zhu, Kai Xu

entry.summary: DynaMOMA is a dynamic mobile manipulation framework coupling instantaneous grasp-trajectory prediction with whole-body control for grasping moving objects. It uses an anchor-based diffusion model to generate temporally consistent short-horizon grasp trajectories from dynamic observations.

entry.title: Commerge: Communication-Efficient, Robust, and Fast LiDAR Map Merging Framework for Multi-Robot Coordination in Resource-Constrained Scenarios

author.name: Hogyun Kim, Jiwon Choi, Juwon Kim, Geonmo Yang, Seokhwan Jeong, Hyungtae Lim, Younggun Cho

entry.summary: Commerge is a communication-efficient multi-robot LiDAR map merging framework that uses graph-theoretic selective data exchange, reducing inter-robot communication by up to 5000x while maintaining alignment accuracy. Its key insight is that only a small subset of carefully selected scans suffices for robust merging.

entry.title: MAPL: Multi-Objective Preference Learning for Robot Locomotion

author.name: Xiyue Chen, Muhan Lin, Shuyang Shi, Joseph Campbell

entry.summary: MAPL learns robot locomotion rewards from high-level natural-language objectives by prompting an LLM to compare trajectories independently along multiple semantically meaningful criteria, rather than a single overall judgment. This captures competing objectives underlying high-quality locomotion that single-preference methods miss.

entry.title: WOLF-VLA: Whole-Body Humanoid Optimal Locomotion Framework for Vision-Language-Action Learning

author.name: Melya Boukheddimi, Omar Adjali, Daniel Sontag, Frank Kirchner

entry.summary: WOLF-VLA integrates whole-body optimal-control motion synthesis with a large multimodal dataset to train vision-language-action models that generate humanoid locomotion policies from natural-language instructions. It addresses data scarcity and the lack of dynamically consistent demonstrations for contact-rich humanoid locomotion.

entry.title: SA-LIVO: Efficient LiDAR-Inertial-Visual Odometry with Subspace-Aware Degeneracy Handling

author.name: Yinong Cao, Xin He, Yuwei Chen, Shijie Liu, Chunlai Li, Jianyu Wang

entry.summary: SA-LIVO is an efficient LiDAR-inertial-visual odometry method with subspace-aware degeneracy handling, addressing the direction-dependent structure of the joint information matrix rather than modality-level degeneracy detection. It prevents visual residuals from corrupting pose directions where LiDAR is well-constrained.

entry.title: MIL-LC: A Robust Magnetometer-Inertial-LiDAR Fusion Multimodal Localization Framework

author.name: Qiyang Lyu, Zhenyu Wu, Wei Wang, Hongming Shen, Danwei Wang

entry.summary: StairMaster is a three-stage RL framework for quadruped locomotion on risky hollow stairs, integrating cross-attention to extract structure from noisy depth and a spatial-aware recurrent unit for spatio-temporal memory against perception blind spots. It includes a high-fidelity sim-to-real depth sensor modeling pipeline to bridge the perception gap.

entry.title: Omni-Perception Policy Optimization for Multimodal Emotion Reasoning

author.name: Zhiyuan Han, Beier Zhu, Wenwen Tong, Pengyang Shao, Peipei Song, Xinyi Wang, Jiangnan Chen, Lewei Lu, Xun Yang

entry.summary: Proposes OPPO, an RL framework for multimodal emotion reasoning that uses an Omni-Perception Reward decomposing reasoning into visual, acoustic, and emotion cues plus a perception loss to reduce cross-modal hallucination. Targets faithful omni-modal understanding.

entry.title: Failure Modes of Large Language Models on Research-Level Mathematics: A Taxonomy and an Empirical Characterisation

author.name: Arnesh Banerjee, Ayushi Bhattacharjee

entry.summary: Builds a taxonomy of LLM failure modes on research-level mathematics (citation fabrication, premise smuggling, silent reformulation, compatibility gaps) and audits Gemini 2.5 Flash proofs, arguing RAG does not fix these. Characterizes confident wrong proofs.

entry.title: Reliable Conformal Prediction for Ordinal Classification Using the Ranked Probability Score

author.name: Stefan Haas, Luca Killmaier, Alireza Javanmardi, Eyke H\"ullermeier

entry.summary: Introduces a conformal prediction method for ordinal classification using the ranked probability score as a nonconformity measure, yielding median-centered contiguous prediction sets that respect ordinal error severity. Improves uncertainty quantification for ordinal tasks.

entry.title: Uncertainty-aware reinforcement learning for chemical language models

author.name: Borja Medina, Jon Paul Janet

entry.summary: Introduces uncertainty-aware reinforcement learning for chemical language models in de novo molecular design, accounting for scoring-function prediction uncertainty to avoid exploring poorly-supported high-scoring regions. Stabilizes RL-based molecular optimization.

entry.title: SoK: AI Secure Code Generation: Progress, Pitfalls, and Paths Forward

author.name: Rupam Patir, Keyan Guo, Haipeng Cai, Hongxin Hu

entry.summary: This Systematization of Knowledge paper surveys AI secure code generation across prompting, fine-tuning, RL, and agentic workflows, introducing a three-level framework measuring natural-language understanding, code-level actuation, and security outcomes. It identifies why substantial security failures persist.

entry.title: Beyond Visual Forensics: Auditing Multimodal Robustness for Synthetic Medical Image Detection

author.name: Ching-Hao Chiu, Hao-Wei Chung, Gelei Xu, Xueyang Li, Pin-Yu Chen, John Kheir, Meysam Ghaffari, Carlos Morato, Ahmed Abbasi, Yiyu Shi

entry.summary: This work uncovers a multimodal vulnerability in synthetic medical image detection: when given both an image and accompanying records, VLMs may overweight text context such that the same image gets different authenticity judgments depending on its text. It audits robustness for combined image-record inputs increasingly used in clinical deployment.

entry.title: LibEvoBench: Probing Temporal Knowledge Stratification in Code Generation Models

author.name: Daniele Cipollone, Sergey Titov, Maliheh Izadi, Egor Bogomolov, Arie van Deursen

entry.summary: LibEvoBench probes temporal knowledge stratification in code-generation models, evaluating whether LLMs can maintain knowledge of multiple library API versions rather than only the latest, introducing the Software Evolution Understanding Score metric. It reveals anachronistic API errors from temporally mixed training corpora.

entry.title: Weave of Formal Thought

author.name: Alexandre Bouayad

entry.summary: WoFT (Weave of Formal Thought) is a paradigm that formally guarantees syntactic validity of LLM code output while letting models learn which hierarchical grammatical structure to expose, supporting context-sensitive lexing and maximal-munch tokenization. It addresses limitations of rigid constrained-decoding frameworks. Relevant for reliable code generation.

entry.title: A Zeroth-Order Deep Learning Method for Fully Nonlinear Parabolic Partial Differential Equations with Unknown Coefficients

author.name: Yanwei Jia, Du Ouyang, Huy\^en Pham, Xun Yu Zhou

entry.summary: This work introduces a zeroth-order deep learning method for solving high-dimensional fully nonlinear parabolic PDEs with unknown coefficients, avoiding repeated automatic differentiation instabilities and not requiring explicit dynamics knowledge. It uses simulators with a representing-then-learning approach. Relevant for scientific ML and continuous-time RL.

entry.title: Forget to Improve: On-Device LLM-Agent Continual Learning via Budget-Curated Memory

author.name: Beining Wu, Zihao Ding, Jun Huang, Yanxiao Zhao

entry.summary: This work proposes a budget-curated memory governance approach for on-device LLM agents that improve via retrieved experience rather than weight updates, using a net-value-per-byte score where the budget acts as curator scoring entries as value minus harm. It treats memory poisoning as a governance problem. Relevant for safe, efficient on-device agents.

entry.title: The Gentle Collapse: Distributional Metrics for Continual Learning

author.name: Ahmed Anwar, Andreas Wagner, Federico Raue, Tobias Nauen, Andreas Dengel

entry.summary: This paper introduces six softmax-derived metrics for continual learning that characterize catastrophic forgetting continuously rather than via discrete accuracy collapse, spanning true-label rank, predictive confidence, and distributional divergence. It shows these metrics carry information where accuracy saturates, even at zero accuracy. Matters for finer-grained forgetting analysis and mitigation.

entry.title: Black-Box Assisted Regression: Phase Transitions and Minimax Optimality

author.name: Yan Zhou

entry.summary: This paper provides a finite-sample minimax analysis of black-box assisted nonparametric regression, where a learner uses a fixed foundation-model predictor as a possibly biased reference. It characterizes a phase transition in risk and proposes a Safe Residual Estimator that learns corrections around the black-box prediction.

entry.title: Tensorion: A Tensor-Aware Generalization of the Muon Optimizer

author.name: Vladimir Bogachev, Vladimir Aletov, Alexander Molozhavenko, Sergei Kudriashov, Maxim Rakhuba

entry.summary: Tensorion generalizes the Muon optimizer from matrices to higher-order tensors, performing steepest descent under a carefully chosen tensor norm constraint via a linear minimization oracle over a tensor norm ball. It aims to exploit multilinear weight structure ignored by vector-based optimizers like Adam.

entry.title: RAS: Measuring LLM Safety Through Refusal Alignment

author.name: Chang-Chieh Huang, Yan-Lun Chen, Chia-Mu Yu, Wei-Bin Lee

entry.summary: SafeVec is a white-box LLM safety evaluation procedure that measures safety from internal representations rather than generated outputs, extracting layer-wise refusal directions from a reference model and scoring whether a target model's hidden states align with them. It offers a cheaper, judge-independent alternative to output-level safety evaluation.

entry.title: Beyond Function Calling: Benchmarking Tool-Using Agents under Tool-Environment Unreliability

author.name: Yang Tian, Zhengpeng Shi, Bo Zhao

entry.summary: Introduces ToolBench-X, a benchmark evaluating tool-using LLM agents under recoverable reliability hazards like specification errors and unstable tool environments. It moves beyond the assumption of clean, trustworthy tool environments.

entry.title: Chorus II: Cross-Request Sparsity Reuse for Efficient Image-to-Video Generation

author.name: Hao Liu, Chenghuan Huang, Hao Liu, Xing Cai, Chen Li, Ziyang Ma, Jing Lyu, Nong Xiao, Jiangsu Du

entry.summary: Chorus II accelerates serving of image-to-video diffusion models by reusing sparse attention patterns across similar requests as request-conditioned priors, with optional feature reuse. It exploits redundancy in real I2V workloads for efficient large-scale deployment.

entry.title: MRI2Rep: Autoregressive Structured Report Generation for 3D Liver MRI

author.name: Xinran Li, Junlin Yang, Annabella Shewarega, Zongwei Zhou, Julius Chapiro, James S. Duncan, Lawrence H. Staib

entry.summary: MRI2Rep is an autoregressive framework for structured report generation from 3D liver MRI, with a module that canonicalizes free-text reports into closed-vocabulary diagnostic sequences without lesion-level annotations. It substantially outperforms adapted medical VLM baselines on a 10-year cohort.

entry.title: PRISM: Feed-Forward Single-Image 3D Reconstruction via Geometric Warp-Residual Modeling

author.name: Zhijie Zheng, Xinhao Xiang, Jiawei Zhang

entry.summary: PRISM is a feed-forward single-image 3D reconstruction framework that decomposes multi-view latent prediction into a parameter-free geometric forward-warping prior and a learned residual correction, avoiding slow iterative diffusion sampling. It enables fast practical deployment.

entry.title: SSMNBench: Diagnosing Image-based Cross-View Human-Object Understanding via Single-View Sufficiency and Multi-View Necessity

author.name: Tianchen Guo, Chen Liu, Ling Chen, Xin Yu

entry.summary: SSMNBench is a diagnostic benchmark of 3,300 QA pairs separating Single-View Sufficiency from Multi-View Necessity to test whether MLLMs genuinely fuse cross-view evidence rather than tolerating distraction. It perturbs view availability across 17 SOTA MLLMs.

entry.title: MIMFlow: Integrating Masked Image Modeling with Normalizing Flows for End-to-End Image Generation

author.name: Yang Chen, Xiaowei Xu, Shuai Wang, Xinwen Zhang, Qiushi Guo, Tiezheng Ge, Limin Wang

entry.summary: MIMFlow unifies masked image modeling with normalizing flows for end-to-end image generation, using a VAE encoder to infer semantic latents so the flow focuses on generation while MIM handles semantics. This decouples low-level pixel fidelity from high-level structure that pure flows struggle to capture.

entry.title: Invariant Kalman filtering for extended pose estimation in multi-IMU articulated rigid-body systems

author.name: Sven Goffin, C\'edric Schwartz, Silv\`ere Bonnabel, Olivier Br\"uls, Pierre Sacr\'e

entry.summary: This work introduces the relative L-extended pose, a Lie group representation enabling invariant extended Kalman filtering for orientation, velocity, and position estimation in multi-IMU articulated rigid-body systems. It yields group-affine dynamics and incorporates joint kinematic constraints, an open problem for invariant filtering of kinematic trees.

entry.title: Decoupling Semantics and Geometric Grounding: Spatial Visual Prompts for Language-Conditioned Imitation Learning

author.name: Yanzhe Tang, Xinyu Shao, Yuxuan Hu, Siyu Chen, Bowen Yang, Yajun Gao, Tongtong Cao, Xiu Li, Long Zeng

entry.summary: SVP-IL decouples semantic reasoning from spatial control in vision-language-action manipulation by extracting zero-shot geometric masks from foundation models and injecting them as spatial visual prompts into a continuous action generator. This addresses the alignment bottleneck of monolithic VLA models in data-constrained imitation learning.

entry.title: HEART: Coordination of Heterogeneous Expert Agents for Physically Grounded Robotic Task Planning

author.name: Junho Lee, Seabin Lee, Wonjong Lee, Nayoung Kim, Moonjeong Kang, Changjoo Nam

entry.summary: HEART is a heterogeneous multi-LLM framework for physically grounded robotic task planning that decomposes instructions into atomic reasoning tasks allocated to role-specialized expert agents under a token budget. It validates capability, reachability, and logical order to produce feasible plans where monolithic LLM planners fail.

entry.title: SAGE-Nav: Leveraging LLM Planning and Alignment Fusion for Hierarchical Scene Graph-Guided Navigation

author.name: Hao Su, Yuehao Huang, Yukai Ma, Yong Liu, Jiajun Lv

entry.summary: SAGE-Nav is a hierarchical object-goal navigation framework integrating LLM planning with dynamic scene graphs, decoupling asynchronous global semantic planning from a high-frequency reactive control loop. The LLM decomposes instructions into grounded waypoints translated into dense multimodal guidance.

entry.title: Event-Adaptive Motion Planning with Distilled Vision-Language Model in Safety-Critical Situations

author.name: Zhenwei Huang, Changsheng You, Shuai Wang, Chao Zhou, Wei Xu, Yi Gong

entry.summary: EAMP is an efficient framework for VLM-based robot navigation in safety-critical scenarios, using a prompt-configurable semantic event trigger to selectively invoke a distilled VLM rather than calling it every control step. This avoids the destabilizing latency of frequent VLM queries while retaining commonsense reasoning for dynamic-agent hazards.

entry.title: Mixture-of-Experts RL for Fault-Tolerant Legged Locomotion

author.name: Giulio Turrisi, Ozan Pali, Luca Oneto, Claudio Semini

entry.summary: This work proposes a fault-aware modular control architecture for legged locomotion that uses fault-diagnosis information to activate specialized control experts associated with distinct actuator failure modes. It shows explicit fault-conditioned modular policies outperform monolithic policies of comparable size for fault-tolerant locomotion.

entry.title: Offline Multi-agent Continual Cooperation via Skill Partition and Reuse

author.name: Yuchen Xiao, Lei Yuan, Ruiqi Xue, Tieyue Yin, Yang Yu

entry.summary: Proposes COMAD, a framework for continual offline multi-agent skill discovery via skill partition and reuse to avoid catastrophic forgetting and plasticity loss in sequential cooperative tasks. Addresses exponentially growing skill spaces.

entry.title: Confidence Sequences for Online Statistical Model Checking of Markov Decision Processes

author.name: Konstantin Kueffner, Tobias Meggendorfer, Maximilian Weininger, Patrick Wienh\"oft

entry.summary: Provides correct and more efficient confidence-sequence methods for online statistical model checking of Markov decision processes with unknown transition probabilities. Improves statistical guarantees for verification of probabilistic systems.

entry.title: Holographic Memory for Zero-Shot Compositional Reasoning in Knowledge Graphs: A Mechanistic Study of Where and Why It Fails

author.name: Randhir Kumar

entry.summary: A mechanistic study of holographic reduced representations and Hopfield cleanup for zero-shot compositional multi-hop reasoning in knowledge graphs, finding they are good single-hop retrievers but fail at composition. Diagnoses where and why binding-based memory breaks down.

entry.title: Enhancing Clinician Decision-Making via Uncertainty-Aware Multi-Expert Fusion for Stroke Rehabilitation

author.name: Tamim Ahmed, Thanassis Rikakis

entry.summary: Presents xAARA, an uncertainty-aware multi-expert fusion engine that estimates ARAT stroke-rehabilitation assessments from multi-view video with calibrated uncertainty and explanations, designed to augment rather than replace clinicians. Preserves movement-quality detail clinicians need.

entry.title: Silent Failures in Physics-Informed Neural Networks: Parameter Poisoning and the Limits of Loss-Based Validation

author.name: David McShannon, Nicholas Dietrich

entry.summary: This paper shows that physics-informed neural networks can reach low training loss while producing physically incorrect solutions when the encoded PDE parameters are misspecified, undermining loss-based validation. It frames the parameter perturbation as a sensitivity analysis revealing silent failure modes.

entry.title: Decoupling Reconnaissance and Exploitation: Measuring the Capability Boundaries of LLM-Based Web Penetration Testing

author.name: Liwei Yu, Shuo Li, Ming Zhou, Ge Chu, Yan Guo

entry.summary: This paper introduces a two-stage decoupled evaluation framework that separates reconnaissance from exploitation in LLM-based web penetration testing, using ground-truth injection across 70 vulnerability testbeds to isolate true exploitation ability from reconnaissance error cascading. It more accurately characterizes the capability boundaries of five penetration-testing agents.

entry.title: Conformal Recovery-Deadline Certificates for Runtime Assurance of Adapting Controllers

author.name: Alireza Shojaei

entry.summary: This paper introduces conformal recovery-deadline certificates for runtime assurance of online-adapting controllers, providing a distribution-free finite-sample upper bound on recovery time so that safety shields do not prematurely trip during a capable controller's bounded recovery transient. It corrects the pathology of standard latching rules for adaptive controllers.

entry.title: Is GraphRAG Needed? From Basic RAG to Graph-/Agentic Solutions with Context Optimization

author.name: Long Chen, Ryan Razkenari, Yuxuan Zhou, Yuan Tian, Rahul Ghosh, Venkatesh Pappakrishnan, Disha Ahuja, Vidya Sagar Ravipati

entry.summary: This paper introduces a framework to evaluate and compare RAG variants (regular, GraphRAG, Modular, Agentic) on semi-structured knowledge bases across nine standardized scenarios, addressing when and how to use advanced RAG. It provides implementations and experiments spanning simple retrieval to hybrid text-graph and agent-graph integration.

entry.title: Can Trustless Agents Be Trusted? An Empirical Study of the ERC-8004 Decentralized AI Agent Ecosystem

author.name: Xihan Xiong, Zelin Li, Wei Wei, Qin Wang, William Knottenbelt, Zhipeng Wang

entry.summary: This is the first empirical study of the ERC-8004 decentralized AI agent trust protocol across Ethereum, BSC, and Base, examining whether its on-chain identity, reputation, and validation registries provide a trustworthy basis for agent decision-making. It questions whether trustless agents can actually be trusted. Relevant for autonomous agent economies.

entry.title: TriViewBench: Controlled Complexity Scaling for Multi-View Structural Reasoning in MLLMs

author.name: Yu-Yang Chen, Lan-Zhe Guo

entry.summary: TriViewBench is a controlled three-view visual reasoning benchmark from synthetic 3D scenes with parameterized object count and occlusion, containing 1,923 scenes and 14K QA pairs across complexity levels. Evaluating 18 MLLMs reveals an identical capability hierarchy across all models. Matters for understanding multimodal structural reasoning limits.

entry.title: Towards Scalable Multi-Task Reinforcement Learning with Large Decision Models

author.name: Thibaut Kulak

entry.summary: LDM-v0 is a Large Decision Model, a multi-task multi-modal transformer policy trained offline on trajectories from thousands of heterogeneous RL environments via supervised next-action prediction. It investigates whether a unified policy can scale across diverse environments. Relevant for scalable generalist RL agents.

entry.title: Latent Block-Diffusion Temporal Point Processes: A Semi-Autoregressive Framework for Asynchronous Event Sequence Generation

author.name: Shuai Zhang, Yancheng Chen, Chuan Zhou, Yang Liu, Xixun Lin, Xiangyu Zhao, Jun Zhu, Zhi-Ming Ma

entry.summary: LBDTPP is a semi-autoregressive temporal point process framework using latent block diffusion for variable-length asynchronous event sequence generation, combining autoregression over event blocks with non-autoregressive diffusion within blocks. It addresses error accumulation in autoregressive methods and fixed-length limits of diffusion. Relevant for event sequence modeling in social, medical, and financial domains.

entry.title: What's in an Earth Embedding? An Explainability Analysis of Location Encoders

author.name: Livia Betti, Sebastian Ricke, Ivica Obadic, Adam J. Stewart, Esther Rolf

entry.summary: This explainability analysis decomposes geographic implicit neural representation embeddings into human-interpretable features including sparse latent concepts via sparse autoencoders, natural language concepts, and visual features. It provides tools to audit what location encoders capture. Matters for trustworthy geospatial foundation representations.

entry.title: Beyond One-Size-Fits-All: Diagnosis-Driven Online Reinforcement Learning with Offline Priors

author.name: Guozheng Ma, Lu Li, Zilin Wang, Pierre-Luc Bacon, Dacheng Tao

entry.summary: This work introduces diagnosis-driven online RL that adaptively manages offline priors whose validity varies across deployments and shifts during training. It argues no single prior-management strategy is universally optimal and proposes diagnosing prior quality to guide adaptation.

entry.title: RevengeBench: Reverse Engineering Code-Space Policies from Behavioral Experiments

author.name: Babak Rahmani, Sebastian Dziadzio, Joschka Str\"uber, Sergio Hern\'andez-Guti\'errez, Matthias Bethge

entry.summary: RevengeBench is a benchmark testing whether a learner can reconstruct an agent's hidden decision program as executable code from behavioral traces, and how much controlled experimentation improves reconstruction. It comprises 75 LLM-generated Elo-calibrated policies across five game environments.

entry.title: Dustin: Draft-Augmented Sparse Verification for Efficient Long-Context Generation with Speculative Decoding

author.name: WenHung Lee, Jian-Jia Chen, Xiaolin Lin, Pei-Shuo Wang, Chi-Chih Chang, Chun-Che Yang, Ning-Chi Huang, Grace Li Zhang, Kai-Chiang Wu

entry.summary: Dustin is a sparse verification framework for long-context speculative decoding that integrates draft-model lookahead signals with target-model historical attention to identify critical tokens, reducing the KV-cache loading bottleneck. It addresses failures of static eviction and dynamic selection in the verification path.

entry.title: Sample complexity of unbalanced entropic OT

author.name: Francisco Andrade, Gabriel Peyr\'e, Clarice Poon

entry.summary: This paper studies the sample complexity of entropic unbalanced optimal transport at the level of the optimal coupling rather than just the scalar transport value. It develops translation-based analysis bridging entropic regularization and unbalanced relaxations for noisy empirical data.

entry.title: Gaussian Mean Field Variational Inference can Overestimate Predictive Variance

author.name: James Odgers, Ben Riegler, Siddharth Swaroop, Vincent Fortuin

entry.summary: This paper shows that Mean Field Variational Inference, while underestimating posterior variance in parameter space, can overestimate predictive variance compared to the exact posterior—particularly in directions where training data concentrates. It analyzes this via conjugate Bayesian Linear Regression, refining the common characterization of MFVI.

entry.title: Detect, Unlearn, Restore: Defending Text Summarization Models Against Data Poisoning

author.name: Poojitha Thota, Shirin Nilizadeh

entry.summary: Proposes a detect-unlearn-restore framework defending summarization models against fine-tuning data poisoning, using training influence to detect poisoned pairs in white-box settings. It addresses persistent summarization failures induced by adversarial fine-tuning data.

entry.title: SEMIR: Topology-Preserving Graph Minors for Thin-Structure Segmentation

author.name: Luke James Miller, Yugyung Lee

entry.summary: SEMIR replaces the pixel lattice with a parameterized graph minor whose contraction map preserves thin-structure connectivity for segmenting power lines, cracks, and lane markings. It enables full-resolution inference by collapsing pixels into boundary-aligned supernodes.

entry.title: OrthoTrack: Continuous 6-DoF UAV Trajectory Estimation Anchored in Public Orthophotos

author.name: Oussema Dhaouadi, Zuria Bauer, Johannes Michael Meier, Olaf Wysocki, Marc Pollefeys, Daniel Cremers

entry.summary: OrthoTrack is a training-free system estimating continuous 6-DoF UAV trajectories using only public orthophotos and surface models as a map prior, producing absolute metric poses without GPS. It avoids drift and up-to-scale ambiguity of visual odometry.

entry.title: Disease-Centric Vision-Language Pretraining with Hybrid Visual Encoding for 3D Computed Tomography

author.name: Bowen Shi, Weiwei Cao, Ruifeng Yuan, Wanxing Chang, Wenrui Dai, Hongkai Xiong, Ling Zhang, Jianpeng Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes a vision-language pretraining framework for 3D CT with a CNN-ViT hybrid encoder and disease-level contrastive learning using learnable query tokens to extract disease-specific semantics from radiology reports. It addresses inefficient backbones and coarse alignment in 3D medical VLP.

entry.title: FeVOS: Foresight Expression Video Object Segmentation

author.name: Kehan Lan, Kaining Ying, Henghui Ding

entry.summary: FeVOS introduces Foresight Expression Video Object Segmentation, a task requiring pre-decisive spatio-temporal reasoning to segment objects relevant to future events from observed frames. It enables reasoning about upcoming actions, e.g., which tool will be used next.

entry.title: Towards a Dynamic and Fixed-budget Memory Bank for Efficient Streaming Video Understanding

author.name: Baiyang Song, Yuli Lin, Qiong Wu, Tao Chen, Jun Peng, Xiao Chen, Yiyi Zhou, Rongrong Ji

entry.summary: CausalMem is a training-free approach for streaming video understanding that builds a dynamic, fixed-budget memory bank by estimating visual-token redundancy and updating memory to maximize retained information. It mimics brain-like memory management for ever-increasing frames.

entry.title: Falcon: Functional Assembly and Language for Compositional Reasoning in X-ray

author.name: Yonathan Michael, Mohamad Alansari, Natnael Takele, Andreas Henschel, Naoufel Werghi

entry.summary: Falcon formalizes compositional threat reasoning for X-ray baggage screening, modeling risk as a relational property of grounded regions (e.g., battery plus detonator plus charge) rather than independent detections. It abstracts segmentation-aware features into a structured safety state.

entry.title: In-context Region-based Drag: Drag Any Region to Any Shape

author.name: Jiacheng Sui, Tianyu Hao, Bingjie Gao, Li Niu, Guangtao Zhai

entry.summary: ICRDrag introduces in-context region-based image dragging with diffusion models, accepting a source image plus source and target region masks to produce edited results, addressing the ambiguity of point-based drag. It adds attention regularization to maintain image-mask consistency and source-target correspondence.

entry.title: DomainShuttle: Freeform Open Domain Subject-driven Text-to-video Generation

author.name: Nan Chen, Yiyang Cai, Rongchang Xie, Junwen Pan, Cheng Chen, Weinan Jia, Zhuowei Chen, Wen Zhou, Zhenbang Sun, Wenhan Luo

entry.summary: DomainShuttle tackles open-domain subject-driven text-to-video generation that flexibly handles both in-domain fidelity preservation and cross-domain editability such as new styles or attributes. It aims to shuttle between domains rather than maximizing subject fidelity at the cost of adaptability.

entry.title: An Integrated Hardware-Software Design for Low-Data Spatial Defect Detection in Robotic Visual Inspection with Hybrid Optoelectronic Neural Networks

author.name: Chaoqing Tang, Jiaxuan Li, Huanze Zhuang, Guiyun Tian, Chao Wang, Yihao Ouyang, Wenzhong Liu

entry.summary: This work presents a hardware-software integrated optoelectronic architecture for low-data robotic visual inspection, reconfiguring a digital micromirror device as a physical optical convolution layer and using compressed sensing to reduce data volume. Natural language descriptions replace laborious manual defect-shape annotation.

entry.title: AISPO: Enhancing Depth Reliability for Robotic Manipulation of Non-Lambertian Objects via Affine-Invariant Shape Prior

author.name: Zhiming Chen, Linfang Zheng, Kun Zhang, Hyung Jin Chang, Wei Zhang, Hongyu Yu, Hua Chen

entry.summary: AISPO is a depth-completion framework for robotic manipulation of non-Lambertian objects like transparent or specular surfaces, combining multi-scale RGB-D fusion with an affine-invariant shape prior. It emphasizes physical plausibility and structural integrity of completed depth rather than just average accuracy.

entry.title: DSP-SLAM++: A Unified Framework for Multi-Class, High-Fidelity Object SLAM in the Wild

author.name: Ahmad Kourani, Ghina Daoud, Daniel Asmar, Imad Elhajj

entry.summary: DSP-SLAM++ extends object-aware SLAM with an asynchronous mapping pipeline and monocular fisheye-LiDAR sensor fusion to achieve real-time, multi-class, high-fidelity object models. It reduces maximum object processing latency by up to 70 percent while supporting challenging high-rate sensor suites in the wild.

entry.title: Causality-Based Parametric Control Barrier Function for Safe Multi-Vehicle Interaction

author.name: Yiwei Lyu, Caleb Chang, John M. Dolan

entry.summary: This paper studies causality-based parametric control barrier functions for safe multi-vehicle interaction, modeling neighboring vehicles' controllers while disentangling inter-vehicle influence to determine behavioral causality. It avoids assuming fully cooperative homogeneous vehicles for adaptive safe control.

entry.title: RigPI: Dynamic Parameter Identification of Rigid Body via VLM-Seeded Differentiable Simulation

author.name: Xincheng He, Rongrong Zhang, Wei Jiang, Wenqiang Xu

entry.summary: RigPI identifies dynamic parameters of rigid and multi-link bodies during robot-object interaction by integrating vision-language semantic priors, force-torque and motion data within a differentiable simulation pipeline. A VLM seeds informed initialization to overcome sensing noise and limited priors for digital-twin construction.

entry.title: Spatio-Temporal Retrieval-based Priors for Adaptive Computational Teaching in Driving

author.name: Deepak Edakkattil Gopinath, Xiongyi Cui, Jonathan DeCastro, Avinash Balachandran, Guy Rosman

entry.summary: This work proposes an imitation-learning computational model for adaptive coaching in high-performance driving, with a temporal reasoning module that reasons over interaction history under low-data regimes using nearest-neighbor retrieval and cross-attention priors. It captures long-term student learning that local context-only methods miss.

entry.title: One Body, Two Minds: Variable Autonomy Approach for a Co-embodied Robotic Hand

author.name: Piotr Koczy, Yuchong Zhang, Danica Kragic, Michael C. Welle

entry.summary: This work introduces co-embodiment with variable autonomy, where a human and a robot share a single physical body (a wearable robotic hand) and operate at different autonomy levels across task phases. A learning-from-demonstration visuomotor diffusion policy enables autonomous grasping while ceding control during actuation.

entry.title: Learning Asynchronous Upper-body Task-space Trajectory Tracking Policy for Humanoid Robots

author.name: Yumeng Liu, Dongqi Wang, Jiyu Yu, Yijun Fan, Rong Xiong, Yue Wang

entry.summary: This work proposes an asynchronous upper-body task-space trajectory tracking framework for humanoids, addressing the temporal mismatch between sparse low-rate planner outputs and high-frequency controllers. A teacher-student distilled policy conditioned on cached future trajectories with a sliding-window reward reduces frame drift without explicit frame estimation.

entry.title: TacVerse: A Multi-Sensor Dataset and Benchmark for Cross-Sensor Vision-Based Tactile Perception

author.name: Lan Wei, Gurmeher Khurana, Sirine Bhouri, Wenhao Hong, Zeyuan Xin, Qingzheng Cong, Wen Fan, Yanzheng Xiang, Dandan Zhang

entry.summary: This work recovers 3D in-plane inclination of nearby slender vertical objects from FMCW radar shadow effects, exploiting how vehicle chassis occlude radar rays to form consistent geometric shadows. It uses a closed-form analytical mapping to overcome radar's elevation collapse limitation in adverse conditions.

entry.title: Diagnosing and Mitigating Compounding Failures in Agentic Persuasion via Taxonomic Strategy Retrieval

author.name: Pradyumna Narayana, Sana Ayromlou, Purvi Sehgal

entry.summary: Identifies semantic leakage in RAG as a trigger for compounding failures in persuasion-oriented agents and proposes Taxonomic Strategy RAG that routes strategies through a categorical bottleneck to decouple structure from content. Targets reliability of multi-step subjective agentic tasks.

entry.title: BrainAgent: A Large Language Model-Driven Multi-Agent Framework for Autonomous Brain Signal Understanding

author.name: Yangxuan Zhou, Sha Zhao, Jiquan Wang, Shijian Li, Gang Pan

entry.summary: Presents BrainAgent, an LLM-driven multi-agent framework for autonomous brain-signal understanding aimed at lowering expertise barriers and supporting long-horizon BCI workflows. Targets democratization of brain signal analysis.

entry.title: LLM Evolution as an Industry-Scale Ecosystem: A Lifecycle Perspective on Continual Learning

author.name: Hao Jiang, Enneng Yang, Guojie Zhu, Yibin Chen, Yunkun Xu, Zifu Kou, Jiayi Li, Chong Chen, Zhao Cao, Li Shen

entry.summary: Reframes industrial continual learning for LLMs as a closed-loop versioned ecosystem problem where updates propagate hierarchically across model families and applications, identifying core challenges. A survey/perspective on real-world continual learning needs.

entry.title: Are Tabular Foundation Models Robust to Realistic Query Distribution Shifts in Microbiome Data?

author.name: Giulia Perciballi, Ahmad Fall, Federica Granese, Edi Prifti, Jean-Daniel Zucker

entry.summary: Benchmarks robustness of tabular foundation models on gut microbiome data under biologically inspired perturbations in an in-context learning setting, isolating robustness beyond shortcut features via controlled perturbation strategies. Evaluates TFM reliability under realistic shifts.

entry.title: TokenMinds: Pretrained User Tokens and Embeddings for User Understanding in Large Recommender Systems

author.name: Qingyun Liu, Bo Yan, Yang Liu, Yuji Roh, Ekansh Sharma, Likang Yin, Emma Olowo, Min-hsuan Tsai, Yuxuan Li, Diego Uribe, Saksham Aggarwal, Siqi Wu, Yuan Hao, Vikas Kedigehalli, Lukasz Heldt, Lichan Hong, Li Wei, Xinyang Yi

entry.summary: TokenMinds is an industrial-scale system that extends Semantic ID-based tokenization from items to users in recommender systems, producing discrete user tokens grounded to item attributes. It addresses limitations of dense user embeddings and text-based user tokens for capturing sequential behavior.

entry.title: Supervised Post-training of Speech Foundation Models for Robust Adaptation in Speech Deepfake Detection

author.name: Zihan Pan, Sailor Hardik, Jinyang Wu

entry.summary: This work proposes a mix-frame post-training strategy for speech foundation models that creates localized spoof perturbations and uses frame-level supervision to learn local inconsistencies for deepfake detection. It achieves state-of-the-art EER on ASVspoof5 and balanced robustness across distortion conditions.

entry.title: From Sounds to Scenes: A Benchmark for Evaluating Context-Aware Auditory Scene Understanding in Large Audio Language Models

author.name: Pengfei Zhang, Hoang H Nguyen, Kazi Shaharair Sharif, Yutong Song, Wenjun Huang, Henry Peng Zou, Pinxin Liu, Honghui Xu, Amir M. Rahmani

entry.summary: This paper introduces CASU and an accompanying benchmark to evaluate whether large audio language models can interpret holistic auditory scenes by integrating co-occurring speech, acoustic events, and background sounds, rather than evaluating each layer in isolation. It reveals a gap in contextual scene understanding.

entry.title: STEB: A Speech-to-Speech Translation Expressiveness Benchmark for Evaluating Beyond Translation Fidelity

author.name: Sitong Cheng, Weizhen Bian, Songjun Cao, Jin Li, Bei Liu, Chunyang Jiang, Yike Zhang, Weihao Wu, Yiming Li, Chi-Min Chan, Long Ma, Wei Xue

entry.summary: STEB is a 32.6-hour Chinese-English benchmark for speech-to-speech translation that evaluates expressiveness dimensions (emotion, scenario style, nonverbal vocalizations) alongside standard fidelity, speaker similarity, and duration alignment. It uses a caption-based approach to circumvent the impracticality of reference-based expressiveness evaluation.

entry.title: When Do Conservation Laws Survive Learned Representations? Certified Horizons for Latent World Models

author.name: Hongbo Wang

entry.summary: This work asks when conservation laws remain certifiable after a model learns latent representations, deriving certified horizons that bound how many rollout steps stay on a physical invariant's level set. It certifies the decoded physical invariant rather than learned latent quantities. Matters for trustworthy physical world models.

entry.title: Speculative Decoding at Temperature Zero: A Scoped Safety-Invariance Screen with a 48,072-Sample Expansion

author.name: Sahil Kadadekar

entry.summary: TAIS is a behavioral-equivalence screen testing whether speculative decoding at temperature zero lets draft-model behavior leak into safety-scored outputs, using byte-identity, TOST equivalence, and Cohen's h thresholds over 48K samples. It addresses a concrete safety question about acceleration techniques. Matters for safe inference optimization.

entry.title: Variational Inference via Entropic Transport Descent

author.name: Vincent Pacelli, Akash Ratheesh, Evangelos Theodorou

entry.summary: Entropic Transport Descent reframes particle-based variational inference as an entropy-regularized optimal transport problem solved via Sinkhorn iterations, addressing variance and mode collapse in high-dimensional and multimodal targets. It provides global transport structure absent from kernel-based methods like SVGD.

entry.title: Is Variational Monte Carlo Robust? Sharp Moment Thresholds and Heavy-tailed Stochastic Optimization

author.name: Philipp Grohs, Davide Nobile

entry.summary: This work analyzes the robustness of Variational Monte Carlo, showing the stochastic optimization is governed by the nodal geometry of the wave function which determines integrability of local energy and gradient estimators. It establishes sharp moment thresholds and heavy-tailed behavior for ansatz classes including Slater-Jastrow wave functions relevant to neural approaches like FermiNet.

entry.title: Extreme Meta-Classification for Large-Scale Zero-Shot Retrieval

author.name: Sachin Yadav, Deepak Saini, Anirudh Buvanesh, Bhawna Paliwal, Kunal Dahiya, Siddarth Asokan, Yashoteja Prabhu, Jian Jiao, Manik Varma

entry.summary: This paper develops extreme meta-classification for large-scale zero-shot retrieval, combining the representation capacity of per-item classifiers with the ability to handle continuously arriving novel items that Siamese encoders support. It addresses the capacity limitations of small encoders for complex retrieval tasks.

entry.title: MedGuards: Multi-Agent System for Reliable Medical Error Detection and Correction

author.name: Congbo Ma, Hu Wang, Yichun Zhang, Farah E. Shamout

entry.summary: MedGuards frames medical error detection and correction as a multi-agent in-context learning task, with specialized agents for detection, localization, and correction plus a confidence-guided arbitration mechanism. It targets patient-safety risks from LLM-generated medical text.

entry.title: Fully Differentiable Neural Forced Alignment via Soft Dynamic Programming

author.name: Rotem Rousso, Eyal Cohen, Joseph Keshet

entry.summary: Proposes a fully differentiable neural forced alignment architecture using soft dynamic programming, with dual encoder branches for phoneme identity and boundary detection. It modernizes forced alignment which still relies on HMM-GMM frameworks.

entry.title: Hypergraph Normal World Models for Logical Visual Anomaly Detection

author.name: Weizhi Nie, Zibo Xu, Weijie Wang, Yuting Su

entry.summary: The Hypergraph Normal World Model detects logical visual anomalies (violations of count, co-occurrence, or spatial relations) using only normal images by distilling DINOv2 tokens into patch, relation, and hypergraph statistics with spatial hyperedges. It scores images via an information quotient.

entry.title: Dual Distribution Estimation for Zero-shot Noisy Test-Time Adaptation with VLMs

author.name: Wenjie Zhu, Yabin Zhang, Liang Xu, Xin Jin, Wenjun Zeng, Lei Zhang

entry.summary: DDE introduces a training-free Gaussian distribution estimation method for noisy test-time adaptation of vision-language models, filtering out-of-distribution outliers while preserving in-distribution accuracy. It shifts the paradigm from instance-level discriminative training to distribution modeling for better efficiency and calibration.

entry.title: USS: Unified Spatial-Semantic Prompts for Embodied Visual Tracking with Latent Dynamics Learning

author.name: Yuchen Xie, Xinyu Zhou, Kuangji Zuo, Yanshuo Lu, Fengrui Huang, Boyu Ma, Jianfei Yang

entry.summary: USS reframes embodied visual tracking from text-only target indication to unified spatial-semantic prompting supporting text, points, and boxes, addressing ambiguity in cluttered scenes. It uses latent dynamics learning in an end-to-end framework for continuous active target following.

entry.title: Toward Low-Latency Vision-Language Models with Doubly-Correct Predictions in Egocentric Visual Understanding

author.name: Qitong Wang, Fan Du, Pranav Maneriker, Jihui Jin, Christopher Rasmussen

entry.summary: This study analyzes VLM pruning through a doubly-correct prediction lens for low-latency egocentric understanding in human-robot collaboration, requiring outputs to be both accurate and evidentially grounded. It finds existing pruning methods often degrade this grounded correctness.

entry.title: SurveilNav: Collaborative Object Goal Navigation with Robot and Surveillance System

author.name: Ming-Ming Yu, Qunbo Wang, Rongtao Xu, Yanghong Mei, Yirong Yang, Longteng Guo, Wenjun Wu, Jing Liu

entry.summary: SurveilNav presents a collaborative object-goal navigation dataset built on Habitat-Sim with 206 cameras across 74 floors, and a framework integrating robot perception with fixed surveillance cameras via active camera scheduling. It targets multi-view collaboration in large environments beyond single-robot perception.

entry.title: Learning Perceptive Platform Adaptive Locomotion Controllers for Quadrupedal Robots

author.name: David Rytz, Kim Tien Ly, Ioannis Havoutis

entry.summary: This work studies how perception should be integrated into morphology-aware RL for quadrupedal locomotion, extending the MorAL framework to train perceptive controllers that generalize across related quadruped morphologies. It addresses the tradeoff between noise-sensitive perceptive policies and terrain-unaware blind controllers.

entry.title: Generative AI for Safe and Photorealistic Drone Light Shows

author.name: Pascal Reinhold, Alexander Gr\"afe, Sebastian Trimpe

entry.summary: SWAN is an end-to-end pipeline that synthesizes photorealistic, collision-free drone light show choreographies directly from text prompts, converting text to reference videos and translating pixel dynamics into swarm kinematics via an adaptive point-tracking algorithm. The tracker maintains coherence through occlusions and topological shifts.

entry.title: Beyond a Shadow of a Doubt: Close Proximity Geometry Reconstruction Using FMCW Radar Shadow Effects

author.name: Felix de Trogoff du Boisguezennec, Benjamin Ramtoula, Daniele De Martini

entry.summary: MIL-LC is a robust magnetometer-inertial-LiDAR fusion localization framework for GNSS-denied, geometrically repetitive, or textureless environments like offices and underground parking. It leverages ambient magnetic field cues, which require no infrastructure beacons, to complement geometric sensing.

entry.title: ForceBand: Learning Forceful Manipulation with sEMG

author.name: Botao He, Zhi Wang, Linna Kuang, Ishaan Ghosh, Jitendra Malik, Cornelia Fermuller, Tingfan Wu, Jiayuan Mao, Ruoshi Liu, Haozhi Qi, Yiannis Aloimonos
