entry.summary: Presents ForceBand, a low-cost wrist-worn sEMG system that converts human muscle activity into force-enriched demonstrations for robot manipulation learning. They collect a 10-hour multimodal dataset and pre-train an EMG2Force model to predict per-finger forces, addressing the missing contact-force signal in video and mocap demos.

entry.title: Agentic System as Compressor: Quantifying System Intelligence in Bits

author.name: Zihan Qin, Hongrui Zhang

entry.summary: Operationalizes the compression-is-intelligence view by measuring agentic system intelligence as bits saved when reconstructing target objects under fixed budgets, across five domains. Shows agentic components reduce codelength.

entry.title: EPTS: Elastic Post-Training Sparsity for Efficient Large Language Model Compression

author.name: Ke Xu, Jiaqi Wan, Wenhao Hu, Han Pu, Xiaoyun Wang

entry.summary: EPTS is an elastic post-training sparsity framework that produces a single model maintaining strong performance across multiple sparsity levels, avoiding the need to re-optimize for each target sparsity. It enables flexible LLM deployment across diverse hardware.

entry.title: FactorLibrary: From Polynomials to Circuits via Recursive Subgoals

author.name: Rohan Pandey, Michael Ruofan Zeng, Weikun K. Zhang, Kaijie Jin, Naomi Morato, Archit Ganapule, Bhaumik Mehta, Jarod Alper

entry.summary: FactorLibrary formulates finding minimal arithmetic circuits for polynomials over finite fields as a reinforcement learning problem in both bottom-up and top-down directions, storing reusable factorizable subexpressions as subgoals to tame the combinatorial search. The PPO+MCTS top-down agent finds certified optimal circuits up to complexity 8 with high success.

entry.title: Reclaim Evaluation: A Lossy Memory Is Worse Than an Empty One

author.name: Alex Kwon

entry.summary: This single-author paper argues that a lossy memory can be worse than no memory for language models: a memory keeping a wrong conclusion but dropping its reasoning makes the model confidently emit stale answers, whereas an empty memory leads to abstention. It introduces reclaim evaluation to test correctability across seven models.

entry.title: Pulmonary Embolism Risk Stratification from CTPA and Medical Records: Vascular Graphs Are Not All You Need

author.name: Nathan Painchaud, Tristan Hab\'emont, Morgane des Ligneris, Allan Serva, Pierre Croisille, Laurent Bertoletti, Thomas Lampert, Johannes F. Lutzeyer, Odyss\'ee Merveille

entry.summary: This work studies whether models can classify pulmonary embolism risk from medical records and CTPA-derived biomarkers without blood tests, comparing tabular models with vascular graph neural networks. The provocative finding is that vascular graphs are not strictly necessary. Relevant for clinical risk stratification under missing data.

entry.title: Conformal Orbit-Valid Trust Horizons for Equivariant World Models

author.name: Hongbo Wang

entry.summary: This companion paper studies trust-horizon certification for latent world models with known group symmetries, using conformal calibration to produce orbit-valid trust horizons. It shows exact equivariance transports calibrated trust curves across the symmetry orbit. Relevant for reliable equivariant world models.

entry.title: TRACER: Training-Free Closed-Loop Structured Inference for Traffic Accident Reconstruction

author.name: Yanchen Guan, Chengyue Wang, Bin Rao, Haicheng Liao, Jiaxun Zhang, Shang Gao, Chengzhong Xu, Zhenning Li

entry.summary: TRACER is a training-free framework for traffic accident reconstruction formulated as closed-loop structured inference, iteratively refining event-anchored motion hypotheses under geometric, kinematic, and interaction constraints guided by structured case memory. It targets physical consistency rather than just visual realism. Relevant for forensic inverse problems.

entry.title: Curvature-Guided Mixing for MLLM Adaptation

author.name: Jinglong Yang, Jiaxuan He, Wenjian Huang, Zhan Zhuang, Jianguo Zhang

entry.summary: Curvature-Guided Mixing merges pre-trained and fine-tuned multimodal LLMs using a second-order Hessian approximation to analytically derive an optimal closed-form soft mixing ratio based on relative task-specific curvatures. It combats catastrophic forgetting during MLLM fine-tuning, with a sparse hard-mixing variant.

entry.title: When Does Synthetic Data Augmentation Improve Score-Based Imbalanced Classification?

author.name: Zhengchi Ma, Pengfei Lyu, Anru R. Zhang

entry.summary: This paper develops a theoretical framework characterizing when synthetic minority data augmentation improves score-based imbalanced classification metrics like AUROC, AUPRC, and balanced accuracy. It separates augmentation effects into effective class reweighting and a discrepancy between synthetic and true minority distributions.

entry.title: AI translation of literary texts is "fine", but readers still prefer human translations

author.name: Yves Ferstler, Adam Podoxin, Ty Brassington, Roman Grundkiewicz, Maite Taboada, Marzena Karpinska

entry.summary: Has 15 avid readers compare human versus agentic LLM literary translations across 15 novels in French, Polish, and Japanese. It finds AI translations are adequate but readers still prefer human translations for immersiveness and literary effect.

entry.title: FreeStory: Training-Free Character Consistency for Free-Form Visual Storytelling

author.name: Sibo Dong, Ismail Shaheen, Sarah Adel Bargal

entry.summary: FreeStory is a training-free framework for character-consistent visual storytelling under free-form prompts, reformulating consistency as entity-grounded feature reuse without repeating full character descriptions per prompt. It handles natural storytelling with pronouns and type references.

entry.title: Teach-to-Reason: Competition-Guided Reasoning with a Self-Improving Teacher

author.name: Xiao Han, Hao Liu, Zhimin Bao, Jile Jiao, Yue Wang, Hui Guo, Xiaofeng Mou, Yi Xu

entry.summary: Teach-to-Reason introduces comparison-based supervision into chest X-ray VQA chain-of-thought optimization via a self-improving Teacher and a competition-guided Reasoner, overcoming coarse answer-level rewards. It improves reasoning quality where group advantages collapse.

entry.title: LinStereo: Linear-Complexity Global Attention for Multi-Scale Iterative Stereo Matching

author.name: Yiran Wang, Oliver Turner, Viorela Ila

entry.summary: LinStereo builds on Depth Anything V3 with a Position-Aware Linear Attention module that replaces local recurrence with linear-cost global aggregation for multi-scale iterative stereo matching. It tests generalization on degraded underwater scenes.

entry.title: Spatio-Temporal Mixture-of-Modality-Experts Diffusion for Quantitative DCE-MRI Synthesis from Incomplete MR Sequences

author.name: Junhyeok Lee, Kyu Sung Choi

entry.summary: ST-MoME is a conditional diffusion framework synthesizing 3D quantitative DCE-MRI parameter maps from arbitrary subsets of multimodal MRI using a spatio-temporal mixture-of-modality-experts gating network. It handles realistic missing-modality scenarios while preserving quantitative fidelity.

entry.title: FunPiQ: A New Benchmark for Pixel-Level Quality Assessment in Fundus Images

author.name: Pengwei Wang, Jos\'e Morano, Virginia Mares, Hrvoje Bogunovi\'c

entry.summary: FunPiQ is a benchmark for pixel-level quality assessment of color fundus images based on anatomical visibility, arguing this is more task-agnostic and explainable than image-level labels. It enables quantitative evaluation of localized degradations critical for trustworthy ophthalmic screening.

entry.title: TryOnCrafter: Unleashing Camera Trajectories for Realistic Video Virtual Try-on via a Renderable 4D Try-on Proxy

author.name: Hao Sun, Hao Yan, Mengting Chen, Quanjian Song, Yu Li, Juan Cao, Jinsong Lan, Xiaoyong Zhu, Bo Zheng, Sheng Tang

entry.summary: TryOnCrafter introduces camera-controllable video virtual try-on (CaM-VVT) using a renderable 4D try-on proxy, enabling omnidirectional viewpoint exploration rather than passively following source camera trajectories. It targets viewpoint-agnostic texture synthesis with structural synchronization between human dynamics and background.

entry.title: Calousel: Extrinsic Calibration of Non-overlapping Multi-camera Systems from Pure Rotation

author.name: Gwanhyeong Song, Chaehyeon Song, Ayoung Kim

entry.summary: Calousel proposes extrinsic calibration of non-overlapping multi-camera systems using pure rotational motion and a single static calibration board, avoiding large targets or pre-measured multi-target setups. The key idea is having all cameras sequentially observe the same target under a shared geometric reference.

entry.title: Large-Scale Tunnel Air--Ground Collaboration With FLISP: Fast LiDAR-IMU Synchronized Path Planne

author.name: Fenghe Guo, Runjie Shen, Chenyang Sun, Junrui Zhang, Quanxi Zhan, Yongchun Wang, Junjie Zhang

entry.summary: FLISP is a mapless cooperative UGV-UAV path planning framework for hydropower tunnel inspection, using a single UGV-mounted LiDAR-IMU suite to drive synchronized paths for both platforms with platform-specific solvers and hierarchical refinement. It avoids state-estimation drift in a 1.2 km operational tunnel benchmark.

entry.title: Learning to Adapt: Reptile-D-Learning for Robust and Efficient Control Under Parametric Uncertainty

author.name: Haipeng Cao, Zhaolong Shen, Quan Quan

entry.summary: Reptile-D-learning combines Reptile meta-learning with D-learning to learn generalizable Lyapunov network initializations and controllers robust to parametric uncertainty, capturing shared dynamical structure across systems with different parameters. It avoids costly retraining when parameter shifts invalidate stability constraints.

entry.title: Stage-Aware and Roughness-Constrained Diffusion Policy for Multi-Stage Robotic Polishing

author.name: Shuai Ke, Jiexin Zhang, Huan Zhao, Zhiao Wei, Yikun Guo, Tiange Wu, Guoqiang Guo, Haoyuan Zhou, Jie Pan, Han Ding

entry.summary: SRDP is a stage-aware, roughness-constrained diffusion policy for multi-stage robotic polishing that infers the process-stage posterior from multimodal observation histories to condition the denoising process. It handles long-horizon dependencies, uncertain stage transitions, and regulated process parameters in industrial finishing.

entry.title: Preventative Steering has advantages over Inoculation Prompting

author.name: Aansh Samyani

entry.summary: SPAR-fellowship work benchmarking Preventative Steering (PS) against Inoculation Prompting (IP) across four supervised-fine-tuning settings, finding PS often yields stronger undesired-trait suppression, less conditional misalignment, and finer compositional control. Notes PS requires linear trait representations while IP is operationally cheaper.

entry.title: InvestPhilBench: A Multi-Layer Dynamic Benchmark for Evaluating Large Language Model Procedural Reasoning in Expert Investment Philosophy

author.name: Mingguang Chen, Bo Qu

entry.summary: Introduces InvestPhilBench, a multi-layer dynamic benchmark testing whether LLMs can reconstruct and apply expert investors' procedural decision frameworks across eight cognitive tiers, with an automated scoring pipeline. Targets procedural financial reasoning evaluation.

entry.title: When Multi-Sensor Fusion Fails to Generalize: Cattle Posture Classification Under Animal-Level and Temporal Distribution Shift

author.name: Leutrim Uka, Severino Pinto, Gundula Hoffmann, Marina M. -C. H\"ohne

entry.summary: Examines whether multi-sensor fusion improves generalization for cattle posture classification under animal-level and temporal distribution shift, finding that near-perfect in-distribution accuracy can mask reliance on context-specific signals that fail under shift. A cautionary robustness study.

entry.title: Geo-Strat-RL: Learning Geological Event Reasoning from Verifiable Tasks

author.name: Lukas Mosser

entry.summary: Investigates whether defining verifiable geological reasoning tasks lets vision-language models learn to reconstruct geological event histories consistent with evidence and principles, despite non-unique ground truth. Explores RL from verifiable geology tasks.

entry.title: ASAP: Agent-System Co-Design for Wall-Clock-Centered Auto HPO Research for ML Experiments

author.name: Taicheng Guo, Haomin Zhuang, Kehan Guo, Yujun Zhou, Nitesh V. Chawla, Olaf Wiest, Xiangliang Zhang

entry.summary: ASAP is an agent-system co-design framework for hyperparameter optimization that uses LLMs but evaluates by wall-clock time rather than iteration count, addressing how prior LLM-HPO methods misleadingly report per-iteration gains. It treats the LLM as more than a drop-in surrogate replacement.

entry.title: Memory Makes the Difference: Evaluating How Different Memory Roles Shape Conversational Agents

author.name: Yuxin Wang, Paul Thomas, Zhiwei Yu, Yuan Gao, Saeed Hassanpour, Soroush Vosoughi, Robert Sim, Nick Craswell

entry.summary: This work probes how conversational memories with different functional roles shape RAG-based agent responses, providing a fine-grained taxonomy of memory types and analyzing their distinct behavioral effects beyond storage and retrieval. It moves past reference-based evaluation to capture preference-related nuances.

entry.title: Anatomically-conditioned Latent Diffusion Model for Data-Efficient Few-Shot Cross-Domain 3D Glioma MRI Synthesis

author.name: Salman Shaik, Truong Thanh Hung Nguyen, Hung Cao

entry.summary: ALDM is an anatomically-conditioned latent diffusion model for data-efficient few-shot 3D glioma MRI synthesis, using a 3D VAE to learn anatomical priors and a ControlNet-guided latent diffusion model to generate coherent volumes for data-scarce target domains. With only 16 target images it outperforms GAN and hybrid baselines on FID and downstream tasks.

entry.title: EchoStyle: Unlocking High-Fidelity Video Stylization with Reverse Data Synthesis

author.name: Huaqiu Li, Jiahao Wang, Sijia Cai, Hualian Sheng, Bing Deng, Jieping Ye, Wenhan Luo

entry.summary: EchoStyle is a scalable text-driven framework for high-fidelity video stylization of arbitrary-length videos, using a video-to-video architecture and a pioneering automatic reverse-synthesis pipeline to address data scarcity, content leakage, and style drift. It improves on reference-image methods that suffer from motion distortion.

entry.title: Multi-Agent Goal Recognition with Team- and Goal-Conditioned Reinforcement Learning and Factorized Branch-and-Bound

author.name: Thiago Thomas, Gabriel de Oliveira Ramos, Felipe Meneguzzi

entry.summary: MAGR-BB tackles multi-agent goal recognition, jointly inferring team partitions and per-team goals using a team- and goal-conditioned RL policy as a scoring model inside factorized branch-and-bound search. It matches exhaustive search top hypotheses on a Blocksworld benchmark. Relevant for surveillance and collaborative robotics.

entry.title: Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning for Neural Network Compression (HiReLC): Pruning and Quantization

author.name: Kamar Hibatallah Baghdadi, Kawther Guoual Belhamidi, Sara Belhadj, Aissa Boulmerka, Nadir Farhi

entry.summary: HiReLC is a hierarchical ensemble-RL framework for automated joint quantization and structured pruning of deep neural networks, with low-level per-block agents and high-level agents coordinating budget allocation via Fisher-information sensitivity. An active learning loop reduces evaluation cost. Relevant for automated model compression.

entry.title: Supervised Reinforcement Learning for the Coordination of Distributed Energy Resources

author.name: Haoyuan Deng, Yihong Zhou, Thomas Morstyn, Yi Wang

entry.summary: This paper proposes Supervised Reinforcement Learning for coordinating distributed energy resources, pre-training a policy on demonstration data before RL fine-tuning, inspired by LLM training paradigms. It addresses sample inefficiency and suboptimality of standard RL from scratch. Relevant for power system decarbonization.

entry.title: Frequency Domain Reservoir Computing

author.name: Klaus Schertler, Xiomara Runge, Andrea Ceni, David Kappel, Claudio Gallicchio

entry.summary: FRESCO is a Frequency Domain Reservoir Computing architecture that addresses the O(N-squared) state-update bottleneck of Echo State Networks by operating in the frequency domain, enabling larger expressive reservoirs. It maintains the closed-form training advantage of ESNs. Relevant for efficient recurrent sequence modeling.

entry.title: From Forecasting Leaderboards to Deployment Decisions: A Fail-Closed Certification Protocol

author.name: Geumyoung Kim

entry.summary: This paper introduces a fail-closed certification protocol that determines when a forecasting leaderboard winner can be certified as deployment-actionable for a specified decision interface and utility. Its gates check for friction-caused, statistically supported, recurrent deployment-side reversals. Matters for bridging benchmark rankings and deployment decisions.

entry.title: Bridging Spherical Black-Box Optimizers

author.name: Johannes Ackermann, Stefano Peluchetti

entry.summary: This work unifies several black-box optimization methods (Evolution Strategies, Consensus-Based Optimization, Optimization via Integration) within a common framework distinguished by fitness aggregation and consensus scope. It introduces hybrid optimizers that interpolate between methods, including controlling preference for flat minima.

entry.title: ConSolv: Solvent-Conditional Machine Learning Implicit Solvent Potential

author.name: Linying Zhang, Julija Zavadlav

entry.summary: ConSolv is a solvent-conditional machine learning implicit solvent potential that incorporates solvent effects via an attention-based solvent-embedding block, trained on combined experimental and ab initio data. A single model transfers across 66 organic solvents, extending implicit-solvent MLPs beyond aqueous environments.

entry.title: Minimax PAC Bounds for Learning in Exogenous Contextual MDPs

author.name: Corentin Pla, Hugo Richard, Marc Abeille, Vianney Perchet

entry.summary: This work establishes minimax PAC bounds for learning in tabular discounted MDPs with exogenous i.i.d. contexts that affect rewards and transitions but remain uncontrolled by the agent. It characterizes sample complexity across different oracle-access regimes.

entry.title: Learning Optimization Proxies for Sequential Contextual Stochastic Programs: An Order Fulfillment Application

author.name: Tinghan Ye, Shuaicheng Tong, Changkun Guan, Beste Basciftci, Pascal Van Hentenryck

entry.summary: This work trains a learning-based optimization proxy—a scenario-embedded neural network on solver-generated labels—to provide sub-second decisions for sequential contextual stochastic programs in order fulfillment. It targets the gap where exact solvers take seconds to minutes, too slow for peak-period planning.

entry.title: Security and Privacy in Retrieval-Augmented Generation: Architectures, Threats, Defenses, and Future Directions for Building Trustworthy Systems

author.name: Balamurugan Palanisamy, G S S Chalapathi, Vikas Hassija, Rajkumar Buyya

entry.summary: A comprehensive survey of security and privacy in Retrieval-Augmented Generation systems, covering architectures, threats, defenses, and future directions across centralized, on-device, and federated deployments. It maps risks like index exposure and knowledge-base poisoning.

entry.title: Cross-Modality Structural Guidance in 3D Latent Diffusion for Robust FLAIR Super-Resolution

author.name: Haoyu Lan, Jiazhen Zhang, John Onofrey, Bino Varghese, Nasim Sheikh-Bahaei, Arthur W. Toga, Jeiran Choupan

entry.summary: MR-DiffuSR is a 3D latent diffusion super-resolution framework that uses high-resolution T1w structural priors via cross-modality swin-attention to restore thick-slice FLAIR MRI while reducing anatomical hallucination. It targets diagnostic fidelity in accelerated MRI.

entry.title: Invoice Haystack: Benchmarking Document Retrieval and Visual Question Answering Under Strong Visual Homogeneity

author.name: Heethanjan Kanagalingam, Thenukan Pathmanathan, Mokeeshan Vathanakumar, Basim Azam, Sarah Monazam Erfani

entry.summary: Invoice Haystack is a benchmark of 1,500 invoice images and 200 discriminative QA pairs that stress-tests document retrieval and VQA under strong visual homogeneity, identifying embedding collapse. It reflects enterprise repositories where records share identical templates.

entry.title: C2RM-Seg: Causal Counterfactual Reasoning with Structural-Semantic Priors for Weakly Supervised Histopathological Tissue Segmentation

author.name: Hualong Zhang, Siyang Feng, Zihan Huan, Yi Qian, Zhenbing Liu, Rushi Lan, Xipeng Pan

entry.summary: C2RM-Seg is a weakly supervised histopathology segmentation framework using causal counterfactual reasoning to refine CAM pseudo-labels toward true tissue morphology rather than staining cues, plus structure-aware semantic enhancement. It reduces spurious localization.

entry.title: TensorLDM: A Component-Wise Latent Diffusion Model for Volumetric DTI Reconstruction from Sparse DWIs

author.name: Junhyeok Lee, Kyu Sung Choi

entry.summary: TensorLDM is a component-wise latent diffusion model reconstructing volumetric diffusion tensors from sparse DWIs using group-specific encoders and cross-component attention to maintain anatomical and physical plausibility. It accelerates DTI acquisition clinically.

entry.title: ScaleHP: Estimating Hand Pose in Metric Space

author.name: Ruitao Jing, Xingyu Chen, Hongyang Li, Qing Jiang, Yukai Shi, Lei Zhang

entry.summary: ScaleHP estimates hand pose in absolute metric space by leveraging stable anthropometric bone-proportion priors via a transformer decoder with a scale token, bypassing fragile extrinsic depth modules. It targets immersive HCI and robotics.

entry.title: ADM-Fusion: Adaptive Deep Multi-Sensor Fusion for Robust Ego-Motion Estimation in Diverse Conditions

author.name: Hasan Moughnieh, Ibrahim Ghaddar, Hadi Elham, Imad H. Elhajj, Daniel Asmar

entry.summary: ADM-Fusion is an end-to-end deep multi-sensor fusion method for ego-motion estimation that uses an adaptive mixture-of-experts with content-aware routing to dynamically weight sensor modalities under degradation. This adaptivity targets robustness across diverse and degraded conditions where modalities fail differently.

entry.title: Dual Agreement Consistency Learning for Semi-Supervised Fetal Ultrasound Segmentation

author.name: Fangyijie Wang, Gu\'enol\'e Silvestre, Ziyang Wang, Kathleen M. Curran

entry.summary: DACL is a semi-supervised framework for fetal ultrasound segmentation that jointly trains a lightweight CNN and a transformer via cross pseudo supervision, adding a dual-agreement consistency loss combining probabilistic divergence and entropy-guided confidence alignment. It addresses the scarcity of pixel-level annotations in maternal-fetal imaging.

entry.title: GROVE: Grounded Pedestrian Simulation via Natural Language for Interactive Social Robot Navigation

author.name: Duc Tai Nguyen, Volodymyr Shcherbyna, Anh Do Duc, Zhengcheng Shen, Teham Buiyan, Linh K\"astner

entry.summary: GROVE is a text-to-scenario pedestrian simulation framework for social robot navigation, generating realistic, socially challenging crowd scenarios from presets or free-form prompts. Multiple modules ensure realism across long-horizon human behavior, pedestrian navigation, and interactions.

entry.title: GUI agent: Guided Exploration of User-Sensitive Screens

author.name: Aradhana Nayak, Mussadiq Nazeer, Wang Peng, Feng Liu

entry.summary: Develops an explorer agent that systematically identifies and categorizes user-sensitive screens in GUI environments to flag when task execution should be handed back to users. Aims to improve safety of GUI automation agents.

entry.title: Convex--Concave Quadratic Spectral Filtering for Graph Neural Networks

author.name: Ranhui Yan, Jia Cai, Mengzhu Chen, Haodong Yang

entry.summary: Proposes DCQ-GNN, a spectral GNN using a compact bank of adaptive convex-concave quadratic filters that improves spectral selectivity without high-order polynomials, fused via node-adaptive gating. Improves filter expressivity efficiently.

entry.title: Noise-Aware Boundary-Enhanced Generative Learning for Ultrasound Speckle Reduction

author.name: Yuexi Gu, Mengqi Wu, Yongheng Sun, Virginie Papadopoulou, Mingxia Liu, Maureen Kohi

entry.summary: Proposes NBGL, a noise-aware boundary-enhanced generative framework for ultrasound speckle reduction with separate speckle-reduction and boundary-enhancement branches that preserves anatomical boundaries across varying noise levels. Improves medical image quality without over-smoothing.

entry.title: Communicability-Inspired Positional Encoding (CIPE)

author.name: Yipeng Zhang, Zhongtian Sun, Pietro Li\`o, Kelin Xia

entry.summary: CIPE is a positional encoding for graph Transformers built from communicability, a measure aggregating path contributions of all lengths, producing inner products that recover meaningful structural relatedness as an attention-ready geometry. It addresses the difficulty of designing effective positional encodings for non-Euclidean graphs.

entry.title: C3-Bench: A Context-Aware Change Captioning Benchmark

author.name: Jae-Woo Kim, Hyeongbeom Kim, Ue-Hwan Kim

entry.summary: C3-Bench is a context-aware change-captioning benchmark with 4,996 human-labeled image pairs across 51 real-world change contexts in four domains, plus the first LLM-as-Judge evaluation framework for the task. It enables fine-grained assessment of change captioning in diverse real-world settings.

entry.title: Staying In Character: Perspective-Bounded Memory For Book-Based Role-Playing Agents

author.name: Xushuo Tang, Junhe Zhang, Zihan Yang, Yifu Tang, Sichao Li, Longbin Lai, Zhengyi Yang

entry.summary: REVERIEMEM is a three-layer (episodic, semantic, personality) perspective-bounded memory architecture for book-based role-playing agents that prevents factual overreach (using facts outside a character's perspective) and stylistic monotony. It is evaluated with the new KBF-QA benchmark of 4,386 questions.

entry.title: Power-Budgeted Underwater Vehicle Control via Constrained Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Yinuo Wang, Gavin Tao, Yuze Liu

entry.summary: This paper applies constrained reinforcement learning to underwater vehicle control with an explicit power budget, replacing the unit-less energy-penalty weight (which must be re-tuned per vehicle and can backfire) with a physically meaningful target power constraint. It extends mission range by completing tasks while drawing less thruster power.

entry.title: Swarm-Inspired Generation of Collective Behaviors in Graph Dynamical Systems

author.name: Ji Chen, Song Chen, Chengzhang Gong, Li Fan, Chao Xu

entry.summary: SIES is a swarm-inspired graph-dynamical framework that learns generalizable local interaction laws to produce controllable collective behaviors across graphs, dynamics, and tasks. Each node is an agent-like unit with signed source-target attention as adaptive coupling. Matters for designing emergent collective organization.

entry.title: Learning Dynamical Systems from Multiple Sparse Datasets: A Hierarchical Bayesian Modeling Approach

author.name: Cristian Brugnara, Lea Multerer, Marco Forgione, Laura Azzimonti

entry.summary: This work proposes a hierarchical Bayesian framework for probabilistic meta-learning in dynamical systems, modeling dataset-specific parameters as draws from a shared population distribution, with an ODE solver embedded in gradient-based MCMC. It improves prediction over unpooled methods from sparse noisy data. Relevant for data-efficient system identification.

entry.title: A Framework for Directed Hypergraph Signal Processing via tensor t-SVD

author.name: Carlos Mundo-Levano, Nicol\'as Bello, Daniel L. Lau, Gonzalo R. Arce

entry.summary: This paper introduces Directed Hypergraph Signal Processing using tensor t-SVD, extending graph signal processing to handle both higher-order polyadic and asymmetric directional relationships simultaneously. It defines a novel adjacency tensor, shift operator, and lossless Fourier transform, outperforming matrix-based baselines on traffic denoising. Relevant for structured signal processing.

entry.title: Lifelong In-Context Learning with Transformers Requires Parametric Forms of Attention

author.name: Luke McDermott, Robert W. Heath jr., Rahul Parhi

entry.summary: This paper argues that lifelong in-context learning with transformers requires parametric forms of attention that learn key-value relationships at test time via regression, overcoming the quadratic cost of standard attention. It frames lifelong learning as extended in-context learning on fixed hardware budgets.

entry.title: Laplace--Fisher Gate Identities for Optimal Matrix-Gated Blended Score Estimation

author.name: Alois Duston, Tan Bui Tanh

entry.summary: This paper derives the variance-optimal matrix-valued gate for blended score estimation when sampling from unnormalized targets by reversing an Ornstein-Uhlenbeck diffusion. The closed-form Laplace-Fisher Gate Identity replaces rigid scalar blends to handle singular or strongly anisotropic targets.

entry.title: Knowledge Cascade: Reverse Knowledge Distillation on Nonparametric Multivariate Functional Estimation

author.name: Luyang Fang, Haoran Lu, Yongkai Chen, Wenxuan Zhong, Ping Ma

entry.summary: Knowledge Cascade introduces reverse knowledge distillation, using a small inexpensive student model to guide construction of a more complex teacher in nonparametric multivariate functional estimation where building the teacher is the bottleneck. Despite being counterintuitive, the authors show student-to-teacher transfer can be principled and beneficial.

entry.title: Invisible to humans, visible to machines: a preregistered audit of Unicode fidelity across four biomedical bibliographic APIs

author.name: Przemys{\l}aw Czuma

entry.summary: A preregistered audit testing whether four biomedical bibliographic APIs faithfully reproduce Unicode characters from published abstracts, against PMC JATS XML ground truth. It exposes silent data fidelity issues affecting text mining and LLM training corpora.

entry.title: How Robust is OCR-Reasoning? Evaluating OCR-Reasoning Robustness of Vision-Language Models under Visual Perturbations

author.name: Yuxing Cheng, Yuan Wu, Yi Chang

entry.summary: Introduces OCR-Robust, a benchmark of 812 samples evaluating VLM OCR-reasoning robustness under controlled visual perturbations across documents, charts, and diagrams. It exposes how visual corruption propagates into reasoning errors.

entry.title: Follow Your Track: Precise Skeleton Animation Controlled by 3D Trajectories

author.name: Yueting Liu, Yanqin Jiang, Nian Liu, Jingmen Zhou, Zhengjun Zha, Weiming Hu, Jin Gao

entry.summary: Follow Your Track enables precise skeleton animation for 4D generation controlled by 3D trajectories, decoupling from dense mesh/Gaussian representations to reduce cost and temporal artifacts. It addresses limitations of text and video control for fine-grained motion.

entry.title: PatchINR: Patch-Based Implicit Neural Representations for Efficient and Scalable Inference

author.name: Jiachen Ren, Wenyong Zhou, Taiqiang Wu, Yuxin Cheng, Xincheng Feng, Zhengwu Liu, Ngai Wong

entry.summary: PatchINR predicts entire pixel patches in a single forward pass for implicit neural representations, reducing inference queries from per-pixel quadratic growth, with an FPGA hardware acceleration architecture. It targets efficient high-resolution INR inference.

entry.title: Auto-Labelling-Based Domain Transfer for 3D Object Detection on a Bicycle-Mounted LiDAR Platform

author.name: Mario Finkbeiner, Max A. Buettner, Kanak Mazumder, Fabian B. Flohr

entry.summary: Provides a 3D object detection benchmark of 1,027 annotated LiDAR keyframes from a bicycle-mounted platform in urban Munich and evaluates how nuScenes-pretrained detectors generalize to the cyclist perspective via auto-labelling domain transfer. It addresses scarce VRU-perspective annotated data.

entry.title: What Does the Brain See? Multiview Neural Representations to Demystify the Brain-Visual Alignment

author.name: Salini Yadav, Taveena Lotey, Pravendra Singh, Partha Pratim Roy

entry.summary: Presents a unified multiview EEG representation learning framework for zero-shot visual decoding that jointly models temporal state-space dynamics, learnable wavelet spectral decomposition, and spatial structure to align brain responses with visual semantics. It improves on holistic EEG embeddings.

entry.title: Naturalness Predicts but Does Not Cause Transferability in Image Encodings of Real-World Streams

author.name: Faruk Alpay, Baris Basaran

entry.summary: This study examines whether the visual naturalness of images encoded from 1D signals predicts transfer accuracy under frozen vision backbones, using a 299-series corpus called WorldStream. It finds that Frechet distance to natural images predicts but does not causally drive transferability.

entry.title: A Benchmark for Heterogeneous Stereo Deblurring with Physically- and Epipolar-constrained Cross Attention

author.name: Hoju Shin, Jiah Kim, Seung-Wook Kim, Seowon Ji

entry.summary: This work addresses heterogeneous stereo deblurring caused by asymmetric camera modules in smartphones, introducing the HSD dataset and a physically- and epipolar-constrained cross-attention module. It restricts cross-view matching to optics-derived disparity windows for efficient asymmetric deblurring.

entry.title: fARfetch: Enabling Collocated AR-HRC in Large Visually Diverse Environments with VLM-Driven AR Content Adaptation

author.name: Christian Fronk, Hanting Ye, David Hunt, Miroslav Pajic, Maria Gorlatova

entry.summary: fARfetch is an AR human-robot collaboration system for large outdoor environments combining shared semantic mapping, a world-in-miniature representation, and VLM-driven adaptation of AR content legibility. It supports landmark-grounded navigation commands and path authoring beyond visual line of sight.

entry.title: Delta-Position Estimation-Based IMU Odometry: A Comparison of MLP and Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks

author.name: Osman Tokluoglu, Emin Keresteci

entry.summary: This study compares MLP and Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks for learning-based inertial odometry, estimating incremental displacement over 50ms windows rather than absolute position. The KAN achieves 44 percent lower cumulative drift with 6.9x fewer parameters than the MLP on the EuRoC benchmark.

entry.title: Reasoning and learning about injected concepts in language models

author.name: Samarth Bhargav

entry.summary: SPAR-mentored interpretability study testing whether LLMs can verbalize properties of injected steering vectors, such as the layer region, magnitude, and semantic meaning, via in-context learning. Finds Qwen3-32B and Gemma-4-31B achieve high accuracy and can gate behavior on detecting specific injections zero-shot.

entry.title: Retrieval-Augmented Personalization with Foundation Models for Wearable Stress Detection

author.name: Louis Simon, Mohamed Chetouani

entry.summary: Proposes retrieval-augmented personalization for wearable stress detection that uses frozen out-of-domain foundation models to retrieve a user's similar past patterns into a compact personalized embedding modulating a lightweight transformer. Avoids costly per-user fine-tuning.

entry.title: Heterogeneous and Adept Snapshot Distillation for 3D Semantic Segmentation

author.name: Xiaopei Wu, Yuenan Hou, Junkai Xu, Wenxiao Wang, Binbin Lin, Yu Li, Ping Li, Haifeng Liu, Deng Cai, Wanli Ouyang

entry.summary: This paper proposes heterogeneous snapshot distillation for 3D semantic segmentation, transferring knowledge from multi-modal (point cloud plus image) and multi-expert teachers into a single point-cloud network without auxiliary inputs at inference. It boosts segmentation accuracy while avoiding heavy computational cost.

entry.title: Sarashina2.2-TTS: Tackling Kanji Polyphony in Japanese Speech Generation via Data Scaling and Targeted Data Synthesis

author.name: Lianbo Liu, Shiao Zhu, Kai Washizaki, Reo Yoneyama, Haesung Jeon, Mengjie Zhao, Yusuke Fujita, Hao Shi, Nao Yoshida, Yuan Gao, Roman Koshkin, Yukiya Hono, Yui Sudo

entry.summary: Sarashina2.2-TTS is a Japanese-centric LLM-based text-to-speech system that tackles context-dependent kanji polyphony through scaling to 361k hours of speech and targeted data augmentation. It addresses a linguistic challenge underserved by English- and Chinese-focused TTS systems.

entry.title: Expresso-AI: Explainable Video-Based Deep Learning Models for Depression Diagnosis

author.name: Felipe Moreno, Sharifa Alghowinem, Hae Won Park, Cynthia Breazeal

entry.summary: Expresso-AI presents explainable video-based deep learning models for depression diagnosis that aim for affect-specific, interpretable temporal predictions usable by health care professionals. It addresses the gap where automated depression diagnosis methods lack interpretability and affect specificity.

entry.title: Point Cloud Diffusion with Global and Local Reconstruction for Instance-Level 3D Anomaly Detection

author.name: Linchun Wu, Qin Zou, Jiwen Lu, Qingquan Li

entry.summary: PCDiff is a point cloud diffusion framework for instance-level 3D anomaly detection that combines global and local reconstruction to detect weak defects (deviations as small as 1e-3) while reducing positional-bias false positives in non-defective regions. It targets high-precision industrial manufacturing inspection.

entry.title: A Spectral Phase Diagram for Binary Few-Shot Classification: Intrinsic Dimensionality, Geometric Saturation, and Representational Diagnosis

author.name: Arnav Gupta

entry.summary: This paper introduces a saturation index measuring the ratio of effective rank of within-class covariance to shot count for few-shot binary classification, provably indicating when enough labeled examples have been collected. It is computable from support features alone without test labels. Matters for deciding when to stop labeling.

entry.title: Closed-Loop Graph Algorithm Execution with Small Language Models: Step Accuracy and Rollout Reliability

author.name: Michal Podstawski

entry.summary: This paper studies closed-loop graph algorithm execution with small language models as repeated next-action prediction, evaluating both local step accuracy and global rollout reliability across classical graph procedures. It assesses constraint validity and prefix survival via intervention diagnostics. Matters for understanding SLM algorithmic reasoning.

entry.title: Leaking Circuit Secrets: Gradient Leakage Attacks on Graph Neural Networks

author.name: Rupesh Raj Karn, Johann Knechtel, Ozgur Sinanoglu

entry.summary: This paper presents the first comprehensive evaluation of gradient leakage attacks on graph neural networks in circuit-design and hardware-security tasks. It shows that GLAs can expose sensitive netlist information like gate types and hardware Trojan properties across multiple GNN architectures.

entry.title: Two-dimensional Hyperbolic RNN Neural Quantum State

author.name: H. L. Dao

entry.summary: This work constructs the first two-dimensional hyperbolic neural quantum state via a Lorentz 2D-RNN and benchmarks it against Euclidean RNNs on the 2D transverse-field Ising model. It finds hyperbolic NQS outperform at the phase-transition point where the physics is described by a conformal field theory dual to hyperbolic AdS space.

entry.title: HiFiVe: High-Fidelity Vehicle Generation Leveraging Auto-Regressive 2D Generative Priors

author.name: Hongli Xiao, Youjian Zhang, Qi Zheng, Zhaohui Hu, Yaohui Jin, Xiaoguang Ren, Wenjing Yang, Long Lan

entry.summary: HiFiVe is a training-free framework for high-fidelity 3D vehicle modeling using auto-regressive 2D generative priors with 3D geometric constraints for cross-view consistency, refining textures from arbitrary viewpoints. It avoids costly fine-tuning of multi-view diffusion models.

entry.title: Cross-View Variance Correlation in Path-Traced Stereo:A Hidden Shortcut in Synthetic Training Data

author.name: Po-Ting Lin

entry.summary: Reports that path-traced synthetic stereo training data have correlated per-pixel variance fields across the two cameras once aligned by ground-truth disparity, despite independent noise streams. This hidden shortcut could be exploited by disparity-estimation networks.

entry.title: From Sparse and Imperfect 2D Anchors to Consistent 3D Gaussian Street Scenes: Support-Aware Appearance

author.name: Long Cao, Zhongquan Wang, Jie Li, Yuhan Chen, Kefei Qian, Xiangfei Huang, Guofa Li

entry.summary: This paper introduces teacher-relative appearance residual distillation for baking consistent appearance into 3D Gaussian street scenes from sparse, imperfect 2D anchors. It uses frequency decomposition, confidence estimation, and support-aware aggregation to avoid propagating view-specific noise.

entry.title: Elo-Disentangled Player-Style Embeddings for Human Chess via Rating-Conditioned Residual Move Model

author.name: Jason Carlson

entry.summary: Learns per-player chess style embeddings disentangled from skill level via a rating-conditioned residual move model built on Maia and Stockfish features. Notably improves move prediction while isolating stylistic deviations.

entry.title: On-Device Neural Architecture Search

author.name: Andrea Mattia Garavagno, Edoardo Ragusa, Paolo Gastaldo, Antonio Frisoli, Claudio Loconsole

entry.summary: Proposes performing lightweight neural architecture search directly on the deployment device to adapt tiny networks to real-time sensor data, validated on an Italian Sign Language EMG dataset. Targets near-sensor, per-user adaptive models.

entry.title: Attractive and Repulsive Pattern Control in Sequence Generation

author.name: Francois Pachet

entry.summary: Introduces signed pattern control for variable-order Markov sequence generation, using a weighted recurrence automaton and belief propagation to exactly sample from a pattern-biased distribution, suppressing or attracting target patterns. Useful for controllable symbolic generation like music.

entry.title: Quantifying Explainable AI-introduced signal noise on ECG data with Spectral Entropy

author.name: David A. Kelly, Nathan Blake

entry.summary: Proposes using spectral entropy to quantify the signal noise that explainability techniques introduce into ECG attributions, helping distinguish model signal from XAI artifacts. Demonstrated on arrhythmia classification with multiple post-hoc methods.

entry.title: Reward-Conditioned Attention: How Reward Design Shapes What Autonomous Driving Agents See

author.name: Mohamed Benabdelouahad, Ahmed Djalal Hacini, Nadir Farhi, Aissa Boulmerka

entry.summary: This work analyzes how reward design alters the internal cross-attention patterns of Perceiver-based RL agents trained for autonomous driving, using identical architectures with differing rewards across Waymo scenarios. A key methodological finding is that naive timestep pooling underestimates attention-risk relationships, requiring within-episode correlation with Fisher z aggregation.

entry.title: FDN: Interpretable Spatiotemporal Forecasting with Future Decomposition Networks

author.name: Nicholas Majeske, Ariful Azad

entry.summary: FDN is an interpretable spatiotemporal forecasting model that provides predictions via classification, reveals latent activity patterns, and matches state-of-the-art accuracy at far lower memory and runtime cost. It is evaluated on hydrologic, traffic, and energy datasets.

entry.title: ESTANet: Efficient Online Error Detection in Procedural Videos via Prediction Inconsistency

author.name: Shih-Po Lee, Reza Ghoddoosian, Faizan Siddiqui, Enna Sachdeva, Behzad Dariush

entry.summary: ESTANet detects errors in procedural videos online by exploiting the prediction inconsistency of action detectors themselves rather than designing complex architectures, leveraging detectors' differing sensitivity to input dynamics. It offers a lightweight real-time approach for guiding users to correct mistakes.

entry.title: TopoCast: A Topological Fidelity Framework for Evaluating Transformer-Based Time Series Forecasting

author.name: Sandeepa Weerasekara, Sandareka Wickramanayake

entry.summary: TopoCast is a topology-driven evaluation framework for transformer-based time-series forecasting that reconstructs phase-space representations to assess structural fidelity (recurrent dynamics, oscillation, phase alignment) beyond pointwise error metrics like MSE. It exposes forecasts that score well numerically despite structural degradation.

entry.title: A Red Teaming Framework for Large Language Models: A Case Study on Faithfulness Evaluation

author.name: Abrar Alotaibi, Raed Mughus, Moataz Ahmed

entry.summary: This paper presents a red-teaming framework with a multi-role architecture of target, attacker, and jury models that generates escalating adversarial prompts to expose LLM vulnerabilities, demonstrated on faithfulness evaluation. Exploitative prompts substantially increased unfaithfulness in responses.

entry.title: TL++: Accuracy and Privacy Preserving Traversal Learning for Distributed Intelligent Systems

author.name: Erdenebileg Batbaatar, Young Yoon

entry.summary: TL++ is a two-mode traversal-learning framework for distributed training that constructs virtual cross-node batches to recover centralized mini-batch gradient behavior, exchanging cut-layer activations and gradients (base mode) or secret-sharing them (secure mode) instead of full models. It addresses heterogeneity, communication, and privacy limitations of federated and split learning.

entry.title: AutoRelAnnotator: Calibrated Model Cascades for Cost-Efficient Relevance Evaluation in Sponsored Search

author.name: Md Omar Faruk Rokon, Shasvat Desai, Hong Yao, Kuang-chih Lee

entry.summary: AutoRelAnnotator uses calibrated model cascades that route queries through progressively larger fine-tuned classifiers for cost-efficient relevance annotation in sponsored search. The key insight is that accuracy comes from fine-tuning while cost comes from cascading, with isotonic calibration added. Industrially useful for scalable annotation.

entry.title: Measurable Majorities Are Not Finitely Axiomatizable

author.name: Lawrence S. Moss, Arthur Paul Pedersen

entry.summary: This theoretical note proves that the coherence criterion characterizing strict majority reasoning in finite social decision frames cannot be replaced by any bounded finite fragment. It constructs frames with arbitrarily long shortest coherence violations, resolving a stated conjecture. Matters for social choice and logic foundations.

entry.title: Low-Cost High-Order Singular Value Decomposition for Tensor-Based Reconstruction from Sparse Sensor Measurements: Urban Flow and Air-Quality Applications

author.name: Arindam Sengupta, Paul Jeanney, Ricardo Vinuesa, Jose Miguel Perez, Soledad Le Clainche

entry.summary: This paper introduces low-cost High-Order Singular Value Decomposition (lcHOSVD), a tensor-based sparse-sensing reconstruction framework that preserves multidimensional structure rather than flattening data into matrices. It is applied to urban flow and air-quality field reconstruction from sparse sensors. Relevant for environmental digital twins and data assimilation.

entry.title: Distill on a Diet: Efficient Knowledge Distillation via Learnable Data Pruning

author.name: Yifan Wu, Yiqi Wang, Xichen Ye, Wenjing Yan, Xiaoqiang Li, Cheng Jin, Xiangyu Yue, Weizhong Zhang

entry.summary: IF-Beta is an efficient data pruning framework for knowledge distillation that combines influence functions with a tailored objective to select training subsets aligned with what distillation actually requires. It reduces the compute overhead of distillation itself rather than just inference.

entry.title: Solving Markov Decision Processes with Future Information via MPC

author.name: Shambhuraj Sawant, Akhil S Anand, Dirk Reinhardt, Sebastien Gros

entry.summary: This work shows how to solve Markov decision processes with future information (forecasts, prices, reference trajectories) using MPC treated as a parameterized policy model adjusted via reinforcement learning. It extends MPC-RL combinations beyond classical MDPs to settings where future information is available at decision time.

entry.title: LLM-Based Scientific Peer Review: Methods, Benchmarks, and Reliability Challenges

author.name: Thi Huyen Nguyen, Zahra Ahmadi

entry.summary: This survey provides a systems-level analysis of LLM-based scientific peer review, focusing on critique generation and score prediction, with a taxonomy of modeling approaches and a synthesis of reliability, robustness, and security concerns. It examines whether LLMs are dependable as decision-support evaluators amid growing submission volumes.

entry.title: A Survey of Toxicity Detection and Mitigation Strategies for Multilingual Language Models

author.name: Soham Dan, Himanshu Beniwal, Thomas Hartvigsen

entry.summary: This survey synthesizes toxicity detection and detoxification work for multilingual language models, cataloguing threat models that exploit language choice, translation pivots, code-switching, and fine-tuning to weaken safety alignment. It organizes task formulations, detection approaches, and mitigation strategies across languages.

entry.title: Does Translation-Enhanced Speech Encoder Pre-training Affect Speech LLMs?

author.name: Tomoya Mizumoto, Yusuke Fujita

entry.summary: Argues that speech-translation-based encoder pretraining helps align language-specific speech encoder representations with the LLM's language-agnostic space in Speech LLMs. It experimentally evaluates the impact of translation-enhanced pretraining.

entry.title: CoGeoAD: Hierarchical Color-Geometric Fusion with Multi-View Attention for Zero-Shot 3D Anomaly Detection

author.name: Ke Xu, Xinle Wang, Yanning Hou, Xueliang Ma, Juan Xie, Jianfeng Qiu

entry.summary: CoGeoAD is a CLIP-based zero-shot 3D anomaly detection framework that fuses 2D color and 3D geometric features via multi-view attention and hierarchical fusion for industrial inspection. It detects both surface and structural defects in a unified model.

entry.title: Transferable Attack against Face Swapping in an Extended Space

author.name: Mingzhi Lyu, Yi Huang, Jun Xie, Zihao Zhao, Hong Xu, Adams Wai-Kin Kong

entry.summary: Proposes AIR, a transferable adversarial attack against subject-agnostic face swapping models using reillumination and additive perturbations to extend the attack space for natural-looking adversarial examples. It aims to proactively protect against unseen face swap models.

entry.title: Efficient Real-World Dehazing via Physics-Inspired Global-Local Decoupling

author.name: Yifei Qu, Ru Li, Junjie Chen, Jinyuan Wu

entry.summary: PGL-Net is a lightweight real-world dehazing network that incorporates physical inductive biases via operator-level emulation, decoupling dehazing into global distribution rectification and local structural refinement. It avoids fragile physical inversion and heavy blind models for edge deployment.

entry.title: Hybrid deep learning-based phase diversity method for wavefront reconstruction

author.name: Y. Rodimkov, A. Kotov, K. Burdonov, S. Perevalov, V. Volokitin, I. Meyerov, A. Soloviev

entry.summary: This paper presents a hybrid wavefront reconstruction method for high-power laser adaptive optics, using a CNN to generate an initial wavefront estimate refined by L-BFGS optimization. It combines deep-learning speed with optimization accuracy to compensate non-common path aberrations more efficiently than iterative-only methods.

entry.title: EvoFlock: evolved inverse design of multi-agent motion

author.name: Craig Reynolds

entry.summary: EvoFlock is an automatic evolutionary method for tuning the many control parameters of multi-agent motion models such as bird flocks, crowds, and traffic, posing it as inverse design. It addresses the difficulty of manually finding parameter combinations for desired emergent group behaviors.

entry.title: WaveForward: An Omnidirectional Passive Wheeled Quadruped Robot with Casters

author.name: Chuanlin Zhao, Qifeng Zheng, Shuhan Wang, Tiancheng Ma, Weixian Lin, Xin Luo

entry.summary: WaveForward is a low-cost passive wheeled quadruped robot equipped with standard casters on each leg for omnidirectional mobility without specialized wheel hardware. It uses an asymmetric actor-critic RL structure leveraging privileged caster angle and velocity information plus a posture adjustment strategy.

entry.title: Toy transformers may represent belief-state geometry optimally but not minimally

author.name: LGOICOUR

entry.summary: Extends Shai et al.'s belief-state geometry work, showing a toy transformer retains predictively defunct belief-state information in its residual stream and sheds the oldest such information first only under capacity pressure. Suggests representations are optimal but not minimal.

entry.title: End-to-End Voice Intent Recognition for Spontaneous Human-Drone Interaction with Naive Users

author.name: Allan Henry (GIPSA-COPERNIC, GETALP, LPNC), Solange Rossato (GETALP), Christian Graff (LPNC), Sylvain Huet (GIPSA-COPERNIC), Jose-Ernesto Gomez-Balderas (GIPSA-COPERNIC)

entry.summary: Proposes an end-to-end spoken language understanding architecture for real-time French human-drone interaction handling disfluent naive-user speech, using a frozen SSL encoder, LSTM head, and cross-modal distillation. Introduces a new French spontaneous-speech corpus.

entry.title: UC-Search: Risk-Aware Test-Time Search for Delayed Constrained Time-Series Control

author.name: Xibai Wang

entry.summary: UC-Search is a model-agnostic test-time wrapper for time-series control under delayed decisions and hard feasibility constraints, using a feasibility automaton and bounded search to return risk-adjusted feasible actions. It includes a theorem characterizing when search reduces to one-step greedy versus when non-myopic value emerges.

entry.title: CrossAccent-TTS: Cross-Lingual Accent-Intensity Controllable Text-to-Speech via Disentangled Speaker and Accent Representations

author.name: Ram Annamdevula, Ankit Tatawat, Ashishkumar P. Gudmalwar, Nirmesh J. Shah, Pankaj Wasnik

entry.summary: CrossAccent-TTS enables cross-lingual accent control and conversion with intensity modulation while preserving speaker identity, using disentangled speaker and accent representations and an Accent Intensity Controller that injects weighted language embeddings. It targets low-resource and phonetically diverse Indic languages.

entry.title: HG-Bench: A Benchmark for Multi-Page Handwritten Answer-Region Grounding in Automated Homework Assessment

author.name: Chuangxin Zhao, Boyan Shi, Yanling Wang, Yijian LU, Canran Xiao, Jiali Chen, Jun Xia, Yan Wang, Ji Qi, Juanzi Li

entry.summary: HG-Bench is a benchmark for multi-page handwritten answer-region grounding in automated homework assessment, with 500 human-annotated K-12 samples and a hierarchical containment constraint linking question-level and step-level boxes. It introduces a page-aware evaluation protocol for localizing answers and reasoning steps.

entry.title: Low-Complexity Policy Tessellations in Structured Markov Decision Processes

author.name: Fredy Pokou (CRIStAL)

entry.summary: This paper studies optimal-policy geometry in structured Markov decision processes, showing that optimal policies induce simpler decision tessellations than the high-dimensional value functions typically approximated. It proposes boundary-based policy approximations with a loss decomposition linking performance degradation to action margins near indifference boundaries.

entry.title: Variable Bound Tightening for Nash Equilibrium Computation in Multiplayer Imperfect-Information Games

author.name: Sam Ganzfried

entry.summary: This paper introduces variable bound tightening to improve exact Nash equilibrium computation in multiplayer imperfect-information games via quadratically constrained programs from sequence-form representations. It builds on recent exact-computation approaches. Relevant for computational game theory.

entry.title: Towards Continuous Power Forecasting: Practical Continual Learning for Real-World Energy Systems in Nonstationary Time Series

author.name: Yujiang He, Frederic Uhrweiller, Bernhard Sick

entry.summary: This paper frames power forecasting as a continual learning problem under nonstationary conditions where retraining data is limited, proposing Continuous Power Forecasting using an adaptive continual learning framework for regression. It investigates practical effectiveness in real energy systems. Relevant for deployed forecasting under distribution shift.

entry.title: Multi-Stream Temporal Fusion for Financial Fraud Detection

author.name: Mohammadamin Dashti Moghaddam, Nick Sciarrilli

entry.summary: MSFT is a Multi-Stream Fraud Transformer that encodes heterogeneous event streams (transactions, logins, risk signals) with independent encoders and fuses them via configurable mechanisms. A systematic ablation compares five fusion strategies on a 10M-user dataset. Relevant for financial fraud detection.

entry.title: An iterative energy-based multimodal transformer for joint retrieval of wheat soil moisture, leaf area index, and plant height from Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2 time series

author.name: Shubham Kumar Singh, Peilei Fan, Suraj A. Yadav, Rajendra Prasad, Prashant K Srivastava

entry.summary: iEBT is an iterative energy-based multimodal transformer for joint retrieval of wheat soil moisture, leaf area index, and plant height from Sentinel-1 SAR and Sentinel-2 time series, treating retrieval as iterative energy minimization rather than direct regression to resolve radar-spectral ambiguities. Relevant for precision agriculture.

entry.title: EveLoad: Cognitive Workload Recognition from Event-Based Eye Movements

author.name: Guorui Lu, Shaohua Guan, Zhen Xu, Qinyu Chen

entry.summary: EveLoad recognizes cognitive workload from event-based eye movements captured by event cameras with microsecond temporal resolution, overcoming the limited temporal resolution of frame-based eye trackers during rapid eye movements. It targets adaptive rehabilitation and assistive interfaces. Relevant for human-state sensing in XR and robot-assisted rehabilitation.

entry.title: Learning Subset-Shared Invariances for Domain Generalization with Mixture-of-Experts

author.name: Tien-Hung Nguyen, Tien-Dat Tran, M. -Duong Nguyen, Kok-Seng Wong

entry.summary: This work proposes subset-shared invariance for domain generalization, arguing that enforcing invariance across all source domains discards transferable factors not universally shared. It implements the principle with a mixture-of-experts architecture where each expert aligns specific domain subsets.

entry.title: Graph-Based Phonetic Error Correction of Noisy ASR

author.name: Pratik Rakesh Singh, Mohammadi Zaki, Aneesh Mukkamala, Pankaj Wasnik

entry.summary: G-SPIN is a structured ASR error-correction framework combining a graph neural network that builds acoustically plausible candidate neighborhoods for flagged tokens with a masked language model for contextual correction. It targets residual lexical errors affecting semantically critical tokens like named entities, negations, and sentiment words.

entry.title: Hybrid-IR: Dual-Path Hybrid Retrieval with Iterative Reasoning for Complex Medical Question Answering

author.name: Sheng Wan, Jiahui Zhang, Zicheng Zhao, Shougang Ren

entry.summary: Hybrid-IR is a dual-path hybrid retrieval framework with iterative reasoning for complex medical question answering, addressing fragmented medical knowledge and insufficient static retrieval. It jointly preserves fine-grained semantics and structured global associations to support deeper reasoning while reducing hallucination.

entry.title: When Certainty Is an Artifact: Keyword Lexicon Blindness and the (Mis)Measurement of Rhetorical Stance

author.name: Bo Chen

entry.summary: Demonstrates that a robust keyword-lexicon finding about rhetorical certainty can be entirely a measurement artifact, with correlations collapsing when replaced by LLM-based semantic classification. It is a methodological caution for computational social science.

entry.title: Gastroendoscopy View Synthesis: A New Real Dataset and Evaluation

author.name: Masaki Minai, Yusuke Monno, Masatoshi Okutomi, Sho Suzuki

entry.summary: Introduces GastroNVS, the first real gastroscopy dataset for novel view synthesis with images, camera poses, and point clouds, and evaluates 3DGS methods for endoscopy. It targets applications like field-of-view extension and training digital twins.

entry.title: Reasonable Motion: A General ASP Foundation for Environment Constrained Movement Trajectory Computation

author.name: Julius Monsen, Jakob Suchan, Mehul Bhatt, Lars Karlsson

entry.summary: Introduces position graphs, an answer-set-programming-based hybrid method for computing environment-constrained branching motion trajectories as stable models, applicable to domains like autonomous driving. Combines qualitative and quantitative reasoning.

entry.title: Error-Aware TF-IDF Retrieval-Augmented Generation for ASR Error Correction

author.name: Mohammad Aref Jafari-Raddani

entry.summary: Proposes a lightweight, purely lexical error-aware TF-IDF RAG framework for ASR error correction targeting phonetic and loop hallucinations, integrating text normalization with an error-aware TF-IDF algorithm. Low-latency alternative to heavy cross-modal embeddings.

entry.title: What Does a Pathological Speech Assessment Model Know about Acoustic Features? A Case Study on Oral and Oropharyngeal Cancer Patients

author.name: Tuan Nguyen (LIA, AU), Corinne Fredouille (AU, LIA), Alain Ghio (LPL), Muriel Lalain (LPL), Virginie Woisard (UT2J, UT3, LNPL)

entry.summary: Investigates interpretability of a Wav2Vec 2.0 pathological speech intelligibility model for oral cancer patients via canonical correlation analysis against eGeMAPS acoustic descriptors, finding strongest correlations with spectral and prosodic features. Clarifies what such models encode.

entry.title: BCoughBench: Benchmarking Respiratory Acoustic Foundation Models Under Body-Coupled Wearable Sensor Conditions

author.name: Mayur Sanap, Prasanna Desikan, Edgar Lobaton

entry.summary: BCoughBench benchmarks respiratory acoustic foundation models on body-coupled wearable sensor conditions, showing meaningful AUROC drops compared to smartphone recordings because tissue and bone attenuate high frequencies. It highlights a deployment gap between how these models are evaluated and how they will actually be used clinically.

entry.title: Interpretable Concept-Guided Polynomial Tabular Kolmogorov-Arnold Network for EEG-Based Mild Cognitive Impairment Detection

author.name: Yosef Bernardus Wirian, Qiang Cheng

entry.summary: CPTabKAN is an interpretable EEG-based framework for mild cognitive impairment detection that maps EEG-derived features into physiologically organized concept encoders and uses a polynomial-transformed Kolmogorov-Arnold Network for classification. It unifies concept structure, cross-concept interaction, and interpretable nonlinear classification for sleep-EEG screening.

entry.title: SFL-MTSC: Leveraging Semantic Frame-Level Multi-Task Self-Consistency for Robust Multi-Intent Spoken Language Understanding

author.name: Po-Yen Chen, Berlin Chen

entry.summary: SFL-MTSC is a semantic frame-level multi-task self-consistency framework for multi-intent spoken language understanding that decomposes LLM predictions into intent-specific frames and applies domain-intent grouping, slot clustering, and path-support scoring instead of output-level majority voting. It improves robustness against decoding stochasticity in zero-shot SLU.

entry.title: Gradient-based inverse lithography for EUV masks via the waveguide method and a physics-informed neural operator

author.name: Vasiliy A. Es'kin, Egor V. Ivanov

entry.summary: This paper presents gradient-based inverse lithography for EUV masks using a differentiable waveguide method and a waveguide neural operator as end-to-end physics engines, recovering absorber permittivity via automatic differentiation of the full diffraction model. Numerical experiments on realistic 2D and 3D masks achieve desired wafer fields.

entry.title: Color Matters: Trigger Color Affects Success in Federated Backdoor Attacks

author.name: Kavindu Herath, Joshua C. Zhao, Saurabh Bagchi

entry.summary: This paper studies how trigger color affects success in federated backdoor attacks using natural visual accessories like masks and sunglasses as triggers. It shows that color manipulation alone meaningfully changes attack effectiveness in a controlled federated setting. Matters for understanding federated learning security vulnerabilities.

entry.title: Overview of HIPE-2026: Person-Place Relation Extraction from Multilingual Historical Texts

author.name: Juri Opitz, Maud Ehrmann, Corina Racl\'e, Andrianos Michail, Matteo Romanello, Simon Clematide

entry.summary: This overview paper presents results from HIPE-2026, a shared task on extracting person-place relations from noisy multilingual historical texts with temporally grounded relation types. It evaluated 17 teams on challenges like historical language variation and OCR noise. Relevant for digital humanities and historical NLP.

entry.title: Learning Diachronic Representations of Ancient Greek Letterforms

author.name: John Pavlopoulos, Spyros Barbakos, Lavinia Ferretti, Dionysis Voulgarakis, Asimina Paparrigopoulou, Maria Konstantinidou, Giuseppe De Gregorio, Isabelle Marthot-Santaniello, Paraskevi Platanou, Holger Essler

entry.summary: This work introduces three datasets and methods for diachronic representation learning of ancient Greek letterforms spanning centuries, using a similarity-weighted supervised contrastive loss and lacuna-driven augmentation to handle symbolic variation and degradation. Matters for digital paleography and handwriting analysis.

entry.title: Adaptive Joint Compression and Synchronisation in Federated Split Learning for IoT Rainfall Prediction

author.name: Wenjie Ding, Yi Sin Lin, Jiale Liu, Baoyi Liu, Guanghua Liu, Zhuolu Li, Suleiman Sabo, Chuadhry Mujeeb Ahmed, Aydin Abadi, Rehmat Ullah, Rajiv Ranjan

entry.summary: This paper presents a federated split learning framework for IoT rainfall prediction that jointly regulates activation compression and synchronization interval via a latency-driven scheduler with per-client smoothing. It addresses the communication bottleneck of repeated activation and gradient exchange. Relevant for bandwidth-constrained edge ML.

entry.title: Stagnant Neuron: Towards Understanding the Plasticity Loss in Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning Value Factorization Methods

author.name: Zhengzhu Liu, Zeming Gao, Haoyuan Qin, Jiawei Hu, Junhao Wu, Miao Zhu, Haipeng Zhang, Chennan Ma, Siqi Shen, Cheng Wang

entry.summary: KNIFE diagnoses plasticity loss in multi-agent RL value factorization as caused by stagnant neurons whose gradient updates become negligible relative to weights. It proposes replacing such neurons with composite units to retain knowledge while restoring adaptability.

entry.title: An Analysis of Posterior Collapse, Parameterization and Initialization in Variational Deep Gaussian Processes

author.name: Francisco Javier S\'aez-Maldonado, Juan Maro\~nas, Daniel Hern\'andez-Lobato

entry.summary: This paper analyzes posterior collapse in variational deep Gaussian processes, connecting it to the DSVI algorithm and the linear prior mean function used in intermediate layers. It studies how parameterization and initialization affect whether the variational posterior degenerates to the prior.

entry.title: Riazi-8B: An Urdu Large Language Model for Mathematical Reasoning

author.name: Azher Ali, Ibtsam Haider, Raja Khurram Shahzad, Seemab Latif, Mehwish Fatima

entry.summary: Presents Riazi-8B, an Urdu mathematical reasoning model built via continued pretraining on Urdu Wikipedia and SFT on Urdu chain-of-thought data from GSM8K. It addresses the gap in reasoning resources for low-resource languages.

entry.title: Evaluating Japanese Dialect Robustness Across Speech and Text-based Large Language Models

author.name: Tomoya Mizumoto, Yusuke Fujita, Hao Shi, Lianbo Liu, Atsushi Kojima, Yui Sudo

entry.summary: Investigates dialectal robustness of LLMs and speech-LLMs using Japanese dialects, defining robustness as performance ratio on dialect versus standard inputs. It examines how the base LLM's dialect understanding propagates to speech models.

entry.title: H-Adapter: Pose-Robust Hairstyle Transfer via Attention-Derived, Source-Aligned Hair Masks

author.name: Seulgi Jeong, Yunseong Cho, Sanghun Park

entry.summary: H-Adapter improves pose-robust hairstyle transfer by training with a region-specific loss that disentangles hair and non-hair objectives, inducing spatially disentangled cross-attention to derive a source-aligned hair mask for diffusion inpainting. It handles large head-pose discrepancies.

entry.title: ShutterMuse: Capture-Time Photography Guidance with MLLMs

author.name: Jiayu Li, Yixiao Fang, Tianyu Hu, Wei Cheng, Ping Huang, Zheheng Fan, Gang Yu, Xingjun Ma

entry.summary: ShutterMuse introduces CaptureGuide-Bench, a benchmark evaluating multimodal LLMs on capture-time photography guidance covering both camera composition decisions and subject pose recommendations. It reveals that general MLLMs handle composition decisions but struggle with precise refinement, while specialized cropping models lack subject guidance.

entry.title: Homomorphic Encryptions for Privacy Preserving Vision

author.name: Preey Shah, Rohan Virani, Sanjari Srivastava

entry.summary: This project applies fully homomorphic encryption to enable privacy-preserving computer vision inference on encrypted data, modifying CNN layers to support the additive and multiplicative operations FHE allows. It targets cloud ML-as-a-service for sensitive medical or financial imagery.

entry.title: Self Capacitive Tactile Sensor System designed for Companion Robots

author.name: Mohsin Ali, Hidenobu Sumioka, Shuhei Ikemoto

entry.summary: This paper presents a simple, scalable self-capacitance tactile sensing system for companion humanoid robots using a single conductive fabric layer to achieve low-latency, full-body sensing with minimal computational load. It avoids the complex multilayer structures and wiring of conventional tactile systems.

entry.title: Information from coincidences

author.name: Akshay Balsubramani

entry.summary: Proves a single algebraic mixed-coincidence identity that unifies several information-theoretic variational results, recovering Sanov-type concentration, Chernoff error exponents, and Donsker-Varadhan inequalities. It offers a compact theoretical lens on classical information theory cornerstones.

entry.title: Can weak AI watch strong AI?

author.name: IgorPereverzevDev

entry.summary: A small empirical experiment on scalable oversight, testing whether weaker monitor models can detect misaligned behavior in a stronger coding agent (Sonnet 4.5) across 20 tasks split between clean and misaligned. Examines detection reliability across an ensemble of mostly open-weight monitors.

entry.title: EmotionAI: A Privacy-Preserving Computational Intelligence Pipeline for Speech-Emotion-Grounded Conversational Analysis

author.name: Wai Laam Mak, Isibor Kennedy Ihianle, Pedro Machado

entry.summary: Presents EmotionAI, a fully local privacy-preserving pipeline coupling speech emotion recognition with an adversarial three-model LLM panel for timestamp-grounded, citation-constrained conversational analysis. Exposes cross-corpus fragility in zero-shot SER.

entry.title: Benchmarking the Alignment of Data-Quality Metrics, Human Judgment and Land-Cover Segmentation Performance for Earth Observation

author.name: \"Umit Mert \c{C}a\u{g}lar, Alptekin Temizel

entry.summary: This paper benchmarks whether common image-fidelity metrics (FID, KID, IS, LPIPS, SSIM) align with human judgment and downstream land-cover segmentation performance for Earth observation synthetic data. It finds fidelity metrics often diverge from actual downstream utility.

entry.title: Adaptive Oscillatory Inductive Bias for Modeling Sharp Prosodic Dynamics in Diffusion-Based TTS

author.name: Sandipan Dhar, Nirmesh J. Shah, Ashishkumar P. Gudmalwar, Pankaj Wasnik

entry.summary: This paper introduces an adaptive oscillatory nonlinearity for diffusion-based TTS decoders that improves modeling of sharp prosodic transitions and rapid pitch variations beyond standard Snake activations, while maintaining signal stability via a linear bypass. It addresses expressive speech synthesis limitations.

entry.title: AI-Assisted Computational Reproducibility on the FABRIC Testbed

author.name: Komal Thareja, Paul Ruth, Berent Aldikacti, Michael Zink

entry.summary: This paper demonstrates how the FABRIC testbed combined with LLM coding assistants (LoomAI) can simplify reproducing published experiments across networking, molecular dynamics, and genomics domains. It evaluates whether reproduced experiments support the same scientific conclusions, not just numerical matching. Relevant for AI-assisted computational reproducibility.

entry.title: SE-AGCNet: An End-to-End Framework for Joint Speech Enhancement and Loudness Control in Meeting Scenarios

author.name: Jinming Zhang, Wei Rao, Xionghu Zhong, Eng Siong Chng

entry.summary: SE-AGCNet is an end-to-end framework that jointly optimizes speech enhancement and automatic gain control for meeting scenarios with high volume variation. It leverages synergy where enhancement preserves quiet speech to enable better gain adjustment, plus a data simulation pipeline. Relevant for audio processing pipelines.

entry.title: Digital Twin-Driven Adaptive Sim-to-Real Alignment via Reinforcement Learning for Vibration-Based Bearing Health Monitoring Under Data Scarcity

author.name: Jinghan Wang, Yanjun Chen, Wei Zhang, Wentao Wu, Tianchen Liu, Gaoliang Peng

entry.summary: This work proposes a digital twin-driven sim-to-real alignment framework using RL for vibration-based bearing health monitoring under data scarcity, addressing heterogeneous fault-specific domain gaps. It avoids class-agnostic global transformations that distort inter-class separability. Relevant for predictive maintenance.

entry.title: Auto-Configured Explainable Graph Neural Networks for Multi-Site Pollution Prediction

author.name: Abdelkader Dairi, Fouzi Harrou, Ying Sun

entry.summary: This work introduces auto-configured explainable graph neural networks for multi-site particulate matter prediction, using a confusion-matrix-based graph construction to capture inter-class relationships plus a hybrid loss combining energy distance and Huber loss. It is evaluated on Salt Lake City air pollution data. Relevant for spatiotemporal pollution forecasting.

entry.title: CKM-Driven Communication-Aware UAV Intelligent Trajectory Optimization for Urban Inspection

author.name: Yang Xiaomeng, Jia Ziye, Zhu Qiuming, Wu Qihui

entry.summary: This paper proposes a channel knowledge map-driven trajectory planning framework for multi-UAV urban inspection, using a diffusion model to reconstruct global channel quality from sparse observations and a global-to-local planning scheme. It integrates channel modeling with trajectory decision-making. Relevant for communication-aware UAV operations.

entry.title: Re-mixing Embeddings for Patient Augmentation in Data Scarce Multiple Instance Learning

author.name: Muhammed Furkan Dasdelen, Fatih Ozlugedik, Anastasia Litinetskaya, Nassir Navab, Carsten Marr, Ario Sadafi

entry.summary: This work introduces a statistically grounded patient augmentation method for data-scarce medical Multiple Instance Learning, generating realistic patients in embedding space via Gaussian Mixture Models over pooled instance embeddings. New patients are created by sampling from learned disease-specific cluster distributions without needing examples from all categories.

entry.title: REViT: Roto-reflection Equivariant Convolutional Vision Transformer

author.name: Sheir A. Zaheer, Alexander C. Holston, Chan Y. Park

entry.summary: REViT proposes a discrete roto-reflection group equivariant vision transformer with convolutional attention that preserves rotational, flip, and positional symmetry in feature maps. It offers a simpler way to achieve equivariance in vision transformers compared to prior CNN-focused approaches.

entry.title: FedReLa: Imbalanced Federated Learning via Re-Labeling

author.name: Guangzheng Hu, Patricia Men\'endez, Feng Liu, Mingming Gong, Guanghui Wang, Liuhua Peng

entry.summary: FedReLa addresses coexisting class imbalance and data heterogeneity in federated learning through a feature-dependent label re-allocator that re-labels samples to correct biased global distributions. It targets extreme conditions with severe class absence across clients where data-level methods typically struggle.

entry.title: The Tatoxa System for Text Detoxification in Low-Resource Languages: The Case of Tatar

author.name: Ilseyar Alimova, Bogdan Monogov, Artyom Mazur, Daniil Antonov, Vsevolod Karimov, Vitaliy Egorov, Bulat Khakimov, Alexander Panchenko

entry.summary: Presents Tatoxa, a text detoxification system for Tatar that outperforms open-source and commercial LLMs, with a new dataset and cross-lingual transfer experiments. It extends content-safety tooling to a low-resource language.

entry.title: How Large Language Models Source Brand Reputation Across Languages and Markets

author.name: Dmitrij Zatuchin

entry.summary: Analyzes 167k URL-grounded citations LLMs use to answer brand questions across 12 markets and 13 languages, finding 85.7% point to third-party rather than brand-owned sources. It studies AI brand visibility at the source-attribution level.

entry.title: SAC$^2$-Net: Semantic Anchoring and Complementary-Consensus Fusion for Multimodal Micro-Expression Recognition

author.name: Xuepeng Zheng, Tong Chen

entry.summary: SAC2-Net fuses optical flow and motion magnification modalities for micro-expression recognition, exploiting their asymmetric failure patterns via semantic anchoring and complementary-consensus fusion. It handles cross-modal heterogeneity and spatial misalignment.

entry.title: $S^{2}$-FracMix: Label-Preserving Self-Saliency Mixup Augmentation

author.name: Khawar Islam, Arif Mahmood, Xin Jin, Naveed Akhtar

entry.summary: S2-FracMix is a label-preserving data augmentation method that extracts salient patches and reinserts them into non-salient regions of the same image, avoiding cross-sample semantic disruption common in mixup. It adds a fractal self-similarity mixing scheme to improve robustness and scale-invariant feature learning.

entry.title: Thinking to recall: How reasoning unlocks parametric knowledge in LLMs

author.name: Unknown

entry.summary: A Google research blog post on how reasoning (chain-of-thought style) helps LLMs surface and recall their parametric knowledge, framed under generative AI. The provided content is minimal but the topic concerns reasoning-driven knowledge retrieval.
