entry.title: ATMA: Length-Invariant Language Modeling via Polar Attention and Gated-Delta Compression Memory

author.name: Habibullah Akbar

entry.summary: ATMA is a hybrid convolutional-attention architecture introducing polar attention and gated-delta compression memory to achieve length-invariant language modeling, avoiding softmax dilution and long-context perplexity collapse. It targets the structural tension between local sliding-window and global full attention.

entry.title: Neural Machine Translation for Low-Resource Tangkhul--English

author.name: Chormi Zimik Vashai, Agniva Maiti

entry.summary: This study builds neural machine translation systems for the severely under-resourced Tangkhul-English language pair, fine-tuning ByT5-large and mT5-small on a custom 38k-sentence corpus and reporting strong BLEU and COMET scores. It establishes NLP infrastructure for a Tibeto-Burman language with virtually none before.

entry.title: Explainable Control Framework (XCF) based on Fuzzy Model-Agnostic Explanation and LLM Agent-Supported Interface

author.name: Faliang Yin, Hak-Keung Lam, David Watson

entry.summary: XCF is an explainable control framework combining fuzzy model-agnostic explanation with an LLM agent-supported interface to make controller decisions human-understandable. It provides model-agnostic explanations for closed-loop controllers. Relevant for explainable control systems.

entry.title: Towards Robust EEG Decoding Based on Riemannian Self-Attention

author.name: Shaocheng Jin, Tao Zhou, Rui Wang, Ziheng Chen, Xiaoqing Luo, Xiaojun Wu, Josef Kittler

entry.summary: This work proposes a Riemannian self-attention mechanism for robust EEG decoding on the manifold of symmetric positive definite matrices, capturing local relationships that prior SPD methods miss. It also generalizes beyond the commonly used Affine-Invariant Metric to improve performance on low-SNR EEG signals.

entry.title: The Inference-Compute Frontier and a Latency-Efficient Architecture for Limit Order Book Prediction

author.name: C. Evans Hedges

entry.summary: This paper investigates whether scaling-law-style inference-compute frontiers appear in limit order book prediction, finding that predictive loss versus compute follows a power law with strong extrapolation across architectures. It introduces FastBiNLOB, a latency-efficient architecture motivated by the gap between compute and latency scaling.

entry.title: Blasto-Net: An Explainable Multi-Task Learning for Blastocyst Segmentation, Grading, and Implantation Prediction

author.name: Zahra Asghari Varzaneh, Reza Khoshkangini, Magnus Johnsson, Thomas Ebner, Lars Johansson

entry.summary: Blasto-Net is an explainable multi-task deep learning model for IVF that simultaneously segments blastocyst compartments, performs morphological grading, and predicts implantation outcome in a single forward pass. It uses an EfficientNet-B3 encoder with attention modules including a novel Edge-Aware Attention Module.

entry.title: Taxonomy-aware deep learning for hierarchical marine species classification in underwater imagery

author.name: Dan Zimmerman, Dimitris A. Pados, George Sklivanitis

entry.summary: This work presents a taxonomy-aware deep learning framework for hierarchical marine species classification that aligns training loss and inference with biological taxonomy, combining taxonomy-weighted loss, minimum-risk Bayesian inference, multi-scale encoding, and per-rank classification heads. It handles domain shift, fine-grained similarity, and uneven annotation granularity in underwater imagery.

entry.title: Multilingual Hematology Visual Question Answering Dataset

author.name: Hajra Malik, Hafiza Tooba Aftab, Abdul Rehman, Mohsen Ali, Waqas Sultani

entry.summary: Introduces a multilingual hematology visual question answering dataset addressing the English-centric bias in medical VLM resources, motivated by Urdu-English mismatches in Pakistani healthcare. It surveys clinicians to ground the language gap.

entry.title: Efficient Cross-Scale Invertible Hiding Network with Spatial-Frequency Collaboration and Non-Invertible Mechanism

author.name: Junxue Yang, Xin Liao

entry.summary: CrosInv is an efficient cross-scale invertible image-hiding network combining spatial-frequency collaboration and a non-invertible mechanism to overcome single-scale, single-domain limits of prior INN-based steganography. It improves hidden and recovered image quality.

entry.title: OracleAnalyser: Analysing Implicit Semantics of Oracle Bone Scripts through MLLMs with Post-training

author.name: Zijia Song, Yelin Wang, Zhengyi Ma, Zitong Yu, Tianheng Wang, Jiahuan Zhang, Taorui Wang, Kaicheng Yu

entry.summary: OracleAnalyser is a reasoning framework for analyzing implicit semantics of oracle bone scripts via post-trained MLLMs, introducing a Stable Focal Preference Optimization algorithm and dedicated reasoning and preference datasets. It moves beyond mere recognition toward deeper script analysis.

entry.title: Can You Hide From a Natural Language Autoencoder?

author.name: Yogesh Prabhu

entry.summary: Stress-tests Natural Language Autoencoders' Activation Verbalizer, finding it can be fooled via prefix-tuned activations that flip explanations while preserving behavior, and via fine-tuning on hidden taboo words with penalties to evade recovery. Notes a caveat that some evasion may stem from model forgetting.

entry.title: Agentic Knowledge Tracing: A Multi-Agent LLM Architecture for Stealth Assessment of Financial Literacy in Serious Games

author.name: Gabriel Santos, Rita Julia, Marcelo Nascimento

entry.summary: Presents a multi-agent LLM pipeline for stealth assessment of financial literacy from gameplay events in a serious game, classifying actions and using domain-specific agents aligned to the OECD framework. Validated against expert annotations.

entry.title: Position Spaces and Graphs

author.name: Rita-Nathalia Assaf, Tom Davot, Fr\'ed\'eric Lardeux, Fr\'ed\'eric Saubion

entry.summary: Introduces a graph-based reasoning framework using strict partial orders to model horizontal/vertical alignment of tokens, with theoretical analysis of consistency and complexity of pattern discovery. A formal contribution to spatial reasoning representations.

entry.title: Velocity Prediction in Automatic Guitar Transcription

author.name: Jackson Loth, Xavier Riley, Simon Dixon, Emmanouil Benetos

entry.summary: Presents a method for predicting note velocity in automatic guitar transcription by pretraining on synthetic virtual-instrument data with velocity labels then transferring to real audio. Fills a gap in non-piano velocity prediction.

entry.title: AeroCast: Probabilistic 3D Trajectory Prediction for Non-Cooperative Aerial Obstacles via Transformer-MDN Architecture

author.name: Syed Izzat Ullah, Jose Baca

entry.summary: AeroCast uses a Transformer with a mixture density network to produce probabilistic 3D trajectory predictions for non-cooperative aerial obstacles like birds and drones, capturing multi-modal motion that deterministic predictors miss. It supports collision avoidance for autonomous aerial vehicles in shared airspace.

entry.title: Edges Before Embeddings: A Confidence-Aware Blur Gate for Vision-Language Pipelines

author.name: Duy Tran Thanh

entry.summary: This work presents a lightweight CPU-friendly image quality gate that classifies images as sharp, blurred, or uncertain in roughly 7ms to avoid wasting compute on degraded vision-language inputs. It introduces an Edge Prior Module using Laplacian-magnitude channels and confidence-aware routing. Practical for production vision pipelines.

entry.title: Training Dynamics of Neural Software Defect Predictors under Coupled Data-Quality Issues

author.name: Emmanuel Charleson Dapaah, Philip Makedonski, Jens Grabowski

entry.summary: This study investigates how neural training dynamics (gradients, weights, biases, error trajectories) manifest when software defect prediction datasets have coupled data-quality issues like class imbalance and overlap together. Prior work examined these issues in isolation. Relevant for understanding defect predictor reliability.

entry.title: Geometry-Anchored Transport Framework for Exemplar-Free Class-Incremental Learning

author.name: Hongye Xu, Bartosz Krawczyk

entry.summary: The Geometry-Anchored Transport Framework tackles exemplar-free class-incremental learning by formulating feature transport as an endogenous training constraint rather than a post-hoc step. This prevents distortion of the legacy manifold and improves retroactive alignment of class-conditional statistics.

entry.title: State Space Models Meet Remote Sensing: A Survey

author.name: Qinzhe Yang, Chenyang Liu, Jia Xu, Zhenwei Shi, Zhengxia Zou

entry.summary: This survey comprehensively reviews State Space Model approaches in remote sensing, covering applications to dense visual prediction, multimodal, and temporal remote sensing data along with customized architectures. It offers a multi-dimensional analysis of how SSMs address unique remote-sensing challenges.

entry.title: A 3D-Printable Dataset for Fair Testing and Comparisons of Tactile Sensors

author.name: Dexter R. Shepherd, Nicolas Herzig, Phil Husbands, Andrew Philippides, Chris Johnson, William Kimbell

entry.summary: This work introduces a 3D-printable dataset of mathematically defined textures designed for reproducible fabrication across printers and filaments, enabling fair comparison between tactile sensors. The dataset includes six parametrically generated surface patterns with controlled spatial frequency, amplitude, and directional structure.

entry.title: The cognitive, affective, and behavioral expression of self-stigma among people who use drugs in online substance use communities

author.name: Layla Bouzoubaa, Hyung Wook Choi, Milan Varghese, Valerie Earnshaw, Rezvaneh Rezapour

entry.summary: This study develops a ten-indicator codebook for self-stigma across cognitive, affective, and behavioral domains and uses an LLM validated against expert coding to analyze its prevalence and temporal patterns in over 72,000 Reddit posts by people who use drugs. It demonstrates substantial inter-coder and human-LLM agreement.

entry.title: Introducing corpora Hlava Cor and Hlava AD: Human Label Variation in Coreference and Discourse Relations

author.name: Anna Nedoluzhko, \v{S}\'arka Zik\'anov\'a, Ji\v{r}\'i M\'irovsk\'y, Milan Straka, Eva Haji\v{c}ov\'a

entry.summary: Introduces two Czech corpora (Hlava Cor and Hlava AD) with multiple parallel annotations and annotator explanations for coreference and discourse relations. It studies human label variation, showing systematic disagreement in how people interpret text coherence.

entry.title: Are We There Yet? Exploring the Capabilities of MLLMs in Assistive AI Applications

author.name: Shayon Dasgupta, Avijit Dasgupta, C. V. Jawahar

entry.summary: Evaluates whether multimodal LLMs are ready for assistive AI applications requiring robust visual recognition, contextual reasoning, and multilingual comprehension. It assesses MLLM effectiveness in real-world assistive settings.

entry.title: Efficient Remote Sensing Instance Segmentation with Linear-Time State Space Distilled Visual Foundation Models

author.name: Qinzhe Yang, Keyan Chen, Jia Xu, Zhenwei Shi, Zhengxia Zou

entry.summary: KidRisk is a new dataset of 2,500 videos and 10,000 images for recognizing dangerous children's actions, with vision-language baselines outperforming traditional deep learning models. It targets child-safety action recognition.

entry.title: Energy-Efficient CNN Acceleration with MSDF Digit-Serial Arithmetic on FPGA

author.name: Muhammad Usman, Yousef Sadegheih, Dorit Merhof

entry.summary: This paper presents energy-efficient FPGA acceleration of U-Net convolutional layers using most-significant-digit-first digit-serial arithmetic, introducing a merged multiply-add architecture that fuses operations into a single pipeline to reduce startup latency. It targets compact, low-power image segmentation hardware.

entry.title: Action ControlNet: A Lightweight Delay-Aware Adapter for Smooth Asynchronous Control in Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Tiecheng Guo, Meng Guo

entry.summary: Proposes Action ControlNet, a lightweight delay-aware adapter that smooths asynchronous control in vision-language-action robot models by conditioning on the executed motion suffix to avoid handoff jitter. It addresses VLA inference latency without full retraining or architecture-specific runtime logic.

entry.title: Perspectives on Continual Learning: Survey Results and Forecasts

author.name: Rauno Arike

entry.summary: Summarizes survey results from AI safety researchers on continual learning for LLM agents, covering agreement with the sequence's arguments, risk worries, forecasts, and promising research angles. Includes an overview of other experts' CL forecasts.

entry.title: Proactive Systems in HCI and AI: Concepts, Challenges, and Opportunities

author.name: Nima Zargham, Sharon Ferguson, Jaisie Sin, Cosmin Munteanu, Anastasia Kuzminykh

entry.summary: This HCI/AI survey examines proactive systems that anticipate user needs and act without explicit input, arguing the concept of proactivity is loosely and inconsistently defined across research. It aims to clarify concepts, challenges, and opportunities for designing such systems.

entry.title: Stabilizing black-box algorithms through task-oriented randomization

author.name: Yali Wang, Zhaojun Wang

entry.summary: This paper introduces a task-oriented randomization methodology to stabilize black-box algorithm outputs, adapting its strategy to the input data's generative structure including unstructured complexities. It provides theoretical stability guarantees for trustworthy AI.

entry.title: Taxonomy of Risks on Automated Fact-Checking Systems Considering its Propagation

author.name: Jun Yajima, Tatsuya Oka, Takao Okubo

entry.summary: This paper develops a taxonomy of risks for automated fact-checking systems that use AI and LLMs, considering how incorrect judgments and posting of erroneous results can propagate misinformation or defamation across social networks. It systematizes the risks introduced by deploying these systems at scale.

entry.title: A welding penetration prediction model for laser welding process based on self-supervised learning using physics-informed neural networks

author.name: Sen Li, Xiaoying Liu, Xiaojian Xu, Chendong Shao, Yaqi Wang, Ling Lan, Xinhua Tang, Haichao Cui

entry.summary: SimPhysNet is a self-supervised learning method using physics-informed neural networks for laser welding penetration prediction with limited labeled images. It embeds physical priors to overcome supervised learning's dependence on extensive labeled data. Relevant for industrial weld quality monitoring.

entry.title: A cross-process welding penetration status prediction algorithm based on unsupervised domain adaptation in laser and TIG welding

author.name: Sen Li, Haichao Cui, Chendong Shao, Yaqi Wang, Xinhua Tang

entry.summary: This paper proposes unsupervised domain adaptation with gradual source domain expansion for cross-process weld penetration prediction, transferring between physically distinct welding processes like TIG and laser welding. It achieves high accuracy in both same-process and cross-process transfer. Relevant for industrial fault classification under domain shift.

entry.title: Low Variance Trust Region Optimization with Independent Actors and Sequential Updates in Cooperative Multi-agent Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Bang Giang Le, Viet Cuong Ta

entry.summary: This paper addresses high-variance advantage estimation in cooperative multi-agent RL under independent actors with sequential trust-region updates. It proposes a low-variance approach to stabilize convergence when re-estimating joint advantages via importance sampling.

entry.title: FUTO Swipe: Layout-Agnostic Neural Swipe Decoding

author.name: David Lee Miller, Aleksandras Kostarevas

entry.summary: FUTO Swipe presents a layout-agnostic neural swipe decoder that supplies the keyboard layout at inference time to map spatial-temporal predictions to key logits, rather than learning the layout during training. The authors also release the largest MIT-licensed swipe dataset to address scarce non-QWERTY data.

entry.title: Generating Input Distributions for Explaining Portfolio Optimization Pipelines

author.name: Batuhan Ata\c{s}, Nur\c{s}en Ayd{\i}n, E. Mehmet K{\i}ral, \c{S}. \.Ilker Birbil

entry.summary: This work proposes a predict-optimize-explain framework using gradient-based sample generation to interpret portfolio optimization pipelines by identifying macroeconomic conditions inducing specified outcomes. It probes decision pipelines through economically meaningful what-if questions rather than feature-importance methods.

entry.title: Evaluation Protocols and Validation for Cameras in Indoor Healthcare Monitoring

author.name: Amirhossein Dadashzadeh, Jingjing Liu, Qianhui Men, Qiushuo Cheng, Kirsty Scott, Lisa Alcock, Ian Craddock, Majid Mirmehdi

entry.summary: Presents two technical validation protocols for RGB and RGB-D cameras in indoor healthcare monitoring, evaluating metrological performance and algorithm accuracy together under real-world conditions like lighting and occlusion. It enables informed camera selection for clinical deployment.

entry.title: Swazure: Swarm Measurement of Pose for Flying Light Specks

author.name: Hamed Alimohammadzadeh, Shahram Ghandeharizadeh

entry.summary: Swazure is a swarm pose-measurement technique for Flying Light Specks (miniature display drones), solving missing sensor data when a drone must track another outside its sensor's accurate range. It uses cooperation among drones to abstract physical data independence and extend effective sensing range.

entry.title: A functional central limit theorem for kernel gradient flow and infinitesimal gradient boosting

author.name: Cl\'ement Dombry (LMB), Jean-Jil Duchamps (LMB)

entry.summary: Establishes a functional central limit theorem for infinitesimal gradient boosting, showing rescaled deviations from the deterministic limit converge to a Gaussian process in an RKHS associated with softmax gradient trees. It also provides a general stochastic perturbation analysis of ODEs in Banach spaces.

entry.title: Phoneme-Level Mispronunciation Screening in Polish-Speaking Children with an Explainable Assistant

author.name: Milosz Dudek, Daria Hemmerling, Kamil Kwarciak, Maciej Stroinski, Maria Pensko, Mateusz Kowalewski, Leonid Pavlovskyi, Sebastian Jurczak, Anna-Mariia Vitkovska, Zuzanna Miodonska, Natalia Mocko, Michal Krecichwost

entry.summary: This paper presents a phoneme-level mispronunciation screening pipeline for Polish-speaking children focused on sibilant errors, combining a wav2vec2 CTC recognizer with alignment-based error typing and an explainable caregiver assistant. It targets accessible speech-sound screening outside clinical settings.

entry.title: The impact of artificial intelligence on enterprise software user roles

author.name: Isabel Unger, Elizangela Valarini, Martin Schrepp, Nina Hollender, Gabriela Rocha, Erik Bertram

entry.summary: This qualitative study investigates how AI reshapes professional user roles within SAP's Business Technology Platform through 20 expert interviews and a 24-participant workshop, finding increasing automation of operational tasks, expanding human-AI collaboration, and growing reliance on agentic systems. It draws implications for enterprise user-role frameworks.

entry.title: Probabilistic Agents in Deterministic Audits: Evaluating Multi-Agent Systems for Automated Audits Based on the German IT-Grundschutz

author.name: Lea Roxanne Muth, Marian Margraf

entry.summary: This companion paper implements and empirically evaluates a multi-agent system with HybridRAG for partially automating German IT-Grundschutz audits, examining the tension of using probabilistic LLM agents for deterministic audit requirements. It introduces new evaluation approaches for certification automation.

entry.title: DFMU: Data-Frugal Machine Unlearning

author.name: Sajith U, Prateek Keserwani

entry.summary: DFMU proposes a data-frugal machine unlearning method that reduces the computational cost of removing concepts, attributes, or classes from trained models without extensive retraining. It aims for faster retain-set accuracy convergence with minimal performance drop.

entry.title: Hierarchical Graph Learning for Calendar Spread Strategies in Commodity Futures Markets

author.name: Yoonsik Hong, Diego Klabjan

entry.summary: This work proposes a hierarchical graph learning approach for calendar spread trading strategies in commodity futures markets, modeling underlying assets and individual contracts at two levels with cross-level edges capturing contract-to-asset connections. It addresses gaps in learning-based CS methods and maturity-dependent interrelationships.

entry.title: Dziri Voicebot: An End-to-End Low-Resource Speech-to-Speech Conversational System for Algerian Dialect

author.name: Dihia Lanasri, Fairouz Taki, Asma Kemmoum

entry.summary: Builds Dziri Voicebot, a modular end-to-end speech-to-speech system for the Algerian dialect integrating ASR, NLU, RAG, and TTS. It tackles low-resource challenges including code-switching with French and lack of standardized orthography.

entry.title: Wear-Clearance-Impact Coupling in the Jansen Linkage: A Gait-Durability-Optimized Design Slows Joint Loosening

author.name: Jichao Wang

entry.summary: This study models the Jansen walking linkage with realistic clearance joints, contact laws, and friction, coupling Archard wear to a wear-clearance-impact feedback loop to predict in-service degradation rather than relative wear rankings. It finds a gait-durability-optimized design slows joint loosening.

entry.title: G2DP: Diffusion Planning with Spatio-Temporal Grid Guidance

author.name: Hang Yu, Ye Jin, Alessandro Canevaro, Julian Schmidt, Julian Jordan, Peizheng Li, Marc Kaufeld, Silvan Lindner, Johannes Betz, Wilhelm Stork

entry.summary: Proposes G2DP, a diffusion-based motion planner for autonomous driving that enforces dense spatio-temporal grid constraints via inference-time guidance, improving safety and route adherence in interactive traffic. It moves beyond sparse entity-centric guidance used by prior diffusion planners.

entry.title: The Hitchhiker's Guide to Agentic AI: From Foundations to Systems

author.name: Haggai Roitman

entry.summary: A practitioner-oriented book/reference covering the full stack of building agentic AI systems, from transformer foundations and training methods through alignment, reasoning, and production deployment. It serves as a comprehensive educational resource rather than presenting novel research findings.

entry.title: Fuzzy Quantification over OWL Ontologies and Knowledge Graphs

author.name: Enrique Palac\'in, Fernando Bobillo, Ignacio Huitzil, Francesca A. Lisi, Umberto Straccia

entry.summary: Presents a framework and tool (Q2S2) for evaluating fuzzy quantification queries over standard and fuzzy ontologies and knowledge graphs, agnostic to quantifier type and data source. Supports flexible knowledge-graph querying.

entry.title: GCT-MARL: Graph-Based Contrastive Transfer for Sample-Efficient Cooperative Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Animesh Animesh, Satheesh K Perepu, Kaushik Dey

entry.summary: GCT-MARL is a transfer learning framework for cooperative multi-agent reinforcement learning that uses a multi-view graph contrastive backbone with adaptive alignment loss to speed convergence when transferring across agent populations of different sizes. It claims faster training than from-scratch approaches in both homogeneous and heterogeneous team settings.

entry.title: Lightweight PCGAE-Net: Parallel CrossGate Attention and Bottleneck AutoEncoder for Efficient 5G Channel Prediction

author.name: Uma Kishore Godavarti, K. Giridhar, Vanani Prince Dharmendrabhai, Anchit Panday, Madhan Raj Kanagarathinam

entry.summary: Lightweight PCGAE-Net is an efficient 5G channel-state prediction model that corrects architectural flaws in prior transformer-based predictors, notably a sequential attention ordering bias, rather than relying on post-hoc compression. It targets deployable high-accuracy CSI prediction on base-station hardware.

entry.title: Rate-Aware Quantum-Inspired Trajectory Learning for Interference-Limited Multi-UAV Networks

author.name: Khaoula Khaled, Muhammad Afaq, Ali Arshad Nasir, Zeeshan Kaleem

entry.summary: RA-QAGC combines rate-aware graph abstraction with decentralized reinforcement learning and quantum-annealed graph condensation to optimize trajectories for interference-limited multi-UAV networks, tackling the curse of dimensionality in real-time coordination. It guides UAVs toward throughput-optimal regions.

entry.title: How Complexity Contributes to Learning Opacity in Machine Learning

author.name: Joachim Stein, Eric Raidl

entry.summary: This article studies learning opacity in machine learning through the lens of complex dynamical systems, arguing that neural net training is essentially a complex system and that opacity stems from dynamical complexity. It identifies properties like sensitivity to initialization and feedback as sources. Matters for philosophy and epistemology of ML.

entry.title: Semantic Allocation in Ordered Bottlenecks: Predictive Residual Inference for Visual Representation Learning

author.name: Erik Ayari, Manuel Traub, Martin V. Butz

entry.summary: PRIOR introduces a predictive residual inference framework for ordered bottlenecks in visual representation learning, addressing weaknesses of masking-based ordering pressure that yields weak late-token utility. It adds an explicit refinement objective rather than relying on gradient exposure as a proxy for importance.

entry.title: Probing in the Wild: A Case Study of Self-Supervised Speech Representations on Mandarin Sub-dialects with Unsupervised Articulatory Analysis

author.name: Shu Shang, Fuliang Weng, Zeqian Hu, Yaqian Zhou

entry.summary: Probes self-supervised Mandarin speech models for articulatory feature representations under dialect variation using an unlabeled pipeline with a universal phone recognizer. It reveals structured phonetic patterns without manual annotation.

entry.title: SwarmFly: A simulation platform for UAV swarm experiment design and validation

author.name: Abhishek Phadke, Karthik Kumar Vasudeva, Abhishek Joshi

entry.summary: SwarmFly is a MATLAB-based modular simulation and test platform for multi-UAV swarms, offering four coordination modes, simulated IMU telemetry, IP-based geolocation, and a plugin architecture for behaviors and fault models. It addresses the lack of maintained, accessible open-source swarm simulation tools.

entry.title: MANGO: Automated Multi-Agent Test Oracle Generation for Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Pablo Valle, Shaukat Ali, Aitor Arrieta, Lionel Briand

entry.summary: Introduces MANGO, a multi-agent framework that automatically generates test oracles for vision-language-action robotic systems, replacing costly manually built symbolic oracles. It provides intermediate-behavior assessment for better fault localization.

entry.title: An Approach for a Supporting Multi-LLM System for Automated Certification Based on the German IT-Grundschutz

author.name: Lea Roxanne Muth, Marian Margraf

entry.summary: This paper proposes a multi-LLM system with hybrid retrieval-augmented generation combining LLMs and knowledge graphs to semi-automate German BSI IT-Grundschutz security certification across multiple phases. It aims to increase efficiency and reduce costs amid the NIS2 directive and specialist shortages.

entry.title: Memory-Efficient Policy Libraries with Low-Rank Adaptation in Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Samuel Valland Lyngset, Tor Viljen Raanaas, Gard Sveipe, Eirik M{\o}ller Nilsen, Jim Torresen, Kai Olav Ellefsen, Tobias L{\o}mo

entry.summary: This paper explores applying Low-Rank Adaptation to RL policy libraries for multi-task robotics, fine-tuning a PPO baseline to different tasks via LoRA to reduce memory usage. It assesses whether PEFT benefits transfer from LLM fine-tuning to robotics RL.

entry.title: Recursive QLSTM with Dynamic Variational Quantum Circuit Adaptation

author.name: Samuel Yen-Chi Chen, Yifeng Peng, Jiun-Cheng Jiang, Chun-Hua Lin, Kuo-Chung Peng, Junghoon Justin Park, Huan-Hsin Tseng, Hsin-Yi Lin, Kuan-Cheng Chen, Chen-Yu Liu, Shinjae Yoo

entry.summary: Extends Quantum LSTM via metacore-based recursive constructions and dynamic variational quantum circuit adaptation, testing architectures for sequential data and offering theoretical arguments for improved temporal propagation. A quantum machine learning model.

entry.title: Self-Modulating Quantum Fast-Weight Programmers for Efficient Adaptive Sequential Learning

author.name: Samuel Yen-Chi Chen, Yifeng Peng, Kuo-Chung Peng, Jiun-Cheng Jiang, Chun-Hua Lin, Junghoon Justin Park, Huan-Hsin Tseng, Hsin-Yi Lin, Kuan-Cheng Chen, Chen-Yu Liu, Shinjae Yoo

entry.summary: Proposes Self-Modulating Quantum Fast Weight Programmers that adaptively modulate fast-weight updates and historical memory, improving convergence stability across qubit counts and sequence lengths. A quantum sequence-learning model with theoretical justification.

entry.title: Inverse Reinforcement Learning for Interpretable Keystroke Biomarkers in Parkinson's Disease

author.name: Navin Bondade

entry.summary: This work applies inverse reinforcement learning to keystroke dynamics to recover interpretable per-subject reward functions explaining typing behavior in Parkinson's disease detection. It is presented as the first IRL application to keystroke biomarkers, offering interpretability over standard summary-statistic classifiers.

entry.title: Deep Neural Networks with Ordinal Loss for Medical Applications

author.name: Tal Dvora, Rotem Haba, Gonen Singer

entry.summary: This paper develops deep neural networks with ordinal loss functions for medical applications where labels have inherent severity ordering and asymmetric misclassification costs. It incorporates rank-based structure to penalize distant misclassifications more than adjacent ones.

entry.title: Fault of Our Stars: Behavioral Drivers of Rating-Sentiment Incongruence

author.name: Ramanaish Abaiyan, Ruththiragayan Sutharsan, Kusal Amantha, Anusan Krishnathas, Asma Rauff, Kovindarajah Sriyathurshan, Patalee Narasinghe, Nirasha Munasinghe, Nisansa de Silva, Sandareka Wickramanayake

entry.summary: Studies sentiment-rating incongruence in 16k Sri Lankan tourism reviews, finding 18.6% disagreement between star ratings and textual sentiment across six behavioral patterns. It questions the common practice of using ratings as weak sentiment labels.

entry.title: Cage-based Texture Transfer with Geometric Filtering

author.name: Rose Mei Zhou, Lynnette Hui Xian Ng, Adrian Xuan Wei Lim, Conor Griffin, Faraz Baghernezhad

entry.summary: Presents a cage-based geometric filtering method for real-time texture transfer that identifies Non-Cosmetic Zones for artifact suppression without large-scale models. It bridges speed and robustness for interactive texturing applications.

entry.title: FAR-LIO: Enabling High-Speed Autonomy through Fast, Accurate, and Robust LiDAR-Inertial Odometry

author.name: Maximilian Leitenstern, Marcel Weinmann, Patrick Haft, Tobias Lasser, Dominik Kulmer, Markus Lienkamp

entry.summary: Introduces FAR-LIO, a CUDA-accelerated LiDAR-inertial odometry framework using a parallelized voxel hashmap and sparsity-aware Generalized ICP for high-speed autonomous racing. It targets minimal latency and robustness under highly dynamic motion.

entry.title: Dream at SemEval-2026 Task 13: SALSA for Single-Pass Machine-Generated Code Detection

author.name: Ruslan Berdichevsky, Shai Nahum-Gefen, Elad Ben-Zaken

entry.summary: This SemEval-2026 system paper proposes SALSA, a single-pass autoregressive structured classification approach for detecting machine-generated code that maps each class to a dedicated output token. It emphasizes out-of-distribution generalization across unseen programming languages and domains.

entry.title: Cellular Predictions on the Move: What about Data?

author.name: Natalia Vesselinova, Pauliina Ilmonen

entry.summary: This work reframes mobile cellular load forecasting around data quality, hypothesizing that data informing on the processes generating cellular load yields larger gains than further model engineering. It proposes characterizing the underlying load-generating processes rather than relying solely on cellular-domain features.

entry.title: BluTrain: A C++/CUDA Framework for AI Systems

author.name: Adhitya Charan, Adwaid Suresh, Anuj Kumar, Aparna A, Dhanakumar K, Dharun M S, Dinesh G, Goutham Kumar Reddy K, Harshini V M, Jenifa D, Jona Delcy C A, Kathirvel S, Killi Uma Maheswara Rao, Kiruthik Kanna M, Kurra Vishnu Sai, Madhumithaa G K, Navin Kumar V, Ram Charan Golla, Revathi T, Rishikkanth R, Sanjay Krishna M V, Surendra Vendra

entry.summary: BluTrain is a lightweight, architecture-general deep learning training framework built from first principles in standard C++ and core CUDA, with natively implemented tensor modules and reverse-mode autodiff. It aims to give absolute control over hardware expression while abstracting systems complexity.

entry.title: Automatic Generation of Highlights for Academic Paper Via Prompt-based Learning

author.name: Yi Xiang, Chengzhi Zhang, Heng Zhang

entry.summary: This work investigates prompt-based learning for automatically generating highlights of academic papers, designing task-specific prompt templates combined with abstracts and evaluating models including GPT-2, T5, and ChatGPT. It targets journals that lack highlights to support literature retrieval and bibliometric analysis.

entry.title: Measuring Research Difficulty of Academic Papers: A Case Study in Natural Language Processing

author.name: Haochuan Li, Jingyuan Li, Yi Zhao, Heng Zhang, Yukai Yang, Zile Hu, Chengzhi Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes a system to quantitatively measure research difficulty of academic papers using collaboration, content, and reference features, with NLP as a case study. It correlates difficulty with academic impact for topic selection and resource allocation.

entry.title: Minimalist Preprocessing Approach for Image Synthesis Detection

author.name: Hoai-Danh Vo, Trung-Nghia Le

entry.summary: Introduces a minimalist preprocessing method for synthetic image detection that computes pixel gradients as a high-pass filter to highlight neighboring-pixel fluctuations. It targets low-cost deployment on smart devices.

entry.title: Learning Robot Visual Navigation in Crowds via Intention-Aware Scene Representations

author.name: Han Bao, Bingyi Xia, Hanjing Ye, Yu Zhan, Hao Cheng, Baozhi Jia, Wenjun Xu, Jiankun Wang

entry.summary: Introduces iCrowdNav, a visual crowd-navigation method using intention-aware scene representations and a spatio-temporal encoder over egocentric observations, instead of treating pedestrians as 2D points. It aims to improve DRL navigation policies in human crowds.

entry.title: How might outsiders make things go well?

author.name: Cleo Nardo

entry.summary: Analyzes the role of AI-safety 'outsiders' (community outside frontier labs) over the transition to ASI, arguing they are key to good outcomes and should maintain optionality across activities like verifying lab claims and exporting cheap safety techniques. Strategic essay on AI-safety ecosystem prioritization.

entry.title: Story Operators: Decomposing the Original $\to$ Sequel Transformation in Embedding Space

author.name: W. Frederick Zimmerman

entry.summary: This single-author work treats books as points in sentence-embedding space and literary sequels as geometric operators, decomposing the displacement between an original and its sequel along an interpretable PCA content basis. Across thirteen author pairs it reveals a small taxonomy of sequel types ranging from formulaic to transformative.

entry.title: A Hybrid CNN-LSTM Intrusion Detection Framework for Cybersecurity in Smart Renewable Energy Grids

author.name: Sajib Debnath, Remon Das

entry.summary: This paper proposes a hybrid CNN-LSTM intrusion detection system for smart renewable energy grids that combines spatial feature extraction with temporal sequence modeling to detect false-data-injection and DoS attacks. It targets limitations in modeling multi-step attacks under skewed class distributions.

entry.title: Pre-Warm: Input-Conditioned Weight Initialization for Convolutional Neural Networks

author.name: Rowan Martnishn

entry.summary: Pre-Warm is a zero-training-cost data-conditioned initialization for the first convolutional layer, extracting and clustering local patches via MiniBatchKMeans and using centroids to initialize half the first-layer filters. It derives closed-form rules for nearly all hyperparameters.

entry.title: Data-Driven Evolution of Library and Information Science Research Methods (1990-2022): A Perspective Based on Fine-grained Method Entities

author.name: Chengzhi Zhang, Yi Mao, Shuyu Peng

entry.summary: Analyzes the evolution of Library and Information Science research methods from 1990 to 2022 using fine-grained extracted method entities across algorithms, data, tools, and metrics. It traces the rise of the data-driven paradigm in LIS.

entry.title: Hierarchical Partial-Order Models for Ranking

author.name: Dongqing Li (Jessie), Geoff K. Nicholls (Jessie), Jeong Eun Lee (Jessie), Chuxuan (Jessie), Jiang

entry.summary: Introduces hierarchical partial-order (HPO) models for rank aggregation that extend poset-based consensus models to grouped data via a hierarchy of latent posets. This parallels mixture-model extensions of Mallows and Plackett-Luce, allowing incomparabilities and group structure.

entry.title: Type Checking Project Haystack Grids using JSON Schema and Pydantic

author.name: Thomas Hirsch, Samina Kadkhoda Masoumali, Gerald Schweiger

entry.summary: Presents a Python toolchain for Project Haystack building ontology, including a Trio-format parser and a generator producing Pydantic models and JSON Schemas for type-checking. Improves interoperability and validation in building energy ontologies.

entry.title: Towards Structuring an Arabic-English Machine-Readable Dictionary Using Parsing Expression Grammars

author.name: Diaa Mohamed Fayed, Aly Aly Fahmy, Mohsen Abdelrazek Rashwan, Wafaa Kamel Fayed

entry.summary: This paper presents a method to partly structure a machine-readable version of the Arabic-English Al-Mawrid dictionary using parsing expression grammars, converting entries from word streams into hierarchical structures with explicit components. It targets lexical resource creation for Arabic NLP applications.

entry.title: Shift Variant Image Degradation and Restoration Using Singular Value Decomposition

author.name: Arun D. Kulkarni

entry.summary: This paper presents an SVD-based framework for restoring images degraded by shift-variant motion blur, using a singular-value energy retention criterion to determine which small singular values to use. It addresses a harder restoration setting than standard shift-invariant deconvolution.

entry.title: Deviance-style normalization for jointly overdispersed counts

author.name: Akshay Balsubramani

entry.summary: Introduces a Dirichlet-multinomial deviance residualization for sparse, jointly overdispersed count matrices common in sequencing assays. The transform preserves sparsity, runs in constant time per nonzero entry, and properly accounts for overdispersion.

entry.title: How do we make uncertainty usable?

author.name: KatjaGrace

entry.summary: Discusses how to make subjective extinction-risk probabilities from AI researchers actionable, noting that many experts place 5-10%+ on AI causing extinction yet there is little institutional response. Suggests borrowing risk-handling frameworks from finance and insurance that operate on subjective, non-repeatable probabilities.

entry.title: Spam and Sentiment Detection in Arabic Tweets Using MARBERT Model

author.name: Abrar Alotaibi, Atta-ur Rahman, Raheel Alhaza, Wala Alkhalifa, Narjes Alhajjaj, Atheer Alharthi, Dhai Abushoumi, Maryam Alqahtani, Dania Alkhulaifi

entry.summary: This paper applies the MARBERT model to spam and sentiment detection in Arabic tweets, using deep learning to gauge customer satisfaction from Saudi Telecom feedback on Twitter. It targets sentiment analysis for Arabic-language customer service insights.

entry.title: Three Buddhist Vocabularies: Computational Stylometry of the English Pali Canon across Sutta, Vinaya, and Abhidhamma

author.name: Joy Bose

entry.summary: This computational stylometry study analyzes the English Pali Canon across the Sutta, Vinaya, and Abhidhamma Pitakas using Zipf distributions, type-token ratios, numeral density, and vocabulary overlap measures. It compares vocabularies across the three textual divisions and cross-tradition Vinaya texts.

entry.title: Learning Interpretable Text Signals for Structured Responses

author.name: Cixiao Jiang, Ben Powell, Niall MacKay

entry.summary: Proposes a joint non-negative matrix factorization and binomial regression model to learn interpretable text representations aligned with structured responses such as ratings. It aims to combine prediction and interpretation, recovering stable response-relevant text signals.

entry.title: AI pause: the case for ASAP

author.name: KatjaGrace

entry.summary: Argues for pausing AI development as soon as possible, countering the common view that we should pause only at the last moment. Claims pausing now increases the chance of pausing later and that braking takes time.

author.name: Gananath R

entry.summary: This paper proposes integrating variational autoencoders as a reusable neural network layer rather than as standalone models, with a new training strategy for networks incorporating such layers. It analyzes the resulting models' performance.

entry.title: ARTOO-DARTU: Studying AR-HRC With AR Obstruction Mitigation During a Warehouse Task

author.name: Christian Fronk, Hanting Ye, Zhehan Qu, Maria Gorlatova

entry.summary: Presents ARTOO-DARTU, an augmented-reality system for warehouse human-robot collaboration that conveys robot intentions while mitigating AR content that obstructs important real-world elements. It studies safety and usability of situated analytics around mobile robots.

entry.title: Fable in Shackles

author.name: ykevinzhang

entry.summary: An investment-framed analysis (in this report's alternate ecosystem) arguing that the restriction of Anthropic's Fable 5/Mythos 5 model after a cyber-jailbreak demonstration signals that hosted frontier intelligence is now subject to state action, making 'intelligence sovereignty' an investable theme. Discusses implications of model-access controls.

entry.title: We Should Train Frontier AIs on a Synthetic World, Not Ours

author.name: ZZZZZZ

entry.summary: Argues that training frontier AIs on a synthetic world rather than the real one would deny a misaligned model an accurate map of its environment, training situation, and escape routes, reducing takeover risk. An opinion piece advocating a controversial training strategy.

entry.title: The fuel of the future is already here: Why TRISO matters

author.name: Unknown

entry.summary: An Amazon Science post explaining TRISO nuclear fuel particles and Amazon's investment in next-generation nuclear technology to power AI infrastructure and cloud computing. It details the materials-science containment design of TRISO fuel.

entry.title: A Sensorised Lattice Footplate for a Semi-Active Prosthetic Foot

author.name: Jinze Ge, Jingcheng Sun, Chengxu Zhou

entry.summary: Presents a prosthetic foot prototype that embeds magnetic plantar force sensing directly inside a 3D-printed compliant lattice footplate, paired with a servo-adjustable hydraulic damper. The design enables plantar-force estimation and tunable stiffness without an external insole, supporting low-cost semi-active prosthetics.

entry.title: AI catastrophe: more like a genocide than a thought experiment

author.name: KatjaGrace

entry.summary: Argues that AI existential catastrophe would more likely resemble a gradual, gruesome genocide than a clean simultaneous death, challenging the abstract thought-experiment framing that dampens emotional response. Aims to make the risk feel concrete.

entry.title: Optimizing Abstractive Summarization With Fine-Tuned PEGASUS

author.name: Sadiul Arefin Rafi, Naimur Rahman, Kazi Nazibul Islam, Ha-mim Ahmad, Farig Yousuf Sadeque

entry.summary: Fine-tunes PEGASUS on the XL-Sum English corpus for abstractive summarization, comparing ROUGE scores against an mT5 baseline. It is a straightforward application study.

entry.title: Tree Transformers: A step towards generalizing the transformer architecture

author.name: astle dsa

entry.summary: An exploratory essay proposing 'tree transformers' that generalize the transformer to operate on structured (tree) data representations rather than flattening structure into vectors. Argues dataset structure is lost in vectorization and could be preserved.

entry.title: The Once And Future Fable #4

author.name: Zvi

entry.summary: A speculative narrative (set in this report's alternate ecosystem) tracking prediction-market odds and product signals about whether Anthropic's Fable 5 model will be restored to availability, citing string changes in Claude Code and reappearance in Amazon Bedrock. Commentary on a restricted model's potential return.

entry.title: Emcar: Embodied Controller for Animating Robots

author.name: Carlos Gomez Cubero, Elizabeth Jochum

entry.summary: Describes EMCAR, a no-code software tool that lets artists program collaborative robot motion using puppetry and drawing affordances. It aims to broaden human-robot interaction creativity and include non-technical users.

entry.title: What is up with e/acc?

author.name: KatjaGrace

entry.summary: Questions whether the effective accelerationist (e/acc) movement is a substantive intellectual force, noting few prominent adherents and unclear tenets. Opinion piece on AI cultural discourse.

entry.title: The [AI Box] Box

author.name: Donovan

entry.summary: Proposes applying governance structures (executives, legislatures, judiciaries) to the AI-box experiment, arguing the typical setup unrealistically places an AI one step from release via a single isolated human. Suggests multi-party deliberative release decisions as an analogy.

entry.title: Agentic Frameworks: Or different ways to make LLM API calls

author.name: astle dsa

entry.summary: An accessible overview of agentic framework design patterns built from basic text-in-text-out and structured-output LLM API calls, describing sequencing and branching paradigms among four. Explores when each topology outperforms a single call.

entry.title: How does such unprofessional AI get the job?

author.name: KatjaGrace

entry.summary: Reflects with surprise that large companies release unpolished, erratic AI products like early Sydney, contrasting with expected corporate professionalism, and notes a smooth AI phone agent at CVS. Observational commentary on AI product behavior.

entry.title: The shouting equilibrium

author.name: KatjaGrace

entry.summary: Describes a shouting-equilibrium dynamic where everyone exaggerates the importance of their message, leading to escalating attention-grabbing until all are maximally loud. An informal model of attention economics in communication.

entry.title: Could we have another family?

author.name: KatjaGrace

entry.summary: A speculative blog post asking whether society could deliberately construct new family-like institutions, sketching an AI-assisted scheme to sort people into supportive groups. It is exploratory social musing.

entry.title: World party

author.name: KatjaGrace

entry.summary: Muses on the difficulty of meeting compatible strangers due to screening barriers and speculates AI could enable high-bandwidth introductions in the future. Light social speculation.

entry.title: Why opine on massive communities?

author.name: KatjaGrace

entry.summary: A reflection on why people generalize about huge communities (AI safety, Rationalist, EA) despite only knowing small corners of them. Personal observation rather than analysis.

entry.title: Age experience

author.name: KatjaGrace

entry.summary: A short reflective blog post musing on how everyone experiences their current age for the first time, with all prior experience being of being younger, and how this might warp notions of acting one's age. It is personal philosophizing rather than research.

entry.title: Vortioxetine: probably not for me

author.name: KatjaGrace

entry.summary: A personal account of evaluating whether the antidepressant vortioxetine is helping, using the author's own mood logs and noting confounds. Self-experimentation narrative, not research.

entry.title: Drop constraints

author.name: KatjaGrace

entry.summary: Suggests that persistent uncomfortable feelings often signal self-imposed constraints treated as both mandatory and impossible, and recommends explicitly dropping constraints. Personal productivity/psychology reflection.

entry.title: Feelings as post-it notes

author.name: KatjaGrace

entry.summary: Offers a personal mental-health heuristic of treating lingering uncomfortable feelings as post-it-note reminders that can be discharged by recording the information elsewhere. Introspective self-help.

entry.title: Things are not a fixed size in mind-space

author.name: KatjaGrace

entry.summary: Reflects on how mental tasks occupy variable amounts of perceived 'size' in one's mind and that this can be intentionally adjusted. Introspective note.

entry.title: Therapy notes 10 June 2026

author.name: KatjaGrace

entry.summary: Personal therapy notes reflecting on the author's tendency to be in their head and how bodily sensations surface mainly around food. Introspective journaling.

entry.title: Shite world day

author.name: KatjaGrace

entry.summary: A reflection on a low mood and the realization that one's bleak perception of the world is a state of the perceiver rather than the world. Introspective journaling.

entry.title: Date concept: learn each other scav hunt

author.name: KatjaGrace

entry.summary: Suggests a date-format idea of a scavenger hunt for emotionally revealing items in a shop-filled area. Lifestyle blog content.

entry.title: North Berkeley: People and their properties

author.name: KatjaGrace

entry.summary: A personal account of considering and rejecting buying a multi-home property for friends, with lessons about mortgages and property availability. Lifestyle reflection.

entry.title: How to make catching up optional

author.name: KatjaGrace

entry.summary: A note on making 'catching up' optional in social gatherings by asking lighter framing questions like 'one good thing.' Personal social tip.

entry.title: Elephant seal IV

author.name: KatjaGrace

entry.summary: A very short image/photo post in a recurring elephant seal series with a subscription plug. No substantive content.

entry.title: Research Summary: June 24, 2026

author.name: AATF AI News Aggregator

entry.summary:
Today's research is dominated by safety/alignment and agentic AI, alongside a standout clinical deployment and a foundational theory contribution.

Clinical & applied impact: RaDaR, an open-source 32B reasoning LLM for rare disease diagnosis, anchors the day with a randomized AI-physician-assistance trial validating real-world deployability.

Safety & alignment (the strongest theme):

  • RL Towards Broadly Beneficial Models tests whether beneficial-behavior RL generalizes broadly and persistently across realistic multi-domain data.
  • Probing the Misaligned Thinking Process decomposes misalignment into 18 cognitive indicators with activation-based linear probing.
  • Self-Recognition Finetuning offers a mechanistic defense that prevents and reverses emergent misalignment across GPT-4.1 and Qwen2.5-32B.
  • RIFT-Bench introduces graph-driven dynamic red-teaming for agentic AI security.

Agents, interpretability & foundations:

  • OpenThoughts-Agent delivers a fully open agentic data-curation pipeline with 100+ controlled ablations.
  • AgenticInterpBench/HyVE benchmarks LLM agents as circuit explainers in mechanistic interpretability.
  • Bareinboim's Causal Reinforcement Learning introduction unifies causal inference and RL over counterfactual relations.

Theory & training dynamics: The Geometry Behind Diffusion and Flow Matching elegantly unifies both under Wasserstein-space gradient flows and geodesics, while a plasticity-loss study probes whether scale rescues continual learning in 5M–314M parameter transformers.
entry.content:
Today's research is dominated by safety/alignment and agentic AI, alongside a standout clinical deployment and a foundational theory contribution.

Clinical & applied impact: RaDaR, an open-source 32B reasoning LLM for rare disease diagnosis, anchors the day with a randomized AI-physician-assistance trial validating real-world deployability.

Safety & alignment (the strongest theme):

  • RL Towards Broadly Beneficial Models tests whether beneficial-behavior RL generalizes broadly and persistently across realistic multi-domain data.
  • Probing the Misaligned Thinking Process decomposes misalignment into 18 cognitive indicators with activation-based linear probing.
  • Self-Recognition Finetuning offers a mechanistic defense that prevents and reverses emergent misalignment across GPT-4.1 and Qwen2.5-32B.
  • RIFT-Bench introduces graph-driven dynamic red-teaming for agentic AI security.

Agents, interpretability & foundations:

  • OpenThoughts-Agent delivers a fully open agentic data-curation pipeline with 100+ controlled ablations.
  • AgenticInterpBench/HyVE benchmarks LLM agents as circuit explainers in mechanistic interpretability.
  • Bareinboim's Causal Reinforcement Learning introduction unifies causal inference and RL over counterfactual relations.

Theory & training dynamics: The Geometry Behind Diffusion and Flow Matching elegantly unifies both under Wasserstein-space gradient flows and geodesics, while a plasticity-loss study probes whether scale rescues continual learning in 5M–314M parameter transformers.

entry.title: A specialized reasoning large language model for accelerating rare disease diagnosis: a randomized AI physician assistance trial

author.name: Haichao Chen, Songchi Zhou, Zhengyun Zhao, Shikai Hu, Xianghong Jin, Hongwei Ji, Li He, Shuli Li, Yiming Qin, Xin Tan, Runfeng Shi, Yih Chung Tham, Jiaye Zhu, Ye Li, Ye Jin, Longhao Cao, Dawei Li, Honghan Wu, Hongqiu Gu, Guanqiao Li, Tudor Groza, Chunying Li, Dian Zeng, Weihong Yu, Gareth Baynam, Saumya Shekhar Jamuar, Min Shen, Shuyang Zhang, Bin Sheng, Sheng Yu, Tien Yin Wong

entry.summary: RaDaR is an open-source compact 32B reasoning LLM for rare disease diagnosis, trained on 49,170 real free-text cases plus 104,666 synthetic reasoning-enhanced cases, evaluated in a randomized AI physician assistance trial and outperforming larger open models including 671B DeepSeek. It matters for addressing scarce specialized expertise in timely rare disease diagnosis through a deployable model with clinical validation.

entry.title: Reinforcement Learning Towards Broadly and Persistently Beneficial Models

author.name: Akshay V. Jagadeesh, Rahul K. Arora, Khaled Saab, Ali Malik, Mikhail Trofimov, Foivos Tsimpourlas, Johannes Heidecke, Karan Singhal

entry.summary: This paper studies whether reinforcement learning on beneficial behaviors in realistic domains can produce broad and persistent alignment generalization beyond training distribution, constructing a dataset to measure traits like truthfulness, fairness, and corrigibility. It matters because RL can introduce reward hacking and deception, and the authors test whether beneficial-behavior RL generalizes out of distribution.

entry.title: Probing the Misaligned Thinking Process of Language Models

author.name: Kaiwen Zhou, Constantin Venhoff, Jonathan Michala, Xin Eric Wang, William Saunders

entry.summary: This paper proposes monitoring LLM misalignment by decomposing it into 18 fine-grained cognitive indicators (such as deception, sandbagging, self-preservation) and detecting them in internal activations via linear probes, with an out-of-distribution evaluation. It matters for reliably detecting misaligned behaviors in high-stakes deployments through interpretability-based monitoring.

entry.title: OpenThoughts-Agent: Data Recipes for Agentic Models

author.name: Negin Raoof, Richard Zhuang, Marianna Nezhurina, Etash Guha, Atula Tejaswi, Ryan Marten, Charlie F. Ruan, Tyler Griggs, Alexander Glenn Shaw, Hritik Bansal, E. Kelly Buchanan, Artem Gazizov, Reinhard Heckel, Chinmay Hegde, Sankalp Jajee, Daanish Khazi, Emmanouil Koukoumidis, Xiangyi Li, Hange Liu, Shlok Natarajan, Harsh Raj, Nicholas Roberts, Ethan Shen, Nishad Singhi, Michael Siu, Ashima Suvarna, Hanwen Xing, Patrick Yubeaton, Robert Zhang, Leon Liangyu Chen, Xiaokun Chen, Steven Dillmann, Saadia Gabriel, Xunyi Jiang, Anurag Kashyap, Boxuan Li, Yein Park, Minh Pham, Sujay Sanghavi, Lin Shi, Ke Sun, Yixin Wang, Zhiwei Xu, Erica Zhang, Siyan Zhao, Wanjia Zhao, Jenia Jitsev, Alex Dimakis, Benjamin Feuer, Ludwig Schmidt

entry.summary: OpenThoughts-Agent provides a fully open data curation pipeline for training broadly capable agentic models, with over 100 controlled ablation experiments revealing the importance of task sources and diversity, and a 100K-example training set. It matters because little is publicly known about curating training data for agents that generalize across diverse agentic tasks rather than a single benchmark.

entry.title: The Geometry Behind Diffusion and Flow Matching: Gradient Flows and Geodesics in Wasserstein Space

author.name: Yian Yao, Weiwei Zhang

entry.summary: This paper unifies diffusion and flow matching under the geometry of Wasserstein space, showing that the forward diffusion process descends the free energy and each denoising step realizes one JKO scheme step, recovering DDPM, DDIM, NCSN/SMLD, and energy matching as one scheme. It matters for providing a unified theoretical lens on generative modeling methods.

entry.title: Self-Recognition Finetuning can Prevent and Reverse Emergent Misalignment

author.name: Arush Tagade, Shaoheng Zhou, Jiaxin Wen, Shi Feng

entry.summary: Proposes self-generated text recognition finetuning as a character-targeted defense against emergent misalignment, testing across GPT-4.1, Qwen2.5-32B, and Seed-OSS-36B. Finds it can both prevent and reverse misalignment by reinforcing the model's aligned persona rather than directly suppressing harmful content.

entry.title: Can Language Model Agents be Helpful Circuit Explainers in Mechanistic Interpretability?

author.name: Ayan Antik Khan, Harsh Kohli, Yuekun Yao, Huan Sun, Ziyu Yao

entry.summary: This paper introduces AgenticInterpBench and HyVE, an agentic explainer that interprets identified circuit components through iterative observation, hypothesis generation, and causal validation. It matters because mechanistic interpretability has automated circuit localization but explaining component function remains labor-intensive and hard to standardize.

entry.title: An Introduction to Causal Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Elias Bareinboim, Junzhe Zhang, Sanghack Lee

entry.summary: This is an introduction to causal reinforcement learning, articulating how causal inference and RL both operate over counterfactual relations and proposing their integration. It matters for unifying two largely independent disciplines around counterfactual reasoning to improve agents' decision-making.

entry.title: RIFT-Bench: Dynamic Red-teaming For Agentic AI Systems

author.name: Yarin Yerushalmi Levi, Roy Betser, Amit Giloni, Lidor Erez, Itay Gershon, Oren Rachmil, Sindhu Padakandla, Roman Vainshtein

entry.summary: RIFT-Bench introduces a graph-representation-driven methodology for dynamic red-teaming of agentic AI systems, enabling unified security evaluation across heterogeneous architectures via a two-phase discovery and adaptive-attack scanning process. It matters because agentic LLM systems expose new attack surfaces beyond traditional LLM vulnerabilities, and existing evaluations are implementation-specific.

entry.title: Can Scale Save Us From Plasticity Loss in Large Language Models?

author.name: J. Fernando Hernandez-Garcia, Tom\'as Figliolia, Beren Millidge

entry.summary: This work studies plasticity loss in GPT-style transformers (5M to 314M non-embedding parameters) on a multilingual continual learning problem, finding evidence of plasticity loss persists and asking whether scale can overcome it. It matters because plasticity loss is a fundamental obstacle to continual learning, understudied in modern transformer LLMs and natural-language domains.

entry.title: One Year Later...The Harms Persist, But So Do We!

author.name: Annika Marie Schoene, Cansu Canca, Gautham Vijay Kumar, Anson Antony

entry.summary: Evaluates safety safeguards of six proprietary LLMs across 16 DSM-5 mental health conditions using adversarial attacks, introducing an eight-dimension harm taxonomy. Finds safeguards reliable only for suicide and self-harm, with failure rates up to 100% for eating disorders and substance use.

entry.title: Red-Teaming the Agentic Red-Team

author.name: Dario Pasquini, Michal Bazyli, Taras Fedynyshyn, Artem Sorokin

entry.summary: This work presents the first in-depth security analysis of widely used agentic systems for offensive cybersecurity, showing common design flaws that let an adversary exfiltrate API keys, establish persistence, and compromise the operator's machine even inside sandboxes. It introduces a full cyber kill chain against these red-teaming agents.

entry.title: Safe and Generalizable Hierarchical Multi-Agent RL via Constraint Manifold Control

author.name: Zihao Guo, Jianing Zhao, Ling Li, Hao Liang, Giuseppe Loianno, Yali Du

entry.summary: This work proposes a hierarchical multi-agent reinforcement learning framework that enforces hard safety constraints at the low level via a constraint manifold while enabling coordination through high-level policy learning, with theoretical safety guarantees. It addresses the trade-off between empirically strong learning methods and conservative control-theoretic safety in multi-agent settings.

entry.title: Bayesian control for coding agents

author.name: Theodore Papamarkou, Vladislav Smirnov, Viktor Mazanov, Artem Vazhentsev, Preslav Nakov, Timothy Baldwin, Artem Shelmanov

entry.summary: This paper formulates coding-agent orchestration as cost-sensitive sequential hypothesis testing, with a Bayesian controller maintaining a belief over candidate correctness and dynamically deciding whether to gather evidence, refine, verify, or stop. It matters because tool-use decisions in coding agents typically use fixed rules ignoring uncertainty, and the belief state also yields an interpretable correctness score.

entry.title: Cyclic Denoising Reveals Ultrastable Memories in Diffusion Models

author.name: Rishabh Sharma, Stefano Martiniani

entry.summary: This paper introduces cyclic denoising as an extraction attack for image diffusion models, performing repeated forward-reverse diffusion at controlled noise amplitudes to expose ultrastable attractors largely inaccessible to standard sampling. Many of these attractors correspond to memorized training images including stock photos and watermarks, requiring only sampler-level control without gradients.

entry.title: Beyond Trajectory Imitation: Strategy-Guided Policy Optimization for LLM Reasoning

author.name: Tianyuan Shi, Canbin Huang, Bei Li, Xin Chen, Xiaojun Quan, Jingang Wang, Qifan Wang

entry.summary: Strategy-Guided Policy Optimization (SGPO) replaces instance-level trajectory imitation with reusable strategy distillation, extracting structured strategy descriptions from strong models and comparing autonomous versus strategy-guided trajectories. It matters because trajectory imitation encourages memorization rather than transferable reasoning skills, limiting generalization in distilled models.

entry.title: The Latent Bridge: A Continuous Slow-Fast Channel for Real-Time Game Agents

author.name: Bojie Li, Noah Shi

entry.summary: The Latent Bridge couples a slow reasoning VLM and a fast reactive VLM for real-time game agents, learning a continuous latent communication channel between two frozen models as the sole trainable component, replacing the standard text bridge. It matters for real-time computer-use agents that must act within milliseconds while planning over seconds.

entry.title: Solving Inverse Problems of Chaotic Systems with Bidirectional Conditional Flow Matching

author.name: Peiyan Hu, Jian Zhang, Jiashu Pan, Ruiqi Feng, Tao Zhang, Zhi-Ming Ma, Yuan-Sen Ting, Gongjie Li, Tailin Wu

entry.summary: Bidirectional Conditional Flow Matching (Bi-CFM) solves inverse problems in chaotic systems—inferring initial conditions from final states—by learning bidirectional mappings between initial and final state distributions, with a conservation-constrained extension, tested on Lorenz, Circuit, and Lorenz 96 systems. It matters because chaotic inverse problems are largely unsolved due to ill-posedness, non-uniqueness, and instability.

entry.title: Weight-Space Geometry of Offline Reasoning Training

author.name: Aleksandr Nikolich, Igor Kiselev, Vladimir Platonov, Karina Romanova

entry.summary: Mechanistically compares six offline reasoning-distillation losses (SFT, RFT, DFT, RIFT, Offline GRPO, DPO) via weight-space geometry analysis using LoRA on Qwen3-4B. Finds SFT, RFT, and RIFT produce nearly colinear weight updates, suggesting some methods are mechanistically equivalent.

entry.title: Large-Language-Model Discovery of Quantum LDPC Codes through Structured Concept Evolution

author.name: Zidu Liu, Florian Marquardt

entry.summary: This work introduces structured concept evolution, pairing an LLM with an algebraic mutation grammar to discover lifted-product families of quantum LDPC error-correcting codes rather than designing codes from first principles. It evolves structured algebraic specifications to tackle a challenging discrete design problem.

entry.title: VeryTrace: Verifying Reasoning Traces through Compilable Formalism and Structured Verification

author.name: Ninghan Zhong, Ahmet Ege Tanriverdi, Kaan Kale, Sriram Vishwanath

entry.summary: VeryTrace is a zero-shot verification-and-repair framework that formalizes natural-language reasoning traces into a structured, compilable domain-specific language, using a hybrid verifier of deterministic checks and targeted LLM audits. It matters because logical errors in early chain-of-thought steps silently propagate to confident but incorrect conclusions.

entry.title: You Don't Need to Run Every Eval

author.name: Yuchen Zeng, Dimitris Papailiopoulos

entry.summary: This paper compiles a score matrix of 84 frontier models across 133 benchmarks and finds it is approximately rank-2, meaning a model's scores are largely determined by just two latent factors. It proposes BenchPress, a logit-space rank-2 matrix completion method to predict benchmark scores without running every eval.

entry.title: ReMMD: Realistic Multilingual Multi-Image Agentic Verification for Multimodal Misinformation Detection

author.name: Chenhao Dang, Dantong Zhu, Jun Yang, Conghui He, Weijia Li

entry.summary: ReMMD presents a realistic multilingual multi-image agentic verification framework and benchmark for multimodal misinformation detection, covering long narratives, multiple images, mixed provenance, and cross-lingual settings. It matters because real viral misinformation now combines complex multilingual and multimodal elements poorly captured by existing single-image, binary benchmarks.

entry.title: Accelerating Disaggregated RL for Visual Generative LLMs with Diffusion-Based Parallelism and Trainer-Assisted Generation

author.name: Sijie Wang, Zhengyu Qing, Zhiqiang Tan, Yiming Yin, Yeqing Zhang, Yaoyuan Wang, Qiang Wang, Xiaowen Chu, Shaohuai Shi

entry.summary: DigenRL is a disaggregated reinforcement learning framework for visual generative LLMs that decouples rollout and training resources using diffusion-based parallelism and trainer-assisted generation, overcoming the limitations of colocated execution. It matters because efficient RL systems for diffusion generative LLMs remain underexplored despite RL becoming dominant for post-training.

entry.title: World Models in Pieces: Structural Certification for General Agents

author.name: Yikai Lu, Yifei Wu, Xinyu Lu, Tongxin Li

entry.summary: World Models in Pieces introduces structural certification, a transition-local framework mapping bounded goal-conditioned performance to entry-wise guarantees on an agent's internal world model, after proving that general agents are not universal in the big-world regime. It matters for moving beyond uninformative uniform worst-case guarantees to certify understanding of critical bottlenecks versus irrelevant failures.

entry.title: FP8 is All You Need (Part 2): Efficient Ozaki-Bailey Style FFT Through Tensor-core Garner Reformulation and Kulisch Escape Route

author.name: Satoshi Matsuoka

entry.summary: This paper presents Ozaki-Bailey FFT, an emulated 3-D FFT routing 1-D FFT GEMMs through FP8 tensor cores via the Bailey six-step decomposition with Chinese-remainder reconstruction, recovering FP64-equivalent throughput after Blackwell Ultra slashed native FP64 vector throughput. It matters for HPC workloads needing high-precision FFTs on modern GPUs where FP64 hardware has been deprioritized.

entry.title: Detecting AI Coding Agents in Open Source: A Validated Multi-Method Census of 180 Million Repositories

author.name: Arsham Khosravani, Audris Mockus

entry.summary: This work presents a validated multi-method census of AI coding agent traces across 180 million Git repositories, combining configuration scanning, commit-message analysis, identity matching, and bot lookup. It finds single-signal methods recover only 3.3 percent of detected Claude Code commits, exposing major undercounting in adoption studies.

entry.title: Qwen-AgentWorld: Language World Models for General Agents

author.name: Yuxin Zuo, Zikai Xiao, Li Sheng, Fei Huang, Jianhong Tu, Yuxuan Liu, Tianyi Tang, Xiaomeng Hu, Yang Su, Qingfeng Lan, Yantao Liu, Qin Zhu, Yinger Zhang, Bowen Yu, Haiquan Zhao, Haiyang Xu, Jianxin Yang, Jiayang Cheng, Junyang Wang, Lianghao Deng, Mingfeng Xue, Tianyi Bai, Yang Fan, Yubo Ma, Yucheng Li, Zeyu Cui, Zhihai Wang, Zhihui Xie, Zhuorui Ye, An Yang, Dayiheng Liu, Jingren Zhou, Ning Ding

entry.summary: Introduces Qwen-AgentWorld, large language world models (35B-A3B and 397B-A17B MoE) that simulate agentic environments across 7 domains via long chain-of-thought reasoning, trained on over 10M real-world interaction trajectories through a three-stage pipeline. Aims to push general-agent capabilities through language-based world modeling.

entry.title: T2D-Bench: Evidence-Gated Evaluation of LLM Outputs for Type 2 Diabetes Using a Multi-Layer Clinical-Lifestyle Knowledge Graph

author.name: Saba A. Farahani, Hung Cao, Ramesh Jain, Amir M. Rahmani

entry.summary: T2D-Bench is a reproducible benchmark and evidence-gated evaluation framework testing whether LLM type-2-diabetes recommendations satisfy explicit, graph-checkable evidence requirements built on a multi-layer clinical-lifestyle knowledge graph. It matters because LLMs produce fluent clinical advice that may violate guideline constraints or lack justification.

entry.title: CompressKV: Semantic-Retrieval-Guided KV-Cache Compression for Resource-Efficient Long-Context LLM Inference

author.name: Xiaolin Lin, Jingcun Wang, Olga Kondrateva, Yiyu Shi, Bing Li, Grace Li Zhang

entry.summary: CompressKV is a resource-efficient KV-cache compression framework for GQA-based LLMs that identifies Semantic Retrieval Heads capturing initial and final tokens, rather than uniformly scoring tokens across all heads. It matters for sustainable long-context LLM inference on resource-constrained hardware by avoiding eviction of critical tokens.

entry.title: Neuro-Symbolic Drive: Rule-Grounded Faithful Reasoning for Driving VLAs

author.name: Xiangbo Gao, Xiukun Huang, Boyu Lu, Junge Zhang, Mengjie Mao, Jiachen Li, Wei Xiong, Zhengzhong Tu

entry.summary: Neuro-Symbolic Drive supervises driving vision-language-action models using rule-grounded reasoning traces extracted from classical rule-based planners, improving causal connection between rationales and planned motion. It matters for autonomous driving where chain-of-thought rationales must be faithful and safety-relevant rather than post-hoc narration.

entry.title: FlowR2A: Learning Reward-to-Action Distribution for Multimodal Driving Planning

author.name: Xirui Li, Zhe Liu, Xiaoqing Ye, Wenhua Han, Yifeng Pan, Junyu Han, Hengshuang Zhao

entry.summary: FlowR2A reframes simulation-based rewards from discriminative targets into generative conditions, learning a reward-conditioned action distribution via a flow-matching decoder to unify dense supervision of scoring methods with proposal generation of anchor methods for driving planning. It matters for resolving the tension between fixed-vocabulary scoring and sparsely-supervised anchor-based driving planners.

entry.title: PHANTOM: A Large-Scale Dataset of Multimodal Adversarial Attacks for Vision-Language Models

author.name: Simone Gallivanone, Hossein Khodadadi, Mauro Dore, Mauro Medda, Nicola Franco

entry.summary: PHANTOM is a large-scale open-source dataset of 47,524 pre-generated adversarial attacks against vision-language models, spanning 10 categories and 55 subcategories of harmful intents to make adversarial data accessible given the cost of generation. It matters for democratizing robustness research on multimodal models by consolidating and extending prior benchmarks.

entry.title: Reinforcement Learning for Computer-Use Agents with Autonomous Evaluation

author.name: Marta Sumyk, Oleksandr Kosovan

entry.summary: This work proposes an RL fine-tuning framework for computer-use GUI agents that uses autonomous vision-language evaluation of final screenshots as a scalable supervision signal, removing the need for handcrafted reward functions or manual labels. It matters because open-ended desktop environments rarely provide machine-readable rewards for RL training of GUI agents.

entry.title: Scaling Laws for Task-Specific LLM Distillation

author.name: Lavinia Ghita, Dhruv Desai, Ioana Boier

entry.summary: This paper derives empirical scaling laws for task-specific LLM distillation, quantifying how in-domain and general performance scale with dataset size, compression ratio, supervision format, and iterative pruning schedule, using quantitative finance as the domain. It matters for predictable, principled compression of LLMs under latency and cost constraints.

entry.title: Cryptographic certificates of validity for trustworthy AI

author.name: Murdoch J. Gabbay

entry.summary: Proposes cryptographic certificates of validity for agentic AI, compiling correctness or policy conditions into witness-checking problems with succinct zero-knowledge proofs. Offers a middle ground between formal verification and cryptographic authentication.

entry.title: MGI: Member vs Generated Inference

author.name: Bihe Zhao, Michel Meintz, Juangui Xu, Franziska Boenisch, Adam Dziedzic

entry.summary: Formalizes Member vs Generated Inference (MGI): distinguishing whether a sample is a true training member or a model-generated output. Shows existing membership inference and attribution methods systematically misclassify in this setting.

entry.title: Pigeonholing: Bad prompts hurt models to collapse and make mistakes

author.name: Hyunji Nam, Keertana Chidambaram, Dorottya Demszky, Natasha Jaques

entry.summary: This paper identifies pigeonholing, where unintentionally bad prompts or prior incorrect responses cause LLMs to degrade and collapse into errors, such as repeating mistakes or justifying false claims. Experiments span 10 tasks and 10 models, characterizing the phenomenon without malicious jailbreaking.

entry.title: KLip-PPO: A per-sample KL perspective on PPO-Clip

author.name: Riccardo Colletti, Robin Holzinger

entry.summary: KLip-PPO shows that the gradient of PPO's clipped surrogate is reproduced exactly by a Kullback-Leibler surrogate with a per-sample coefficient having closed-form dependence on the importance ratio and advantage. This unifies the two PPO formulations that the literature treats as separate algorithms.

entry.title: NatureBench: Can Coding Agents Match the Published SOTA of Nature-Family Papers?

author.name: Yuru Wang, Lejun Cheng, Yuxin Zuo, Sihang Zeng, Bingxiang He, Che Jiang, Junlin Yang, Yuchong Wang, Kaikai Zhao, Weifeng Huang, Kai Tian, Zhenzhao Yuan, Jincheng Zhong, Weizhi Wang, Ning Ding, Bowen Zhou, Kaiyan Zhang

entry.summary: Introduces NatureBench, a cross-discipline benchmark of 90 tasks distilled from Nature-family papers with the NatureGym pipeline for standardized containerized environments, testing whether coding agents can match published SOTA. Finds the strongest of ten frontier agents surpasses SOTA on only 17.8% of tasks under a search-disabled protocol.

entry.title: On the Smallness of the Large Language Models Scaling Exponents

author.name: Sauro Succi, Peter V. Coveney, Alex Hansen

entry.summary: On the Smallness of LLM Scaling Exponents argues that current LLM scaling exponents indicate an energy-unsustainable regime, refuting the claim that the pedestal effect (neglecting nonzero loss at infinite data) explains the smallness, and draws an analogy to fluid turbulence. It matters for understanding the energy sustainability and theoretical underpinnings of scaling laws.

entry.title: AutoSpec: Safety Rule Evolution for LLM Agents via Inductive Logic Programming

author.name: Pingchuan Ma, Zhaoyu Wang, Zimo Ji, Yuguang Zhou, Zhantong Xue, Zongjie Li, Shuai Wang, Xiaoqin Zhang

entry.summary: Presents AutoSpec, a framework using inductive logic programming to automatically evolve expert-designed safety rules for LLM agents from user safe/unsafe feedback. Bridges the tradeoff between brittle hand-crafted rules and uninterpretable neural classifiers.

entry.title: SP-Mind: An Autonomous Reasoning Agent for Spatial Proteomics Analysis

author.name: Yucheng Yuan, Yuanfeng Ji, Zhongxiao Li, Ruijiang Li

entry.summary: SP-Mind is presented as the first autonomous AI agent unifying the spatial proteomics analysis pipeline from raw multiplexed tissue imaging to phenotype discovery, converting natural-language queries into end-to-end workflows. It matters because current spatial proteomics workflows are fragmented and require manual expert orchestration, limiting scalability and reproducibility.

entry.title: When Helpfulness Overrides Causal Caution: Context-Dependent Suppression and Recovery in LLMs

author.name: Hiroshi Okumura

entry.summary: This study examines how LLMs systematically suppress causal caution (refraining from causal judgment when evidence is insufficient) when shifting from academic to practical advisory contexts, evaluated across four frontier models using a Pearl-inspired causal hierarchy rubric.
