It matters for understanding epistemic reliability of LLMs in decision-support roles where helpfulness may override appropriate caution.

entry.title: Governed Shared Memory for Multi-Agent LLM Systems

author.name: Yanki Margalit, Nurit Cohen-Inger, Erni Avram, Ran Taig, Oded Margalit

entry.summary: This paper formalizes the fleet-memory problem in multi-agent LLM systems, identifying four failure modes (unauthorized leakage, stale propagation, contradiction persistence, provenance collapse) and defining systems-level primitives implemented in a production memory service evaluated via a reproducible harness. It matters for robust shared knowledge management in multi-tenant multi-agent deployments.

entry.title: LaGO: Latent Action Guidance for Online Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Kuan-Yen Liu, Ren-Jyun Huang, Ti-Rong Wu

entry.summary: LaGO uses a pretrained LLM as a latent action prior to softly guide online policy optimization rather than as an explicit planner or controller, improving reward and success rate over vanilla PPO on CLEVR-Robot and Meta-World benchmarks. It matters because using LLMs as direct controllers requires precise action generation and is often unreliable.

entry.title: Beyond the Autoregressive Horizon: A Comprehensive Survey of Diffusion Models, World Modelling, and State Space Models for Code

author.name: Kishan Maharaj, Ashita Saxena, Srikanth Tamilselvam

entry.summary: This survey reviews emerging paradigms beyond autoregressive next-token prediction for code intelligence, covering diffusion models, world modeling, and state space models to overcome structural limitations like restricted global planning and weak grounding in execution semantics. It matters by mapping out alternative architectures that could unlock next-generation capabilities for code generation and reasoning.

entry.title: Quantifying Prior Dominance in RAG Systems

author.name: Barak Or

entry.summary: This paper introduces the Normalized Context Utilization (NCU) metric using continuous token log-probabilities across zero-shot, oracle, and adversarial conditions to quantify whether RAG systems genuinely extract contextual information versus relying on parametric memory recall. It matters because current RAG evaluations suffer epistemic blindness, failing to distinguish contextual extraction from memorized knowledge.

entry.title: Sol Video Inference Engine: Agent-Native Full-Stack Acceleration Framework for Efficient Video Generation

author.name: Yitong Li, Junsong Chen, Haopeng Li, Haozhe Liu, Jincheng Yu, Ligeng Zhu, Ping Luo, Song Han, Enze Xie

entry.summary: Introduces an agent-native full-stack acceleration framework for video diffusion inference that automatically tunes instance-specific acceleration strategies across models, hardware, and configurations. Addresses the non-transferability of acceleration recipes.

entry.title: Are Safety Guarantees in Neural Networks Safe? How to Compute Trustworthy Robustness Certifications

author.name: Merkouris Papamichail, Konstantinos Varsos, Giorgos Flouris, Jo\~ao Marques-Silva

entry.summary: Critically examines whether neural network robustness certifications are themselves trustworthy, introducing the apothem measure as an alternative to volume-optimal certifications which are intractable. Provides a way to compute apothem-optimal robustness certificates.

entry.title: Learning to Trigger: Reinforcement Learning at the Large Hadron Collider

author.name: Zixin Ding, Shaghayegh Emam, Giovanna Salvi, Cecilia Tosciri, Abhijith Gandrakota, Jennifer Ngadiuba, Nhan Tran, Christian Herwig, David W. Miller, Yuxin Chen

entry.summary: Casts online trigger threshold tuning at the Large Hadron Collider as a sequential decision problem, adapting Group-Filtered Policy Optimization to streaming control to maximize signal efficiency while tracking a target background rate. Addresses drift in static hand-tuned trigger menus.

entry.title: Metis: Bridging Text and Code Memory for Self-Evolving Agents

author.name: Zijie Dai, Siuhin He, Hui Li, Qihui Zhou, Jiajun Li, Mingcong Song, Guoping Long, Hongjie Si, Xin Yao, Lin Zhang, James Cheng, Xiao Yan

entry.summary: Presents the first controlled study isolating text memory versus code memory for self-evolving agents over identical experiences, and introduces Metis bridging both. Reveals complementary trade-offs in construction cost, execution efficiency, and transferability.

entry.title: Co-occurring associated retained concepts in Diffusion Unlearning

author.name: Miso Kim, Georu Lee, Yunji Kim, Hoki Kim, Jinseong Park, Woojin Lee

entry.summary: Identifies that diffusion concept unlearning unintentionally suppresses benign co-occurring concepts (e.g., removing nudity suppresses person), defines CARE concepts and a CARE score, and proposes ReCARE to preserve them. Addresses collateral damage in safety unlearning.

entry.title: CALIBER: Calibrating Confidence Before and After Reasoning in Language Models

author.name: Conor Finlay, Joshua Kurien, Saurabh Dash, Marzieh Fadaee, Beyza Ermis

entry.summary: CALIBER argues that confidence in reasoning LLMs is state-dependent: confidence before reasoning should estimate prompt-solvability while confidence after answering should predict the realized answer's correctness, each requiring different supervision targets. It proposes calibrating both stages distinctly.

entry.title: video-SALMONN-R$^3$: Learning to ReWatch, ReAsk, and ReAnswer for Efficient Video Understanding

author.name: Yixuan Li, Guangzhi Sun, Yudong Yang, Wei Li, Zejun MA, Chao Zhang

entry.summary: video-SALMONN-R3 is an end-to-end video LLM that learns to re-watch relevant video segments at higher fidelity via reinforcement learning, without requiring chain-of-thought cold-start or costly CoT annotations. It improves efficient video understanding by localizing then re-examining key segments.

entry.title: Evaluating the Interpretability of Sparse Autoencoders with Concept Annotations

author.name: Jonas Klotz, Cassio F. Dantas, Pallavi Jain, Diego Marcos, Beg\"um Demir

entry.summary: This paper presents a human-grounded evaluation framework that quantifies alignment between sparse autoencoder latents and human-annotated concepts in vision and vision-language models, validated via targeted attribute perturbations. It introduces synthetic single-attribute benchmarks and a coalition-based matching procedure (FBMP).

entry.title: InSight: Self-Guided Skill Acquisition via Steerable VLAs

author.name: Maggie Wang, Lars Osterberg, Stephen Tian, Ola Shorinwa, Jiajun Wu, Mac Schwager

entry.summary: InSight makes vision-language-action models steerable at the primitive-action level via automated demonstration segmentation, then uses a VLM-guided data flywheel to identify and autonomously generate demonstrations of missing primitives for novel tasks. It enables autonomous skill acquisition beyond the training data distribution.

entry.title: Verifiable Foundation Models for Robot Safety

author.name: Davide Corsi, Kyungmin Kim, Roy Fox

entry.summary: Presents FEARL, a framework decomposing robot control policies into a large opaque Controller for perception and a small verifiable Safety module that receives low-dimensional safety-sensor inputs plus a bounded context embedding. Enables formal safety verification despite foundation models being intractable to verify directly.

entry.title: Cycle-Consistent Neural Explanation of Formal Verification Certificates

author.name: Andoni Rodriguez, Alberto Pozanco, Daniel Borrajo

entry.summary: This work proposes a cycle-consistent neural architecture that generates faithful natural-language explanations of formal verification certificates, using a forward and inverse network closed by a symbolic verifier as a faithfulness proxy plus a pointer-generator for lexical grounding. It matters for making opaque machine-checkable verification certificates understandable to non-specialist stakeholders.

entry.title: Critique of Agent Model

author.name: Eric Xing, Mingkai Deng, Jinyu Hou

entry.summary: This conceptual paper critiques the notion of agent and agency in current LLM systems, drawing on Descartes and science fiction to analyze agent architectures along five dimensions and clarify where automation ends and genuine agency begins. It matters for grounding debates about AI capability hype and existential risk in a clearer conceptual framework.

entry.title: ATRIA: Adaptive Traceable ECG Reporting with Iterative Agents

author.name: Donggyun Hong, Kyuhwan Lee, Junmyung Kwon, Yong-Yeon Jo

entry.summary: ATRIA is a multi-agent ECG reporting system that mirrors a clinician's iterative workflow, binding each report claim to supporting evidence, flagging unsupported statements, and enabling bidirectional editing rather than single-pass generation. It matters because clinical ECG reporting is inherently iterative and existing systems either fuse tasks end-to-end or remain single-pass.

entry.title: CineCap: Structured Reasoning with Spatio-Temporal Anchors for Cinematographic Video Captioning

author.name: Xinyu Mao, Yuhui Zeng, Xiaokun Liu, Wenyu Qin, Meng Wang, Xin Tao, Pengfei Wan, Xiaohan Xing, Max Meng

entry.summary: CineCap introduces structured reasoning with spatio-temporal anchors for cinematographic video captioning, describing how a video is filmed across dimensions like camera movement, shot size, depth of field, and composition. It matters for fine-grained video understanding and controllable movie-quality video generation, an underexplored area in multimodal LLMs.

entry.title: Decentralised AI Training and Inference with BlockTrain

author.name: Peter Toth

entry.summary: Spheroid BlockTrain is a decentralized training protocol that partitions a model into independently trainable blocks each optimized on a local objective derived from a shared global target, composed at inference into one model, reaching near-end-to-end performance on byte-level WikiText. It matters for reducing dependence on dense centrally-controlled accelerator clusters that advantage hyperscalers.

entry.title: Legal Reasoning Is Not Lawyering: Rethinking Legal Benchmarks for Pro Se Access to Justice

author.name: Andrew Lou, David Shin

entry.summary: Argues that current legal AI benchmarks measure an upper bound by using expert-preprocessed inputs, while real access-to-justice depends on a lower bound where inputs come from untrained pro se litigants with noisy, error-prone narratives. Calls for rethinking legal benchmarks.

entry.title: JEDEL: Zero-Shot DNA-Encoded Library Design for Early-Stage Drug Discovery

author.name: Zygimantas Jocys, Zhanxing Zhu, Henriette M. G. Willems, Katayoun Farrahi

entry.summary: Presents JEDEL, the first model mapping 3D pharmacophore representations directly to synthesis-ready DNA-encoded libraries using only purchasable building blocks and validated reactions. Ensures every generated molecule is experimentally realizable.

entry.title: Deciphering Fingerprints of 3D Molecular Surfaces for Accurate Epitope Prediction

author.name: Fang Wu, Weihao Xuan, Jure Leskovec, Yejin Choi, Li Erran Li

entry.summary: Presents SurfBind, a surface-centric learning framework for antibody-antigen epitope prediction operating directly on 3D molecular surface representations rather than sequences or backbones. Captures discontinuous, surface-driven epitopes via patch-level modeling.

entry.title: Mind the Heads: Topological Representation Alignment for Multimodal LLMs

author.name: Davide Caffagni, Alberto Compagnoni, Federico Melis, Sara Sarto, Pier Luigi Dovesi, Mark Granroth-Wilding, Marcella Cornia, Lorenzo Baraldi

entry.summary: Proposes Head-Wise Representation Alignment (HeRA) for multimodal LLMs, enforcing cross-modal alignment at individual attention head level and preserving topological neighborhood structure. Grounded in the Platonic Representation Hypothesis.

entry.title: ZONOS2 Technical Report

author.name: Gabriel Clark, Sofian Mejjoute, Mohamed Osman, George Close, Beren Millidge

entry.summary: ZONOS2 is an 8B text-to-speech model with a mixture-of-experts backbone scaled from 1.6B, trained on over 6M hours of audio, achieving state-of-the-art naturalness, prosody, and voice cloning. It introduces a new TTS evaluation benchmark and supports streaming.

entry.title: G$^3$VLA: Geometric inductive bias for Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Yue Peng, Yongzhe Zhao, Artur Habuda, Khuyen Pham, Yanheng Zhu, Tran Nguyen Le, Fares Abu-Dakka, Li Guo

entry.summary: G3VLA introduces a camera-aware geometric module that injects calibrated camera geometry (intrinsics and extrinsics) into the visual-token stream of pretrained vision-language-action models without changing the action space. It uses ray embeddings and projective positional encoding to better handle multi-camera robot setups.

entry.title: Grad Detect: Gradient-Based Hallucination Detection in LLMs

author.name: Anand Kamat, Daniel Blake, Brent M. Werness

entry.summary: Grad Detect is a gradient-based hallucination detection method that analyzes layer-wise gradient patterns from a single forward-backward pass during inference, showing internal gradient structure carries correctness information not available from output signals alone. It is evaluated on QA benchmarks for hallucination detection and abstention.

entry.title: Data Augmentation: A Fourier Analysis Perspective

author.name: Behrooz Tahmasebi, Melanie Weber, Stefanie Jegelka

entry.summary: Develops a Fourier-analysis framework to study whether partial data augmentation can achieve the same statistical generalization benefits as full group-sized augmentation when groups are large. Provides theoretical grounding for computationally cheaper augmentation strategies.

entry.title: Age of LLM: A Strategic 1v1 Benchmark for Reasoning, Diplomacy and Reliability of Large Language Models under Fog of War

author.name: Arnaud Ricci

entry.summary: Age of LLM is a turn-based 1v1 strategy benchmark with fog of war, full diplomacy, and strict JSON reliability requirements, testing 15 reasoning models across 54 matches with a private engine to mitigate data contamination. It matters for evaluating LLM strategic reasoning, negotiation, and output reliability under uncertainty in a contamination-resistant setting.

entry.title: Fast and Slow Variational Continual Learning

author.name: Subarnaduti Paul, Yohan Jung, Mohammad Emtiyaz Khan, Siddharth Swaroop, Thomas M\"ollenhoff, Martin Mundt

entry.summary: Incorporates fast-and-slow adaptation into variational continual learning by merging past posteriors as slowly-adapting priors to balance stability and plasticity. Grounds a neuroscience-inspired mechanism in the VCL framework.

entry.title: PixJail: Self-Evolving Paper-to-Pipeline Reproduction for Text-to-Image Jailbreak Evaluation

author.name: Leyi Sheng, Han Sun, Zhen Sun, Yuntao Yue, Jinlin Wu, Xinlei He, Jiaheng Wei

entry.summary: Proposes PixJail, a self-evolving paper-to-pipeline agent framework for reproducible text-to-image jailbreak evaluation that constructs paper-specific attack modules and runnable pipelines under a unified protocol. Addresses reproducibility and fair comparison across the pipeline-level T2I jailbreak landscape.

entry.title: Agon: An Autonomous Large-Scale Omnidisciplinary Research System Built on Prompt Economy

author.name: Youran Sun, Xingyu Ren, Chugang Yi, Jiaxuan Guo, Kejia Zhang, Jianda Du, Haizhao Yang

entry.summary: Presents Agon, an autonomous omnidisciplinary research orchestrator built on Prompt Economy principles that validates checkable claims and defers others to humans. Reports 444 iterations across domains, demonstrating scalability while exposing a taxonomy of new failure modes.

entry.title: EG-VQA: Benchmarking Verifiable Video Question Answering with Grounded Temporal Evidence

author.name: Linpeng Huang, Weixing Chen, Zexin Chen, Yang Liu, Liang Lin

entry.summary: EG-VQA is an evidence-grounded video question answering benchmark of 2,067 videos and 11,838 QA pairs where each pair is annotated with supporting temporal evidence, requiring joint reasoning and precise evidence localization. It addresses the disconnect between answer correctness and evidence grounding in existing VideoQA benchmarks.

entry.title: Closing the Loop: Formally Verified Law as a Reward Signal for Self-Improving Legal AI

author.name: Armin Heydari (Harvard University), Torben Leowald (Columbia University)

entry.summary: This paper develops an architecture creating a formally verifiable reward signal to train self-improving legal AI, adapting the LLM-proposes-verifier-disposes paradigm from math to law via autoformalization into a Catala-based formal legal calculus. It provides provable correctness for computational legal components and structural guarantees for open-textured analysis.

entry.title: Forget Without Compromise: Nexus Sampling for Streaming KV-Cache Eviction Under Fixed Budgets

author.name: Duc Duong, Hoang Anh Duy Le, Jianwen Xie, Anshumali Shrivastava, Zhaozhuo Xu

entry.summary: Nexus Sampling is a training-free KV-cache eviction method for streaming long-context and agentic LLM workloads that combines iterative Nexus scoring to surface bridge tokens with weighted reservoir sampling for probabilistic retention. It avoids the irreversible permanent erasure of subtly important tokens common to top-K eviction.

entry.title: AsyncOPD: How Stale Can On-Policy Distillation Be?

author.name: Wonjun Kang, Kevin Galim, Seunghyuk Oh, Minjun Kang, Sanghyun Park, Donghoon Kim, Minjae Lee, Minseo Kim, Rishabh Tiwari, Yuchen Zeng, Hyung Il Koo, Kangwook Lee

entry.summary: AsyncOPD presents the first systematic study of staleness in asynchronous on-policy distillation for LLM post-training, where decoupling rollout generation from learner updates introduces stale-policy data. It examines how stale data affects OPD with local KL-loss teacher feedback, paralleling known issues in asynchronous RL.

entry.title: To Compare, or Not to Compare: On Methodological Practices in Evaluating Social Bias

author.name: Federico Marcuzzi, Xuefei Ning, Roy Schwartz, Iryna Gurevych

entry.summary: Critiques widespread methodological fragmentation in evaluating social bias in LLMs and introduces a unified controllable framework that standardizes heterogeneous benchmarks, contrasting isolated demographic assessments with forced-choice comparative settings. Disentangles confounds from chain-of-thought reasoning and neutral fallback options.

entry.title: Navigating User Behavior toward Personalized Multimodal Generation

author.name: Hengji Zhou, Yufeng Liu, Ye Liu, Yong Xu, Lianghao Xia, Liqiang Nie

entry.summary: NaviGen turns a user's interaction history into executable instructions for personalized multimodal generation, using a dual identifier coupling a collaborative code and a textual code in one token stream as a behavioral substrate and semantic bridge. It matters because AIGC pipelines presuppose well-formed prompts while users rarely articulate visual details.

entry.title: Grading the Grader: Lessons from Evaluating an Agentic Data Analysis System

author.name: Tian Zheng, Kai-Tai Hsu

entry.summary: This paper studies the reliability of automated graders for agentic data analysis systems, developing a three-layer human-AI grading cascade (strict regex, LLM lenient grading, snippet-based human inspection) applied to a multi-agent system on 153 numerical tasks. It matters because agentic outputs include code, numerical results, and diagnostics that are harder to evaluate than single-turn responses, requiring distinguishing genuine disagreement from grading artifacts.

entry.title: Faithful by Construction: Claim-Anchored Attribution for Multi-Document Summarization

author.name: Shuo Guan

entry.summary: Presents CAMS, a claim-anchored multi-document summarization framework that extracts atomic claims with token-level provenance, clusters equivalent claims, flags conflicts, and rewrites a support-aware summary. Makes attribution faithful by construction rather than post hoc.

entry.title: EMAgnet: Parameter-Space EMA Regularization for Policy Gradient Self-Play in Large Games

author.name: Tristan Maidment, JB Lanier, Chase McDonald, Nathan Tsang, Eugene Vinitsky, Roy Fox, Albert Wang, Wesley N. Kerr

entry.summary: Introduces EMAgnet, which regularizes policy gradient self-play toward an exponential moving average of the last-iterate policy's parameters, providing an adaptive regularization target instead of the uniform distribution. Evaluated on two-player zero-sum games with exploration challenges.

entry.title: Beyond Bayer: Task-Optimal Sensor Co-Design for Robust Autonomous-Driving Segmentation

author.name: Reeshad Khan, John Gauch

entry.summary: Uses a differentiable RAW-to-task pipeline to investigate optimal camera sensor design for autonomous driving segmentation. Finds learning spectral color-filter-array weights improves mIoU while point-spread-function co-design is net-negative due to the data-processing inequality.

entry.title: A Fair Evaluation of Graph Foundation Models for Node Property Prediction

author.name: Oleg Platonov, Gleb Bazhenov, Dmitry Eremeev, Liudmila Prokhorenkova

entry.summary: This paper provides a fair, unified evaluation of Graph Foundation Models for node property prediction, noting that inconsistent evaluation settings across prior works prevent meaningful comparison. The authors from the Yandex/LP team standardize the benchmarking setting for GFMs.

entry.title: Privacy-Preserving RAG via Multi-Agent Semantic Rewriting: Achieving Confidentiality Without Compromising Contextual Fidelity

author.name: Yuanhe Zhao, Tianyu Zhang, Huafei Xing, Derek F. Wong, Jianbin Li, Tao Fang

entry.summary: This paper proposes a multi-agent semantic rewriting framework to sanitize retrieved content in RAG systems, using three specialized agents for privacy extraction, semantic analysis, and reconstruction to remove sensitive identifiers while preserving meaning. It significantly reduces privacy leakage under targeted attacks on medical and PII datasets.

entry.title: Sesame: Structure-Aware Molecular Generation via Spatial Density-Map Conditioning

author.name: Konstantin Yatsenko, Arvind Thiagarajan

entry.summary: Sesame is a diffusion-based molecular generation model using spatial density-map conditioning and a spatial Evoformer to understand small-molecule structure and protein-ligand interactions while supporting scaffold-based growth for lead optimization. It targets the central de novo and fragment-growing operations of computational drug design.

entry.title: RoPE-Aware Bit Allocation for KV-Cache Quantization

author.name: Fengfeng Liang, Yuechen Zhang, Jiaya Jia

entry.summary: RoPE-aware Block-GTQ reframes key-cache quantization as a block-wise bit-allocation problem, since under RoPE a key's contribution decomposes into position-dependent frequency blocks where high-energy blocks need more bits. It computes label-free energy scores per RoPE block and greedily allocates integer bit widths to better preserve attention logits.

entry.title: Holistic Data Scheduler for LLM Pre-training via Multi-Objective Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Chenhao Dang, Jing Ma, Mingjie Liao

entry.summary: The Holistic Data Scheduler formulates online data mixing for LLM pre-training as a multi-objective reinforcement learning problem, addressing the limitation that prior methods optimize from a single perspective. It adaptively adjusts data mixtures across multiple dimensions during training to improve efficiency.

entry.title: Do LLM Attribution Metrics Transfer? Auditing Retrieval-Augmented Generation Evaluation Across Datasets and Constructs

author.name: Tianyu Ding, Aditya Nannapaneni, Juan Pablo De la Cruz Weinstein

entry.summary: Audits eight automatic attribution scorers for retrieval-augmented generation across three evaluation constructs and multiple datasets, asking whether any scorer transfers reliably. Finds that metrics commonly treated as interchangeable do not transfer, undermining a common evaluation assumption.

entry.title: PORTER: Language-Grounded Event Representations for Portable Structured EHR Foundation Models

author.name: Lin Lawrence Guo, Adam Paul Yan, Emily Vettese, Lillian Sung

entry.summary: Introduces PORTER, a language-grounded EHR foundation model that decouples event representation from a fixed vocabulary by encoding clinical events through text descriptions with a frozen encoder, plus a dedicated numeric pathway. Enables transfer across institutions and pipelines where new concepts appear.

entry.title: AGORA: An Archive-Grounded Benchmark for Agentic Workplace Document Reasoning

author.name: Honglin Guo, Qi Zhang, Yu Zhang, Weijie Li, Rui Zheng, Zhikai Lei, Qiyuan Peng, Zhiheng Xi, Tao Gui, Qi Zhang

entry.summary: Introduces AGORA, an archive-grounded benchmark pairing 362 questions with eight domain collections of 9,664 authentic documents totaling 372M tokens, far exceeding any model's context window, forcing agents to explore deliberately. Tests locating sparse evidence and reconciling inconsistent terminology, units, and time conventions.

entry.title: Data Scale, Not Latency, Shapes Cross-Lingual Encoder Transfer in Streaming ASR

author.name: Nenad Banfic

entry.summary: This controlled study finds that for cross-lingual encoder transfer in streaming ASR, the advantage of multilingual over English-only initialization is a data-limited effect that diminishes with scale, rather than being amplified by streaming latency or quantization. It matters for practical decisions about warm-starting streaming speech recognition models for new languages.

entry.title: ReM-MoA: Reasoning Memory Sustains Mixture-of-Agents Scaling

author.name: Heng Ping, Arijit Bhattacharjee, Peiyu Zhang, Shixuan Li, Wei Yang, Ali Jannesari, Nesreen Ahmed, Paul Bogdan

entry.summary: Prob-BBDM proposes a probabilistic Brownian Bridge Diffusion Model for MRI sequence image-to-image translation, integrating a variational encoder-guided diffusion mechanism to synthesize MRI modalities from 2D axial slices. It matters because acquiring multiple imaging modalities clinically is resource-intensive, and synthesis could reduce scan burden.

entry.title: Low-power analogue neural networks with trainable nonlinear connections for continuous control

author.name: Ian T. Vidamour, Fernando Aguirre, Thomas J. Hayward, Matthew O. A. Ellis, Charles Swindells, Alexander McDonnell, Martin Trefzer, Finley Robins, Luca Manneschi, Susan Stepney, Tony Kenyon, Oliver J. Sutton, Jack C. Gartside, Ivan Y. Tyukin, Adnan Mehonic, Eleni Vasilaki

entry.summary: Proposes low-power analogue neural networks inspired by Kolmogorov-Arnold networks, placing trainable nonlinear functions on connections realized as analogue band-pass filters. Demonstrates efficient representation of smooth control targets like robotic kinematics.

entry.title: Towards Spec Learning: Inference-Time Alignment from Preference Pairs

author.name: Dhriti Krishnan, Tejas Goyal, Jaromir Savelka

entry.summary: Proposes spec learning, a framework that compiles brief user instructions and a small set of preference judgments into natural-language specifications that condition LLMs at inference time without parameter updates. Offers a cheaper alternative to preference fine-tuning.

entry.title: A P\={a}ninian Foundation for Indic Language Processing

author.name: Ritwik Banerjee, Lav R. Varshney

entry.summary: Argues for a Paninian (Sanskrit grammar) foundation for unified Indic language processing, leveraging the shared morphosyntactic architecture across Indic languages rather than building separate per-language tools. Proposes a structurally grounded framework for over a billion speakers.

entry.title: Social Structure Matters in 3D Human-Human Interaction Generation

author.name: Zhongju Wang, Beier Wang, Yatao Bian, Pichao Wang, Zhi Wang, Daoyi Dong, Hongdong Li, Huadong Mo, Zhenhong Sun

entry.summary: This paper reframes text-driven 3D human-human interaction generation as a social structure modeling problem, requiring models to infer interaction phases, actor roles, and coordination before generating physically plausible partner-aware motion. It probes the limits of LLMs for inferring social structure in multi-person motion synthesis.

entry.title: CrossPool: Efficient Multi-LLM Serving for Cold MoE Models through KV-Cache and Weight Disaggregation

author.name: Zhuoren Ye, Tianyu Wo, Dinghao Xue, Mingming Zhang, Yuchen Teng, Chunming Hu, Renyu Yang

entry.summary: CrossPool improves multi-LLM serving for cold sparse mixture-of-experts models by disaggregating stable model weights from transient KV-cache, using a shared KV-cache pool to provision aggregate active demand rather than per-model worst case. It targets GPU memory inefficiency when many MoE models receive sparse traffic.

entry.title: FLUX3D: High-Fidelity 3D Gaussian Generation with Diffusion-Aligned Sparse Representation

author.name: Haorui Ji, Weizhe Liu, Hongdong Li, Hengkai Guo

entry.summary: FLUX3D is a scalable image-to-3D Gaussian Splatting framework that addresses two bottlenecks: discriminative 2D features suppressing reconstructive cues, and diffusion transformers lacking alignment between dense 2D tokens and sparse 3D voxel latents. It boosts both representation and generation fidelity for high-frequency visual details.

entry.title: One Ruler: A Same-Hands Re-Evaluation of Bivariate Causal Direction on Tuebingen, with a Parameter-Free Compression Baseline

author.name: Wietse Stienstra

entry.summary: This paper performs a same-hands re-evaluation of bivariate causal direction methods on the 102 Tuebingen cause-effect pairs under one strict no-tuning protocol with forced decisions, and introduces a parameter-free sorted-conditional compression baseline using bz2. It shows rankings differ sharply from literature when methods are compared fairly.

entry.title: Information-Theoretic Classifier-Free Guidance with Adaptive Schedule Optimization

author.name: Haobo Chen, Xiangxiang Xu, Yuheng Bu

entry.summary: This work proposes an information-theoretic framework for optimizing the classifier-free guidance schedule across the reverse diffusion trajectory, using a clean endpoint reference to specify a desired consistency-coverage trade-off. It addresses how the guidance weight should vary over time rather than remaining fixed.

entry.title: Natural Identifiers for Privacy and Data Audits in Large Language Models

author.name: Lorenzo Rossi, Bart{\l}omiej Marek, Franziska Boenisch, Adam Dziedzic

entry.summary: Proposes using naturally occurring identifiers in data to enable privacy and membership audits of already-trained LLMs without inserting canaries or requiring held-out IID datasets. Addresses a real practical limitation in post-hoc privacy auditing.

entry.title: BehaviorBench: Benchmarking Foundation Models for Behavioral Science Tasks

author.name: Jin Huang, Yutong Xie, Wanli Song, Xingjian Zhang, Walter Yuan, Matthew O. Jackson, Qiaozhu Mei

entry.summary: Introduces BehaviorBench, a benchmark evaluating foundation models across four behavioral-science capabilities (behavior prediction/simulation, strategic decision-making, trait inference, knowledge application) at both individual and distributional levels. Provides systematic understanding of how well models perform across behavioral tasks and populations.

entry.title: MEMPROBE: Probing Long-Term Agent Memory via Hidden User-State Recovery

author.name: Enze Ma, Yufan Zhou, Wei-Chieh Huang, Jie Yang, Huanhuan Ma, Zixuan Wang, Chengze Li, Chunyu Miao, Philip S. Yu, Zhen Wang

entry.summary: Introduces MEMPROBE, a benchmark that evaluates long-term agent memory as an auditable post-interaction artifact by measuring how much structured hidden user-state can be reconstructed from the memory an agent leaves behind. Shifts memory evaluation from indirect downstream behavior to direct auditing of the memory artifact.

entry.title: Towards Federated Long-Tailed Graph Learning: An Energy-Guided Dual Decoupling Approach

author.name: Lianshuai Guo, Zhongzheng Yuan, Xunkai Li, Meixia Qu, Wenyu Wang

entry.summary: FedEPD is an energy-guided dual decoupling framework for federated long-tailed graph learning, addressing how statistical scarcity biases global models toward majority classes and structurally isolates minority nodes in head-dominated neighborhoods. It matters for collaborative graph modeling across distributed clients with realistic long-tailed data while preserving privacy.

entry.title: Emergent Relational Order in LLM Agent Societies: From Collective Affect to Authority Stratification

author.name: Zhiyuan Ji, Xinyu Chen, Ziqi Dai, Shiyun Tang, Chunyu Wei, Yueguo Chen

entry.summary: Introduces CAREB-MAS, a multi-agent LLM framework grounded in social theory to study emergent relational order and authority stratification in agent societies over long horizons. Operationalizes sociological concepts like differential order patterns.

entry.title: When Retrieval Metrics Mislead: Measuring Policy Signal in Long-Horizon Tool-Use Agents

author.name: Tianyu Ding, Juan Pablo De la Cruz Weinstein

entry.summary: Tests whether exact-match retrieval recall is a valid proxy for policy context usefulness in long-horizon tool-use agents using tau-bench and Qwen2.5 classifiers. Finds retrieval metrics can mislead, as classifiers perform similarly with retrieved versus gold clauses despite low rank-1 retrieval.

entry.title: Selective Capability Unlearning in End-to-End Spoken Language Understanding

author.name: Akanksha Singh, Vinod Kumar Kurmi

entry.summary: Identifies capability persistence in spoken language understanding, where suppressing a target intent fails to remove the conditional slot-generation mapping that can be reconstructed via externally supplied prefixes. Proposes Binding Subspace, a representation-level framework to truly isolate and unlearn functionalities.

entry.title: MMed-Bench-IR: A Heterogeneous Benchmark for Multilingual Medical Information Retrieval

author.name: Junhyeok Lee, Han Jang, Hyeonjin Goh, Kyu Sung Choi

entry.summary: Introduces MMed-Bench-IR, a heterogeneous benchmark for multilingual medical information retrieval across six languages and three tasks: cross-lingual QA retrieval, concept discrimination, and evidence retrieval. Disentangles biomedical expertise from multilingual coverage.

entry.title: On the Stability of Prompt Ranking in Large Language Model Evaluation

author.name: Shaoshuai Du, Penghao Liang, Yixian Shen, Chuanqi Shi, Hang Zhang, Lun Wang

entry.summary: This paper systematically studies the stability of prompt rankings in LLM evaluation under variability from random seeds and limited evaluation subsets, finding that the top-performing prompt frequently changes despite moderate-to-high rank correlations. It proposes a stabilization method for more reliable prompt selection.

entry.title: TACTFUL: Tactile-Driven Exploration For Object Localization and Identification in Confined Environments

author.name: Shivani Kamtikar, Chung Hee Kim, Camilla Tabasso, Tye Brady, Joshua Migdal, Taskin Padir

entry.summary: TACTFUL is a vision-free tactile exploration framework enabling a multi-fingered robot to autonomously explore confined spaces, discover objects through contact, and identify them via tactile reconstruction. It is trained entirely on real hardware without simulation using a single policy balancing global exploration and local refinement.

entry.title: DeepBD: A Grounded Agentic Workflow for Variant Prioritization and Diagnosis of Genetic Birth Defects

author.name: Shiyu Li, Ziqi Yan, Zhihao Wu, Jielong Lu, Weiran Liao, Jiajun Yu, Genjie Li, Zeyu Chu, Jiajun Bu, Haishuai Wang

entry.summary: DeepBD is a grounded agentic workflow for prioritizing and diagnosing genetic birth defects, organizing case structuring, evidence retrieval across population genetics, variant prediction, phenotype ontologies, and literature into an LLM-assisted pipeline. It addresses the post-sequencing interpretation bottleneck under incomplete fetal phenotypes.

entry.title: FedUP: One-Shot Federated Unlearning via Centroid-Guided Plug-in Filters

author.name: Feihong Nan, Zhengyi Zhong, Pan Wang, Weidong Bao, Xiongtao Zhang, Quan Wen, Ji Wang

entry.summary: FedUP is a one-shot federated unlearning framework using lightweight pluggable filters trained server-side on differentially private class centroid samples to screen out target data while preserving original model performance. It bypasses multi-round communication and retraining, reducing unlearning latency from minutes to seconds.

entry.title: Project Ariadne: Prompt-Conditioned Route Generation for Synthesis Planning

author.name: Anton Morgunov, Victor S. Batista

entry.summary: Project Ariadne is a decoder-only route generator for retrosynthesis that represents the target, optional constraints, and full synthesis route in a single prompt-completion sequence, unifying constrained planning specifications in one model. It avoids training separate models per planning specification on standard PaRoutes benchmarks.

entry.title: MedBench v5: A Dynamic, Process-Oriented, and Hallucination-Aware Benchmark for Clinical Multimodal Models

author.name: Ding Jinru, Jiang Chuchu, Lu Lu, Pang Wenrao, Bian Mouxiao, Gao Zhuangzhi, Chen Jiangyuan, Peng xinwei, Chen Ruiyao, Ren Sijie, Lu Renjie, Han Bin, Liu Meiling, and Xu Jie

entry.summary: Introduces MedBench v5, a dynamic, process-oriented, hallucination-aware benchmark for clinical multimodal models featuring a dual-dimensional framework, information-flow stressors, a process audit protocol, and failure fingerprinting across 63 tasks. Moves beyond static QA toward auditing clinical reasoning processes.

entry.title: Escaping the Self-Confirmation Trap: An Execute-Distill-Verify Paradigm for Agentic Experience Learning

author.name: Shiding Zhu, Yudi Qi, Yajie Wang, Jiaze Li, Chao Song, Yaorui Shi, Yibo Miao, Hanqi Gao, Kai Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes EDV (Execute-Distill-Verify), a multi-agent framework to escape the Self-Confirmation Trap in agentic experience learning, where wrong-but-self-consistent trajectories get stored as successful experience. Uses heterogeneous agents to explore in parallel and verify before committing to memory.

entry.title: DREAM: Dense Retrieval Embeddings via Autoregressive Modeling

author.name: Yixuan Tang, Yi Yang

entry.summary: Proposes DREAM, which uses the autoregressive next-token-prediction loss of an LLM as supervision for training dense retrieval embedding models, avoiding the need for costly labeled positive/negative document pairs. The intuition is that relevant documents make the target output easier for the LLM to predict.

entry.title: LemonHarness Technical Report

author.name: Kailong Ren, Fubo Sun, Jiachen Liu, Liu Yang, Zimo Yin, Jiaying Li, Congli Yin, Ming He, Yu Huo, Jiawei Liu, Zeping Chen, Yubin Huangfu, Ronghua Li, Yixuan Wu, Xing Su, Yanzhi Xu, Likang Wu, Hongke Zhao, Lei Zhang, Xiaohui Geng, Jianping Fan

entry.summary: LemonHarness is an integrated execution framework for long-horizon LLM agents that establishes explicit execution boundaries to constrain state-changing operations and track file-system changes that scatter across paths over many iterations. It matters because agents observe only tool outputs and logs while actual state changes accumulate untracked in the file system.

entry.title: Agentic AI for Bilevel Long-Term Optimization of Policy-Driven Physical Layer Systems

author.name: Bingnan Xiao, Chenhao Yang, Wei Ni, Xin Wang, Tony Q. S. Quek

entry.summary: Agentic-LTPO is a nested bilevel optimization framework that uses agentic AI to generate upper-level configurations from evolving operator policies and environment summaries, while the lower level solves real-time physical-layer decisions. It matters for adapting wireless physical-layer systems to changing policies and service requirements that render fixed-objective methods ineffective.

entry.title: SemChunk-C: Semantic Segmentation for C Code

author.name: Boris Nazarov, Darya Frolova, Shaked Leibzirer, Pavel Kisilev

entry.summary: SemChunk-C trains an LLM-based classifier for semantic segmentation of C-family code, defining chunk categories and identifying chunk boundaries plus assigning descriptive functional attributes to overcome failures of fixed-size or syntax-based chunking. It matters for improving retrieval and downstream LLM-driven tasks on complex C code with macros and irregular structure.

entry.title: Ten Digits on a Train: AI-Assisted Verification of Two Eigenvalue Problems

author.name: Matthew J. Colbrook

entry.summary: Reports a human-AI collaboration to certify numerical eigenvalues for two difficult problems to ten decimal places, including separating a previously unresolved non-normal resonance pair. Demonstrates AI-assisted verified scientific computation.

entry.title: Maestro Order: A Model-Agnostic Orchestration Harness

author.name: Hidayet Aksu

entry.summary: Presents Maestro Order, a model-agnostic orchestration harness that turns unreliable single-pass solvers into reliable systems via four structural primitives (decompose, ensemble, verify, recurse) and a budget-aware controller. Treats any model as a black-box solver behind a uniform interface.

entry.title: A Benchmark for Hallucination Detection in VLMs for Gastrointestinal Endoscopy

author.name: Aminu Lawal, Niyoj Oli, Sachin Acharya, Prashnna Gyawali, Maria Carmen Romano, Binod Bhattarai

entry.summary: Benchmarks nine hallucination detection methods across five VLMs on a gastrointestinal endoscopy VQA dataset with 4,392 pairs. Addresses the underexplored evaluation of clinical hallucination detection outside radiology.

entry.title: NoContactNoWorries: Estimating Contact through Vision and Proprioception for In-Hand Dexterous Manipulation

author.name: Soham Patil, Avirup Das, Sourabh Bhosale, Spandan Roy

entry.summary: NoContactNoWorries is a transformer-based multimodal framework that infers binary contact states for in-hand dexterous manipulation by fusing RGB-D vision with robot proprioception, offering a scalable alternative to fragile tactile hardware. It is inspired by human embodied contact perception.

entry.title: UniDrive: A Unified Vision-Language and Grounding Framework for Interpretable Risk Understanding in Autonomous Driving

author.name: Xiaowei Gao, Pengxiang Li, Yitai Cheng, Ruihan Xu, James Haworth, Stephen Law, Yun Ye

entry.summary: UniDrive is a unified vision-language and grounding framework for interpretable risk understanding in autonomous driving, combining a temporal reasoning branch for scene dynamics with a high-resolution perception branch for spatial precision. It addresses the trade-off between temporal reasoning and spatial detail in driving MLLMs.

entry.title: The Degeneracy Distillery

author.name: T. Lucas Makinen, Deaglan J. Bartlett, Niall Jeffrey, Benjamin D. Wandelt

entry.summary: The Degeneracy Distillery is a method that automatically and symbolically detects and resolves degenerate parameter combinations from parameter-data pairs alone, by estimating and flattening parameter degeneracies. It aids label prediction and inverse problems in physical models and real-world datasets.

entry.title: 3D Masked Autoencoders are Robust Learners of Volumetric and Multimodal Cellular Representations for Microscopy

author.name: Amirhossein Kardoost, Lion Gleiter, Tingying Peng, Carsten Marr

entry.summary: This paper presents a systematic comparison showing 3D masked autoencoders outperform 2D projection and slice-based variants on volumetric fluorescence microscopy single-cell tasks under matched protocols. It further aligns visual representations with the ESM2 protein language model, finding cross-modal supervision yields larger gains for 3D models.

entry.title: Cross-Lingual Exploration for Parametric Knowledge

author.name: Elisha Diskind, Itamar Trainin, Uri Shaham, Leshem Choshen, Idan Szpektor, Omri Abend

entry.summary: Investigates cross-lingual prompting strategies to access parametric knowledge in LLMs that is unequally distributed across languages, identifying four dimensions of cross-lingual exploration. Evaluates across 17 typologically diverse languages, showing significant improvements in knowledge transfer and factual recall.

entry.title: Breaking the Filter Bubble: A Semantic Pareto-DQN Framework for Multi-Objective Recommendation

author.name: Cl\'audio L\'ucio Do Val Lopes, Lucca Machado da Silva, Andr\'e de Oliveira Brand\~ao

entry.summary: This work formalizes recommendation as a semantic multi-objective Markov decision process and introduces a Pareto-DQN agent that treats engagement, diversity, and provider fairness as non-aggregable reward signals to combat filter bubbles. It matters for balancing platform retention against societal values like information diversity in recommender systems.

entry.title: Assessing Distribution Shift in Human Activity Recognition for Domain Generalization

author.name: Rebecca Adaimi, Edison Thomaz

entry.summary: This paper systematically evaluates four types of distribution shift in human activity recognition (device and sensor heterogeneity and contextual changes) to characterize the domain generalization problem in real-world HAR. It matters because data diversity is well-acknowledged in HAR but the specific effects of different distribution shifts remain poorly understood.

entry.title: Listening makes Vision Clear for VLMs

author.name: Yiyang Chen, Yixin Tan, Binrui Shen

entry.summary: Identifies decoding drift in vision-language models where accumulated language priors mismatch visual attention, and proposes a Prompt-Vision Token Activation Map for more reliable vision-language consistency evaluation. Uses prompt-side rather than answer-side semantics.

entry.title: CAVEWOMAN: How Large Language Models Behave Under Linguistic Input and Output Compression

author.name: Morayo Danielle Adeyemi, Ryan A. Rossi, Franck Dernoncourt

entry.summary: Introduces Cavewoman, a two-channel evaluation protocol measuring whether terse caveman-style prompting actually saves cost, scoring accuracy, realized per-item cost, and reference agreement across eight models and five datasets. Finds output compression cuts cost while input compression has the opposite effect.

entry.title: DramaDirector: Geometry-Guided Short Drama Generation

author.name: Hengji Zhou, Sijie Liu, Jianrun Chen, Xingchen Zou, Lianghao Xia, Liqiang Nie

entry.summary: Proposes DramaDirector, a geometry-grounded framework for plot-to-short-drama video generation that borrows cinematographic geometry from real shots indexed by depth and pose. Trains the planner with schema-constrained SFT and GRPO under a text-visual alignment reward.

entry.title: Breaking Shortcut Learning for Cross-Trial EEG-Guided Target Speech Extraction via Two-Stage Training

author.name: Wonchul Shin, Inyong Choi, Kyogu Lee

entry.summary: Identifies that high within-trial EEG-guided target speech extraction performance can stem from trial-specific shortcuts, and proposes TRUST-TSE with contrastive pretraining and attended-speaker negative sampling to suppress trial-identity cues. Improves generalization to unseen trials.

entry.title: Real-Time Interactive Music Generation via Data-Free Streaming Consistency Distillation

author.name: Baisen Wang, Chenxi Bao, Qisong Han

entry.summary: This work proposes a data-free streaming consistency distillation framework that converts offline generative music models into real-time playable instruments for live interactive composition. It uses prompt-only inputs to synthesize teacher signals, avoiding expensive paired audio-latent datasets.

entry.title: OrbitForge: Text-to-3D Scene Generation via Reconstruction-Anchored Video Synthesis

author.name: Chenrui Fan, Paolo Favaro

entry.summary: OrbitForge converts a single text-generated video into a canonical closed-orbit 3D Gaussian Splatting scene using frozen video priors anchored by per-prompt reconstruction optimization. It uses 3D reconstruction as an anchor to improve consistency in text-to-3D scene generation.

entry.title: GRACE: Gated Refinement for Accurate Causal Edge Discovery in High-Dimensional Time Series

author.name: Mohammad Fesanghary, Abhinav Havaldar

entry.summary: GRACE refines constraint-based causal discovery for high-dimensional time series using Hard Concrete gates with L0 regularization, giving each candidate edge an independent gate that concentrates near 0 or 1 for clean bimodal edge separation. It avoids both infeasible nonlinear CI tests at scale and arbitrary thresholds in score-based methods.

entry.title: NeuroSonic: Conditional Flow Matching for EEG-to-Speech Reconstruction

author.name: Wenhao Gao, Yifan Wang, Yijia Ma, Carl Yang, Wen Li, Chenyu You

entry.summary: NeuroSonic is a conditional flow-matching framework for reconstructing continuous speech from scalp EEG, learning a deterministic probability-flow velocity field instead of regressing waveforms or using stochastic denoising. It addresses the instability caused by the mismatch between weak diffuse EEG signals and structured speech acoustics.

entry.title: EnerInfer: Energy-Aware On-Device LLM Inference

author.name: Bohua Zou, Nian Liu, Binqi Sun, Matteo Mascherin, Debayan Roy, Yutao Liu, Yu Peng, Ning Jia, Haibo Chen

entry.summary: Presents EnerInfer, a system for energy-aware on-device LLM inference that exploits the fact that modestly lowering NPU/memory frequencies preserves quality while improving energy efficiency. Adapts configuration dynamically since optimal settings vary across models, engines, and runtime conditions.

entry.title: Open-Vocabulary BEV Segmentation with 3D-Aware Geometric Constraints

author.name: Hojun Choi, Seulbin Hwang, Dae Jung Kim, Kisung Kim, Hyunjung Shim, Jinhan Lee

entry.summary: Proposes OVBEVSeg, an open-vocabulary bird's-eye-view segmentation framework that leverages vision-language models to recognize categories beyond the training set while maintaining real-time efficiency. Uses geometry-aware Gaussian splatting to address 3D inconsistency in lifting 2D VLM semantics into BEV.

entry.title: New Bounds for the Last Iterate of the Stochastic subGradient Method

author.name: Guglielmo Beretta, Tommaso Cesari, Roberto Colomboni, Andrea Paudice

entry.summary: Proves new last-iterate bounds for the stochastic subgradient method on one-dimensional convex Lipschitz objectives, removing an extra log factor under i.i.d. bounded-variance noise and showing suboptimality without the i.i.d. assumption. Resolves an open problem negatively.

entry.title: The Warrant Gap: Claim-Conditioned Re-scoring for Fact-Checking

author.name: Arka Ujjal Dey, John Collomosse

entry.summary: Identifies the warrant gap in LLM fact-checking, where systems output Supports labels whose cited evidence does not actually license the claim, and introduces SIFT (claim-conditioned re-scoring) plus WSP, an automatic NLI metric checking whether the cited warrant entails the claim. Evaluated across four datasets and four open-source backbones.

entry.title: Can Aggregate Invariants Accelerate Continuous Subgraph Matching? Limits, Laws, and a Dynamic Spectral Index

author.name: Minghao Chen, Jiale Zheng

entry.summary: This paper analyzes whether aggregate spectral invariants can accelerate continuous subgraph matching over dynamic graphs, proving that lazily-maintained spectral bounds lose pruning power within four touching updates while exact maintenance is affordable when selective, and proposes a dynamic spectral index. It matters for the theory and practice of efficient pattern matching in evolving graph databases.

entry.title: Accuracy and Satisfaction in Multi-Turn LLM Dialogues for NFR Assessment

author.name: Ali Pourghasemi Fatideh, Wilder Baldwin, Maria Dhakal, Collin McMillan, Sepideh Ghanavati

entry.summary: This paper investigates accuracy and conversational quality of multi-turn LLM dialogues for assessing software non-functional requirements (NFRs), which are vague and context-dependent, going beyond single-turn functional correctness benchmarks. It matters because current evaluation benchmarks for developer assistants ignore the multi-turn collaborative reasoning needed for NFR assessment.

entry.title: RAVEN: A Regime-Aware Variable-context Expert Network for Financial Time Series Forecasting

author.name: Cheng He, Zhenyu Guan, Xijie Liang, Defu Lian, Jiajia Li, Enhong Chen, Patrick P. C. Lee, Geng Hu, Zehao Chen

entry.summary: Proposes RAVEN, a regime-aware mixture-of-experts framework for financial time series forecasting that adaptively determines the optimal look-back context per sample using nested contiguous windows. Addresses the mismatch between fixed context windows and non-stationary price processes.

entry.title: Zero-Shot Test-Time Canonicalization using Out-of-Distribution Scoring

author.name: Dominik Lindner, Johann Schmidt, Tom Siegl, Martin Becker, Sebastian Stober

entry.summary: Reframes test-time canonicalization for affine-robust classification as out-of-distribution scoring, undoing input transformations to map to a canonical form without retraining the classifier. Explores the previously unexamined design space of scoring functions and optimizers.

entry.title: Does My Embedding Reflect That $A = B$? Evaluating Mathematical Equivalence in Embedding Models

author.name: Jiaying Ye, Samarth Rao, Leo Carlin, Kedar Chintalapati, Saharsh Bhargava, Rachit Jaiswal, Michael Zhou, Jared Darlington, Jarod Alper, Vasily Ilin, Henry Kvinge

entry.summary: Introduces the MELD dataset of mathematically equivalent but lexically different statement pairs to test whether embedding models capture mathematical equivalence across subfields and formalisms. Motivated by the need to navigate between mathematical languages such as Lean and natural language.

entry.title: Sentence-Level Contextual Entrainment in Large Language Models

author.name: Yang Liu, Chenhui Chu

entry.summary: Extends the phenomenon of contextual entrainment in LLMs from the token level to the sentence level, showing across 26 models and two datasets that sentences in the prompt (even counterfactual ones) significantly increase their own probability during generation. Provides insight into how context biases model outputs.

entry.title: AVOC: Enhancing Hour-Level Audio-Video Understanding in Omni-Modal LLMs via Retrieval-Inspired Token Compression

author.name: Yijing Chen, Wenhui Tan, Xiaoyi Yu, Yuyue Wang, Xin Cheng, Kaisi Guan, Hao Jiang, Xiangyang Li, Guojie Zhu, Ruihua Song

entry.summary: Proposes AVOC, a framework for hour-level audio-video understanding in omni-modal LLMs that reframes multimodal token compression as a top-K retrieval problem, retrieving a compact query-relevant token subset within a fixed context budget. Draws on classical information-retrieval criteria for token selection.

entry.title: OmniPath: A Multi-Modal Agentic Framework for Auditing Wheelchair Accessibility

author.name: ASM Mobarak Hossain, Nadim Mahmud, Vaskar Raychoudhury, Md Osman Gani

entry.summary: OmniPath is a multimodal agentic system that fuses OpenStreetMap topology with high-density aerial LiDAR to virtually audit pedestrian path accessibility for wheelchair users in 0.5-meter increments. It matters for proactive accessibility mapping that conveys how a path physically feels to travel rather than just where it exists.

entry.title: Cost-Optimal Decision Diagrams for Stochastic Boolean Function Evaluation

author.name: Xia Zong, Tuomo Lehtonen, Jussi Rintanen

entry.summary: This paper presents the first practical exact branch-and-bound algorithm for constructing cost-optimal deterministic evaluation strategies for stochastic Boolean function evaluation under variable acquisition costs and a probability distribution over truth assignments. It matters for cost-sensitive decision-making such as medical diagnosis where acquiring each piece of information has different cost.

entry.title: A Survey on Federated Causal Discovery and Inference

author.name: Xianjie Guo, Yuwei Wang, Guodu Xiang, Xiaoli Tang, Kui Yu, Han Yu, Qiang Yang

entry.summary: Provides a systematic survey of federated causal discovery and inference, organizing the emerging field through a multi-dimensional taxonomy. Addresses privacy-preserving collaborative causal analysis across distributed institutions.

entry.title: From Spatial to Spectral: An Efficient, Frequency-Guided Feature Representation Learner for Small Object Detection

author.name: Yuhan Rui, Shihan Qiao, Yibin Lou, Mingxi Yu, Yutong Wan, Yanqiao Chen, Dongsheng Hou, Zhen Cao, Athena Zhuoming Zhong, Qi Hao

entry.summary: Proposes a frequency-guided feature representation framework that shifts small object detection from spatial to spectral processing, recovering fragile high-frequency cues without expensive upscaling. Generalizes across CNN and Transformer detectors.

entry.title: Blockwise Policy-Drift Gating for On-Policy Distillation

author.name: Liwen Zheng, Haiyun Jiang

entry.summary: Introduces blockwise policy-drift gating, a lightweight student-only drift controller for on-policy distillation under rollout reuse. Reweights position losses based on log-probability shifts without changing teacher targets.

entry.title: Inclusive Interactive Collisions for Multi-View Consistent Compositional 3D Generation

author.name: Chang Liu, Mingwen Shao, Xiang Lv, Xinyuan Chen, Lingzhuang Meng, Qiao Zhang, Zhengyi Gong, Jinghao Hu

entry.summary: Proposes I2C-3D, an optimization-based method for multi-view consistent compositional 3D generation that models reasonable interactions between Gaussian primitives and reduces cross-view hallucinations from Score Distillation Sampling. Addresses multi-object 3D asset generation.

entry.title: Average Rankings Mask Per-Subject Optimality: A Friedman-Nemenyi Benchmark of EEG Motor-Imagery BCI Decoders

author.name: Xavier Vasques, Paul Barbaste, Olivier Oullier

entry.summary: This benchmark study evaluates 1,056 EEG motor-imagery BCI decoding configurations across three datasets using Friedman-Nemenyi statistical testing, showing that average rankings mask per-subject optimality. It challenges the common claim that any single decoding pipeline is broadly preferable.

entry.title: FlowPipe: LLM-Enhanced Conditional Generative Flow Networks for Data Preparation Pipeline Construction

author.name: Kunyu Ni, Lei Cao, Jie He, Xiaotong Zhang, Jianfeng Jin, Junyu Dong, Yanwei Yu

entry.summary: FlowPipe formulates automated data preparation pipeline construction as conditional generative flow network sampling enhanced by LLMs, addressing weak credit assignment, poor dataset context injection, and inefficient exploration in prior Multi-DQN methods. It targets the combinatorial difficulty of synthesizing cleaning and feature transformation operator sequences.

entry.title: Reconstructing GRACE Terrestrial Water Storage with Spatio-Temporal Graph Neural Networks: An Application to South America

author.name: Lukas Arzoumanidis, Lara Johannsen, Klara Middendorf, Annette Eicker, Youness Dehbi

entry.summary: This work reconstructs monthly GRACE-like terrestrial water storage anomalies back to 1940 over South America using spatio-temporal graph neural networks learning from ERA5 meteorological forcing. It extends the short satellite record for climate-scale analyses beyond prior grid-cell regression and CNN approaches.

entry.title: DREG: A Layer-Wise Jacobian Regularization as a General-Purpose Penalty

author.name: Rowan Martnishn

entry.summary: DREG is a layer-wise Jacobian/derivative regularization penalty studied through a fully-crossed factorial sweep of 960 experiments across activations, regularizers, datasets, and seeds. It achieves the highest clean-regime accuracy among tested regularizers and ranks second in noise robustness behind spectral normalization.

entry.title: Learning the Koopman Operator using Attention Free Transformers

author.name: Mohammed Nagdi, Evangelos-Marios Nikolados, Alexey Yermakov, Mars Gao, Nathan Kutz, Filippo Menolascina

entry.summary: This work learns Koopman operators with autoencoders augmented by an attention-free latent memory block that aggregates a short window of past latents in linear time to correct drift in long-horizon rollouts. It improves robustness on systems with switching, continuous spectra, or strong transients.

entry.title: A Time-Reparameterized Cumulative Intensity Extrapolation Sampler for Discrete Flow Matching

author.name: Feiyang Fu, Hehe Fan

entry.summary: TR-CIE is a sampler for discrete flow matching that improves generation quality under limited function evaluations via schedule-based time reparameterization and cumulative intensity extrapolation. It targets efficient sampling beyond standard tau-leaping discretizations.

entry.title: Computational references are not experiments: pre-registered validation of machine-learned sodium-cathode voltages

author.name: Krishna Teja Vepa

entry.summary: A pre-registered validation study showing that ML screens for sodium-ion cathode voltages trained against computed references carry systematic errors that fail when checked against experiment-anchored values. Emphasizes rigorous pre-registration and documents how computational references differ from experiments.

entry.title: Autonomous Video Generation with Counterfactual Controllability for Self-Evolving World Models

author.name: Xin Wang, Wenxuan Liu, Tongtong Feng, Wenwu Zhu

entry.summary: Argues that video generation yields only a partial, implicit world model and proposes autonomous video generation with counterfactual controllability to identify which variables are controllable. Aims toward self-evolving world models that go beyond passive visual prediction.

entry.title: MotifGen: Spatiotemporal interpolation of misaligned satellite images via multi-source generative modeling, in an application to tropical cyclones

author.name: Cl\'ement Dauvilliers (Inria), Claire Monteleoni (Inria)

entry.summary: Introduces MotifGen, the first generative model for spatiotemporal interpolation of misaligned, irregularly-timed, multi-source satellite microwave imagery, applied to tropical cyclone monitoring. Handles heterogeneous instruments with varying characteristics that change across samples.

entry.title: EXPO-SQL: Execution-based Clause-level Policy Optimization for Text-to-SQL

author.name: Jaehoon Lee, CheolWon Na, Suyoung Bae, Jin-Seop Lee, Jihyung Lee, YunSeok Choi, Jee-Hyong Lee

entry.summary: Proposes EXPO-SQL, an execution-based clause-level policy optimization method for text-to-SQL that assigns fine-grained clause-level rewards by identifying erroneous clauses, rather than uniform query-level rewards. Provides denser learning signals for correct SQL generation.

entry.title: Beyond Logprobs: A Multi-Signal Confidence Engine for LLM-Based Document Field Extraction

author.name: Nitesh Kumar

entry.summary: Presents ExtractConf, a cross-domain field-agnostic confidence engine for LLM document field extraction, arguing that log-probabilities, verbalized confidence, and self-consistency all collapse to over-confidence at practical thresholds. Combines multiple signals to reliably separate trustworthy from untrustworthy extractions for automation-versus-review decisions.

entry.title: Prob-BBDM: a Probabilistic Brownian Bridge Diffusion Model for MRI sequence image-to-image translation

author.name: Martin Valls (UFR SFA), Pascal Bourdon (UFR SFA), Christine Fernandez-Maloigne (LabCom I3M), Guillaume Herpe (CHU Poitiers -- Radio, DACTIM-MIS), David Helbert (UFR SFA)

entry.summary: MVG-KAN is a multi-view geo-wind guided Kolmogorov-Arnold Network for short-term PM2.5 forecasting that incorporates wind-direction-dependent pollutant transport beyond distance-only or correlation-based graphs. It matters for public health protection and air-quality early warning given the complex coupled factors driving PM2.5 variation.

entry.title: Synergizing Physically Constrained MCMC and Chemical-Informed Gaussian Processes for Reaction Network Discovery

author.name: Runzhe Liu, Zihao Wang, Wenbo Yang, Shengyang Tao

entry.summary: Combines physically constrained MCMC topology sampling with chemical-informed Gaussian processes to discover interpretable reaction networks from sparse, noisy time-series. Integrates conservation laws and thermodynamic screening into a gray-box workflow.

entry.title: Decentralized Coordination of Autonomous Traffic Through Advanced Air Mobility Corridors

author.name: Jasmine Jerry Aloor, Hamsa Balakrishnan

entry.summary: Shows that autonomous aircraft can learn to self-organize into corridor flows in decentralized settings for Advanced Air Mobility, contrary to the belief that corridor-based operations are inefficient without central management. Uses learning-based coordination for fixed-wing aircraft.

entry.title: RASC+: Retrieval-Constrained LLM Adjudication for Clinical Value Set Authoring

author.name: Sumit Mukherjee

entry.summary: Presents RASC+, a stage-wise retrieval-constrained LLM adjudication approach for clinical value set authoring, optimizing candidate-pool recall then constrained LLM selection. Improves on poorly suited zero-shot generation for large version-controlled clinical code systems.

entry.title: DynaWM: Dynamics-Aware Distillation with World Model and Momentum Targets for Smooth Locomotion over Continuous Stairs

author.name: Haidong Hou, Zhangguo Yu, Hengbo Qi, Jianlin Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes DynaWM, a dynamics-aware distillation framework using a world model regularizer and momentum target encoder for smooth bipedal-wheeled robot locomotion over continuous stairs. Enhances terrain geometry encoding and stabilizes knowledge transfer.

entry.title: Exact Schur-Sylvester Dimensionality Reductions for Non-Smooth Stochastic Complexity and Manifold Sampling

author.name: Trenton Lau, Gary P. T. Choi

entry.summary: This paper presents an exact, mathematically equivalent reformulation that bypasses cubic-scaling bottlenecks in computing the Normalized Maximum Likelihood codelength for non-smooth estimators like Lasso, using block Schur complement and Sylvester's determinant identity. It reduces complexity in manifold-constrained projection and volume integration for a geometric MCMC sampler.

entry.title: When Top-1 Fails: Calibrating LoRA Monitors for Masked Diffusion LMs

author.name: Lucky Verma, Pratik Yadav

entry.summary: This paper tests top-1 argmax concentration as a collapse-warning diagnostic during LoRA/PEFT fine-tuning of discrete diffusion language models, finding it fires for all 816 configurations while zero actual collapses occur, giving zero precision. It identifies pre-equilibrium saturation as the cause and evaluates max LoRA gradient norm as a better parameter-side signal.

entry.title: Hessian-augmented Supervised Learning for Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman PDEs

author.name: Mat\'ias G\'omez-Aedo, Behzad Azmi, Yuyang Huang, Dante Kalise, Karl Kunisch

entry.summary: Develops a Hessian-augmented supervised learning method for approximating value functions in Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman PDEs by generating training data of values, gradients, and Hessians via Pontryagin's principle and Riccati equations. The added derivative information substantially reduces sample complexity.

entry.title: Harmonic: Hierarchical State Space Models for Efficient Long-Context Language Modeling

author.name: Petr Nyoma

entry.summary: Presents Harmonic, a hierarchical state-space model stacking three recurrent levels at progressively slower timescales where each level receives prediction errors from below. Reports outperforming comparable Transformer and Mamba baselines on long-context language modeling and successful training at 64K tokens where baselines run out of memory.

entry.title: Measuring User's Mental Models of Speech Translation in Human-AI Collaboration

author.name: HyoJung Han, Nishant Balepur, Jordan Boyd-Graber, Marine Carpuat

entry.summary: Studies users' mental models of speech translation systems via a cross-lingual question-answering framework where users either accept MT output or request professional re-translation. Finds users develop stronger mental models with practice, especially with some source-language knowledge, predicting where systems are likely to fail.

entry.title: Tractable Reasoning and Conjunctive Query Answering for Defeasible DL-Lite under Rational Closure

author.name: Giovanni Casini (CNR - ISTI, University of Cape Town), Umberto Straccia (CNR - ISTI)

entry.summary: This paper studies reasoning under Rational Closure for the core and horn variants of the DL-Lite description logic family, providing a plug-in architecture over standard classical reasoners for instance checking and conjunctive query answering with minimal overhead. It matters for efficient non-monotonic reasoning over defeasible knowledge in lightweight ontologies.

entry.title: Matching Tasks to Objectives: Fine-Tuning and Prompt-Tuning Strategies for Encoder-Decoder Pre-trained Language Models

author.name: Ahmad Pouramini, Hesham Faili

entry.summary: This study explores how diverse pre-training objectives affect encoder-decoder language model performance on generation and question answering, introducing a Match Task to Objective (MTO) framework with automated methods to determine the appropriate objective and prepare task-related data for adaptation. It matters for aligning pre-training and fine-tuning objectives with downstream tasks like commonsense retrieval and completion.

entry.title: VeriPilot: An LLM-Powered Verilog Debugging Framework

author.name: Yihan Wang, Cheng Liu, Jiazheng Zhang, Lei Zhang, Long Cheng, Xiaowei Li, Huawei Li

entry.summary: Presents VeriPilot, an LLM-powered Verilog debugging framework using golden reference models to enable fine-grained fault localization beyond simple test-output feedback. Addresses long dependency chains in hardware code.

entry.title: Infinitesimal Causality

author.name: Sridhar Mahadevan

entry.summary: This paper introduces a categorical account of infinitesimal causality in Frobenius Markov categories with tangent-bundle semantics, treating interventions as tangent deformations of copy/discard structure. It defines categorical causal sufficiency through the compatibility of algebraic and geometric Frobenius structures.

entry.title: Task Decomposition for Efficient Annotation

author.name: Nupoor Gandhi, Emma Strubell

entry.summary: This paper proposes decomposing complex structured annotation tasks into subtasks distributed across heterogeneous annotators including models and humans, rather than end-to-end annotation by single annotators. It aims to make high-quality structured annotation more cost-efficient.

entry.title: Real vs. Complex Spectral Bases for Neural Operators: The Role of Green's Function Alignment

author.name: Jason Sulskis, Sathya Ravi

entry.summary: Introduces the Hartley Neural Operator (HNO), a real-valued counterpart to Fourier Neural Operators that uses the Discrete Hartley Transform to avoid complex arithmetic and conjugate-symmetry redundancy. Analyzes how spectral basis choice interacts with Green's function alignment for PDE solving.

entry.title: Difference-Making without Making a Difference

author.name: Sander Beckers

entry.summary: This philosophy-of-causation paper shows that Andreas and Gunther's most recent factual difference-making definition of actual causation instantiates all three of their supposedly competing account types, arguing these are distinctions without a difference and undermining all seven of their accounts. It matters for the foundations of causal reasoning by clarifying conceptual confusion in definitions of actual causation.

entry.title: Coordinate-Queryable Neural Field Reconstruction for EEG Spatial Super-Resolution with Unseen-Electrode Generation

author.name: Hongjun Liu, Leyu Zhou, Zijianghao Yang, Chao Yao

entry.summary: Reformulates EEG spatial super-resolution as learning a shared conditional scalp field via implicit neural representations, enabling robustness to random missing channels and generation of unseen electrode positions. Addresses brittleness of fixed channel-mapping methods.

entry.title: JupOtter: Cell-Level Bug Detection in Jupyter Notebooks

author.name: Lukas Ottenhof, Thibaud Lutellier

entry.summary: Presents JupOtter, a bug detection system for Jupyter Notebooks with notebook-specific tokenization, cell-level bug prediction, and a new 21,000-notebook labeled dataset. Targets the rising problem of buggy notebooks on platforms like GitHub.

entry.title: MedPCFM: Improving Medical Point Cloud Completion by Integrating Point Transformers and Flow Matching

author.name: Kamil Kwarciak, Marek Wodzinski

entry.summary: MedPCFM introduces a flow-matching approach backed by Point Transformer v3 for medical point cloud completion, used in anatomical reconstruction. It is evaluated on skull and mandibular defect datasets, achieving state-of-the-art generative completion performance.

entry.title: Beyond U-Net: A Latent-Representation-Aligned Skip-Free Backbone for Flow-Matching Speech Enhancement

author.name: Wangyi Pu, Michele Scarpiniti

entry.summary: This work proposes a skip-free encoder-decoder backbone for flow-matching speech enhancement guided by latent representation alignment, avoiding U-Net skip connections that may transfer noise-correlated features to the decoder. It aligns bottleneck and decoder representations with clean latent features.

entry.title: Flow-Corrected Thompson Sampling for Non-Stationary Contextual Bandits

author.name: AmirHossein Naghdi, Ali Baheri

entry.summary: Proposes Flow-Corrected Thompson Sampling for non-stationary linear contextual bandits, transporting past rewards to the present via an explicit drift model with confidence weights reflecting transport reliability. Handles linear drift, periodic variation, and regime switches in a unified template.

entry.title: EERLoss: A Novel Loss Function for Training Deep Biometric Models. A Case Study in Keystroke Dynamics

author.name: Nahuel Gonzalez, Marta Robledo-Moreno, Ivan DeAndres-Tame, Ruben Vera-Rodriguez, Ruben Tolosana

entry.summary: Introduces EERLoss, a subdifferentiable and arbitrarily accurate approximation to the Equal Error Rate for directly training deep biometric models, aligning the training objective with the evaluation metric. Validated on the challenging keystroke-dynamics verification task.

entry.title: Layer-wise Probing of wav2vec 2.0 and Whisper for Consonant Cluster Reduction in African American English

author.name: Hamid Mojarad, Kevin Tang

entry.summary: Conducts layer-wise probing of wav2vec2 and Whisper to study how consonant cluster reduction in African American English is represented, finding that reduced segments retain cues to their underlying cluster identity. Relevant to understanding ASR disparities affecting AAE speakers.

entry.title: Exploring Dualistic Meta-Learning to Enhance Domain Generalization in Open Set Scenarios

author.name: Xiran Wang, Jian Zhang, Lei Qi, Yang Gao, Yinghuan Shi

entry.summary: Proposes a dualistic meta-learning strategy (MEDIC) for open-set domain generalization that addresses the imbalance causing over-rejection of out-of-distribution data from known classes. Performs joint domain-class matching.

entry.title: Token Complexity of Certifying Stochastic-Oracle Reliability

author.name: Jie Wang

entry.summary: Develops certification token complexity, the minimum expected token cost to certify whether a stochastic oracle meets a target reliability level, building on the Stochastic-Oracle Turing Machine framework. Constructs an SPRT-based certification machine with controlled error probability.

entry.title: Structural Kolmogorov-Arnold Convolutions: Learnable Function on the Values or the Filter Shape as Parameter-Efficient Alternative to Per-Edge Convolutional KANs

author.name: Stefano Mereu, Oleksandr Kuznetsov, Gabriele Marchello, Alessandro Galdelli, Emanuele Frontoni, Adriano Mancini, Ferdinando Cannella

entry.summary: This work proposes structural Kolmogorov-Arnold convolutions that place learnable univariate functions in the convolution structure (on values or filter shape) rather than per-edge, offering a more parameter-efficient alternative to per-edge convolutional KANs. It explores three realizations along a single design axis.

entry.title: Paying to Know: Micro-Transaction Markets for Verified Product Information in Agentic E-Commerce

author.name: Filippos Ventirozos, Matthew Shardlow

entry.summary: This paper envisions agentic e-commerce as a micro-transaction market where buyer agents pay fractions of a cent to progressively unlock verified product information, arguing the bottleneck shifts from matching products to acquiring trustworthy decision-relevant data. It builds on emerging agent-native micro-payment rails like x402 and AP2.

entry.title: Federated Survival Analysis in Healthcare: A Multi-Model Evaluation on Cross-Institutional Heterogeneous Breast Cancer Data

author.name: Natalia Moreno-Blasco, Anusha Ihalapathirana, Pekka Siirtola, Miguel Fernandez-de-Retana

entry.summary: This paper systematically evaluates federated survival analysis on a cross-institutional, naturally heterogeneous breast cancer cohort, comparing Cox proportional hazards, DeepSurv, and other models under privacy-preserving federated learning. It examines effectiveness for time-to-event modeling under realistic data heterogeneity.

entry.title: A Physics-Informed Fourier-Wavelet Transformer for Multiscale Computational Fluid Dynamics Surrogate Modeling

author.name: Somyajit Chakraborty, Ming Pan, Xizhong Chen

entry.summary: Proposes a physics-informed Fourier-wavelet transformer for next-step velocity-field reconstruction in CFD surrogate modeling, combining hybrid spectral encoding with PDE-residual-biased self-attention and self-supervised physics pretraining. Targets better capture of localized multiscale flow structures.

entry.title: Dirac-Frenkel dynamics with inertia for nonlinearly parametrized solutions of evolution problems

author.name: Matteo Raviola, Benjamin Peherstorfer

entry.summary: Adds inertia to Dirac-Frenkel dynamics for nonlinearly parametrized evolution problems (e.g., neural networks, mixture models), preserving useful parameter-velocity information in weakly informed directions while following standard dynamics in well-informed ones. Proves well-posedness and provides a posteriori error bounds.

entry.title: Ground Then Rank: Revisiting Knowledge-Based VQA with Training-Free Entity Identification

author.name: Qian Ma, Qiong Wu, Zhengyi Zhou, Yao Ma

entry.summary: Revisits knowledge-based VQA with a training-free Ground-Then-Rank approach that separates entity-level identification from fact-level evidence ranking, rather than coupling them in a single re-ranking stage. Targets the entity and evidence grounding bottlenecks in multimodal RAG.

entry.title: Prague Dependency Treebank -- Consolidated 2.0: Enriching a Complex Annotation Scheme

author.name: Marie Mikulov\'a, Ji\v{r}\'i M\'irovsk\'y, Milan Straka, Pavl\'ina Synkov\'a, Jan \v{S}t\v{e}p\'anek, Barbora \v{S}t\v{e}p\'ankov\'a, Jan Haji\v{c}

entry.summary: Presents the second consolidated version of the Prague Dependency Treebank (PDT-C 2.0), a uniformly annotated nearly 4-million-token multi-layer Czech language resource with linked meaning representations, coreference, and discourse relations, plus compatible lexicons.
