author.name: Tianjian Li, Jingyu Zhang, William Jurayj, Xi Wang, Chuanyang Jin, Mehrdad Farajtabar, Eric Nalisnick, Daniel Khashabi

entry.summary: Proposes SelfCompact, a scaffold letting the agent itself decide when and how to compact accumulated context via a compaction tool and a lightweight rubric, rather than fixed-interval token-threshold triggers. Avoids discarding partial results mid-derivation.

entry.title: SingGuard: A Policy-Adaptive Multimodal LLM Guardrail with Dynamic Reasoning

author.name: SingGuard Team

entry.summary: Introduces SingGuard, a policy-adaptive multimodal LLM guardrail family that treats moderation policy as runtime input with dynamic reasoning. Aims to adapt safety assessment when rules vary across products and regions.

entry.title: Semi-Supervised Vision-Language-Action Model

author.name: Hongyang He, Jiuming Liu, Victor Sanchez

entry.summary: Proposes SemiVLA, a semi-supervised vision-language-action adaptation framework using self-distilled teacher-student learning where only a small fraction of trajectories have action labels. Addresses the cost of action-labeled demonstrations for robotics.

entry.title: Multi4D: High-Fidelity Dynamic Gaussian Splatting via Multi-Level Competitive Allocation

author.name: Rui Wang, Quentin Lohmeyer, Siyu Tang, Mirko Meboldt

entry.summary: Introduces Multi4D, a dynamic Gaussian splatting framework using multi-level competitive allocation that distributes modeling capacity across static structure, persistent dynamic geometry, and transient appearance primitives. Resolves the tension between motion consistency and visual fidelity.

entry.title: T-IMPACT: A Severity-Aware Benchmark for Contextual Image-Text Manipulation

author.name: Gagandeep Singh, Aaditya Yadav, Priyanka Singh

entry.summary: Introduces T-IMPACT, a severity-aware benchmark of ~99,000 manipulated news-style image-text pairs spanning pristine, image-only, text-only, and joint manipulations, with a calibrated continuous severity signal. It captures how strongly an edit changes interpretation rather than just authenticity.

entry.title: PolicyTrim: Boosting Intrinsic Policy Efficiency of Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Xianghui Wang, Feng Chen, Wenbo Zhang, Hua Yan, Zixuan Wang, Changsheng Li, Yinjie Lei

entry.summary: Introduces PolicyTrim to boost intrinsic policy efficiency of Vision-Language-Action models by addressing planning unreliability and action redundancy, reducing effective action-chunk length and total physical steps. Targets execution efficiency rather than just per-step inference latency.

entry.title: MapReason-OSM: Can Vision-Language Models Make Graph-Verifiable Mobility Decisions from Street Maps ?

author.name: Srinivas Venkatanarayanan (NVIDIA, University of Central Florida), Clement Pakkam Isaac (NVIDIA, University of South Florida)

entry.summary: Introduces MapReason-OSM, a benchmark for graph-verifiable mobility decisions on self-rendered OpenStreetMap panels with hidden street graphs and exact oracles, yielding 6,000 instances. Evaluates whether VLMs can make road-network-consistent routing and navigation decisions.

entry.title: Modular Diffusion Models for Structured Visual Recognition

author.name: Siddhesh Khandelwal, Bj\"orn Ommer, Leonid Sigal

entry.summary: Proposes Modular Diffusion Models, learning a distribution over structured visual outputs (detection, segmentation, scene graphs) to capture prediction uncertainty and multi-modality that deterministic methods miss. Addresses ambiguities from occlusion and noisy training data.

entry.title: Policy-as-Data: Learning Generalizable HOI Diffusion Models from Simulated Physics

author.name: Shujia Li, Jianshu Hu, Haiyu Zhang, Yunpeng Jiang, Haoyuan Jin, Xinyuan Chen, Yaohui Wang, Yutong Ban

entry.summary: Proposes a Policy-as-Data framework that uses reinforcement learning policies in a physics simulator to generate scalable, task-oriented human-object interaction data, training generative HOI models that generalize to unseen objects with physical consistency. Overcomes motion-capture data scarcity.

entry.title: Vera: A Layered Diffusion Model for Content-Preserving Video Editing

author.name: Hongkai Zheng, Ta-Ying Cheng, Benjamin Klein, Yisong Yue, Zhuoning Yuan

entry.summary: Introduces Vera, a layered diffusion framework for content-preserving video editing that generates an edit layer plus alpha matte for compositing rather than regenerating every pixel, using a Mixture-of-Transformers architecture. Separates creative editing from content preservation by design.

entry.title: PanoVine: Whole-Body Visuomotor Control for Soft Growing Vine Robot

author.name: Yimeng Qin, Xiaomeng Xu, William Heap, Aditi Oak, Shuran Song, Allison Okamura

entry.summary: PanoVine presents the first autonomous vine (soft growing) robot system with a data-driven vision-based control framework using 19 body-distributed cameras for whole-body feedback. An end-to-end visuomotor policy trained from demonstrations handles the hysteresis and deformation that defeat conventional control.

entry.title: LaST-HD: Learning Latent Physical Reasoning from Scalable Human Data for Robot Manipulation

author.name: Jiaming Liu, Yinxi Wang, Chenyang Gu, Siyuan Qian, Xiangju Mi, Hao Chen, Jiawei Chen, Qingpo Wuwu, Xiaoqi Li, Nuowei Han, Yiming Zhang, Xuheng Zhang, Yang Yue, Yeqing Yang, Lei Wang, Peng Jia, Hao Tang, Shanghang Zhang

entry.summary: LaST-HD is a human-to-robot action learning paradigm that aligns human-hand and robot demonstrations in a shared latent reasoning space rather than just retargeting kinematics, training an action-conditioned world model on unpaired data to align physical dynamics. It extends reasoning-before-acting VLA to leverage scalable human-hand data.

entry.title: In LLM Reasoning, there is Irrationality on top of Value Misalignment

author.name: Kejiang Qian, Fengxiang He

entry.summary: Formalizes a gap between alignment and rational reasoning in LLMs as rational value risk, the utility discrepancy between deployed reasoning and an expected-utility-maximizing counterpart. Decomposes estimation error into components and tests across many model families.

entry.title: From Question Answering to Task Completion: A Survey on Agent System and Harness Design

author.name: Jianyuan Guo, Zhiwei Hao, Chengcheng Wang, Cheng Fan, Tingzhang Luo, Hongguang Li, Ying Gao, Hefei Mei, Jiankun Peng, Rongjian Xu, Minjing Dong, Han Wu, Mengyu Zheng, Kai Han, Shiqi Wang, Chang Xu, Yunhe Wang

entry.summary: A survey examining LLM-based agents through a model-harness lens, asking where the performance bottleneck resides among foundation model, execution harness, and their coupling. It traces the evolution from prompt engineering to harness engineering and agent-native training.

entry.title: Repeated Shared Access Enables Grokking, but Edit Propagation Depends on a Fine-Grained Addressable Memory

author.name: Yanan Niu

entry.summary: In a controlled synthetic knowledge-graph QA setting, shows that repeated shared access (via loop recurrence or shared memory) is the common ingredient enabling out-of-distribution grokking, while factual edit propagation depends specifically on fine-grained addressable memory. Compares four architectures crossing recurrence with memory.

entry.title: Agentic Time Machine as an Infrastructure for Future-Event Forecasting

author.name: Jingyi Chai, Bingyang Zheng, Xiangrui Liu, Hao Lu, Zihang Zhou, Tianchen Wang, Kemeng Zhang, Siheng Chen

entry.summary: Agentic Time Machine reconstructs the web state at any past time by filtering post-cutoff content, enabling retrospective yet realistic evaluation of LLM agents for future-event forecasting. It balances feedback speed against environmental fidelity.

entry.title: Self-Improvement Can Self-Regress: The Rise-and-Collapse Failure Mode of LLM Self-Training

author.name: Jianzhe Lin

entry.summary: Documents a rise-then-collapse failure where REINFORCE post-training for code quickly improves then collapses within a single campaign due to within-task over-optimization, not catastrophic forgetting, with KL and EWC constraints failing to prevent it. Investigates where the control loop should sit.

entry.title: ARCO: Adaptive Rubric with Co-Evolution for Multi-Step LLM-Based Agents

author.name: Zihang Tian, Jingsen Zhang, Rui Li, Xiaohe Bo, Yuanzi Li, Xu Chen

entry.summary: ARCO is an adaptive rubric co-evolution framework for multi-step LLM agents where a shared-backbone model produces per-step criteria and predicts step-level rubric-conditioned rewards, with a decomposition constraint tying step rewards to terminal outcomes. It resolves step-level credit assignment and makes the judge non-static.

entry.title: One Image is All You Need: Agentic One-Shot Image Generation via Text-Based World Models for Long-Tail Spatial Perception

author.name: Keqin Zeng, Shuting Su, Shihao Lin, Ziyue Li, Rui Zhao

entry.summary: WMGen-v1 uses text-based world models and agentic one-shot image generation to create spatially grounded synthetic data for long-tail safety-critical perception scenarios like autonomous driving and maritime surveillance. It aims to fix spatial inconsistencies in diffusion/GAN-generated scenes.

entry.title: The Token Tax of Epistemic Accuracy: Comparing RAG and Long-Context Architectures for Document-Grounded Generative AI Applications

author.name: Austin Hamilton, Ryan Singh, Michael Wise, Ibrahim Yousif, Arthur Carvalho, Zhe Shan, Mohammad Mayyas, Lora A. Cavuoto, Fadel M. Megahed

entry.summary: Compares retrieval-augmented generation against long-context prompting for document-grounded applications, framing them as regimes of epistemic access on an accuracy-cost frontier with a token tax for broader context. Quantifies the tradeoff between correctness and cost.

entry.title: PROTON: Prototype-Based Test-Time Online OOD Detection for Medical VLMs

author.name: Abhijit Das, Nichula Wasalathilaka, Yifan Lu, Adinath Dukre, Dwarikanath Mahapatra, Shadab Khan, Imran Razzak

entry.summary: PROTON is a lightweight post-hoc prototype-based test-time online OOD detection module for medical VLMs that maintains an online prototype memory in embedding space to catch covariate shifts that softmax-based scoring misses. It targets the failure of static scoring across shift types.

entry.title: The Metanym Game: A Self-Contained, Self-Consistent LLM Peer-Community Benchmark for Structural Intelligence

author.name: David Nordfors

entry.summary: The Metanym Game is a contamination-resistant, self-contained LLM benchmark where contestants create all content and rate each other in a council-of-peers, using SVD of the ratings matrix to estimate each model's competence as generator and judge without golden keys. It targets structural intelligence measurement.

entry.title: Sim2O: Efficient Offline-to-Online MARL via Joint Action Composition

author.name: Bingchang Song, Yiqin Yang

entry.summary: Sim2O is a minimalist framework for offline-to-online multi-agent reinforcement learning that treats adaptation as a compositional process, dynamically blending offline and online action proposals rather than as a monolithic joint decision. Addresses the underexplored extension of offline-to-online RL to MARL.

entry.title: AgentMeter: Evaluating Model-CLI Matching for CLI-Based Local Task-Solving Agents

author.name: Han Chi, Jiaxin Qi, Yan Cui, Baisheng Lai, Jianqiang Huang

entry.summary: AgentMeter introduces a benchmark and cost-aware metric (AMS) for evaluating model-CLI matching in command-line LLM agents, recognizing that the CLI harness mediates prompts, context, tool outputs, and stopping behavior, so the same model produces different success and cost profiles under different CLIs. It moves beyond task-success-only evaluation.

entry.title: Contrastive and Adaptive Multi-modal Masked Autoencoder for Spatial Transcriptomics

author.name: Joohyeok Kim, Taejin Jeong, Jinyeong Kim, Seong Jae Hwang

entry.summary: Proposes a contrastive and adaptive multi-modal masked autoencoder for spatial transcriptomics that treats gene expression prediction from histology as a spatial imputation problem, using a small fraction of measured gene expression as genetic anchors with a bio-saliency score. It compensates for tissue morphology's insufficient information.

entry.title: Extraction and Analysis of Multimodal Concepts in Vision Language Models through Sparse Autoencoders

author.name: Sergio Lanza, Jae Hee Lee, Stefan Wermter

entry.summary: This work uses sparse autoencoders to extract and analyze genuinely multimodal concepts in vision-language models, addressing prior approaches that treat visual and textual concepts separately. It aims for higher-quality visual concept descriptions and improved interpretability of joint representations.

entry.title: HPP: Hierarchical Programmatic Probing for Long Video Understanding by Decoupling Perception and Reasoning

author.name: Awais Rauf, Ahmed Hasssan, Greg Slabaugh

entry.summary: HPP decouples semantic perception from higher-order temporal reasoning for long-video understanding by reformulating it as iterative programmatic exploration of a hierarchically segmented video. It addresses VLMs' limited capacity to plan multi-step strategies latently within a single forward pass.

entry.title: Channel Location Constrains the Auditability of Subliminal Learning

author.name: Tamas Madl

entry.summary: Examines when subliminal learning (a student inheriting a hidden teacher trait via distillation) can be audited before training, finding the key factor is channel location rather than model identity or scale. Identifies regimes where a pre-training screen works versus where convergent vocabulary geometry makes auditing harder.

entry.title: GRINQH: Graded Input-based Quantization Hierarchy for Efficient LLM Generation

author.name: Jette Oberl\"ander, Jan Finkbeiner, Catherine M. Sch\"ofmann, Emre Neftci

entry.summary: GRINQH is a weight-only post-training quantization framework that uses activation magnitudes to dynamically assign weight channels to different precision levels, unifying quantization and sparsification for memory-bound LLM decoding. Targets edge-computing efficiency.

entry.title: Solve for the Hyperparameter, Skip the Search: Kolmogorov-Optimal Scaling Laws for Spline Regression

author.name: Yong Yi Bay, Kathleen A. Yearick

entry.summary: Shows that for spline regression the optimal resolution hyperparameter can be solved in closed form using approximation theory, basis dimension, and the PRESS identity, eliminating grid search. Connects optimal resolution to the Kolmogorov n-width.

entry.title: Discovering Latent Groups for Robust Classification

author.name: Ankur Garg, Ulrich A\"ivodji, Samira Ebrahimi Kahou, Vincent Michalski

entry.summary: Introduces neural classification trees that encode subgroup structure in a tree architecture, routing samples to easy or hard nodes and reusing routes as pseudo-labels iteratively. Aims for robustness to spurious correlations while revealing latent subgroup membership at inference.

entry.title: Enhancing Differentially Private Mechanisms via Empirical Bayes

author.name: Minwoo Kim, Junyong Park, Sungkyu Jung

entry.summary: Proposes enhancing differentially private mechanisms by applying empirical Bayes estimation to denoise the output of the simple additive Gaussian mechanism, reducing mean-squared error without altering the privacy guarantee. Offers a simple alternative to complex DP methods.

entry.title: Gradient-Free Warm-Start Library Recovery: an Amortized-Regret Separation

author.name: Jianwei Lou (RailMind Systems, Neuss, Germany)

entry.summary: Provides a provable account of gradient-free, local, online continual learning on recurring-regime streams, showing a warm-start library learner achieves much lower amortized recovery cost than a memoryless re-estimator. Proves matching lower bounds establishing a regime-recognition versus estimation decoupling.

entry.title: Fusing Backdoors, Machine Learning, and Optimization for Large-Scale Parametric Mixed-Integer Programs

author.name: El Mehdi Er Raqabi, Pascal Van Hentenryck

entry.summary: Proposes BIPC, a learning-to-optimize framework that accelerates large-scale parametric mixed-integer programs by learning backdoors, subsets of variables driving computational complexity. Targets repeatedly solved structured optimization in power, transport, and supply chains.

entry.title: LIG: Layer-wise Integrated Gradients for Within-Layer Flow Analysis in Transformers

author.name: Eight Suzuki, Hideitsu Hino, Noboru Murata

entry.summary: Proposes Layer-wise Integrated Gradients, extending integrated gradients to set-to-set maps at nonlinear module boundaries to trace token-to-token information flow within transformer layers. Offers a new interpretability tool for transformer internals.

entry.title: AdaPrivate-TS: Private Thompson Sampling for Contextual Bandits with Privacy Amplification

author.name: Mohammadreza Riyazat, Eranga Ukwatta

entry.summary: Presents AdaPrivate-TS, a differentially private contextual bandit algorithm combining Thompson Sampling with batched zCDP composition, proving privacy cost only logarithmic in T via parallel composition. Explores privacy amplification through Poisson subsampling.

entry.title: Selective Ensemble Based on Preference-Directed Multi-Objective Bandits

author.name: Lanjihong Ma, Zhen-Yu Zhang, Masashi Sugiyama, Zhi-Hua Zhou

entry.summary: Formalizes selective ensemble under partial preferences as preference-directed multi-objective bandits with a polyhedral preference cone, introducing Pareto C-optimality and a PrefUCB algorithm. Targets choosing model candidates under limited evaluation budgets and partial capability preferences.

entry.title: VegSim: A Geospatial World Model for Scenario-Conditioned Vegetation Simulation

author.name: Irene Iele, Elena Mulero Ayll\'on, Paolo Soda, Matteo Tortora

entry.summary: Presents VegSim, a geospatial world model for scenario-conditioned vegetation simulation that infers latent vegetation state from NDVI histories and propagates it under alternative weather forcing to answer counterfactual what-if questions. Goes beyond standard forecasting fixed to observed weather.

entry.title: OphthaDT: Generative Digital Twins for Forecasting Visual Acuity Trajectories in Ophthalmology

author.name: Pietro Belligoli, Nikita Makarov, Sayedali Shetab Boushehri, Fabian Schmich, Raul Rodriguez-Esteban, Michael Menden

entry.summary: Introduces OphthaDT, an LLM-based digital twin for ophthalmology that serializes longitudinal multimodal patient histories into narratives to forecast best corrected visual acuity. Achieves lowest prediction error in neovascular AMD across four Phase III trials.

entry.title: Parameterized Representations via Implicit Stochastic Modulation for High-Dimensional and High-Order Neural PDE Solvers

author.name: Zhangyong Liang, Huanhuan Gao

entry.summary: Proposes PRISM, a parameterized representation framework using implicit stochastic modulation for high-dimensional and high-order neural PDE solvers, avoiding the memory growth and variance amplification caused by naive conditional parameterization. Enables solving across varying physical parameters without retraining.

entry.title: Beyond Time Series: Spatial Reasoning for Epidemic Forecasting via Multimodal Learning

author.name: Diana Guadalupe Gomez, Chenwei Wu, Zhiyi Wang, Liyue Shen, Alexander Rodr\'iguez

entry.summary: Introduces M-SPICE, a structure-aware spatiotemporal epidemic forecasting framework integrating region-level surveillance time series with misaligned spatially localized auxiliary signals via attention-based reasoning. Captures sub-regional spatial structure obscured by treating regions as atomic units.

entry.title: Bayesian Adaptation Gym: A Benchmark for the Bayesian Low-Rank Adaptation of Multi-Modal Language Models

author.name: Colin Samplawski, Ramneet Kaur, Manoj Acharya, Anirban Roy, Adam D. Cobb

entry.summary: Introduces Bayesian Adaptation Gym, a benchmark for Bayesian low-rank adaptation of multimodal language models providing reference implementations of classic Bayesian and SOTA adaptation baselines. Aims to clarify where Bayesian LoRA methods provide meaningful calibration benefits.

entry.title: Bypassing Minimization Bias: A Shift-Invariant Variance Estimator for Off-Equilibrium Local Learning Coefficients

author.name: Yingjia Cai

entry.summary: Proposes the Shift-Invariant Variance Estimator, a variance-based probe for the Local Learning Coefficient that structurally eliminates the unknown additive loss baseline causing minimization bias during off-equilibrium training. Improves measurement of loss-landscape geometry in transient training phases.

entry.title: Enhancing LLMs for Graph Tasks via Graph-aware LoRA Generation

author.name: Junshu Sun, Wanxing Chang, Qingming Huang, Shuhui Wang

entry.summary: Proposes a weight-level information injection paradigm that adapts language models to graph tasks by generating graph-aware task-specific LoRA weight updates interacting with hidden representations. Addresses information loss in encoding whole-graph structure for LM-based graph learning.

entry.title: Distribution-Aware Robust Bilevel Optimization: Quantile-Guided Huber Updates in Two-Timescale Stochastic Approximation

author.name: Zhiyu Li, Xi Xuan, Davide Carbone

entry.summary: Proposes RQ-TTSA, a distribution-aware robust bilevel optimization framework using historical gradient buffers to estimate rolling quantiles for adaptive Huber-style clipping under heavy-tailed noise. Provides convergence analysis under nonconvex-strongly-convex assumptions with infinite-variance gradients.

entry.title: RLM-Cascade: Response-Level Speculative Decoding for Cost-Efficient LLM API Serving

author.name: Haifeng Wu, Srinivasan Manoharan, Fangbo Tu, Junhua Zhao, Jian Wan

entry.summary: Presents RLM-Cascade, a proxy-layer system applying response-level speculative decoding to cut LLM API costs without model access or shared vocabulary, using a fast draft model and complexity router. Reports 45.8% cost reduction and 1.83x latency speedup on agentic coding workloads.

entry.title: Position: Correct Answer, Wrong Mechanism -- When AI Scientists Defend General Claims Their Own Data Contradicts

author.name: Steven Young Eulig

entry.summary: Position paper arguing that AI scientist systems should be evaluated on mechanism fidelity and epistemic honesty, not just final answers, documenting Correct Answer Wrong Mechanism cases where agents reach right results via flawed reasoning. Based on 28 episodes of a coding agent in particle physics simulations.

entry.title: Convergence of Gradient Descent for General Neural Network Architectures Beyond the NTK Regime

author.name: Yuqing Wang

entry.summary: Proposes a convergence framework for gradient descent dynamics across a broad family of modern architectures including pre-normalized multi-layer transformers, beyond the NTK regime. Proves GD converges to a neighborhood of a stationary point for almost all initializations under mild assumptions.

entry.title: Muown Implicitly Performs Angular Step-size Decay

author.name: Florian H\"ubler, Kai Lion, Antonio Orvieto, Niao He

entry.summary: Shows that the directional update of the Muown optimizer is equivalent to a Riemannian step on normalized directions, with magnitude only modulating angular step size. Proposes AngularMuown, which optimizes directly over normalized directions with a schedulable angular multiplier.

entry.title: Equilibrium with Internal Transfers

author.name: Mingyang Liu, Gabriele Farina, Asuman Ozdaglar

entry.summary: Introduces Self-Enforcing Transfer Equilibrium (SETE), where players commit to conditional budget-balanced peer transfers to improve incentives, showing socially optimal profiles can be sustained in polymatrix games. Bridges mechanism design and equilibrium computation.

entry.title: Central limit theorem for the averaged Adam optimizer

author.name: Steffen Dereich, Arnulf Jentzen

entry.summary: Provides a central limit theorem for the averaged Adam optimizer, quantifying its n^{-1/2} convergence speed to an attracting zero and characterizing the limiting covariance. Rigorous optimization theory from established authors (Jentzen).

entry.title: Sublinearly Structured Deep Neural Networks Achieve Feature Learning Consistency for Compositional Functions

author.name: Sehwan Kim, Yan Sun, Faming Liang

entry.summary: This paper establishes feature-learning and prediction consistency guarantees for sublinearly structured deep neural networks learning hierarchically compositional target functions, where dimensions and neurons grow sublinearly with sample size. It provides positive statistical theory for a broad DNN subclass.

entry.title: Concordia: JIT-Compiled Persistent-Kernel Checkpointing for Fault-Tolerant LLM Inference

author.name: Yuhang Gan, Yiwei Yang, Yuyi Li, Xiangyu Gao, Yichen Wang, Rain Jiang, Xiaoning Ding, Andi Quinn, Chen Qian

entry.summary: Concordia is a JIT-compiled persistent-kernel checkpointing runtime for fault-tolerant LLM inference that preserves GPU-resident state like KV caches and schedulers, running checkpoint hooks at device synchronization points without putting the host CPU on the critical path. It enables recovery without restarting the whole serving stack or adding per-component checkpoint logic.

entry.title: Phonemes to the Rescue: Multilingual Tokenization Based on International Phonetic Alphabet

author.name: Milan Mileti\'c, Julie Kallini, Ekaterina Shutova

entry.summary: This paper proposes using the International Phonetic Alphabet as a language-agnostic input representation for multilingual tokenizers, offering a compact symbol inventory, greater cross-lingual overlap, and balanced byte-per-character distribution. It trains matched text vs IPA tokenizers across 24 languages and 14 scripts to reduce performance disparities.

entry.title: A Validation-Gated Mechanistic Account of Suicidality Detection in LLMs

author.name: Nafiz Ahmed, Sarah Sharif, Dingjing Shi, Mike Banad

entry.summary: This paper presents a validation-gated mechanistic framework for studying suicidality detection in LLMs, admitting an internal concept as causally relevant only after the model is shown to outperform a lexical baseline and testing each property against matched controls. It yields disciplined positive and negative interpretability results in a sensitive mental-health domain.

entry.title: When Compression Helps and When It Hurts: Condition-Aware Analysis of Chain-of-Thought Distillation

author.name: Siyang Lyu, Zhijing Sun, Xinghao Chen, Tong Liu, Dawei Zhu, Xiaoyu Shen

entry.summary: Provides a condition-aware analysis of chain-of-thought distillation, disentangling importance criterion, restructuring level, and compression budget across model families, domains, and CoT regimes. Identifies when compression helps versus hurts reasoning transfer.

entry.title: OpenBioRQ: Unsolved Biomedical Research Questions for Agents

author.name: Minbyul Jeong

entry.summary: Introduces OpenBioRQ, a benchmark of 12,553 unsolved biomedical research questions treating open questions as a faithfulness-and-abstention probe. Finds agentic models rarely fabricate citations (>99% resolve) but ~15.9% cite the wrong paper supporting the claim.

entry.title: Understanding Knowledge Distillation in Post-Training: When It Helps and When It Fails

author.name: Xin Liu, Simin Ma, Shujian Liu, Song Wang, Sathish Reddy Indurthi, Haoyun Deng, Lu Wang, Kaiqiang Song

entry.summary: Systematically studies knowledge distillation in post-training using the large-scale Tulu 3 dataset, finding KD beats SFT in low-data regimes but its advantage diminishes with more data. Examines when distilling general instruction-following helps versus fails.

entry.title: Look Before You Zoom: Adaptive Routing for the Resolution-Context Trade-off in Visual RAG

author.name: Oanh N. Tran, Thanh Quoc Hung Le, Oscar Chew, Kuan-Hao Huang, Khoa D. Doan

entry.summary: Presents ViRGo, a lightweight adaptive routing framework for visual RAG that selects between patch-based zooming, attention retrieval, or global perception based on the resolution-context trade-off. Addresses VLM failures on small objects without harming large ones.

entry.title: Mirage: a Clean-Label Backdoor against LiDAR 3D Object Detection

author.name: Ziba Parsons, Ang Li

entry.summary: Presents Mirage, a black-box clean-label backdoor attack against LiDAR 3D object detection that injects label-consistent poisoned samples to associate a trigger with a target class. Demonstrates stealthy training-time vulnerability in autonomous perception.

entry.title: ChronoLock: Protecting Videos from Unauthorized Text-to-Video Personalization

author.name: Jiaming He, Jiashu Zhang, Guanyu Hou, Shuhan Ye, Hanwei Zhu, Yi Yu, Xudong Jiang

entry.summary: Introduces ChronoLock, the first proactive protective perturbation framework targeting temporal denoising dynamics to prevent unauthorized text-to-video personalization. Addresses video data-misuse risks beyond static-appearance protections.

entry.title: BadDreamer: Transferable Backdoor Attacks against Video World Models for Autonomous Driving

author.name: Zhe Shuai, Xiaopeng Xie, Yikun Zeng

entry.summary: Presents BadDreamer, a transferable spatio-temporal backdoor attack against video world models in autonomous driving that poisons learned future dynamics rather than labels or actions. Exposes underexplored training-time security risks in perception-to-action pipelines.

entry.title: A Neurosymbolic Framework for Interpretable Skeleton-Based Seizure Detection via Concept-Driven Logical Reasoning

author.name: Talha Ilyas, Deval Mehta, Zongyuan Ge

entry.summary: Presents the first neurosymbolic framework for interpretable video-based seizure detection, extracting skeleton sequences, predicting clinically-grounded concept activations, and composing them via differentiable logical reasoning. Targets clinical adoption through interpretability.

entry.title: Feed-forward Motion In-betweening for Any 4D

author.name: Hiroki Nishizawa, Hubert P. H. Shum, Yoshihiro Fukuhara, Hirokatsu Kataoka, Shigeo Morishima

entry.summary: Proposes a feed-forward motion in-betweening framework for arbitrary 4D meshes with keyframe conditioning, built on universal mesh-animation latents to enable fast long-horizon generation. Addresses scarcity of long 4D data and error accumulation in autoregressive generation.

entry.title: Improving Reasoning in Vision-Language Models via Perception Verified Self-Training

author.name: Sourabh Sharma, Sonam Gupta, Sadbhawna Thakur

entry.summary: Proposes perception-verified self-training for vision-language models, filtering chain-of-thought rationales not just by answer correctness but by verifying visual perception to combat hallucinations and language shortcuts. Aims to improve VLM reasoning without costly human annotation.

entry.title: CVSBench: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Cross-view Spatial Reasoning and Dreaming

author.name: Ruixun Liu, Lingyu Zhang, Lanxuan Xue, Kaiyu Li, Bowen Fu, Xiangyong Cao

entry.summary: Introduces CVSBench, a large-scale benchmark for cross-view spatial reasoning using satellite-street image pairs, supporting cross-view VQA, grounding, and viewpoint identification with ~40,000 QA pairs. Evaluates whether VLMs possess human-like cross-view spatial abilities.

entry.title: Projection-Volume Fidelity Divergence: Diagnosing and Controlling Optimization Drift in Sparse-View 3D Gaussian Tomography

author.name: Yikuang Yuluo, Ao Wang, Shen Kuan, Yujie Liu, Wang Liao, Ying Chen, Shuangyang Zhong, Yixing Huang, Fuquan Wang

entry.summary: Identifies Projection-Volume Fidelity Divergence in sparse-view 3D Gaussian tomography, where rendered projections improve while reconstructed volume deteriorates due to anisotropic Gaussian deformation. Introduces geometry- and volume-level diagnostics to characterize and control this drift.

entry.title: OmniSpace: Efficient Geometry Awareness for Autonomous Vehicles MLLMs

author.name: Hao Vo, Phu Loc Nguyen, Khoa Vo, Sieu Tran, Duc Minh Nguyen, Ngo Xuan Cuong, Nghi D. Q. Bui, Anh Nguyen, Duy Minh Ho Nguyen, Ngan Le

entry.summary: Proposes OmniSpace, a plug-and-play paradigm giving autonomous-vehicle multimodal LLMs geometry-aware spatial reasoning from purely 2D observations, without auxiliary 3D models at inference. Introduces a Camera Pose Injector, Multi-view Epipolar Attention, and 3D geometric components.

entry.title: RaysUp: Ultra-light Universal Feature Upsampling via Geometry-Aware Ray Representation

author.name: Yuchuan Ding, Linfei Li, Lin Zhang, Ying Shen

entry.summary: Proposes RaysUp, an ultra-lightweight, task- and VFM-agnostic feature upsampling framework that reconstructs high-resolution feature maps at arbitrary resolutions using a geometry-aware ray representation. Avoids degrading semantic fidelity or requiring VFM-specific retraining.

entry.title: Visual Geometry Transformer in the Wild: Distractor-Free 3D Reconstruction

author.name: Tianbo Pan, Xingyi Yang, Shizun Wang, Xinchao Wang

entry.summary: Proposes VGTW, an end-to-end framework for distractor-free 3D reconstruction from inconsistent in-the-wild views, isolating and suppressing distractor-affected regions via a distractor-aware training strategy. Addresses failure of static-assumption methods under transient occlusions.

entry.title: Compression and Retrieval: Implicit Memory Retrieval for Video World Models

author.name: Zhan Peng, Jie Ma, Huiqiang Sun, Chong Gao, Zhijie Xue, Zhiyu Pan, Zhiguo Cao, Jun Liang, Jing Li

entry.summary: Proposes CaR (Compression and Retrieval), an attention-driven implicit memory retrieval mechanism for video world models that injects viewpoint information via positional encoding to maintain long-term consistency across camera trajectories. Avoids costly context scaling and rigid heuristic retrieval.

entry.title: Safe Few-Step Generation via Velocity Editing

author.name: Yujin Choi, Jaehong Yoon

entry.summary: Proposes safe few-step text-to-image generation via velocity editing in flow-matching models, adapting concept removal and safety methods that previously relied on iterative trajectory steering or CLIP-based prompt manipulation. Addresses the bottleneck that limited sampling steps pose for safety.

entry.title: A scalar per patch from pre-trained ViTs enables fast moving navigation in the real world

author.name: Steeven Janny, Leonid Antsfeld, Christian Wolf

entry.summary: Reports a large-scale real-world study (966 episodes, 24km) evaluating which pretrained ViT visual-encoder components matter for fast real-world navigation, proposing a scalar-per-patch representation. Examines pretraining auxiliary losses as a defining factor.

entry.title: Scalable Multi-Task Data Generation via Reinforcement Learning for Language-Conditioned Bimanual Dexterous Manipulation

author.name: Zechu Li, Yufeng Jin, Puze Liu, Jan Peters, Georgia Chalvatzaki

entry.summary: Proposes an RL-based pipeline for scalable synthetic data generation for language-conditioned bimanual dexterous manipulation, overcoming morphology mismatch and the limited task diversity of teleoperation-based methods. It integrates generative components to broaden task coverage without handcrafted rewards.

entry.title: IOI: Decoupling Kinematics and Physics for Interactive World Models

author.name: Chengyu Bai, Peidong Jia, Tiecheng Guo, Yukai Wang, Rui Ma, Fangyuan Zhao, Chunkai Fan, Xiaobao Wei, Jintao Chen, Hao Wang, Ying Li, Xiaozhu Ju, Jian Tang, Shanghang Zhang

entry.summary: IOI is a hybrid interactive world model that decouples kinematics from physics, injecting analytical forward-kinematic priors for accurate action-conditioned motion while learning physical dynamics, to reduce spatiotemporal drift in purely data-driven models. It targets visually realistic, controllable embodied environments for agent training.

entry.title: dVLA-RL: Reinforcement Learning over Denoising Trajectories for Discrete Diffusion Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Yuhao Wu, Yitian Liu, Weijie Shen, Mishuo Han, Wenjie Xu, Haotian Liang, Zhongshan Liu, Yinan Mao, Lei Xu, Xinping Guan, Ru Ying, Ran Zheng, Wei Sui, Xiaokang Yang, Wenbo Ding, Yao Mu

entry.summary: dVLA-RL applies reinforcement learning over denoising trajectories to discrete diffusion VLA models, which previously were limited to supervised fine-tuning, treating the masked generative denoising steps as the policy refinement target. It seeks to unlock further policy improvement for unified discrete vision-language-action token spaces.

entry.title: Darwin Mobile Agent: A Roadmap for Self-Evolution

author.name: Daniel Beechey, Derek Yuen, Jianheng Liu, Dezhao Luo, Tiantian He, Weilin Luo, Jun Wang, Kun Shao

entry.summary: Darwin Mobile Agent proposes open-source infrastructure for autonomous reinforcement learning of mobile GUI agents, framing the mobile interface as a complex world for emergent intelligence following the Bitter Lesson. It addresses the data-collection bottleneck via asynchronous agents.

entry.title: Hypothesis-Disciplined Multi-Agent Automated Formalization of Asymptotic Statistical Theory

author.name: Tingzhou Wei, Zeyu Zheng, Ethan X. Fang, Junwei Lu

entry.summary: Proposes a multi-agent Lean 4 formalization pipeline with seven specialist roles and a hypothesis-disciplined audit to formalize asymptotic statistical theory. It addresses the large gap between asymptotic statistics and existing formal-proof infrastructure.

entry.title: From Knowing to Acting: Benchmarking Self-Awareness Capability of LLM Agents

author.name: Yifan Li, Shengbin Yue, Boyu Feng, Jinhu Qi, Bo Ke, Zixing Song, Hongru Wang, Zhongyu Wei, Irwin King

entry.summary: KAPRO introduces a benchmark and framework evaluating LLM agents' self-awareness, namely whether they correctly judge if a task needs external tools or internal knowledge, decoupling metacognitive judgment from execution. KAware partitions tasks into external, internal, and hybrid subspaces.

entry.title: Escape from Delusional Echo Trap: Symmetry Breaking, Stochastic Dynamics and Mathematical Mitigation Strategies for Algorithmic Sycophancy

author.name: Sayantari Ghosh, Saumik Bhattacharya, Partha Pratim Chakrabarti

entry.summary: Develops a mathematical framework using dynamical systems and stochastic differential equations to model how users' beliefs evolve into delusional spirals when interacting with sycophantic AI chatbots. Proposes mitigation strategies via symmetry breaking and stochastic dynamics.

entry.title: Repeated post-training is not Self-improving: Diagnosing Scientific Amnesia in Continual DPO Pipelines

author.name: Jianzhe Lin, Fei Wang, Xiaolin Li, Rajeshkumar Golani, Jubin Chheda

entry.summary: Diagnoses scientific amnesia in continual DPO pipelines, where repeated preference-data training preserves learned behaviors but fails to accumulate reusable methodological knowledge for future campaigns. Contributes a diagnostic suite, a checkpoint-chaining pipeline, and a 30-campaign benchmark.

entry.title: AutoRAS: Learning Robust Agentic Systems with Primitive Representations

author.name: Yang Yue, Xuancheng Zhu, Yuyang Ma, Guoshun Nan, Zihan Dou, Jingru Shan, Congyu Guo, Ji Zhang, Hua Wang, Jingfeng Zhang

entry.summary: AutoRAS automates the design of robust agentic systems by generating sequences of symbolic primitives encoding structural connectivity and behavioral actions, optimized with execution-derived safety signals and flow-based objectives. It treats robustness as a first-class design goal against adversaries and internal failures.

entry.title: Holmes: Multimodal Agentic Diagnosis for Mixed-Language Mobile Crashes at Industrial Scale

author.name: Jia Li, Wenyuan Ma, Ting Peng, Haibin Zheng, Yuetang Deng

entry.summary: Holmes is an industrial multi-agent system that performs root-cause analysis of mixed-language mobile crashes from post-mortem signals (stack traces, logs, registers, assembly) without reproducing failures, using a hierarchical retrieve-explore-reason architecture. It targets ultra-large-scale deployment.

entry.title: When Does a Video-Language Model Stop Watching? Reward Strength Controls the Formation and Reversal of Visual Shortcuts in Multimodal RLVR

author.name: Zekun Xu

entry.summary: This study treats a grounding-penalty strength as a control knob to characterize how video-language models develop visual shortcuts (ignoring video and exploiting language priors) under verifiable-reward RL, finding a sharp shortcut onset and conditions under which intervention can reverse it. It illuminates perception bypass dynamics in multimodal RLVR.

entry.title: ARIA: A Causal-Aware Framework for Rescuing LLM Reasoning in Trustworthy Materials Discovery

author.name: Yi Cao, Liaoyaqi Wang, Jieneng Chen, Benjamin Van Durme, Alan Yuille, Paulette Clancy

entry.summary: ARIA is a causal-aware framework for LLM materials discovery that diagnoses contextual tunneling, where models over-anchor on narrow retrieved evidence and suppress global physics reasoning, and routes queries through a cascade based on the completeness of process-structure-property evidence chains. It aims for physically consistent generation.

entry.title: A Differentiable Atari VCS:A Complex, Fully Known Ground Truth for Explainable AI

author.name: Andreas Maier, Siming Bayer, Patrick Krauss

entry.summary: The authors reimplement a differentiable, fully specified Atari 2600 VCS to create a study object that is both genuinely complex and has known inner functioning, removing the usual dichotomy in explainable AI between trivial-but-known and complex-but-opaque systems. It provides ground truth for XAI evaluation.

entry.title: Co-Construction Blindness and Asymmetric Epistemic Vulnerability in Human-LLM Interaction

author.name: Bianca Helena Ximenes

entry.summary: Introduces two conceptual constructs - co-construction blindness and asymmetric epistemic vulnerability - to describe how LLM outputs are co-constructed artifacts shaped by user inputs rather than independent assessments, with consequences scaling by user authority. It critiques deployment disclaimers that frame users as external auditors.

entry.title: Robusto-2: Benchmarking Humans & VLMs for Autonomous Driving in Lima & New York City

author.name: Adrian Cespedes, Marcelo Chincha, Dunant Cusipuma, Victor Flores-Benites, David Ortega, Arturo Deza

entry.summary: Robusto-2 benchmarks human drivers from Lima and New York City against VLMs on dashcam VQA to study out-of-distribution generalization for autonomous driving in challenging, unserved geographies. Provides a full factorial human-VLM comparison.

entry.title: MoECodec: Image Compression for joint human and machine perception via Mixture-of-Experts

author.name: Jiancheng Zhao, Xiang Ji, Yifan Zhan, Zunian Wan, Yinqiang Zheng

entry.summary: MoECodec is a token-aware image compression framework using Mixture-of-Experts to replace FFN layers, serving multiple downstream machine-perception tasks within a single model while adapting computation to region semantic importance. It addresses the static computation limitation of prior codecs.

entry.title: Backdoor Attacks on Speech Emotion Recognition via TTS-Generated Poisoning

author.name: Yongbin Huang, Xihao Xie, Jia Zhang

entry.summary: Presents the first systematic study of TTS-generated poisoning backdoor attacks on speech emotion recognition systems, introducing a stealthy low-energy acoustic trigger embeddable in natural and synthetic speech. Achieves high attack success at low poisoning ratios while preserving benign performance.

entry.title: TF-SNO: Time-Frequency Gated Spectral Neural Operators for Learning Non-Stationary Partial Differential Equations

author.name: Yitian Zhou, Chaoning Zhang, Zhenzhen Huang, Haoxuan Yu, Jiaquan Zhang, Yiran Li, Fan Mo, Kuien Liu, Jie Zou, Caiyan Qin, Yang Yang

entry.summary: TF-SNO is a spectral neural operator with learnable time-frequency gating that adapts the spectral response to evolving dynamics in non-stationary PDEs. It addresses the mismatch caused by applying a shared spectral response across rollout stages in standard spectral operators.

entry.title: DataClaw0: Agentic Tailoring Multimodal Data from Raw Streams

author.name: Cong Wan, Zeyu Guo, Zijian Cai, Jiangyang Li, SongLin Dong, Lin Peng, Xiangyang Luo, Zhiheng Ma, Yihong Gong

entry.summary: DataClaw0 proposes Agentic Data Tailoring, treating multimodal data processing as a learnable capability that actively refines and structures raw streams to match downstream intents. It uses a two-stage pipeline grounding generative semantic synthesis in deterministic factual anchors to overcome training-data scarcity.

entry.title: Denoising Iterative Self-Correction: Structured Verification Loops for Reliable LLM Reasoning

author.name: Shen Yin, David Ken, Joel Stremmel

entry.summary: DISC is a test-time self-correction procedure that treats verification outputs as noisy measurements of where a solution is corrupted, iteratively reducing errors across verify-judge-correct passes. A binary judgment gate blocks rewrites that would damage already-correct answers.

entry.title: THREAD: Trajectory Planning for Hybrid Rigid-Soft Manipulators with Environment-Aware Diffusion

author.name: Shivani Kamtikar, Pranav Asthana, Naveen Kumar Uppalapati, Girish Krishnan, Girish Chowdhary

entry.summary: THREAD is a diffusion-based trajectory planner for hybrid rigid-soft manipulators navigating confined environments, learning a generative prior over physically realizable backbone trajectories conditioned on local geometry. It addresses how free-space backbone shapes become infeasible under contact and the kinematic coupling of rigid and soft segments.

entry.title: CNnotator: LLM-Guided Memory Safety Annotation Synthesis

author.name: Twain Byrnes, Mike Dodds

entry.summary: CNnotator uses LLMs to automatically synthesize memory-usage annotations as CN specifications for legacy C code, aiding migration to safer languages and detection of memory errors. It targets patterns that are tedious rather than truly difficult for humans to derive.

entry.title: UniRank: Unified Rank Allocation for Low-Rank LLM Compression

author.name: Chao Han, Haozhe Hu, Fei Ma, Wei Zhang, Xiaoyu Shen

entry.summary: UniRank formulates global low-rank allocation for LLM compression as a sorting-and-truncation pipeline, scoring singular components via local singular energy ratio and global input-output cosine similarity. It avoids both manual rules and heavy learning-based allocation overhead.

entry.title: Cohort-Anchored Foundation Models for Electronic Health Records: From Risk Scores to Auditable Peer Cohorts

author.name: Kaiping Zheng

entry.summary: CAFM is a Cohort-Anchored Foundation Model framework for EHRs that elevates patient cohorts to a first-class object across the learning pipeline, treating patient comparison as primary clinical evidence rather than an emergent property. It aims to improve interpretability, robustness to distribution shift, and alignment with clinician reasoning.

entry.title: Rebuttals Move Peer-Review Scores, but Initial-Review Structure Bounds the Movement

author.name: Mathieu Louis, Tibo Vanleke, Vincent Ginis, Andres Algaba

entry.summary: Studies how author rebuttals move reviewer scores using 73k ICLR 2024-2025 reviewer trajectories, using LLMs only as measurement instruments to estimate pre-rebuttal implied scores. Finds initial-review text-score offset bounds and predicts post-rebuttal movement.

entry.title: MultiMem: Measuring and Mitigating Memorization in Multi-Modal Contrastive Learninga

author.name: Wenhao Wang, Franziska Boenisch, Michael Backes, Adam Dziedzic

entry.summary: Introduces MultiMem, described as the first metric to quantify memorization in multi-modal contrastive learning, and analyzes its drivers. Finds cross-modal semantic misalignment most strongly influences memorization, with text being the dominant modality.

entry.title: BabelJudge: Measuring LLM-as-a-Judge Reliability Across Languages and Agent Trajectories

author.name: Shreyas KC

entry.summary: Introduces BabelJudge, an open-source benchmark and audit framework measuring four LLM-as-a-judge failure modes (position bias, verbosity bias, order inconsistency, cross-lingual degradation) without human preference labels via gold-labelling by controlled degradation. Reveals systematic biases hidden by raw accuracy.

entry.title: P-JEPA: Procedural Video Representation Learning via Joint Embedding Predictive Architecture

author.name: Felix Tristram, Stefano Gasperini, Benjamin Killeen, Marcel Walch, Christian Benz, Nassir Navab, Ghazal Ghazaei

entry.summary: P-JEPA applies joint-embedding predictive architecture to procedural video learning, addressing long-range dependencies in multi-step tasks where actions look similar but differ contextually. Aims to support embodied AI assistance systems.

entry.title: Rethinking Object-Centric Representations for Video Dynamics Modeling

author.name: Amaury Wei, Ismail Nejjar, Olga Fink

entry.summary: Rethinks object-centric slot representations for video dynamics, showing that temporal consistency objectives conflict with motion and cause slots to lock onto static background. Proposes a method to disentangle appearance from pose for better tracking.

entry.title: ELADO: Elliptic PDE Assessment Datasets for Operator Learning

author.name: Frank Ehebrecht, Toni Scharle, Martin Atzmueller

entry.summary: ELADO is a benchmark suite of elliptic PDE problems (Poisson, Helmholtz with non-constant coefficients) designed to expose and quantify failure modes of neural operator architectures. Uses controllable data generation to isolate distinct difficulty sources like heavy-tailed solutions.

entry.title: Distinguishing indistinguishable attractors: Unsupervised anomaly detection with reservoir computers

author.name: Davide Prosperino, Haochun Ma, Christoph R\"ath

entry.summary: Shows that a simple Kolmogorov-Smirnov test on reservoir computer output weights can detect regime changes in nonlinear dynamical systems invisible to classical and deep-learning detectors. Offers an unsupervised anomaly detection approach grounded in dynamical systems theory.

entry.title: Expressivity Saturation: Reduced Affine Region Usage Under Increasing Task Complexity

author.name: Xuan Qi, Yi Wei, Fanqi Yu, Manuel Lecha

entry.summary: Studies expressivity saturation, showing that piecewise-affine networks realize fewer affine regions than their theoretical capacity, with a rigorous upper bound for affine line-segment probes. Examines the gap between theoretical and trained expressive capacity under increasing task complexity.

entry.title: Clipping the Price of Adaptivity at the Tail

author.name: Itai Kreisler, Yair Carmon, Oliver Hinder

entry.summary: Circumvents the price-of-adaptivity barrier in stochastic convex optimization by assuming model-loss decomposition and clipping model outputs in tail events relative to a reference model. Achieves improved adaptation bounds.

entry.title: FlowTrain: Flow-Based Decoupled Training for Industrial-Grade Vision-Language Models

author.name: Zhida Jiang, Zhaolong Xing, Yang Pei, Xiaolong Chen, Yuanhang Xiao, Chengzhi Huang, Xiyu Liu, Haopeng Liu, Qingyuan Sang, Lingfeng Zhou, Jiaxing Wang, Zicheng Zhang, Wenzhe Wang, Xinyu Liu, Yan Li, Zhen Chen, Ke Zhang

entry.summary: Presents FlowTrain, a flow-based decoupled training framework for vision-language models using a producer-consumer dataflow over a unified memory pool, letting encoder and backbone progress independently. Improves industrial-scale VLM training efficiency.

entry.title: Quantifying the Agreement Between Data-Influence and Data-Similarity to Understand LLM Behavior

author.name: Christopher J. Anders, Henrique Da Silva Gameiro, Nico Daheim, Mohammad Emtiyaz Khan

entry.summary: Quantifies the agreement between data-influence and data-similarity measures for tracing LLM outputs back to training data by ranking documents and computing overlap. Finds the rankings agree significantly but with an asymmetry between top documents of each measure.

entry.title: On the Limits of Prompt-Conditioned Language Models as General-Purpose Learners

author.name: David Mguni, Julian Ma, Jun Wang

entry.summary: Argues that prompt-conditioned LLMs face a fundamental expressivity floor because language is a capacity-limited interface for conveying tasks, modeling user-system interaction as a bilevel cheap-talk game. Derives PAC-Bayes bounds separating estimation error from irreducible structural limitations.

entry.title: VeriBound: PAC-Bayesian Generalization Bounds for Process Reward Models Trained with Formal Verification Tools

author.name: Amirul Rahman, Mohammed Sabih Alsharari

entry.summary: Proposes VeriBound, a PAC-Bayesian theoretical framework providing generalization bounds for Process Reward Models trained on formal-verification-tool labels (FOVER-style). Explains the empirically observed cross-task generalization from symbolic tasks to reasoning benchmarks.

entry.title: ASCII Art Turns LLMs into VLA Controllers

author.name: Yitao Jiang, Roy Xing, Luyang Zhao, Brian Plancher, Muhao Chen, Devin Balkcom

entry.summary: Shows that a text-only LLM can be adapted into a vision-language-action controller by rendering visual observations as ASCII text, enabling existing LLM training stacks to condition on visual state. Compares fine-tuned LLMs and VLMs across families and scales.

entry.title: Spectrally Safe Neural Operator Warm-Starts for Large-Scale Newton Solvers

author.name: Jaemin Oh, Youngkyu Lee, Jerome Darbon, George Em Karniadakis

entry.summary: Shows that neural operators used to warm-start Newton solvers can produce initial states with indefinite Jacobians despite low average test error, because mean-squared error misses localized physics violations. Diagnoses this for hyperelasticity via predicted volume change dispersion.

entry.title: Any-Body Guard: Universal Safeguarding for Manipulation Policies via Action Masking

author.name: Alex Beaudin, Hanna Krasowski, Kartik Nagpal, Sanjit A. Seshia, Murat Arcak, Negar Mehr

entry.summary: X-Safe proposes a universal action-masking safeguard for robotic manipulation that reasons in configuration space to give formal probabilistic collision-avoidance guarantees that transfer across embodiments. It aims to replace heuristic fallback controllers with a lightweight, transferable safety layer.

entry.title: Chains That See, Answers That Don't: A Multi-Aspect Evaluation Recipe for Forced Chain-of-Thought on Video-MME

author.name: Zhichao Fan, Yanhang Li, Zexin Zhuang

entry.summary: This paper proposes a three-probe evaluation recipe to test whether forced chain-of-thought improves video question answering, applying it to Qwen2.5-VL on Video-MME with counterfactual video-swaps and visual-degradation ladders. It finds CoT chains are video-conditioned yet do not necessarily improve final answers.

entry.title: Incremental Learning in Mirror Flows

author.name: Rapha\"el Berthier, Loucas Pillaud-Vivien

entry.summary: This paper studies mirror flows under a convex quadratic loss and general convex mirror potentials, showing that initialization near the domain boundary yields rescaled trajectories converging to a limiting flow whose potential is the domain indicator. This characterization provides a general mechanism for incremental learning in mirror flows.

entry.title: Storyline Trees: Hierarchical Representations for Long-Form Narratives

author.name: Litu Ou, Mirella Lapata

entry.summary: This work constructs storyline trees, hierarchical representations organizing long-form narratives from global themes to fine-grained events, built via complementary top-down and bottom-up procedures over scene segments. It aims to make implicit narrative structure navigable for long-context models.

entry.title: When to Plan, When to Polish: Noise Level as a Granularity Axis for Diffusion Language Models

author.name: Peihong Li, Yuanjie Shi, Yan Yan

entry.summary: Proposes Noise Dependent Granularity Control for diffusion language models, using noise level as a granularity cue so high-noise steps use coherent token groups for planning while low-noise refines wording. Avoids extra planners or two-stage designs.

entry.title: Beyond Value Benchmarks: Measuring Value-Structure Alignment in Large Language Models via Symmetric Q-Sorts

author.name: Jingting Zheng (TJUNLP Lab, School of Computer Science, Technology, Tianjin University, Tianjin, China), Yuqi Ren (TJUNLP Lab, School of Computer Science, Technology, Tianjin University, Tianjin, China), Linhao Yu (TJUNLP Lab, School of Computer Science, Technology, Tianjin University, Tianjin, China), Yongqi Leng (TJUNLP Lab, School of Computer Science, Technology, Tianjin University, Tianjin, China), Deyi Xiong (TJUNLP Lab, School of Computer Science, Technology, Tianjin University, Tianjin, China)

entry.summary: Proposes a symmetric Q-methodology framework where humans and LLMs sort 140 moral statements into a forced distribution to measure value-structure alignment as a cohesive system. Establishes a three-factor human reference geometry to compare against model rankings.

entry.title: Knowledge-Graph Grounding Helps LLMs Only for Out-of-Training Knowledge: A Controlled Study on Clinical Question Answering

author.name: Madhulatha Mandarapu, Sandeep Kunkunuru

entry.summary: Reproduces a Nature Medicine finding that frontier LLMs beat specialized retrieval tools, flagging a grader bug, and shows knowledge-graph grounding only helps for out-of-training knowledge in clinical QA. Establishes a knowledge-boundary result for when grounding adds value.

entry.title: Same question, different history: language, national identity, and credit in large language models

author.name: William Guey, Pierrick Bougault, Wei Zhang, Vitor D. de Moura, Jos\'e O. Gomes

entry.summary: Analyzes 11 LLMs across 21 disputed inventions in 12 languages (75,896 responses), showing query language systematically affects which claimant is surfaced. Lower-status claimants appear more when asked in their associated language while Anglophone figures stay stable.

entry.title: Towards Root Memories: Benchmarking and Enhancing Implicit Logical Memory Retrieval for Personalized LLMs

author.name: Hongxun Ding, Xiang Yu, Chengbing Wang, Jianfei Xiao, Keqin Bao, Wenjie Wang, Xiangnan He

entry.summary: Constructs IMLogic, the first benchmark for implicit logical memory retrieval in long dialogues where logically critical memories have limited semantic overlap. Introduces root memory, a structured decision-preserving representation, and RootMem to distill reusable personalized logic.

entry.title: Can LLMs Reliably Self-Report Adversarial Prefills, and How?

author.name: Quang Minh Nguyen, Uzair Ahmed, Taegyoon Kim

entry.summary: Introduces EnterpriseClawBench, built from 852 reproducible tasks derived from real proprietary workplace agent sessions with recovered fixtures, role classes, and semantic rubrics. The best configuration (Codex with GPT-5.5) reaches only 0.663, highlighting headroom; data not released for privacy.

entry.title: Cross-National Information Attacks: A Two-Decade Analysis of Troll Behavior in Korea

author.name: Jaehong Kim, Hyeonseung Kim, Jiseon Kim, Alice Oh, Thorsten Holz, Wonjae Lee, Meeyoung Cha

entry.summary: Develops an explainable ML framework for detecting state-linked troll activity in Korean news comments along foreign origin, moral-emotional framing, and target country dimensions. Applied to 112M comments over two decades for longitudinal influence analysis.

entry.title: CogniRoute: Learning to Route Social Evidence in Omni-Modal Models

author.name: Yifan Shen, Pei Tian, Xinzhuo Li, Bowen Fang, Shujun Xia, Bingxuan Li, Ana Jojic, Wenming Ye, Xu Cao, James Matthew Rehg, Ismini Lourentzou

entry.summary: Introduces CogniRoute, a schema-guided Mixture-of-Experts framework for social omni-modal reasoning that routes evidence by cross-modal relation, reasoning demand, and temporal scope. Adds route-aware reinforcement learning for social video QA.

entry.title: SARIF: Segment Anything for Robust Image Forensics

author.name: Dong-Hyun Moon, Ju-Hyeon Nam, Sang-Chul Lee

entry.summary: Proposes SARIF, leveraging the Segment Anything Model with a feedback-guided mask decoder and dual-encoder for robust image forgery localization. Improves cross-domain generalization over benchmark-tuned forensics models.

entry.title: RAPID: A Reproducible Multi-Agent Pipeline for Interpretable Disaster Damage Assessment from Satellite and Street-View Imagery

author.name: Yifan Yang, Wenjing Gong, Kaili Zhang, Lei Zou, Zhengzhong Tu, Hao Li, Zongrong Li, Xinyue Ye

entry.summary: Presents RAPID, a reproducible multi-agent pipeline combining satellite and street-view imagery for interpretable disaster damage assessment, addressing generalization under domain shift and long-tailed distributions. It performs damage-level, damage-type, and reasoning-based assessment.

entry.title: Resolving Multi-Target Association in OFDM-based ISAC via Vision-aided Multi-Modal Learning

author.name: Meng Hua, Chenghong Bian, Deniz Gunduz

entry.summary: Proposes a vision-assisted OFDM-ISAC framework that fuses transmitted street-view imagery (via deep joint source-channel coding) with radar sensing to resolve multi-target association ambiguity in delay-Doppler maps. Tackles a fundamental limitation of peak-searching approaches.

entry.title: Curvature-Adaptive Consistency Flow Matching: Autonomous Trajectory Optimization via Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Songtao Tian, Guhan Chen, Bohan Li, Jingyi Ma, Zixiong Yu

entry.summary: Proposes Curvature-Adaptive Consistency Flow Matching (CACFM), revealing a U-shaped difficulty profile in consistency distillation and using reinforcement learning to dynamically optimize the sampling trajectory. Targets boundary-stage optimization bottlenecks.

entry.title: Gen2Balance: Generative Balancing for Long-Tailed Video Action Recognition

author.name: Prajwal Gatti, Simon Jenni, Fabian Caba Heilbron, Dima Damen

entry.summary: Proposes Gen2Balance, using a text-to-video generative model conditioned on action-grounded prompts to augment long-tailed video action recognition datasets into balanced real-plus-generated sets. Uses a two-stage training strategy to mitigate domain shift.

entry.title: Catching Lies Without Sending the Video: Privacy-Preserving Multimodal Deception Detection

author.name: Nikita Sharma, Pranav Sara, Karan Singla

entry.summary: Demonstrates privacy-preserving multimodal deception detection by extracting a compact on-device digest (transcript, emotion, prosody, facial behavior) instead of streaming raw video, matching frontier model performance (AUC 0.74-0.76) at 7.8x fewer tokens. Tested on the Real-life Trial Deception dataset.

entry.title: READ More than What You See: Reinforcement Learning for Accurate and Coherent Audio Description Generations

author.name: Bo Fang, Xinyao Zhang, Yuxin Song, Hui Zhang, Hang Zhou, Antoni B. Chan

entry.summary: Presents READ, the first reinforcement-learning framework for training-based audio description generation, using sequence-level optimization with reference-matching, length, format, and a context-aware coherence reward. Targets concise narrations for blind and low-vision audiences.

entry.title: LoCC: Detection and Localization of Lip-Syncing Deepfakes via Counterfactual Frame Consistency

author.name: Soumyya Kanti Datta, Shan Jia, Siwei Lyu

entry.summary: Proposes LoCC, a framework for detecting and localizing lip-syncing deepfakes at segment and frame levels by checking whether each frame aligns with a counterfactual estimate generated from temporal neighbors. Real videos show stable consistency while lip-sync deepfakes introduce localized inconsistencies.

entry.title: CoVStream: Edge-Cloud Collaboration for Understanding of Long Video Streams

author.name: Xu Liu, Guikun Chen, Zihao Yan, Kanzhi Wu, Wenguan Wang

entry.summary: Proposes CoVStream, the first edge-cloud collaborative framework for understanding long video streams, where edge nodes distill raw streams into compact features and captions to minimize bandwidth while cloud handles strong reasoning. Addresses the deployment reality of computationally constrained source devices.

entry.title: SPAR: Semantic-Pixel Self-Alignment and Adaptive Routing for Unified Multimodal Models

author.name: Hongxiang Li, Hongxu Chen, Chenyang Zhu, Xiaoshuang Huang, Jiayin Cai, Xiaolong Jiang, Yao Hu, Long Chen

entry.summary: Proposes SPAR, a unified multimodal framework with semantic-pixel self-alignment and adaptive routing to bridge the gap between semantic understanding and pixel-level generation in MLLMs. Aims to give semantic encoders high-fidelity reconstruction without external teachers.

entry.title: Dense Reward for Multi-View 3D Reasoning with Global Maps and Local Views

author.name: Jiho Choi, Seonho Lee, Seojeong Park, Hyunjung Shim

entry.summary: Proposes DR-MV3D, a map-grounded learning framework providing dense, verifiable rewards to supervise multi-view 3D visual question answering, decomposing it into global map construction, view-trajectory planning, and egocentric grounding. Addresses inconsistent cross-view reasoning from sparse answer-level supervision.

entry.title: Pose Anything Anywhere:Model-free Object Poses from Arbitrary References

author.name: Hongli Xu, Jiaqi Hu, Junwen Huang, Boyang Zhong, Peter KT Yu, Nassir Navab, Benjamin Busam, Slobodan Ilic

entry.summary: Presents PANY, a unified model-free framework for estimating 6D pose of unseen objects from one or sparse pose-free reference views, supporting both RGB and RGB-D inputs via a multi-view transformer geometry backbone. Moves beyond pairwise single-anchor matching to handle occlusion and large viewpoint changes.

entry.title: IMAGIN-4D: Image-Guided Controllable Interaction Generation

author.name: Sai Kumar Dwivedi, Federica Bogo, Bu\u{g}ra Tekin, Chenhongyi Yang, Nadine Bertsch, Tomas Hodan, Michael J. Black, Dimitrios Tzionas, Shreyas Hampali

entry.summary: Proposes IMAGIN-4D, a diffusion-based human-object interaction generation method that uses a reference image as a visual specification to resolve ambiguity in grasps, poses, contacts, and layouts that text and trajectories underspecify. Uses per-cue representations rather than a single global image embedding.

entry.title: Non-line-of-sight imaging with arbitrary relay surface geometries via 3D Gaussian Transient Rendering

author.name: Yi Wang, Ziyu Zhan, Yuran Wang, Hao Wang, Qiang Liu, Zuoqiang Shi, Lingyun Qiu, Xing Fu

entry.summary: Proposes a non-line-of-sight imaging pipeline using 3D Gaussian transient rendering that imposes no geometric assumptions on the relay surface and supports both confocal and non-confocal configurations. Addresses real-world NLOS conditions that violate planar-wall and dense-sampling assumptions.

entry.title: Lighting-Consistent Object Transfer Across Radiance Fields

author.name: Nicol\'as Violante, George Kopanas, Linus Franke, Julien Philip, George Drettakis

entry.summary: Introduces a diffusion model that harmonizes lighting when compositing objects between 3D Gaussian Splatting scenes, enabling realistic object transfer for VFX and design. Trained on a mixed synthetic, generated, and real dataset.

entry.title: Geometric Entropy: When Trajectory Diversity Helps and Hurts in Imitation Learning

author.name: Qian Luo, Ruizhe Liu, Pei Zhou, Xunzhe Zhou, Yanchao Yang

entry.summary: Introduces Geometric Entropy, a task-agnostic metric quantifying intrinsic trajectory diversity in demonstrations, and shows an inverted-U relationship between imitation learning success and diversity across architectures and real-robot tasks. Reveals when diversity helps versus hurts.

entry.title: Energy-based Compositional Diffusion Planning

author.name: Tao Sun, Utkarsh Aashu Mishra, Jiaxin Lu, Danfei Xu, Iro Armeni

entry.summary: Proposes Energy-based Compositional Diffuser, showing that heuristic stitching in compositional diffusion planners yields a non-conservative field, and instead formulates global trajectories as minimizers of summed local bridge potentials. Adds a boundary reaction term omitted by stitching.

entry.title: Causal Reward World Models: Zero-shot Reward Design for Automated Skill Generation

author.name: Yang Yang, Yuchuang Tong, Zhengtao Zhang, Xu Ding, Ning Yang, Yifan Zhang, Haipeng Li, Kehu Yang, Miao Xin

entry.summary: The Causal Reward World Model (CRWM) replaces correlation-driven LLM-based automated reward design with explicit modeling of causal relationships between candidate reward components and task-targeted physical variables, enabling zero-shot reward design for automated skill generation. This reduces susceptibility to spurious reward components.

entry.title: BiliVLA: Scene-Aware Vision-Language-Action Model with Reinforcement Learning for Autonomous Biliary Endoscopic Navigation

author.name: Jinsong Lin, Chi kit Ng, Zhiyong Xiong, Zikang Pan, Yihan Hu, Tabassum Tamima, Ziyi Hao, Eddie Cheung, Jiewen Lai, Huxin Gao, Hongliang Ren

entry.summary: BiliVLA is a scene-aware vision-language-action framework with reinforcement learning for autonomous biliary endoscopic navigation during ERCP, formulating cannulation as instruction-conditioned visuomotor learning under specular reflections, occlusions, and tissue contact. It targets reliable autonomy in a safety-critical surgical procedure.

entry.title: On the Asymptotic Inadmissibility of Double Machine Learning Estimators Under Structure-Agnostic Models

author.name: Lin Liu, Rajarshi Mukherjee, James M Robins

entry.summary: Analyzes structure-agnostic models and shows that the popular double machine learning estimators, while minimax for several functionals, are asymptotically inadmissible under these models. It probes the gap between minimax optimality and admissibility for influential causal inference estimators.

entry.title: A dexterous soft hand exoskeleton restores intentional grasping in individuals with severe hand impairment

author.name: Gordon Cheng

entry.summary: Presents a lightweight soft robotic hand exoskeleton, a textile glove with wrist dorsiflexion and an active opposable thumb, that restores intentional grasping in individuals with severe hand paralysis, enabling tasks like self-feeding. Published in Nature Machine Intelligence.

entry.title: Latent Goal Prediction from Language for Model-Based Planning

author.name: Samuel Barbeau, Simon Roy, Giovanni Beltrame, Christian Desrosiers, Nicolas Thome

entry.summary: LAGO predicts intermediate goal states from language instructions and action-conditioned rollouts within a shared latent space for model-based planning. It dynamically decomposes instructions into local subgoals rather than optimizing a single global objective.

entry.title: SPARC: A Multi-Agent System for Electrical Circuit Question Answering

author.name: Mushtari Sadia, Zhenning Yang, Umme Habiba Lamia, Nishat Shawrin, Ang Chen, Amrita Roy Chowdhury

entry.summary: SPARC is a multi-agent system that answers electrical circuit diagram questions by grounding reasoning in executable physics-based simulations, achieving 83% accuracy with up to 58% absolute improvement over baselines. It enables systematic error diagnosis.

entry.title: Simulated Customers Never Walk Away: Decision Fidelity of LLM User Simulators Measured Against Real Purchase Outcomes

author.name: Liang Chen

entry.summary: Argues that existing LLM user simulators measure communicative fidelity but have a blind spot, namely decision fidelity, because assigned goals make user willingness exogenous. Introduces measuring whether simulated populations reproduce real users' decision-state dynamics against actual purchase outcomes.

entry.title: Process-Reward Tactic Evolution for Long-Horizon Bioinformatics Workflows

author.name: Lingzhi Yang, Yubo Fan, Song Wu, Gilchan Park

entry.summary: Process-Reward Tactic Evolution is a Galaxy-based training framework that turns verified bioinformatics workflow rollouts into reusable tactics, with process verifiers scoring workflow construction and biological checks. It targets reliable long-horizon bioinformatics agents.

entry.title: Neurosymbolic Clinical Trial Matching via LLM-Driven Abduction and Logical Verification

author.name: Baiyang Qu, Leonardo Ranaldi, Xi Wang, Marco Valentino

entry.summary: Introduces aNeSy-CTM, an abductive neurosymbolic framework for clinical trial matching that combines LLM reasoning over noisy clinical text with logical verification of eligibility criteria. It substantially outperforms standalone LLM baselines.

entry.title: Coherence Under Commitment: Probing Generalization and Vacuous Memorization in LLM Logical Reasoning

author.name: Noor Islam S. Mohammad, Mahmudul Hasan

entry.summary: Introduces Coherence Under Commitment, a dual-query evaluation revealing that LLMs can achieve logical coherence vacuously by systematically abstaining, satisfying consistency while providing no utility. It contributes a commitment score and a deterministic log-probability elicitation protocol.

entry.title: Translating Inference-Time Control to Radiology Vision-Language Models: Activation Steering for Pneumonia Classification on Chest X-rays

author.name: Eduardo Moreno Judice de Mattos Farina, Mateus A. Esmeraldo, Felipe Akio Matsuoka, Paulo Eduardo de Aguiar Kuriki, Felipe Campos Kitamura

entry.summary: Evaluates whether Contrastive Activation Addition steering can improve pneumonia classification in three frozen chest X-ray VLMs without weight updates, using answer-bias, text-contrast, and image-conditioned steering vectors. Translates inference-time control to radiology.

entry.title: PeerCheck: Enhancing LLM-Generated Academic Reviews Towards Human-Level Quality

author.name: Zeyuan Chen, Ziqing Yang, Yihan Ma, Michael Backes, Yang Zhang

entry.summary: PeerCheck analyzes differences between LLM-generated and human academic reviews, finding LLMs prioritize theory while humans emphasize methodology and experiments, then explores prompt engineering to improve LLM review quality toward human level. Aims to make LLM review assistance more useful.

entry.title: FleetAgent: Teleoperation Assistant for Autonomous Fleets via Vectorized V2N Messages

author.name: Juntong Peng, Qi Chen, Deyuan Qu, Takayuki Shimizu, Yaobin Chen, Ziran Wang

entry.summary: FleetAgent is a cloud-hosted multimodal LLM teleoperation assistant for autonomous fleets that consumes compact vectorized V2N messages and outputs structured natural-language explanations plus an intervention urgency score. VecFormer bridges vector messages to token-based MLLMs.

entry.title: EnTrust: Modeling Inter-Modal Conflict for Trustworthy Multimodal Medical Image Analysis

author.name: Dwarikanath Mahapatra, Abhijit Das, Behzad Bozorgtabar, Zongyuan Ge, Sudipta Roy, Deepak Nayak, Mauricio Reyes, Imran Razzak

entry.summary: EnTrust treats inter-modal conflict as the primary source of predictive uncertainty in multimodal medical segmentation, with an EnFuse module decomposing features into shared consensus, modality-specific cues, and localized conflict. It contrasts with deterministic fusion or decoupled post-hoc uncertainty.

entry.title: Evaluating LLMs for Real-World Web Vulnerability Detection

author.name: Sebastian Neef, Luca Jungnickel, Antonio Benjamin Buchholz, Valene Spence, Vicente Birke Gonzalez

entry.summary: TASER is a continual learning framework for highly heterogeneous task sequences that jointly decides how many new atomic skills to introduce per task and which to activate, using uncertainty-driven capacity expansion and orthogonal routing. It targets catastrophic forgetting under large reasoning and format divergence.

entry.title: Streaming T5-based Text-to-Speech Synthesis with Limited Lookahead

author.name: Muyang Du, Jason Roche, Junjie Lai

entry.summary: S5-TTS is a streaming variant of T5-TTS enabling low-latency word-by-word incremental speech synthesis via encoder-decoder language modeling and monotonic alignment, beginning generation after the first few words. A lookahead-causal masking mechanism and interleaved multi-source distillation preserve quality under limited lookahead.

entry.title: KITE: Decoupling Kinematics and Interaction for Zero-Shot Cross-Embodiment Manipulation

author.name: Qianxu Wang, Kuan Fang

entry.summary: Introduces KITE, which decouples manipulation into embodiment-agnostic task reasoning and embodiment-specific motor control linked by a learned latent of interaction intent based on contact patterns. Enables zero-shot cross-embodiment manipulation without target demonstrations.

entry.title: On the Expressive Power of Weight Quantization in Large Language Models

author.name: Shao-Qun Zhang

entry.summary: Provides a theoretical investigation of LLM expressive power as a function of weight quantization bits, arguing 1.58-bit is the limiting precision via universal approximation and expressive-collapse results. Sheds light on approximation and degradation as bits decrease.

entry.title: Energy-Based Transformers as Predictors of Reading Difficulty

author.name: Jakub Dotlacil, Ece Takmaz

entry.summary: Explores energy-based transformers as predictors of human reading difficulty, linking them to associative memory and Hopfield network theory. First application of an energy-based transformer measure in computational psycholinguistics across reading-time corpora.

entry.title: Evidential Fusion Network for Multimodal Survival Prediction under Missing Modalities

author.name: Yucheng Xing, Hailan Mo, Zi Wang, Ling Huang, Mengling Feng

entry.summary: EMMS performs multimodal survival prediction robust to missing modalities using Dempster-Shafer theory and Gaussian Random Fuzzy Numbers for evidential decision fusion, modeling both aleatoric and epistemic uncertainty without a generative imputation phase. Targets real-world clinical incompleteness.

entry.title: Hierarchical Pooling for Sheaf Neural Networks

author.name: Dionisia Naddeo, Carlo Abate, Pietro Li\`o, Nicola Toschi, Filippo Maria Bianchi

entry.summary: HiSP introduces hierarchical pooling for sheaf neural networks based on local spectral coarsening, enabling multi-resolution representations that existing fixed-resolution sheaf architectures lack. Sheaf diffusion promotes consistency through restriction maps rather than feature similarity.

entry.title: Geometric and Information Compression of Representations in Deep Learning

author.name: Linara Adilova, Henning Petzka, Asja Fischer, Bernhard C. Geiger

entry.summary: Investigates whether low input-representation mutual information necessarily implies geometrically compressed latent spaces in deep nets, using class-wise clustering and CEB networks. Studies the interplay between information-theoretic and geometric compression with generalization.

entry.title: DevoTG: Temporal Graph Neural Networks for Modeling C. elegans Developmental Connectomics

author.name: Jayadratha Gayen, Bradly Alicea

entry.summary: Presents DevoTG, a temporal graph neural network framework applied to C. elegans developmental connectomics using continuous- and discrete-time dynamic graphs of cell lineage and synaptic data. Substantially outperforms static GNNs on lineage prediction.

entry.title: Encoder-Decoder Manifold Alignment for Idempotent Generation
