author.name: Jaehyuk Jang, Minseok Seo. Seungju Cho, Kangwook Ko, Changick Kim

entry.summary: Proposes T-VSS, a lightweight test-time defense improving adversarial robustness of vision-language models by adapting directly in the visual feature space via a sample-specific low-rank subspace. Contrasts with indirect prompt-based or pixel-space adaptations.

entry.title: GeoFidelity-Bench: Evaluating Segment-Level Geographic Fidelity in Text-to-Image Street-View Generation

author.name: Kaizhen Tan, Hanzhe Hong, Siru Tao

entry.summary: Introduces GeoFidelity-Bench, a reference-panel benchmark testing whether text-to-image street-view generation corresponds to a requested road segment rather than a generic city prior, using 7,117 Mapillary images over 109 named OpenStreetMap segments across 25 cities. Frames the test as local discrimination among nearby segments.

entry.title: Spectral GS-SLAM: Observability-Aware, Degeneracy-Robust Tracking for Real-Time 3D Gaussian Splatting SLAM

author.name: Edward Beng Wai Tan, Siew-Kei Lam, Dongshuo Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes Spectral GS-SLAM, an observability-aware tracking framework for real-time 3D Gaussian Splatting SLAM that integrates ICP with complementary feature constraints and adaptively compensates under-constrained directions in degenerate scenes. Improves robustness in textureless or geometrically degenerate environments.

entry.title: Scaling up fine-grained intracranial vessel annotations in computed tomography angiography

author.name: Chu-Hsuan Lin, Alberto Mario Ceballos-Arroyo, Jisoo Kim, Shrikanth M. Yadav, Huaizu Jiang, Lei Qin, Geoffrey S. Young

entry.summary: Presents SemanticVessel, a dataset for fine-grained brain vessel segmentation in CT angiography built from dynamic 4D-CTA scans, with 20 expert-annotated arterial classes and intensity-guided region growing for vascular territories. Unlike prior datasets, it retains minor arteries as a generic class rather than discarding them.

entry.title: Mesh2GS: White-Box 3DGS Construction via Plenoptic Sampling

author.name: Haoran Zhu, Youcheng Cai, Huangsheng Du, Jingyang Meng, Ligang Liu

entry.summary: Proposes Mesh2GS, a white-box framework that converts a mesh directly into 3D Gaussian Splatting based on plenoptic sampling theory, achieving Nyquist-level quality for global illumination rendering rather than heuristically binding Gaussians to the mesh. Reverses the more common 3DGS-to-mesh direction.

entry.title: MV-WAM: Manifold-Aware World Action Model with Value Augmentation

author.name: Jintao Chen, Peidong Jia, Qingpo Wuwu, Jiaming Liu, Mengfei Du, Chun-Kai Fan, Xiaowei Chi, Hao Chen, Chengyu Bai, Zezhong Qian, Hao Wang, Jiajun Cao, Weishi Mi, Xiaozhu Ju, Jian Tang, Shanghang Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes MV-WAM, a manifold-aware world action model with value augmentation that jointly models visual prediction, action generation, and value estimation to improve out-of-distribution manipulation generalization. Attributes OOD gaps to visual-action manifold mismatch.

entry.title: TEXEDO : Test Time Scaling for Controller-aware Language-conditioned Humanoid Motion Generation

author.name: Jianuo Cao, Yuxin Chen, Yuzhen Song, Masayoshi Tomizuka, Chenran Li, Thomas Tian

entry.summary: TEXEDO is a test-time scaling framework for text-conditioned humanoid motion generation that samples multiple candidates and selects controller-feasible motions, addressing the gap where retargeted human motion is semantically plausible but physically unexecutable. It improves motion quality without a stronger generator.

entry.title: Beyond Fixed Budgets: Characterizing the Inelasticity and Limitations of Tree-of-Thought Reasoning Strategies

author.name: Atkia Mahila, Avinash Maurya, M. Mustafa Rafique, Bogdan Nicolae

entry.summary: An empirical study characterizing how Tree-of-Thought reasoning strategies behave across compute budgets, model sizes, and problem difficulties, finding two representative methods exhibit opposing limitations. It provides practical guidance on deploying ToT search under constraints.

entry.title: AlphaMemo: Structured Search-Process Memory for Self-Evolving Alpha Mining Agents

author.name: Hang Yu, Zifan Zheng, Jeff Z. Pan, Tongliang Liu, Zhiyong Wang, Fengxiang He

entry.summary: AlphaMemo is a self-evolving alpha mining agent that records reusable evidence about which edit motifs succeed under specific factor contexts, extracted from AST differences. It addresses combinatorial search and overfitting in financial factor discovery.

entry.title: SignVLA: Real-Time Sign Language-Guided Robotic Manipulation via Attention LSTM and Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Ningwei Bai, Xinyu Tan, Harry Gardner, Zhengyang Zhong, Liuhaichen Yang, Luoyu Zhang, Zhekai Duan, Monkgogi Galeitsiwe, Zezhi Tang

entry.summary: SignVLA is a real-time sign-language-guided vision-language-action framework for robotic manipulation, using an attention-enhanced LSTM to convert sign gestures into semantic instructions for downstream VLA policies. It improves accessibility for deaf and speech-impaired users.

entry.title: Power Systems Agent Benchmark: Executable Evaluation of AI Agents in Electric Power Engineering

author.name: Sergei Trashchenkov

entry.summary: Introduces the Power Systems Agent Benchmark, an executable evaluation where AI agents return structured solutions to power-engineering tasks verified by a deterministic evaluator checking operational constraints. It brings executable evaluation to electric power engineering.

entry.title: AutoACSL: Synthesizing ACSL Specifications by Integrating LLMs with CPG-Based Static Analysis

author.name: Han Zhou, Yu Luo, Dianxiang Xu

entry.summary: AutoACSL synthesizes formal ACSL specifications for C programs by integrating LLM prompting with semantic features from Code Property Graphs, producing more verifiable contracts. It encodes arithmetic, loop/recursion, and return-propagation features into structured prompts.

entry.title: Mind the Noise: Sensitivity of Transformer-based Interaction-Aware Trajectory Prediction Models to Noisy Data

author.name: Shahab Salehi, Luca Lusvarghi, Miguel Sepulcre, Javier Gozalvez

entry.summary: Studies the sensitivity of Transformer-based interaction-aware trajectory prediction models to noisy real-world object-state data, contrasting with the clean datasets they are typically trained on. It highlights a robustness gap relevant to autonomous vehicle deployment.

entry.title: Entropy Objectives in Markov Decision Processes

author.name: S. Akshay, Raghav Goyal, Aditya Neeraje, Piyush Srivastava

entry.summary: A formal study of synthesizing control policies that enforce entropy-based concentration objectives on state distributions in Markov Decision Processes, proving hardness and giving a sound, conditionally complete synthesis method via convex duality and invariant synthesis. The work targets a niche but rigorous corner of formal control.

entry.title: ForEx: A Formal Verification Framework for Explainable Reasoning in Logical Fallacy Detection and Annotation

author.name: Pei-Cing Huang, Chienyu Liu, Chan Hsu, Ci-Siang Chen, Pei-Ju Lee, Yihuang Kang

entry.summary: ForEx translates LLM-generated fallacy-detection explanations into Lean4 and checks whether the stated rationale is formally derivable, separating label correctness from the formal soundness of the supporting reasoning. It shows most LLM outputs have unverifiable rationales despite confident labels.

entry.title: REBA: A Revealed Belief Automaton Framework for Online Planning in Continuous POMDPs

author.name: Xiangwei Chen, Lingling Fang, Andreas Holzinger, Liming Chen

entry.summary: REBA introduces an event-driven Revealed Belief Automaton for online planning in continuous POMDPs under omega-regular specifications, certifying symbolic states from noisy online beliefs rather than relying on global belief-space discretization. It targets long-horizon temporal-logic planning.

entry.title: SVGym (SciVerseGym): An Environment for Reinforcement Learning and Bayesian Optimization in Crystal Discovery

author.name: Bin Cao

entry.summary: SciVerseGym (SVGym) is a Gymnasium-compatible environment that frames sequential crystal discovery as an MDP, letting agents apply chemically meaningful edits and receive feedback from machine-learned interatomic potentials. It unifies fragmented crystal-search pipelines for RL and Bayesian optimization.

entry.title: Grounded Scaling: Why Agentic AI Needs Deterministic Environments

author.name: Liang Ding, Xintong Wang

entry.summary: This position paper argues that environment determinism is a binding axis for agentic scaling, formalizing how k-step chain success degrades as determinism raised to the k and presenting bounds like a determinism-efficiency relationship and a verifier-Goodharting floor. It complements the AGI-to-ASI scaling debate.

entry.title: XmoPipe: A Pipeline for Large-Scale In-the-Wild Human Motion Dataset Construction

author.name: Nathan Salazar, Emmanuel Dellandr\'ea, Mathieu Lefort, Alexandre Meyer

entry.summary: XmoPipe is a scalable pipeline that builds in-the-wild human motion datasets from online videos given a few keywords, extracting 3D body and facial motion plus textual descriptions. It enables targeted collection of diverse motions and interactions.

entry.title: Structure-Aware Graph Multi-Task Learning for Dynamic Sparse OD Demand Prediction

author.name: Ming Xu, Jiawei Cao

entry.summary: SAGMTL is a structure-aware graph multi-task learning framework for dynamic sparse origin-destination demand prediction that decomposes the task into structural state modeling and flow regression to handle long-tailed, intermittent zero-flow patterns. It distinguishes whether a connection is active from how much demand it carries.

entry.title: LLM-Based Multi-Reference Evaluation for Efficient and Robust Assessment of Phrase Break Annotations

author.name: Younghan Park, Hoyeon Lee, Hawon Jeong, Jong-Hwan Kim

entry.summary: Proposes LLM-based Multi-Reference Evaluation for phrase break annotations that models the one-to-many nature of prosodic phrasing by generating multiple valid phrasings from minimal demonstrations. Shows stronger alignment with human judgment than single-reference evaluation on a Korean testbed.

entry.title: MS-rPPG: Multi-spectral State Space Model for Remote Photoplethysmography in Driver Monitoring Systems

author.name: Jiho Choi, Sang Jun Lee

entry.summary: MS-rPPG is a multi-spectral state-space framework combining RGB and near-infrared face video with cross-spectral fusion for remote heart rate estimation in challenging driving conditions with varying illumination and head movement. Targets driver health monitoring.

entry.title: Sexualised synthetic personas encode and amplify gendered power asymmetries through voice

author.name: Alice Ross, Ariadna Sanchez, Elin Kanhov, Catherine Lai, Eva Szekely

entry.summary: Using a Feminist HCI lens and a listening experiment with acoustic analysis, this work examines how a commercial platform's sexualized synthetic voices reproduce gendered power asymmetries. It finds these voices encode and amplify heteronormative and gendered performances.

entry.title: Improving Text-to-Music Generation with Human Preference Rewards

author.name: Yonghyun Kim, Junwon Lee, Haiwen Xia, Yinghao Ma, Chris Donahue

entry.summary: A challenge entry for text-to-music generation adding a learned human-preference reward from a pairwise ranker (TuneJury) used both as a training conditioning signal and a sample-selection criterion. It combines five engineering decisions on a 120M-parameter audio backbone.

entry.title: RARM: Confidence-Gated Progress Reward Modeling for RL in Manipulation

author.name: Pengzhi Yang, Xinyu Wang, Pengyu Jing, Kehan Wen, Yiduo Qu, Zhenhao Huang, Minghao Fu, Xin Liu, Yaheng Shen, Fan Shi

entry.summary: Introduces RARM, a reference-anchored reward model that converts a single successful demonstration into a dense progress-aware reward for RL robot manipulation. Uses confidence gating to avoid rewarding visually plausible but physically incorrect states.

entry.title: NL2Scratch: An Executable Benchmark and Evaluation for Block-Based Programming

author.name: Heejin Do, Alexandre Ballenghien, Yang Wu, April Yi Wang

entry.summary: Introduces NL2Scratch, an executable benchmark of over 311k natural-language-to-Scratch program pairs from real projects, plus a Semantic Alignment Consistency metric for evaluating block-based program generation. Targets the underexplored area of NL2Code for event-driven visual programming education.

entry.title: SAGE: An Expert-Annotated South Asian GI Endoscopy Dataset for Multimodal Learning and Hallucination Analysis

author.name: Niyoj Oli, Sachin Acharya, Sandesh Pokhrel, Sanjay Bhandari, Ramesh Rana, Nikesh Mani Shrestha, Ram Bahadur Gurung, Yash Raj Shrestha, Prashnna K Gyawali, Binod Bhattarai

entry.summary: Introduces SAGE, an expert-annotated South Asian gastrointestinal endoscopy dataset for multimodal learning and hallucination analysis, addressing geographic bias in existing GI datasets dominated by European data. Supports AI-assisted diagnosis in underrepresented regions.

entry.title: Delta-Diffusion: Modeling Longitudinal Brain Amyloid-PET Trajectories via Conditional Poisson Diffusion Bridge

author.name: Yongheng Sun, Minhui Yu, Mengqi Wu, Maureen Kohi, Mingxia Liu

entry.summary: Proposes Delta-Diffusion, a conditional Poisson Diffusion Bridge framework for synthesizing longitudinal brain amyloid-PET trajectories that models temporal transitions rather than replicating baseline intensities. Aims to reduce reliance on costly, radiation-heavy repeated PET imaging.

entry.title: Diffusion Integrated Gradients: Controllable Path Generation for Flexible Feature Attribution

author.name: Soyeon Kim, Kyowoon Lee, Jaesik Choi

entry.summary: Proposes Diffusion Integrated Gradients (DiffIG), reformulating attribution-path generation as conditional generative modeling using a diffusion model trained on paths from a Stick-Breaking Process. Aims to produce flexible, less noisy feature attributions than fixed-path Integrated Gradients.

entry.title: Not All Claims Are Equally Risky: FACTOR for Adaptive Verification in Factual Long-Form Generation

author.name: Areeba Hassan, Arooj Kausar, Syeda Kisaa Fatima, Gibrail Islam, Mehwish Fatima

entry.summary: Proposes FACTOR, an inference-time method that adapts verification criteria to claim-level uncertainty in factual long-form generation, allocating verification effort where hallucination risk is highest. Combines uncertainty estimation, adaptive inference verification, and candidate re-ranking, evaluated on FactScore.

entry.title: RS-Gen: A Multi-Stage Agentic Framework for Reasoning and Search-Augmented Image Generation

author.name: Feifei Bian, Zhimin Zheng, Wei Deng, Daiguo Zhou, Jian Luan

entry.summary: Proposes RS-Gen, a training-free multi-stage agentic framework that adds reasoning and external search to image generation for ambiguous intents and out-of-distribution knowledge. Uses a questioning-and-solving loop to improve over standard image models.

entry.title: Distribution-Aware Diffusion-LLM for Robust Ultra-Long-Term Time Series Forecasting

author.name: Falguni Ghosh, Vahid Hashemi, Bernhard Kainz

entry.summary: Proposes Diffusion-LLM, integrating a conditional diffusion model into an LLM-based pipeline for robust ultra-long-term time series forecasting. Adds calibrated probabilistic modeling and improves semantic alignment in a shared latent space.

entry.title: A Generative Model for Closed-Loop Microsimulation of Signalized Intersections

author.name: Yash Ranjan, Rahul Sengupta, Anand Rangarajan, Sanjay Ranka

entry.summary: Enactor is an actor-centric generative model for closed-loop microsimulation of vehicles at signalized intersections, using transformer-based spatial and temporal attention in polar coordinates. Aims for stable long-horizon simulation capturing heterogeneous vehicle interactions.

entry.title: Physics-Guided Dual-Stream Heterogeneous Graph Neural Network for Predicting Full-Field Structural Response of Stiffened Panels

author.name: Yuecheng Cai, Jasmin Jelovica

entry.summary: DS-HGNN is a dual-stream heterogeneous graph neural network for full-field stress and displacement prediction in stiffened-panel structures, with physics-guided edge states from boundary kinematics. Aims to replace expensive finite element analysis in iterative design.

entry.title: A Reward-Petri-Net Interpretation of Temporal Behavior Trees

author.name: Till Schmeil, G\"unther Waxenegger-Wilfing, Sebastian Schirmer

entry.summary: Interprets Temporal Behavior Trees as Reward-Petri-Nets to design RL reward functions for complex hierarchical robotic tasks with temporal constraints expressed in linear temporal logic. Aims to simplify reward shaping for long-horizon robotics.

entry.title: Embedding Linear Equality Constraints in Probabilistic Neural Networks for Dynamic Modelling

author.name: Matthew Marsh, Benoit Chachuat, Antonio del Rio Chanona

entry.summary: Proposes a probabilistic neural network framework guaranteeing satisfaction of linear equality constraints within tolerance while quantifying aleatoric uncertainty, applied to chemical process dynamic modeling. Demonstrated on batch reactor mass balances.

entry.title: Decision-Focused Learning: When and Why Traditional Prediction Models Fail

author.name: Mo Liu

entry.summary: A tutorial reviewing decision-focused learning, explaining when and why predict-then-optimize and traditional statistical tools fail for downstream decision quality, focused on stochastic linear programming. Synthesizes methodological insights for the operations research community.

entry.title: What Do Lorentz-Equivariant Jet Taggers Learn?

author.name: Jay Agarwal, Siddharth Khare, Dhruv Kumar

entry.summary: Probes what Lorentz-equivariant jet taggers learn internally using linear probes and grade ablations across five models, finding they suppress frame-dependent features while encoding jet mass and N-subjettiness. Characterizes which physical features carry discriminative information.

entry.title: Ranking-and-Selection with Multiple Correct Answers and Non-Answerable Estimates

author.name: Qiaoqiao Wang, Wei You

entry.summary: Studies fixed-precision ranking-and-selection where the correct answer may be non-unique or temporarily non-existent, proposing ENDS, a unified procedure with answer-wise acceptance sets and cost-aware selection. Applies to multi-fidelity selection and Condorcet winner identification.

entry.title: Early-Exit Graph Neural Networks for Link Prediction

author.name: Roman Knyazhitskiy, Andrea Giuseppe Di Francesco

entry.summary: Explores early-exiting strategies for graph neural networks to accelerate link prediction without auxiliary losses, letting early exit emerge as an implicit architectural property. Moves the speed/quality Pareto frontier on the HeaRT benchmark for GCN and SAS-GNN backbones.

entry.title: The Scissors Effect: When Resize-Based Input Diversity Helps or Hurts Transfer Attacks

author.name: Yuhang Jiang, Xiaojing Chen

entry.summary: Identifies the Scissors Effect: input diversity augmentation in transfer-based adversarial attacks helps standard surrogates but hurts robustly trained ones. Provides empirical evidence across multiple architectures and attacks on ImageNet.

entry.title: Error Highways: Scaling Predictive Coding to Very Deep Networks

author.name: Amirhossein Mohammadi, Alexander G. Ororbia

entry.summary: Proposes highway error propagation (HEP) to scale predictive coding networks to deep architectures by adding feedback matrices coupling hidden states to output error, countering signal decay in interior layers. Advances biologically-plausible local learning.

entry.title: GRAIN: Group Aggregation via Min-Norm Objective

author.name: Nghia Bui, Jiarui Yao, Lijing Wang

entry.summary: Introduces GRAIN, a lightweight group-aggregation min-norm objective to reduce training instability and variance in overparameterized fine-tuning of large pretrained models. Avoids costly repeated runs for variance reduction.

entry.title: Unlocking In-Context Learning in Audio-Language Models from Decentralized Medical Audio

author.name: Ran Piao, Tsai-Ning Wang, Martijn den Dekker, Linda Moonen, Hareld Kemps, Yuan Lu, Aaqib Saeed

entry.summary: Proposes Federated Self-Contextualization (FSC), an audio-language model framework enabling in-context clinical audio diagnosis across federated hospitals using pseudo-label episodes from unsupervised clustering. Bypasses scarce diagnostic labels via a progressive three-stage pipeline.

entry.title: Collapsed Effective Operators for Higher-order Structures

author.name: Maximilian Krahn, Lennart Bastian, Vikas Garg, Bj\"orn Schuller, Tolga Birdal

entry.summary: Introduces Collapsed Effective Operators that condense higher-order topological structures into a single vertex-level operator via Schur complementation of a graded Laplacian. Preserves positive semi-definiteness and encodes long-range topology-mediated interactions.

entry.title: Provably Sub-Linear Two-Timescale NeuroEvolution with Online Plasticity

author.name: Shishen Lin, Yixin Chen

entry.summary: Provides the first regret analysis for a two-timescale NeuroEvolutionary Online Learning framework that decouples architecture search from online weight adaptation. Proves provably sub-linear regret for the NEOL approach.

entry.title: Physics-Preserving Latent Compression for Zero-Shot Resolution Transfer in 3D Turbulence

author.name: Yilong Dai, Yiming Sun, Yiheng Chen, Ziyi Wang, Shengyu Chen, Xiaowei Jia, Runlong Yu

entry.summary: Proposes Physics-Preserving Latent Compression (PPLC), a patch-local latent compressor for 3D turbulence that preserves physical diagnostics and enables zero-shot resolution transfer from low- to high-resolution fields without retraining. Addresses resolution-dependence of learned compressors.

entry.title: Where Does the Signal Live? A Web Data Recipe for Medical Encoder Pretraining

author.name: Bofeng Huang, Jacques Sun, Diane Bouchacourt, Nicolas Barascud, Fajwel Fogel

entry.summary: Investigates whether web-scale data curation benefits encoder masked language model pretraining in the dense-terminology medical domain, introducing medical-term density filtering and LLM-based signal-amplifying rephrasing. Demonstrated on French medical encoders by Meta-affiliated authors.

entry.title: Null-Calibrated Conformal Selection via Target-Membership Scores

author.name: Seungjin Choi

entry.summary: This paper argues that the natural nonconformity score for conformal selection is the target-membership probability rather than residual-based scores inherited from prediction, yielding the Neyman-Pearson oracle ranking. The distinction matters for interval-valued, multimodal, or variance-driven targets.

entry.title: MaRS: Robust Out-of-Distribution Detection via Mahalanobis Residual Scoring

author.name: Francesco Di Salvo, Sebastian Doerrich, Christian Ledig

entry.summary: MaRS improves reconstruction-based out-of-distribution detection in medical foundation-model embeddings by replacing L2 residual norms with Mahalanobis residual scoring that respects the anisotropic feature geometry. It targets reliable OOD detection under patient, device, and acquisition shifts.

entry.title: LOLLA: Deep Reinforcement Learning for Closed-Loop Link Adaptation Towards a GPU-Accelerated AI-RAN

author.name: Rui Wang, Linchao Zhang, Qiang Liu, Kun Yang

entry.summary: LOLLA is a deep reinforcement learning framework replacing the conventional 5G outer-loop link adaptation staircase with a learned continuous SINR offset conditioned on rich PHY/MAC telemetry, trained with PPO under a Lagrangian block-error-rate constraint while preserving 3GPP-compliant MCS selection. It targets degraded performance under high-mobility, fast-varying channels.

entry.title: Ultra-Peripheral Collisions as a Nuclear-Structure Interferometer with Interpretable Multitask Deep Learning

author.name: Jing-Zong Zhang, Wang-Mei Zha, Lingxiao Wang, Guo-Liang Ma

entry.summary: This work introduces an interpretable multitask deep-learning framework to invert ultra-peripheral-collision diffraction and interference patterns into quantitative nuclear-structure constraints, disentangling deformation and neutron-skin sensitivities. It treats nuclear imaging as a challenging inverse problem.

entry.title: Rubric-as-Experts: Case-Specific MQM Rubrics for Translation Quality Evaluation

author.name: Weilu Xu, Yunzhi Shen, Xinye Wang, Ranfei Dang, Shujian Huang

entry.summary: Proposes case-specific MQM rubrics for translation quality evaluation, dynamically allocating rubric granularity per translation instance rather than using fixed rubrics. Motivated by finding that larger rubric spaces improve coverage but introduce false positives.

entry.title: MindTailor: Personalized Emotional Support via Post History-Grounded Case Formulation and Collaborative Refinement

author.name: Suhyun Han, Kyunghyun Cho, JinYeong Bak

entry.summary: Proposes MindTailor for personalized emotional support, building case formulations from a seeker's post history and refining responses via collaborative critique among counselor agents grounded in distinct counseling strategies. Goes beyond current-state-only personalization.

entry.title: Learning Moral Diversity: Modelling Individual Perspectives in Moral Classification of Texts

author.name: Yi Ren, Lewis Mitchell, Matthew Roughan

entry.summary: Extends a pretrained language model with an annotator-specific feature layer to model moral diversity rather than aggregating crowdsourced labels into a single ground truth. Improves prediction of individual annotations and reveals interpretable annotator moral perspectives.

entry.title: LISE : Listenable Interpretable Speaker Embeddings

author.name: Xiaoliang Wu, Chongxin Gan, Ke Liu, Peter Bell, Jennifer Williams

entry.summary: Proposes LISE, a label-free framework decomposing pretrained speaker embeddings into a small set of listenable, perceptually verifiable components without requiring attribute annotations. Aims to make opaque speaker verification embeddings interpretable while preserving verification performance.

entry.title: An Evaluation Framework for Text-to-Speech Voice Reconstruction

author.name: Ariadna Sanchez, Christoph Minixhofer, Korin Richmond, Ondrej Klejch, Peter Bell, Simon King

entry.summary: Proposes an evaluation framework for TTS-based voice reconstruction for people with speech disorders, combining Best-Worst Scaling subjective measures with a novel dual-reference distributional objective measure. Shows standard metrics fail to predict reconstruction success for highly unintelligible speakers.

entry.title: Automated sign detection across the Electronic Babylonian Library: A large-scale dataset and end-to-end cuneiform OCR pipeline

author.name: Wentao Che, Esteban Garc\'es Arias, Asim Niaz, Andreas Bender, Enrique Jim\'enez

entry.summary: Builds the largest annotated cuneiform sign dataset and an end-to-end OCR pipeline using a Deformable DETR detector with tablet-side extraction and n-gram similarity evaluation. Advances computational decipherment of ancient texts.

entry.title: AEF-Econ: Toward Plug-and-Play Socioeconomic Foundation Embeddings from AlphaEarth for Urban Remote Sensing

author.name: Shuyang Hou, Ziqi Liu, Haoyue Jiao, Lutong Xie, Yaxian Qing, Xiaopu Zhang, Qingyang Xu, Zhangyan Xu, Xuefeng Guan, Huayi Wu

entry.summary: Integrates AlphaEarth foundation embeddings with six other data streams across 36 Chinese cities to build CHN-Econ, a socioeconomic benchmark, and runs 31 controlled experiments on fusion and self-supervised design. Shows AEF alone is limited for socioeconomic tasks but improves with fusion.

entry.title: ELDiff: When Evidential Learning Meets Text-to-Image Diffusion

author.name: Qingtao Pan, Kai Ye, Zhihao Dou, Bing Ji, Shuo Li

entry.summary: Proposes ELDiff, an evidential-learning-supervised text-to-image diffusion model using uncertainty metrics and conflict detection to improve semantic consistency in multi-object generation. Addresses segmentation map bias and semantic overlap conflicts.

entry.title: Unsupervised Domain Adaptation for Sim-to-Real Object Pose Estimation with Contrastive Alignment and Pseudo-Label Refinement

author.name: Nidhal Eddine Chenni, Arunkumar Rathinam, Djamila Aouada

entry.summary: Proposes CAPLR, an unsupervised domain adaptation method for sim-to-real object pose estimation using contrastive alignment of pose-sensitive localized features and pseudo-label refinement. Preserves geometric cues during domain alignment.

entry.title: Synergistic Dual-Branch Adaptation for Multi-modal Generalized Category Discovery

author.name: Yuxun Qu, Minyu Zhou, Yongqiang Tang, Chenyang Zhang, Wensheng Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes SDBA, a synergistic dual-branch adaptation framework for multi-modal generalized category discovery that addresses text noise during encoding and adds fine-grained relational supervision beyond global class anchors. Serves as a plug-and-play module.

entry.title: CurvSegFlow: Time-Conditioned Flow Matching for Robust Segmentation of Curvilinear Structures in Noisy Biomedical Images

author.name: Sidi Mohamed Sid'El Moctar, Achraf Ait Laydi, Alexandre Beber, Marcus Braun, Zdenek Lansky, Yousef El Mourabit, Helene Bouvrais

entry.summary: Proposes CurvSegFlow, a time-conditioned flow-matching framework for segmenting thin curvilinear structures in noisy biomedical images by progressively refining a noisy initialization via a learned velocity field. Targets low-SNR cytoskeletal microscopy.

entry.title: Prompt-Calibrated SAM 3 for Open-Vocabulary Remote Sensing Semantic Segmentation

author.name: Yanghui Song, Nanqing Liu, Haonan Yin, Yingjie Gao, Chengfu Yang, Qi Ming

entry.summary: Proposes ProC-SAM3, a training-free calibration of SAM 3's prompt interface for open-vocabulary remote sensing segmentation, using an offline prompt pool, category matcher, and noise-suppressing aggregation. It addresses semantic coverage and redundant text encoding issues.

entry.title: Customizing Video Portraits via Identity-ActionDecoupling

author.name: Junxiong Lin, Haoran Wang, Xinji Mai, Zeng Tao, Xuan Tong, Ivy Pan, Wenqiang Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes Identity-Action Decoupling for identity-preserving text-to-video generation, separating ID-irrelevant information in facial embeddings to allow accurate prompt-controlled facial dynamics. Introduces identity-decoupling and text-alignment losses without subject-specific fine-tuning.

entry.title: FlowDec: Temporal Conditional Flow Decorruptor for Robust Continuous Vision-Language Navigation

author.name: Yufei Zhang, Changhao Chen

entry.summary: Introduces FlowDec, a temporal conditional flow-based image restoration framework for continuous vision-language navigation robust to real-world visual corruptions. Uses hybrid temporal conditioning and action-centroid guided filtering.

entry.title: Benchmarking Vision-Language Models for Microscopic Plant Image Understanding

author.name: Tianqi Wei, Xin Yu, Zhi Chen, Scott Chapman, Zi Huang

entry.summary: Presents PlantMicro, a benchmark of over 5,000 microscopic plant images and 9,000 VQA pairs across diverse hosts and modalities for evaluating vision-language models on cellular-level plant understanding. Fills a gap left by macroscopic-focused benchmarks.

entry.title: DR-Mamba: Automatic Inference-Time Domain Adaptation for Document Image Binarization via Sample-Conditioned Detail-Background Suppression

author.name: Sheng-Wei Chan, Jen-Shiun Chiang

entry.summary: Proposes DR-Mamba, a sample-conditioned detail-background suppression framework performing automatic inference-time domain adaptation for document image binarization via input-dependent gates in a single forward pass. Requires no target labels, fine-tuning, or test-time parameter updates.

entry.title: Learning Stable Canonical Worlds for Novel View Synthesis and Beyond

author.name: Xiaoyu Xu, Jian Zou, Sheyang Tang, Zhihua Wang, Jing Liao, Kede Ma

entry.summary: Introduces CanonicalGS, a feed-forward Gaussian splatting pipeline that aggregates multi-view evidence into a stable scene-centric canonical representation using uncertainty-aware fusion. Aims to converge to consistent scene representations as views increase rather than accumulating noise.

entry.title: C^2GR: Coupled Comprehensive Generative Replay for a Continually Learnable Universal Segmentation Model

author.name: Wei Li, Jingyang Zhang, Guoan Wang, Junzhi Ning, Yang Chen, Guang Yang, Lixu Gu

entry.summary: Proposes C2GR, a coupled comprehensive generative replay framework for continually-learnable universal medical segmentation that synthesizes image-mask pairs of previous tasks to mitigate forgetting under concurrent appearance and objective shifts. Targets privacy-preserving task-incremental learning across departments.

entry.title: Brain-Adapter: A Dual-Stream Vision-Language MIL Framework for Comprehensive 3D CT Diagnosis of Acute Intracranial Pathologies

author.name: Zhenyu Yi, Zhiyun Song, Yusong Sun, Zelin Liu, Manman Fei, Zhenhao Li, Jiaxuan Zhao, Xu Han, Lichi Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes Brain-Adapter, a dual-stream multiple-instance-learning framework that transfers 2D biomedical vision-language models to 3D brain CT diagnosis, using a text-conditioned attention mechanism driven by raw diagnostic reports for scan-level multi-label classification. Addresses the 2D-to-3D transfer problem.

entry.title: PIAvatar: Physically Interactive Avatars via Deformation Gradient Decoupling

author.name: Sang-Hun Han, Min-Gyu Park, Jisu Shin, Seunghyun Shin, Jin-Hwi Park, Hae-Gon Jeon

entry.summary: Presents PIAvatar, a framework enabling physically-aware avatar-avatar and avatar-environment interactions plus non-rigid deformable body simulation by decoupling kinematic velocity from deformation gradient. Aims for richer physical deformations and interaction behaviors than prior physics-aware avatars.

entry.title: Unsupervised Susceptibility Distortion Correction of EPI without Calibration Scans via Image Translation-Based Registration

author.name: Wooseung Kim, Sung-Hong Park

entry.summary: Proposes SACRED, an unsupervised, calibration-scan-free susceptibility distortion correction framework for echo-planar fMRI that corrects geometric distortions via image translation-based registration using only routinely acquired data. Removes dependence on field maps or reverse phase-encode acquisitions.

entry.title: DE-FIVE: Detecting Malicious Image Prompts via Fourier Features and Image Vector Embeddings

author.name: Xingwei Zhong, Varun Sharma, Kar Wai Fok, Vrizlynn L. L. Thing

entry.summary: Proposes DE-FIVE, a detector for malicious image prompts in vision-language models using Fourier features and image embeddings, targeting indirect prompt injection without heavy retraining. Addresses an underexplored VLM security gap.

entry.title: VolHuMe: a High-Resolution Large Scale Dataset of Volumetric Human Meshes

author.name: Giulia Martinelli, Niccol\`o Bisagno, Nicola Garau, Esa Rahtu, Nicola Conci

entry.summary: Presents VolHuMe, a high-resolution 4D human scan dataset captured with 64 RGB and 32 depth cameras across 104 subjects, with extensive ground truth including SMPL-X, meshes, and garment segmentation. Benchmarks 3D/4D human reconstruction methods.

entry.title: Heterogeneous Policy Networks for Composite Robot Team Communication and Coordination

author.name: Esmaeil Seraj, Rohan Paleja, Luis Pimentel, Kin Man Lee, Zheyuan Wang, Daniel Martin, Matthew Sklar, John Zhang, Zahi Kakish, Matthew Gombolay

entry.summary: Presents heterogeneous policy networks for multi-robot communication and coordination that explicitly model agent role heterogeneity, addressing limitations of homogeneous graph-network MARL. Targets composite teams with differing state, action, and observation spaces.

entry.title: Pose-Agnostic Robotic Functional Grasping via Observation-Action Canonicalization

author.name: Le Qiu, Cole Harrison, Jiankai Sun, Yao Liu, Suning Huang, Qianzhong Chen, Yang You, Marco Pavone

entry.summary: Introduces AnyMug, a canonicalized visuomotor RL framework for pose-agnostic functional grasping that uses observation-action canonicalization to handle diverse object poses, studied via mug-handle grasping. Decouples visual and action variation induced by object placement.

entry.title: Remember what you did?: Learning Behavioral Memories for Partially Observable Object Manipulation

author.name: Kuancheng Wang, Seungho Yeom, Jinglin Cao, Yuheng Zhi, Nikhil Shinde, Michael Yip

entry.summary: Proposes CAMP, a Compressed Action Memory Policy that learns a compact self-supervised representation of a robot's own action history to handle partially observable, long-horizon contact-rich manipulation. Treats action history as an informative memory signal.

entry.title: A Stitch in Time Saves Nine: Preserving Policy Compatibility Under Perception Updates in End-to-End Autonomous Driving

author.name: Yueyuan Li, Yifei Xiao, Mingyang Jiang, Xiang Zuo, Songan Zhang, Ming Yang

entry.summary: Formulates the model stitching problem for end-to-end autonomous driving and shows that lightweight latent-space alignment (linear/convolutional stitchers) can preserve policy compatibility when perception models are updated. Avoids costly policy retraining or architectural decoupling.

entry.title: SurGE: Surrogate Gradient-guided Evolution for Co-design of Legged Robots with Parallel Elasticity

author.name: Yulun Zhuang, Yue Qin, Justin Lu, Zelin Shen, Yichen Wang, Sicheng He, Yanran Ding

entry.summary: Presents SurGE, a framework that computes surrogate gradients through a differentiable kinodynamic single-rigid-body model and design-aware policy, injecting them into CMA-ES for co-design of legged robots with parallel elasticity. Improves convergence stability over vanilla CMA-ES with hardware validation.

entry.title: CoRDE: Concept-Prior Routed Diffusion Experts for Structural Generalization in Robot Manipulation

author.name: Haidong Huang, Xixin Zhao, Yaohua Zhou, Jiayu Song, Jiayi Zhang, Jun Ma, Haiyue Zhu, Xiaocong Li

entry.summary: Proposes CoRDE, a concept-prior routed diffusion-experts framework that uses semantic distributions from a frozen concept encoder to guide variational distillation and avoid MoE routing collapse for structural generalization in multi-task manipulation. Reduces parameter explosion from full-scale experts.

entry.title: From Pixels to Concepts: Growing Rich 3D Semantic Scene Graph Forests utilizing Foundation Models

author.name: David Oberacker, Meike Deitersen, Niklas Spielbauer, Tristan Schnell, Georg Heppner, Arne Roennau

entry.summary: Builds forests of hierarchical 3D semantic scene graphs with open-vocabulary relationships using foundation models, going beyond rigid predetermined relationship classes to capture causal connections and environmental contexts. It aims to give robots richer functional scene understanding.

entry.title: One-Bit Clustering for Two Component Sub-Gaussian Mixture Models

author.name: Junren Chen, Yun Yang

entry.summary: Proposes the first one-bit clustering method for two-component sub-Gaussian mixtures, using a single bit per entry via a dithered quantizer, and shows a Lloyd's-algorithm variant achieves exponentially decaying misclassification with near-optimal separation thresholds. It demonstrates extreme quantization need not sacrifice statistical performance.

entry.title: Near-Lipschitz stability of the Kim--Milman flow map

author.name: Sinho Chewi, Katharina Eichinger, Aram-Alexandre Pooladian

entry.summary: Proves the Kim-Milman flow map has favorable stability properties with respect to target-measure variations, including relative-entropy stability and near-Lipschitz stability in 2-Wasserstein distance up to a logarithmic factor, provided one target is sufficiently regular. It also gives a general existence theorem for these maps.

entry.title: FairTutor: Equity-Aware Pedagogical LLM Routing for Budget-Constrained AI Tutoring

author.name: Qingyang Xu

entry.summary: FairTutor is an equity-aware model-routing framework for budget-constrained AI tutoring that combines pedagogical planning, low-cost generation, critique-and-revision, and selective escalation to premium models. It introduces an access-tier advantage gap metric to measure educational inequity.

entry.title: Answer Engineering: Local Trajectory Editing for Protocol-Constrained Decision Making in Large Language Models

author.name: Victor Lavrenko, Anastasiia Molodnitskaia

entry.summary: Answer Engineering applies deterministic localized rule-guided interventions to an LLM's visible reasoning trajectory at generation time to enforce protocol compliance without retraining, evaluated on a clinical hearing-loss benchmark. It finds step-by-step reasoning shifts rather than eliminates protocol errors.

entry.title: Social World Model for Lifelong Social Intelligence

author.name: Yu Luo

entry.summary: Proposes a Social World Model that decomposes social interaction into five dimensions to build a closed-loop framework for lifelong social intelligence in language agents. It aims to unify capability improvement and retention rather than studying them in isolation.

entry.title: Composing Verifiable Conceptual Models via Building Blocks: Towards Design-Time Verification of Agentic AI Workflows

author.name: Noe Y. Flandre, Alexander C. Nwala, Philippe J. Giabbanelli

entry.summary: Proposes design-time verification of agentic AI workflows by modeling them as compositions of reusable building blocks checked against twelve structural compatibility rules, implemented in a prototype and evaluated on two datasets. It shifts safety from runtime safeguards toward design-time checks.

entry.title: Can LLMs Reason About Brand Ownership? An Empirical Study of Domain Attribution Intelligence

author.name: Fathima Mashood, Mohamed Nabeel

entry.summary: Empirically studies whether LLMs can reason about brand-domain ownership to resolve ambiguity between attacker squatting sites and legitimate brand-registered domains. Assesses LLM reliability for brand attribution intelligence in a security context.

entry.title: Detecting Satellites in Radio-Frequency Data via Semi-Supervised Learning

author.name: Cade W. Trotter, Maksim E. Eren, Justin C. Holmes, J. Brent Parham, David Ewing, Boian S. Alexandrov, Gian Luca Delzanno

entry.summary: Presents a semi-supervised learning workflow for detecting and classifying satellites, debris, and ionospheric background in radio-frequency data with few labels for space domain awareness. Uses unlabeled observations to reveal latent patterns for expert interpretation.

entry.title: CodeTeam: An LLM-Powered Multi-Agent Framework for Repository-Level Code Generation

author.name: Yifei Wang, Ruiyin Li, Peng Liang, Qiong Feng, Zengyang Li, Mojtaba Shahin, Arif Ali Khan

entry.summary: Proposes CodeTeam, an LLM multi-agent framework for repository-level code generation that separates planning (competing Architect agents and a CTO selector), decision making, and implementation into coordinated stages. Targets NL2Repo's needs for long-horizon planning and cross-file consistency.

entry.title: Dual-Stream EEG Decoding for 3D Visual Perception

author.name: Ninon Liz\'e Masclef, Taisija Demcenko, Antonella Catanzaro, Nataliya Kosmyna

entry.summary: Proposes a bio-inspired dual-pathway EEG decoding model that separately decodes object identity and spatial orientation (mirroring ventral/dorsal streams) during continuous rotations, with EEG-conditioned multiview diffusion for 3D reconstruction. Decodes 3D shape perception from neural activity.

entry.title: Evaluating Large Language Models for Hausa and Fongbe Machine Translation: Benchmarks, Failures, and Metric Reliability

author.name: Mahounan Pericles Adjovi, Roald Eiselen, Prasenjit Mitra

entry.summary: Evaluates four LLMs on English-to-Hausa and English-to-Fongbe translation and assesses whether standard automatic metrics align with human judgment for these low-resource West African languages. Finds quality varies substantially by language and questions metric reliability.

entry.title: Large Language Model-Assisted Cleaning of Report-Derived Labels in a Large-Scale Chest CT Dataset

author.name: Yosuke Yamagishi, Atsushi Takamatsu, Mototsugu Sato, Tomohiro Kikuchi, Shouhei Hanaoka, Takeharu Yoshikawa, Osamu Abe

entry.summary: Evaluates whether GPT-5.4-assisted label cleaning can identify label-report discordance in CT-RATE, a large public chest CT dataset, by regenerating binary labels from report text and comparing against existing labels with radiologist adjudication. Demonstrates LLM-assisted dataset quality auditing at scale.

entry.title: DreamUV: Unwrap Artist-like UV by End-to-End Flow Matching

author.name: Quanyuan Ruan, Jiabao Lei, Xingyi Du, Xifeng Gao

entry.summary: Presents DreamUV, an end-to-end flow-matching framework for UV unwrapping that learns a mesh-conditioned transport process producing artist-like UV layouts with straightened seams and axis-aligned islands. Bridges the gap between geometric distortion objectives and stylistic preferences of professional artists.

entry.title: Training-Free Semantic Correction for Autoregressive Visual Models

author.name: Junhao Chen, Chanyu Zhu, Zheqi Lv, Keting Yin, Shengyu Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes a training-free semantic correction method for autoregressive visual models based on next-scale prediction, addressing the difficulty of identifying and correcting semantic errors across discrete generation scales. Uses intermediate generation states that prior training-free methods neglect to prevent error accumulation.

entry.title: Decentralized Autonomous Traffic Management through Corridor Networks

author.name: Jasmine Jerry Aloor, Aadarsh Govada, Hamsa Balakrishnan

entry.summary: Extends multi-agent reinforcement learning to decentralized traffic flow management in advanced air mobility corridor networks, testing policies trained on single corridors against increasingly complex multi-corridor scenarios. Targets scalable coordination of crewed and uncrewed aircraft.

entry.title: Rejections Based on Predictive Uncertainty Enable Reliable Routine Soil Spectroscopy

author.name: Jonas Schmidinger, Robin Gebbers, Marc-Olivier Gasser, Viacheslav Barkov, G. Mick Wu, Viacheslav I. Adamchuk

entry.summary: Introduces reject-to-remeasure, combining probabilistic modeling with uncertainty-guided rejection so unreliable soil spectroscopy predictions trigger conventional lab remeasurement. Balances cost and reliability for routine agricultural soil analysis.

entry.title: Retrieval-Augmented Multimodal Learning for Enzyme-Substrate Interaction Prediction Under Low-Homology Shift

author.name: Chen Liu, Bingxin Zhou, Xinyuan Wang, Ming Li, Guisheng Fan, Liang Hong

entry.summary: Presents RAMMESI, a retrieval-augmented multimodal framework for enzyme-substrate interaction prediction that is robust under low-homology distribution shift via inference-time retrieval and recombination. Addresses sparse supervision in biocatalyst discovery.

entry.title: Stochastic Signed Distance Processes

author.name: Hiroki Sakuma, Masatoshi Okutomi

entry.summary: Reformulates SDF-based volume rendering as probabilistic surface rendering, introducing Stochastic Signed Distance Processes that model pixel color as a mixture induced by random ray-surface intersection. Targets multi-view surface reconstruction.

entry.title: Bayesian three-dimensional seismic travel-time tomography for active- and passive-source seismic data using physics-informed neural network

author.name: Ryoichiro Agata, Kazuya Shiraishi, Gou Fujie, Dan Bassett

entry.summary: Develops a meshless 3D Bayesian seismic travel-time tomography using physics-informed neural networks for combined active/passive source data, enabling rigorous uncertainty quantification while avoiding grid-based curse of dimensionality. Targets seismicity monitoring and hazard assessment.

entry.title: Beyond Flat Labels: Level-Restricted Contrastive Learning for Hierarchical Fine-Grained Vision Classification

author.name: Zhiyuan Tao, Srikumar Sastry, Matthew J Thompson, Elizabeth G Campolongo, Net Zhang, Ziheng Zhang, Hilmar Lapp, Yu Su, Tanya Berger-Wolf, Nathan Jacobs, Wei-Lun Chao, Jianyang Gu

entry.summary: Proposes level-restricted contrastive learning for hierarchical fine-grained vision classification, restricting contrastive comparisons to same-level taxonomic categories with a group-balanced design to avoid cross-level false negatives and inconsistent predictions. Improves taxonomic consistency in zero-shot classification.

entry.title: FeLoG: Scalable and Efficient Distributed Graph Embedding with Feedback Loop Mechanism

author.name: Peng Fang, Arijit Khan, Ziqiang Wu, Zhenli Li, Yibo Zhou, Fang Wang, Dan Feng

entry.summary: Introduces FeLoG, a distributed graph embedding framework with a feedback loop mechanism that couples sampling to evolving embedding quality, reducing redundant exploration and communication. Targets billion-edge graph embedding for recommendation, fraud detection, and GraphRAG.

entry.title: GARIP: A Running-Average Moving Reference for Last-Iterate Self-Play in Two-Player Zero-Sum Games

author.name: Can Savc{\i}

entry.summary: GARIP studies last-iterate convergence in two-player zero-sum self-play by anchoring policy updates to a running-average reference, proving the running average uniquely minimizes peak reference lag versus periodic snapshots. It clarifies why reference choice controls cycling and collapse.

entry.title: Who Owns the AI Recommendation? A Multi-Industry Empirical Map of Brand Category Ownership Across Large Language Models

author.name: Dmitrij \.Zatuchin

entry.summary: This empirical study probes which brands LLMs recommend across 50 brands, five industries, and 250 brand-free category queries on GPT-5.2, Gemini 3 Flash, and Perplexity sonar-pro, proposing metrics like a Category Ownership Index and Competitive Vacuum Index to measure recommendation concentration. References to GPT-5.2 and Gemini 3 Flash are analyses of existing deployed models, not releases.

entry.title: Curiosity as Linguistic Intervention: Using LLM Tutoring Dialogues to Influence Exploratory Learning Behavior

author.name: Gevindu Ganganath, Pasindu Bolonghege, Qianru Lyu, Pradeep Varakantham, Thivya Kandappu

entry.summary: Introduces CURIOBOT, operationalizing Berlyne's collative variables (novelty, complexity, conflict, uncertainty) as adaptive linguistic interventions in tutoring dialogues. Across 270 conversations, curiosity-oriented interventions increased exploratory behaviors up to 2.4x.

entry.title: moBERTo: A Modern Encoder for Portuguese via Continued Pretraining of ModernBERT

author.name: Thiago Laitz, Thales Sales Almeida, Jo\~ao Guilherme Alves Santos, Giovana Kerche Bon\'as

entry.summary: Introduces moBERTo, a Portuguese ModernBERT obtained via continued pretraining on 60B tokens, preserving rotary embeddings, alternating attention, and flash attention. Evaluated across retrieval (up to 8K tokens), classification, NER, and NLU.

entry.title: On the Effect of Segmentation Width and Cluster Size on Speech Resynthesis and Continuation in Generative Spoken Language Models

author.name: Shunsuke Kando, Wataru Nakata, Shinnosuke Takamichi, Yusuke Miyao

entry.summary: Investigates how segmentation width and K-means cluster size affect speech resynthesis and continuation in Generative Spoken Language Modeling across bitrate settings. Finds intelligible speech can be synthesized at lower bitrates than baseline, suggesting conventional GSLM settings may be redundant.

entry.title: The Language Blind Spot: How Query Language and Brand Recognition Tier Shape AI-Constructed Brand Reputation Across Twelve European Languages

author.name: Dmitrij \.Zatuchin (Estonian Entrepreneurship University of Applied Sciences)

entry.summary: Measures how query language and brand recognition tier shape AI-constructed brand reputation across twelve European languages using three grounded LLMs and multilingual embeddings. Finds reputation is language-bound, challenging English-only monitoring.

entry.title: GIM-ENDO: A Multimodal Endoscopic Image and Video Dataset for Gastric Intestinal Metaplasia Morphology and Pathology

author.name: Mojgan Forootan, Mahziar Setayeshfar, Ali Darvishi, Mohammad Tashakoripour, Hamidreza Bolhasani

entry.summary: Releases GIM-ENDO, a multimodal endoscopic image and video dataset for gastric intestinal metaplasia with histopathological validation, subtype labels, and standardized grading. Fills a gap for AI-driven early gastric cancer precursor detection.

entry.title: SEED: Simple ViT and Evolving Harness for Explainable Text Forgery Detection

author.name: Kahim Wong, Kemou Li, Yiming Chen, Haiwei Wu, Jiantao Zhou

entry.summary: Presents SEED, a modular system for explainable multilingual text forgery detection combining synthetic augmentation, a DINOv3+LoRA ViT for joint detection and localization, and an evolving harness for forensic report generation. Targets the ACM MM 2026 GenText-Forensics Challenge.

entry.title: OSOG: A Differentiable, Physics-Informed Synthetic Data Engine for Micro-Optical Environments

author.name: Caio Silva

entry.summary: Introduces OSOG, a fully differentiable physics-informed synthetic data engine for micro-optical environments based on wave-optics models of diffraction and phase retardation. Addresses scarcity of densely annotated microscopy data for deep learning.

entry.title: Boundary-by-Mask: Few-Shot Instance Segmentation with Mask-Conditioned Boundary Learning for Texture-Poor Industrial Parts

author.name: Yutaka Yoshinaga, Naoya Chiba, Koichi Hashimoto

entry.summary: Proposes Boundary-by-Mask, a few-shot instance segmentation framework for texture-poor industrial parts that supervises boundaries via a signed distance function head instead of interior appearance. Addresses application-specific instance definitions and domain gaps.

entry.title: GTA-Net: Cooperative Game Theory for Vision-Language Alignment in Chest X-Ray Report Generation

author.name: Saif ur Rehman Khan, Imad Ahmed Waqar, Sebastian Vollmer, Muhammad Nabeel Asim

entry.summary: Proposes GTA-Net, framing chest X-ray report generation as a cooperative game-theoretic vision-language alignment problem with Shapley-inspired importance weighting and disease-aware aligners. Targets explicit region-word correspondence and clinical consistency.

entry.title: Morphology-Aware Multimodal Representation Learning for Insect Phylogenetic Reconstruction

author.name: Zixuan Liu, Kaijie Yu, Chun He, Xiaoxu Cai, Xinhai Ye, Haishuai Wang, Gongyin Ye, Jiajun Bu

entry.summary: Presents a morphology-aware multimodal framework combining insect specimen images with curated morphological text descriptions via parameter-efficient fine-tuning and contrastive learning for phylogenetic reconstruction. Aligns image and text in a shared latent space.

entry.title: Physically-guided Image Generation for Multi-Projection Mapping

author.name: Xingyun Liu, Yuqi Li, Jinhui Xiang, Pinyan Tang, Chong Wang

entry.summary: Proposes ConPhyG, a physically-guided image generation framework for multi-projection mapping, formalizing cooperative (semantic harmonization) and adversarial (radiometric compensation) generative paradigms. Bridges idealized 2D diffusion generation with physical projection constraints.

entry.title: DrivingVoxels: Compositional Sparse Voxel Rasterization for Dynamic Driving Scene Reconstruction

author.name: Tania Aguirre, Luis Rold\~ao, Moussab Bennehar, Nathan Piasco, Dzmitry Tsishkou, Simone Rossi, Pietro Michiardi

entry.summary: Presents DrivingVoxels, a compositional sparse voxel rasterization framework for dynamic driving scene reconstruction that jointly rasterizes multiple octrees in a single pass. Aims for faster, memory-bounded reconstruction compared to dynamic Gaussian splatting.

entry.title: LUMINA-26: Low-Light Understanding for Modeling and Interpreting Night-time Actions

author.name: Aman Kumar Pandey, Anil Singh Parihar

entry.summary: Introduces LUMINA-26, a low-light human action recognition dataset of 6,784 clips across 26 action classes under naturally occurring low-light conditions, plus Illumi-Net, an illumination-adaptive mixture-of-experts network. Addresses scarcity of diverse, realistic low-light action data.

entry.title: LightSTAR: Efficient Visual Document Retrieval via Lightweight Selection with Vision-Adaptive Refinement

author.name: Tongkun Guan, Haocheng Wang, Wei Shen, Xiaokang Yang

entry.summary: Proposes LightSTAR, an efficient visual document retrieval framework that uses LLM-free visual selection exploiting keyword-anchored queries to quickly narrow candidate pages before expensive MLLM encoding. Reduces the prohibitive cost of encoding every page with MLLMs.

entry.title: LOGOS: LiDAR-Only Gaussian Elevation Splatting for Unified Tiny Obstacle Segmentation

author.name: Nan Ming, Yeqiang Qian, Chunxiang Wang, Ming Yang

entry.summary: Presents LOGOS, a LiDAR-only unified tiny obstacle segmentation system that models the road surface via Gaussian elevation splatting to distinguish curbs, gravel, and potholes from road undulations. Targets robustness in degraded off-road LiDAR scenarios.

entry.title: Overcoming Imperfect Kinematics in Surgical Robotics Through Sim-to-Real Visuomotor Learning

author.name: Zhaoxuan Yan, Kaizhong Deng, Zhaoyang Jacopo Hu, George P. Mylonas, Daniel S. Elson

entry.summary: Uses sim-to-real visuomotor learning with a teacher-student framework to actively compensate for imperfect kinematics in surgical robots, fusing unreliable internal readings with precise visual feedback. Addresses control errors from unreliable internal sensors.

entry.title: BIT-Nav: Brain-Inspired Trajectory Memory for Embodied Navigation

author.name: Rithvik Jonna, Aakash Gurram, Man Namgung, Wyatt Mackey, Tinoosh Mohsenin

entry.summary: Introduces BIT-Nav, a brain-inspired compact trajectory memory module that augments frozen VLM navigation pipelines, motivated by hippocampal path integration, to capture turning patterns and path topology beyond sparse frame selection. Targets long-horizon embodied navigation.

entry.title: ACEsplat: Accelerated 3D Gaussian Scene Regression via RGB and Poses Only

author.name: Mingkai Liu, Haohua Que, Dikai Fan, Haojia Gao, Tianle Zhu, Handong Yao, Qian Zhang, Ruopeng Zhang, Xianliang Huang, Fei Qiao

entry.summary: Introduces ACEsplat, a fast per-scene 3D Gaussian Splatting optimization framework that reconstructs from RGB images and poses only using a self-supervised scene-coordinate regression module, avoiding external SfM or depth priors. Builds an internal geometry prior in 4-5 minutes.

entry.title: When Robots Rate Their Own Interactions: Engagement Validity and the Strangeness Failure

author.name: Victor Lockwood, Hasan Mahmud, Mohammad Javad Khojasteh, Prabu David, Jamison Heard

entry.summary: Proposes inverted evaluation in which LLM-powered robots complete standard HRI questionnaires from their own perspective, testing agreement with human ground truth. Across five LLMs and over 1,500 evaluations, LLMs matched humans on engagement dimensions but systematically inverted comfort/strangeness ratings, revealing a key failure mode.

entry.title: TSD: A Physics-Inspired Trajectory Saliency Detector for Efficient Imitation Learning

author.name: Yiming Zhao, Gongrui Ma, Qingkai Li, Mingguo Zhao

entry.summary: TSD is a training-free, plug-and-play trajectory saliency detector that categorizes manipulation motions into transitional, precise, and agile types using physically grounded metrics (spatial entropy and centripetal acceleration) to prioritize task-critical segments for efficient imitation learning. It targets the high cost of collecting high-quality demonstration data.

entry.title: Nonparametric Deconvolution and Denoising using Simulation Based Inference

author.name: Ritwik Vashistha, Abhra Sarkar, Arya Farahi

entry.summary: Presents a likelihood-free, simulation-based framework for nonparametric density deconvolution and empirical Bayes denoising under additive measurement error, using a convolutional maximum mean discrepancy loss to match observed and noise-convolved model distributions. It yields a differentiable objective for multivariate latent signal recovery.

entry.title: A First-Order Mean Field Control Analysis of Transformer Layers under Cross-Entropy Training

author.name: Cheng Huan, Hongwei Yuan

entry.summary: Studies Transformer residual layers under cross-entropy training through a continuous-depth mean field control viewpoint, treating depth as time and proving pathwise approximation of finite-depth trajectories by a continuous controlled flow. It derives a Pontryagin optimality condition and sampling bounds for the empirical risk.

entry.title: Bridging Multi-Valued Heuristics and Dimensionality Reduction in Multi-Objective Search

author.name: Maya Wolff, Ariel Felner, Oren Salzman

entry.summary: Bridges multi-valued heuristics with dimensionality reduction in multi-objective shortest-path search, showing naive combination destroys ordering invariants. Proposes correct integration to retain richer Pareto-frontier guidance.

entry.title: Agent Behavior Mining: Generative AI Agent Governance in Business Processes

author.name: Hoang Vu, Maximilian K\"orner, Adrian Rebmann, Gabriel Kevorkian, Michael Perscheid, Gregor Berg, Timotheus Kampik

entry.summary: Introduces Agent Behavior Mining, applying process mining techniques to make generative AI agent decision-making observable and traceable in business processes. It includes an event data model translating reasoning traces and tool usage into analyzable form.

entry.title: PulseCX: Breaking the Closed-World Assumption in Real-Time CX

author.name: Rajat Agarwal, Suvidha Tripathi, Shubham Sharma

entry.summary: PulseCX breaks the closed-world assumption in customer-experience AI by decoupling knowledge acquisition from consumption via an asynchronous agent building a Decay-Aware Temporal Knowledge Graph governed by reinforcement-decay dynamics. It removes synchronous search latency bottlenecks with under 10ms overhead.

entry.title: Hypothesis-Driven Skill Optimization for LLM Agents

author.name: Fangxin Shang, Yehui Yang

entry.summary: HDSO is a train-free framework in which a frozen curator agent proposes falsifiable hypotheses about useful skills, validates them through paired control/treatment executions, and only commits skill updates that survive testing. It aims to make skill acquisition for agents robust against spurious shortcuts.

entry.title: Efficient Multimodal Clinical Question Answering for Pulmonary Embolism Risk Assessment

author.name: Xiangyuan Xue, Yang Yu, Yan Gao, Junyan Wang, Bin Chen, Lingyan Ruan, Ting Dang, Hong Jia

entry.summary: This work benchmarks compact multimodal LLMs on the INSPECT pulmonary-embolism dataset of over 23,000 CTPA studies, formulating eight diagnostic and prognostic tasks as structured clinical question answering. It evaluates efficient models in a clinically meaningful multimodal setting.

entry.title: PRIME: Evaluating Prompt Resolution Under Incompatible Instructions in LLMs

author.name: Tehreem Javed, Shumaim Fatimah, Masooma Bakhtiari, Gibrail Islam, Mehwish Fatima

entry.summary: PRIME is a framework that constructs calibrated conflicting instructions across length, format, and reasoning dimensions and classifies how LLMs resolve them via a deterministic behavioral taxonomy. It evaluates five open-weight instruction-tuned models on handling incompatible meta-instructions.

entry.title: A Topology-Aware, Memory-Centric Architecture that Separates Root-Cause Derivation from Root-Cause Explanation

author.name: Momil Seedat

entry.summary: OpsCortex is a topology-aware, memory-centric multi-agent prototype for microservice root-cause analysis that separates root-cause derivation from explanation using persistent operational memory across four tiers. It argues operational memory, not bigger models, is the missing ingredient for autonomous operations.

entry.title: BELDE: Building a Large-scale Earth-observation Land-cover Dataset for Europe

author.name: \"Umit Mert \c{C}a\u{g}lar, Alptekin Temizel

entry.summary: BELDE is a publicly available large-scale RGB-based land-cover segmentation dataset for Europe built from Sentinel-2 true-color imagery and ESA WorldCover annotations. It addresses limited geographic coverage and accessibility in existing datasets.

entry.title: ACE-GS: Acing the Trade-off with Accurate, Compact and Efficient 3D Gaussian Splatting

author.name: Jijian Zhao

entry.summary: ACE-GS is a progressive optimization framework for 3D Gaussian Splatting aiming to balance rendering quality, compactness, and reconstruction speed via momentum consistency-guided densification. It targets the trade-off where aggressive pruning loses high-frequency detail.

entry.title: Generating Public Health Responses using Survey-Augmented Large Language Models

author.name: Leonardo Marciaga, Thuyen Pham, Julia Rezvani, Alina Hyk, Chunyang Liao, Konstantinos Mitsopoulos, Raffaele Vardavas

entry.summary: This study generates synthetic survey responses using cluster-informed prompting of LLMs to reproduce vaccination attitude patterns from longitudinal FluPaths surveys. It investigates whether LLMs can substitute for costly repeated epidemiological surveys.

entry.title: Fine-Tuning Large Language Models for Quantum Reasoning

author.name: Katherine Ip, Casey R. Myers, Udaya Parampalli, James Quach, Peiyong Wang

entry.summary: Studies fine-tuning LLMs for genuine quantum reasoning using quantum circuit simulation (predicting measurement outcomes) as a training objective, rather than task-specific pattern matching. Probes whether LLMs can acquire deep domain reasoning in quantum computing.

entry.title: Neural Conjugate Aggregation: Identifiable Unsupervised Multi-Sensor Regression under Heterogeneous Sensor Bias

author.name: Muhammed Faruk Aytin, Zehra Demir, Alper \"Unal, Julian Marshall, G\"ozde \"Unal

entry.summary: Proposes NCAM, a hierarchical Bayesian framework combining neural networks with conjugate Gaussian inference for unsupervised multi-sensor regression under heterogeneous sensor bias without ground-truth labels. Yields identifiable source-specific bias/reliability and decomposed uncertainty.

entry.title: From Speech to Text Corpora: Evaluating ASR-Based Data Acquisition for Low-Resource Fongbe and Hausa

author.name: Mahounan Pericles Adjovi, Victor Olufemi, Roald Eiselen, Prasenjit Mitra

entry.summary: Investigates whether ASR pipelines can extend text corpora for low-resource Fongbe and Hausa, fine-tuning MMS-300M to achieve 9.48 percent WER on Fongbe (a 78 percent relative reduction) while preserving tonal diacritics. Catalogs and transcribes YouTube data to build new corpora.

entry.title: Benchmarking Robot Memory Under Interference

author.name: Soumil Rathi

entry.summary: Introduces RoboMME-Interference, a cross-session robot-memory benchmark built on RoboMME that constructs session histories with controlled numbers of unrelated distractor sessions. Measures how vision-language-action models retain and retrieve information under long-context interference.

entry.title: Adaptive Hard-Soft Physics-Informed Neural Networks for Robust Boundary-Constrained PDE Solving

author.name: Duc Tien Nguyen, Trinh Minh Tuan, Nguyen Duc Manh, Vu Linh Nguyen, Dinh Gia Ninh

entry.summary: Proposes HSPINN, a hybrid hard-soft physics-informed neural network that enforces boundary conditions exactly via analytical lifting while using adaptive loss weighting. Addresses slow convergence and poor boundary enforcement in standard PINNs.

entry.title: DVL-DeepONet: A Physics-Guided Operator Learning for Resilient Underwater Navigation

author.name: Arup Kumar Sahoo, Itzik Klein

entry.summary: DVL-DeepONet uses physics-guided operator learning to estimate underwater vehicle velocity when Doppler velocity log beams are noisy, incomplete, or when inertial sensors are absent. Aims for resilient autonomous underwater navigation under degraded conditions.

entry.title: MedTS-TTT: Test-Time Training for Medical Time Series Classification

author.name: Mingzhi Chen, Yiyu Gui, Guibo Luo

entry.summary: Proposes MedTS-TTT, a test-time training framework for medical time series classification that adapts online to subject-level distribution shift without expensive inner-loop optimization. Targets EEG/ECG applications where individual heterogeneity hurts generalization.

entry.title: Enhancing Creativity in 3D Generative Design via a TRIZ-Inspired Text-to-CAD Framework

author.name: Dongeon Lee, Leekyo Jeong, Soyoung Yoo, Sunwoong Yang, Namwoo Kang

entry.summary: Presents a TRIZ-inspired text-to-CAD framework that embeds inventive problem-solving principles into LLM prompting to generate creative, editable 3D CAD designs. Moves beyond geometric precision toward creative design exploration.

entry.title: One Size does not Fit All: Heterogeneous Latent Space Alignment for Unsupervised Domain Adaptation

author.name: Evangelia Koskinioti, Yi Shen, Georgios Stamou, Michael M. Zavlanos

entry.summary: Proposes ADualVUOT, a dual-encoder VAE with continuous normalizing flows and unbalanced optimal transport for unsupervised domain adaptation in medical image segmentation. Aims to improve expressiveness and robustness to domain shift over static augmentation methods.

entry.title: Stationary Robust Mean-Field Games under Model Mismatches

author.name: Yue Wang

entry.summary: Develops a stationary mean-field game framework incorporating distributional model uncertainty to make robust multi-agent RL tractable as agent counts grow. Establishes robust dynamic programming results under model mismatch.

entry.title: One-Step Flow Matching for Generative Modeling of Path-Dependent Physical Fields

author.name: Yijing Zhou, Jasmin Jelovica

entry.summary: Proposes a transformer-based one-step flow matching model for generating high-resolution path-dependent (plastic) physical stress fields, reducing sampling steps versus diffusion approaches. Targets expensive physical simulations.

entry.title: Towards Robust Personalized Federated Learning: Vulnerability Assessment and Defense Co-Design

author.name: Mingyuan Fan, Cen Chen

entry.summary: Reveals that personalized federated learning methods are more vulnerable to transfer-based adversarial attacks than centralized learning, where malicious clients exploit local models. Proposes a co-designed defense.

entry.title: PromptDyG: Test-Time Prompt Adaptation on Dynamic Graphs

author.name: Guoguo Ai, Chaoxi Niu, Hui Yan, Joey Tianyi Zhou, Yew-Soon Ong, Guansong Pang

entry.summary: Introduces PromptDyG, an unsupervised test-time prompt adaptation framework for discrete-time dynamic graphs that addresses evolving complexity and distribution shift in test snapshots. Moves beyond offline-trained dynamic graph models.

entry.title: Non-asymptotic estimates of the minimal risk in statistical learning

author.name: Liming Wu (Laboratoire de Math\'ematiques Blaise Pascal, CNRS-UMR 6620, Universit\'e Clermont Auvergne), Sen Yang (IASM, Harbin Institute of Technology)

entry.summary: Proves non-asymptotic concentration inequalities providing high-confidence lower and upper bounds on minimal risk in empirical risk minimization, relaxing boundedness to Gaussian/exponential integrability conditions. The lower-bound confidence is dimension- and parameter-count-independent.

entry.title: Input-schema identifiability limits in physics-informed surrogates for mechanics-governed flow

author.name: Daniel Cieslak, Andrzej Czyzewski

entry.summary: Introduces an input-schema identifiability certificate for physics-informed surrogate models, decomposing target fields into measurable, boundary-dependent, and symmetry-ambiguous components. It provides a pre-training audit predicting which interventions can reduce error in mechanics-governed flow modeling.

entry.title: No Reference-Free Generalization in Quantum Machine Learning

author.name: Jeongho Bang

entry.summary: This paper formalizes a fundamental generalization barrier in quantum machine learning: without an external reference frame, a learner cannot assign meaning to unseen quantum directions, and predictions must respect unitary symmetries unbroken by training data. It proves impossibility results when training states fail to span the Hilbert space.

entry.title: Scalable Bayesian Additive Models for Stellar Flare Detection via Amortized Gaussian Process Inference and Hidden Markov Models

author.name: Rodrigo Herrera, Vianey Leos-Barajas, Gwendolyn Eadie, Elizaveta Semenova, James Davenport

entry.summary: This work introduces a VAE-based generative surrogate of the Celerite Gaussian-process prior to enable scalable, amortized Bayesian inference for stellar flare detection in long astronomical time series. It combines hierarchical/additive GP modeling with hidden Markov models.

entry.title: Changing Modalities: Adapting Remote Sensing Models to New Satellites and Sensors

author.name: Tim G. Zhou, Anthony Fuller, Geoff Pleiss, Evan Shelhamer

entry.summary: DeluluNet is an architecture for adapting remote-sensing models to changing sensor modalities across three scenarios: substitution, superset, and subset. It learns a multimodal model from a unimodal teacher to enable redeployment with minimal retraining.

entry.title: Quality and Agreement in Multilabel Emotion Annotation: A Case Study and Evaluation Framework

author.name: Emily \"Ohman, Anna Koufakou

entry.summary: This case study examines multilabel emotion annotation, representing targets as soft vote-share labels instead of collapsing disagreement into majority-vote gold labels, and evaluates both thresholded and probabilistic metrics with disagreement diagnostics. It shows how annotator behavior and aggregation choices affect agreement and downstream classifiers.

entry.title: Towards Pedagogically Aligned LLM Tutors for Math Mistake Remediation

author.name: Kseniia Petukhova, Tien Dat Nguyen, Ekaterina Kochmar

entry.summary: Studies a two-stage SFT plus DPO alignment pipeline for math tutoring that guides students without revealing answers. Builds a dataset mixing real tutoring corpora and synthetic pedagogically-dimensioned data, improving both factual accuracy and pedagogical quality.

entry.title: Benchmarking Large Language Models for Grapheme-to-Phoneme Conversion: A Japanese Case Study

author.name: Tomoki Koriyama

entry.summary: Benchmarks over 30 LLMs on Japanese grapheme-to-phoneme conversion against conventional morphological analyzers on 3,000 annotated sentences. Best LLMs achieve under 0.52% kana CER versus 1.03% for the best traditional tool, with parse mode outperforming direct.

entry.title: Predicate Importance Estimation and Decoupled Rationale-Score Distillation for Entity Alignment

author.name: Keunha Kim, Yoonjin Jang, Hyeon-gu Lee, Sihyung Kim, Youngjoong Ko

entry.summary: Addresses entity alignment for integrating heterogeneous knowledge graphs in KG-RAG via Predicate Importance Estimation and Decoupled Rationale-Score Distillation. PIE encodes subjectless triples to handle predicate-name variation and incomplete neighborhoods.

entry.title: Chehre: An Emoji-Prompted Video Dataset for Perceptually Diverse Facial Expression Recognition

author.name: Bita Azari, Zoe Stanley, Avneet Batra, Poorvi Bhatia, Hali Kil, Manolis Savva, Angelica Lim

entry.summary: Introduces Chehre, an emoji-prompted video dataset of dynamic facial expressions where facial motions are transferred to synthetic faces for privacy. It captures inter-individual perceptual diversity with thousands of annotated videos from hundreds of performers.

entry.title: TeleStyle V2: Beyond Content-Preserving Style Transfer with Self-Distillation and Distribution-Matching-Distillation

author.name: Shiwen Zhang, Yifan Xu, Haibin Huang, Chi Zhang, Xuelong Li

entry.summary: Presents TeleStyle V2, extending content-preserving style transfer to handle all four combinations of realistic and stylized content/style references via self-distillation and distribution-matching distillation. Broadens applicability beyond V1's constraints.

entry.title: LEViL: Label-Efficient Video Learning via Zero-Shot Distillation over VLM-Generated Pseudo-Label Spaces

author.name: Asl{\i} \c{C}elik

entry.summary: Proposes LEViL, a label-efficient video learning framework combining annotation-free VLM-generated pseudo-label pretraining with target-label-set-aware fine-tuning. Reduces reliance on large labeled source datasets for action recognition.

entry.title: Zero-Shot Vision-Language Models for Classroom Engagement Recognition: A Benchmark Study of Prompt Sensitivity and Cross-Dataset Generalization

author.name: Aman Goyal, Kshama Nitin Shah, Kemmannu Vineet Venkatesh Rao

entry.summary: A benchmark study evaluating five vision-language models on zero-shot classroom engagement recognition across two educational datasets, probing prompt sensitivity and cross-dataset generalization. It identifies key failure modes of current VLMs for this task.

entry.title: Interest Entanglement: The Hidden Barrier to Blind Super-Resolution Optimization

author.name: Junxiong Lin, Xinji Mai, Qianyu Guo, Haoran Wang, Zeng Tao, Xuan Tong, Ivy Pan, Wenqiang Zhang

entry.summary: Identifies an Interest Entanglement problem in blind super-resolution multi-objective optimization between fidelity and perceptual quality, exploring frequency-based analysis beyond simple loss-weight tuning. Reframes the fidelity-perception conflict.

entry.title: Venice-H1: Failure-Aware Query Re-Ranking with Multi-Scale Grid Signatures for Referring Image Segmentation

author.name: Nicol\`o Savioli

entry.summary: Introduces Venice-H1, a lightweight post-hoc re-ranking module for referring image segmentation that encodes candidate masks via multi-scale grid signatures with a transformer re-ranker and a failure gate that intervenes only on likely failures. Targets the residual 7-18% of failures dominating the error budget.

entry.title: Full-Body Golf Swing Kinematic Reconstruction From a Smartwatch IMU

author.name: Yuanshuo Tan, Kezhe Zhu, Xiujie Sun, Chunping Liang, Shuoyang Zhu, Chenquan Xu, Licheng Zhong, Huiming Pan, Yinri Jin, Chang Liu, Bo Xiao, Shenglong Le, Bryndan W. Lindsey, Peter B. Shull

entry.summary: Proposes WIT-KinNet, a single wrist-worn IMU approach for reconstructing full-body golf swing joint angles, using modality-specific IMU embeddings and temporal kinematic encoding to learn wrist-to-body motion dependencies. Avoids laboratory-bound motion capture and multi-sensor setups.

entry.title: Concept Alignment Contrast and Long-Short Prompt Memory for Test-Time Adaptation of SAM3 in Medical Image Segmentation

author.name: Yubo Zhou, Jianghao Wu, Ping Ye, Shaoting Zhang, Guotai Wang

entry.summary: Proposes test-time adaptation for SAM3 in medical image segmentation using concept alignment contrast and long-short prompt memory, targeting region-level semantic correctness rather than image-level uncertainty. Addresses the domain gap when applying natural-image foundation models to medical scans.
